records.question: The UAV agent is returning to launch under URLLC slice with 8ms latency, 1ms jitter, 0.05% loss, and 130Mbps throughput, while edge load is at 0.32. Historical data shows eMBB degraded from 12ms to 18ms latency over 6 turns with edge load rising from 0.45 to 0.65. If wind speed increases to 10.5m/s and thermal sensors remain offline, the next 2 turns may see edge load rise to 0.45 under eMBB or 0.38 under URLLC. SLA requires latency under 15ms and throughput above 100Mbps for safety-critical commands. Under worst-case wind and sensor failure, which network slice should the agent maintain for the next 3 turns to minimize maximum regret across latency, throughput, and edge load violation risk? A) Stay on URLLC despite lower throughput. B) Switch to eMBB for higher throughput, accepting latency risk. C) Alternate slices every turn to balance load. D) Request manual override from ground control.

options.A: Stay on URLLC despite lower throughput.
options.B: Switch to eMBB for higher throughput, accepting latency risk.
options.C: Alternate slices every turn to balance load.
options.D: Request manual override from ground control.

records.question: The UAV is returning to launch with battery at 85% and must decide whether to initiate federated model aggregation now or defer until landing. Current eMBB slice offers 840 Mbps throughput but edge load is 0.42 and rising; URLLC slice offers 130 Mbps with edge load 0.32 and stable. Historical data shows edge load increases 0.05 per turn under eMBB and 0.02 under URLLC. Federated aggregation requires 2.1 GB of data transfer and must complete within 3 turns to avoid SLA violation. If edge load exceeds 0.7, latency spikes to 30 ms and throughput drops 60%. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Initiate aggregation now over eMBB: current throughput 840 Mbps allows completion in 2.1 turns, edge load 0.42 is below threshold, and battery is sufficient.
options.B: Defer aggregation until landing: battery will be at 75%, edge load will be 0.57 under eMBB, and throughput may drop to 336 Mbps if load exceeds 0.7.
options.C: Switch to URLLC and initiate now: throughput 130 Mbps requires 16.2 turns, exceeding SLA, but edge load remains safe at 0.32.
options.D: Initiate over eMBB but with throttled rate: reduce throughput to 400 Mbps to cap edge load at 0.5, completing in 4.2 turns, risking SLA violation.

records.question: The UAV is returning to launch under URLLC with 8ms latency, 1% loss, and 130Mbps throughput, while edge load is 0.32. A third-party analytics agent requests access to raw thermal and lidar data for predictive maintenance, citing a 95% trust score and compliance with GDPR. However, thermal and lidar sensors remain offline, and the UAV’s battery is at 100% but will deplete at 2% per minute under current flight profile. The policy allows data exposure only if network latency is under 10ms and edge load remains below 0.4 for the next two turns. Historical data shows edge load increases by 0.05 per turn under eMBB and 0.02 under URLLC. If the UAV switches to eMBB for data upload, latency rises to 14ms and edge load jumps to 0.48, risking SLA violation. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Grant full access under URLLC with current metrics, assuming sensors will reactivate within 2 turns and edge load will not exceed 0.4.
options.B: Deny access and maintain URLLC, preserving safety margins for return, since sensor data is currently unavailable and exposure adds no value.
options.C: Switch to eMBB to enable data upload, accepting 14ms latency and 0.48 edge load, because the agent’s trust score justifies the risk and data is valuable for future missions.
options.D: Grant partial access under URLLC for metadata only, deferring raw data until sensors reactivate and edge load stabilizes below 0.4 for two consecutive turns.

records.question: At turn 11, the UAV is returning to launch with a battery at 100%, but network telemetry shows URLCC slice latency at 8ms, jitter at 1ms, loss at 0.05%, throughput at 130Mbps, and edge load at 0.32. Historical data from turn 5 showed eMBB latency spiking to 16ms with 0.4% loss and edge load at 0.6, and turn 7’s switch to URLLC reduced latency to 9ms but capped throughput at 100Mbps. A new anomaly detection system flags a 15% probability of a replay attack on the control channel if eMBB is reselected, which could increase latency by 3–7ms over the next two turns. The mission SLA requires latency under 12ms for control and throughput above 100Mbps for telemetry. Which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next three turns while maintaining safety and SLA compliance?

options.A: Remain on URLLC: latency 8ms, jitter 1ms, throughput 130Mbps, edge load 0.32 — satisfies SLA and avoids replay risk but may underutilize bandwidth if no attack occurs.
options.B: Switch to eMBB: latency 14ms, jitter 3ms, throughput 840Mbps, edge load 0.42 — exceeds throughput SLA but risks latency violation if replay attack materializes (worst-case latency 21ms).
options.C: Switch to eMBB with 50% bandwidth reservation: latency 14ms, throughput 420Mbps, edge load 0.45 — reduces throughput risk but still exposes to latency violation under attack (worst-case 21ms).
options.D: Initiate isolation mode: disable all network slices, use local GNSS/IMU for return, latency undefined, throughput 0Mbps — guarantees no replay risk but violates SLA and risks mission failure if GNSS degrades.

records.question: At turn 6 the operator requests high resolution imaging while the UAV is in transit and the network slice is eMBB with latency 500 ms, jitter 50 ms, loss 5.0 percent, throughput 200 Mbps, and edge load 0.9. Earlier turns show eMBB latency rising from 12 ms at turn 1 to 15 ms at turn 5 while edge load increased from 0.4 to 0.6. The policy requires safe command and control within the altitude bounds 0 to 300 m, and the UAV is currently at 50 m with battery at 100 percent and speed 35 mps. URLLC at turn 7 shows latency 7 ms, jitter 0.8 ms, loss 0.02 percent, throughput 80 Mbps, and edge load 0.25. The mission intent favors immediate imaging, but network policy prioritizes control reliability during return and landing phases expected within the next two turns. Jitter implies worst case latency could exceed the mean by its full value. If degradation persists for one more turn on eMBB, edge load trends suggest further congestion. Conversely URLLC capacity is lower and sustained imaging could crowd it over multiple turns. Each option below trades imaging fidelity against control margin and future regret over turns 7 to 9. Considering worst case jitter, projected edge load, and the need to minimize maximum regret across the next two turns, which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue imaging immediately on eMBB at 200 Mbps despite 500 ms latency and 5.0 percent loss because throughput meets sensor needs this turn.
options.B: Switch to URLLC and execute only queued non imaging control tasks with 7 ms latency and 0.25 edge load, deferring imaging until after return.
options.C: Remain on eMBB but throttle imaging to reduce edge load from 0.9 while accepting current jitter of 50 ms.
options.D: Switch to URLLC and perform limited imaging using 80 Mbps throughput since current latency is under 10 ms.

records.question: At turn 7 the swarm experiences contention because one UAV has switched to URLLC with latency 7 ms, jitter 0.8 ms, loss 0.02 percent, throughput 80 Mbps, and edge load 0.25 while other members previously observed eMBB degradation at turn 6 with latency 500 ms, jitter 50 ms, loss 5.0 percent, throughput 200 Mbps, and edge load 0.9. Across turns 7 to 10 URLLC latency fluctuates between the observed values of 7 ms and 10 ms and jitter between 0.7 ms and 1.5 ms. The UAV speed is 35.0 mps and battery is 100.0 percent so mission timing pressure is low but collision avoidance remains active. Swarm fairness requires avoiding monopolizing URLLC if safety margins permit, yet safety requires maintaining low latency during deconfliction. If degradation similar to turn 6 recurs for one more turn, eMBB would again see loss 5.0 percent and latency 500 ms with edge load 0.9. If URLLC demand increases, its throughput remains between 80 and 95 Mbps and edge load between 0.24 and 0.3 as observed. The decision must consider worst case latency and jitter over the next two turns rather than the current snapshot. One option favors immediate fairness, one favors strict safety, one ignores uncertainty, and one balances regret. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Keep all swarm members on URLLC because latency has stayed between 7 and 10 ms and loss below 0.1 percent even if throughput is only 80 to 95 Mbps and edge load is around 0.25.
options.B: Immediately revert all non landing traffic to eMBB since current URLLC edge load is only 0.25 to 0.3 and eMBB previously delivered 750 to 850 Mbps throughput.
options.C: Split slices by keeping deconfliction on URLLC and moving imaging and planning to eMBB while monitoring for a repeat of 500 ms latency and 5.0 percent loss.
options.D: Delay any slice changes for one turn because current URLLC jitter is below 1.5 ms and loss below 0.08 percent so fairness can be reassessed later.

records.question: During turn 7 the agent switched to URLLC for agent-to-agent coordination after observing severe eMBB degradation at turn 6. Across turns 3 to 11, URLLC latency varied between 7 and 10 ms, jitter between 0.7 and 1.5 ms, loss between 0.02 and 0.1 percent, throughput between 80 and 95 Mbps, and edge load between 0.24 and 0.35. Over the same episode, eMBB latency ranged from 12 to 500 ms, jitter from 2 to 50 ms, loss from 0.1 to 5.0 percent, throughput from 200 to 850 Mbps, and edge load from 0.4 to 0.9. The UAV is returning at 35.0 mps with battery at 100.0 percent, so coordination must remain stable for at least the next two turns until landing. There is uncertainty whether the eMBB slice will remain congested like turn 6 or recover to turn 5 levels in the next turn. URLLC capacity is lower in throughput, which risks backlog if edge load rises again toward 0.35. Direct agent-to-agent messages are small but timing sensitive, and delayed coordination could propagate errors over two turns. A myopic choice would optimize current latency, while a cautious choice minimizes worst-case regret if congestion persists. The decision must account for worst-case latency and loss rather than mean values alone. Assume no new slices can be created and only routing and prioritization can change. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Keep all agent-to-agent traffic on URLLC with current parameters, accepting 80 to 95 Mbps throughput and edge load up to 0.35 over the next two turns.
options.B: Immediately switch agent-to-agent traffic back to eMBB to exploit potential recovery to 15 ms latency and 750 Mbps throughput seen at turn 5.
options.C: Split agent-to-agent traffic by sending time-critical messages on URLLC and noncritical coordination on eMBB, assuming average rather than worst-case loss.
options.D: Route all agent-to-agent traffic over eMBB but throttle updates to tolerate up to 50 ms jitter if congestion reappears.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV is executing a maneuver while the network slice is mMTC with latency 22 ms, jitter 6 ms, loss 1.2 percent, throughput 0.8 Mbps, and edge load 0.82. The immediately prior turn 6 also used mMTC with latency 18 ms, jitter 5 ms, loss 0.8 percent, throughput 1.2 Mbps, and edge load 0.75, establishing an observed degradation range rather than a single point. Mission intent requires stable navigation and sensing while respecting the policy altitude bounds of 5 to 80 meters, and the UAV is currently at 15 meters with full battery. Earlier turns show that eMBB provides latencies of 10 to 13 ms with throughput 820 to 900 Mbps and edge load near 0.33 to 0.37, while URLLC provides latencies of 7 to 9 ms but throughput only 110 to 130 Mbps with edge load around 0.38 to 0.42. The user intent to resume full sensing at turn 8 succeeded only after returning to eMBB, indicating that mMTC cannot sustain high data demand. However, switching slices too aggressively risks violating mission intent if worst case degradation persists for another turn or if edge load spikes again. Assume the mMTC degradation range of loss 0.8 to 1.2 percent and latency 18 to 22 ms can persist for one to two more turns. Assume also that URLLC throughput remains capped near 120 Mbps and eMBB edge load could rise back toward 0.37 next turn. The conflict is whether to prioritize mission sensing continuity or conservative network policy under uncertainty. Each option below is acceptable in the current turn but differs in worst case future regret over the next two turns. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Remain on mMTC at 22 ms latency and 1.2 percent loss to respect conservative network usage and avoid slice switching overhead despite low throughput of 0.8 Mbps.
options.B: Switch immediately to URLLC with 7 to 9 ms latency and 0.01 to 0.04 percent loss even though throughput is limited to about 115 Mbps and may constrain full sensing next turn.
options.C: Switch to eMBB with 11 to 13 ms latency, 820 to 880 Mbps throughput, and edge load near 0.33 to 0.37 to support sensing while accepting moderate latency.
options.D: Delay any slice change for one more turn on mMTC assuming loss returns to 0.8 percent and latency to 18 ms as seen previously.

records.question: At turn 8 the user resumes full sensing after prior network degradation while the UAV remains within altitude bounds of 5.0 to 80.0 meters. Earlier, edge load rose from 0.75 at turn 6 to 0.82 at turn 7 on mMTC with latency 22 ms and loss 1.2 percent. The resume command coincides with a switch back to eMBB showing latency 11 ms, jitter 1.8 ms, loss 0.08 percent, throughput 880 Mbps, and edge load 0.33. The initial mission intent emphasized navigation and inspection, not sustained high bandwidth streaming under unstable conditions. Over the prior three turns, intent-related actions oscillated between reducing and enabling sensor streaming while network slices changed. If edge load rebounds toward prior mMTC levels within one to two turns, full sensing may again be throttled. The altitude policy range creates uncertainty because maneuvering headroom exists but does not address network stress. A single turn view suggests recovery, but a multi turn view must consider regret if degradation persists. Which option best identifies an intent drift that minimizes worst case regret over the next two turns?

options.A: Treat the resume full sensing at edge load 0.33 as consistent with original inspection intent because current latency 11 ms and loss 0.08 percent are low.
options.B: Flag a potential intent drift because oscillation between reduce and enable sensing across edge load 0.82 to 0.33 suggests a shift toward bandwidth maximization despite earlier adaptation.
options.C: Assume no drift since altitude remains within 5.0 to 80.0 and throughput recovered to 880 Mbps, so intent is unchanged.
options.D: Ignore drift for now and wait one turn because the last URLLC latency of 9 ms previously supported safe maneuvering.

records.question: At turn 7, the swarm experiences contention while the UAV is executing an altitude adjustment after interference was detected. Recent telemetry shows the slice has swung from URLLC latency of 7 to 9 ms with jitter 0.6 to 1.0 ms and loss 0.01 to 0.03, to mMTC latency 18 to 22 ms with jitter 5 to 6 and loss 0.8 to 1.2. Edge load simultaneously rose from 0.38 to 0.82 while throughput collapsed from 130 to 0.8 Mbps, indicating fairness pressure from other swarm members. Maintaining collision safety during maneuvering favors low latency and loss, but starving peers risks future denial of URLLC access. If congestion persists for the next two turns, edge load is likely to remain near its recent peak rather than reverting to the earlier 0.3 to 0.42 levels. The operator must choose a slice allocation that balances immediate safety against fair access over the next three turns. Option A keeps URLLC now because 7 to 9 ms latency looks safest in the current turn despite rising edge load. Option B switches to eMBB at 11 to 13 ms latency and 0.08 to 0.12 loss, narrowly meeting safety at the mean but leaving little margin if jitter rises. Option C stays on mMTC assuming the mean 18 ms latency is acceptable and ignores the 22 ms worst case with 1.2 loss. Which option should be selected to minimize worst case regret across the next one to three turns?

options.A: Keep URLLC with 7 to 9 ms latency and edge load around 0.38 to 0.42, accepting fairness pressure on the swarm.
options.B: Switch to eMBB with 11 to 13 ms latency, 0.08 to 0.12 loss, and lower edge load near 0.33 to 0.37.
options.C: Remain on mMTC with 18 to 22 ms latency, 0.8 to 1.2 loss, and edge load around 0.75 to 0.82.
options.D: Alternate between URLLC and eMBB each turn to average latency near 10 to 11 ms while tolerating edge load volatility.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV is executing a maneuver with speed 18.0 mps at altitude 15.0 while the network slice is mMTC. Telemetry shows latency 22 ms, jitter 6 ms, loss 1.2 percent, throughput 0.8 mbps, and edge load 0.82 after rising from 0.75 at turn 6. Policy altitude bounds remain 5.0 to 80.0 and the geofence is 200.0 by 150.0, so navigation margin is spatially safe but communication margin is tightening. In the previous turn the same slice showed latency 18 ms and loss 0.8 percent, indicating a worsening trend rather than a spike. Full sensing was already reduced once and could be re enabled later if conditions recover. If degradation persists for the next two turns, edge load could approach saturation while the UAV continues at the same speed. A preemptive autonomy downgrade would trade capability now to avoid loss of control later. One option optimizes the current turn by trusting that eMBB recovery like turn 8 will recur. Another option barely meets present conditions but fails if the worst case within policy bounds occurs. Another option ignores uncertainty by assuming the network trend reverses immediately. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Maintain current autonomy and speed 18.0 mps on mMTC since latency 22 ms and loss 1.2 percent are still manageable this turn with edge load 0.82.
options.B: Switch immediately to URLLC and restore full sensing because earlier URLLC showed latency 7 to 9 ms and loss near 0.01 percent.
options.C: Preemptively downgrade autonomy by further reducing sensing and slowing maneuver execution to tolerate throughput 0.8 mbps and rising edge load from 0.75 to 0.82.
options.D: Hold autonomy level but descend toward the lower policy bound of 5.0 to rely on spatial margin while keeping current network settings.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV is mid mission with degraded networking after switching to mMTC and reduced sensor streaming. The current telemetry shows latency 22 ms, jitter 6 ms, loss 1.2 pct, throughput 0.8 Mbps, and edge load 0.82 while flying at 18.0 mps and altitude within the 5.0 to 80.0 bound. Earlier turns showed that edge load can drop back to 0.33 to 0.37 on eMBB but also spike above 0.75 during adjustments. The battery is still at 100.0 pct, but GNSS was degraded at turn 5 and full sensing was only restored at turn 8. The operator must decide whether to conservatively continue the mission plan for the next two turns under uncertainty about whether mMTC conditions persist. If network degradation persists one more turn, higher loss and edge load may compound while altitude must remain within policy bounds. If recovery occurs as at turn 8, throughput and loss improve but only after another maneuver. Each option below incurs some regret either from risking control quality, delaying completion, or increasing future network stress. The decision should minimize the worst case regret across the next one to three turns rather than optimize the current snapshot. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue immediately at 18.0 mps under mMTC with edge load 0.82, accepting loss 1.2 pct and assuming recovery next turn.
options.B: Continue but hold current altitude well within the 5.0 to 80.0 range and keep reduced sensing for two turns to limit edge load growth from 0.82.
options.C: Switch back to eMBB now based on prior latency near 11 ms and edge load near 0.33, assuming the spike at turn 7 was transient.
options.D: Pause forward progress for one turn to wait for network recovery, despite latency already at 22 ms and battery at 100.0 pct.

records.question: At turn 8 the swarm lead observes recovery to an eMBB slice with latency 11 ms, jitter 1.8 ms, loss 0.08 percent, throughput 880 Mbps, and edge load 0.33. Over the prior three turns, URLLC showed latency between 7 and 9 ms, jitter between 0.6 and 1.1 ms, loss between 0.01 and 0.04 percent, throughput between 110 and 130 Mbps, and edge load between 0.38 and 0.42. During degradation the mMTC slice reached latency 18 to 22 ms, jitter 5 to 6 ms, loss 0.8 to 1.2 percent, throughput 0.8 to 1.2 Mbps, and edge load 0.75 to 0.82. The mission phase over the next two turns includes return and landing within altitude bounds 5.0 to 80.0 and requires coordination with two peer agents sharing the same edge. Assume uncertainty persists so that worst case values within the observed ranges can occur again for one more turn. The swarm must negotiate a slice allocation that minimizes maximum regret if interference reappears while still supporting inspection data already captured. Giving all agents URLLC reduces latency now but risks edge load growth, while eMBB maximizes throughput but tolerates higher jitter. mMTC is safest for control chatter but starves data flows. Each option below assigns a dominant slice for the swarm over the next two turns with a stated constraint. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Assign URLLC to all agents for the next two turns, accepting throughput near 110 to 130 Mbps and edge load up to 0.42 to guarantee sub 9 ms latency.
options.B: Assign eMBB to all agents for the next two turns, relying on 820 to 900 Mbps throughput and edge load near 0.33 to 0.37 while accepting jitter around 2.1 ms.
options.C: Assign mMTC to all agents for the next two turns, tolerating latency up to 22 ms and loss up to 1.2 percent to keep edge load below 0.82 under interference.
options.D: Assign URLLC for control and eMBB for data across the swarm, capping edge load at observed 0.41 while allowing throughput above 820 Mbps for one more turn.

records.question: At turn 7 the AI scheduler has reconfigured tasks after sensing degradation while the network slice is mMTC. Recent telemetry shows latency rising from 18 to 22 ms, jitter fluctuating between 5 and 6 ms, loss increasing from 0.8 to 1.2 pct, and edge load climbing from 0.75 to 0.82. Throughput has fallen from 1.2 to 0.8 Mbps while the UAV is executing a maneuver at 18.0 mps and holding altitude within the 5.0 to 80.0 policy bounds. The scheduler must choose a consistent configuration for the next two turns assuming the mMTC condition could persist or recover as it did by turn 8. If degradation persists one more turn, worst case latency would stay at the observed maximum and loss would not improve. If recovery occurs, eMBB characteristics seen earlier could return with latency near 11 ms and edge load near 0.33. Re-enabling full sensing immediately risks overloading the edge if mMTC continues. Keeping reduced sensing too long risks missing inspection consistency before return to base. A hybrid option is to defer scheduler changes until after altitude stabilization from turn 6 completes. The scheduler must minimize maximum regret across these futures while maintaining consistency with prior adaptations. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Immediately switch back to eMBB-style scheduling and full sensing because earlier latency of 11 ms and edge load of 0.33 were acceptable.
options.B: Lock the reduced-sensing mMTC scheduler for the next two turns despite throughput being only 0.8 Mbps and loss up to 1.2 pct.
options.C: Maintain reduced sensing for one more turn under mMTC limits of 22 ms latency and 0.82 edge load, then conditionally revert if metrics improve.
options.D: Force URLLC scheduling now since latency was as low as 7 to 9 ms in later turns and altitude remains within 5.0 to 80.0.

records.question: At turn 7 the agent has reduced sensor streaming after mMTC degradation with latency 22 ms, jitter 6 ms, loss 1.2 percent, throughput 0.8 Mbps, and edge load 0.82. In earlier turns the agent used URLLC with latency between 7 and 9 ms and edge load near 0.4 to execute maneuvers safely. At turn 8 the network shifts back to eMBB with latency 11 ms, jitter 1.8 ms, loss 0.08 percent, throughput 880 Mbps, and edge load 0.33. The policy altitude bounds remain between 5 and 80 meters and the UAV is already flying at 15 meters. Battery is still at 100 percent so energy is not the immediate limiter. The replanning choice must avoid contradicting the prior decision to reduce streaming unless the future regret over the next two turns is lower. If congestion similar to turn 7 recurs once more, edge load could again exceed 0.75 while throughput collapses below 1 Mbps. If full sensing is resumed now, the agent risks repeating a reduce enable flip across consecutive turns. If sensing remains reduced, inspection quality suffers but maneuver stability is preserved across slices. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Immediately resume full sensing on eMBB because latency 11 ms and throughput 880 Mbps are better than at turn 7.
options.B: Keep reduced sensing for the next two turns because edge load previously reached 0.82 and could again exceed 0.75 under mMTC.
options.C: Switch to URLLC and resume full sensing since latency was as low as 7 ms and loss 0.01 percent earlier.
options.D: Alternate sensing modes each turn to track current slice metrics while staying within altitude bounds of 5 to 80 meters.

records.question: At turn 9 the UAV has completed inspection and is on an eMBB slice with latency 13 ms, jitter 2.1 ms, loss 0.12 percent, throughput 820 Mbps, and edge load 0.37. Earlier in the episode the same slice showed throughput as high as 900 Mbps with edge load 0.30, while mMTC degraded to throughput 0.8 to 1.2 Mbps with edge load up to 0.82. The UAV battery is at 100 percent and speed is 18 mps, but return to base is commanded next turn over URLLC where throughput is only about 115 Mbps and edge load about 0.41. Federated learning updates would contend with navigation and sensing traffic for the next two turns if scheduled immediately. Assume network conditions can revert to the worst previously observed values without warning. If training is delayed one turn, only URLLC connectivity is available before landing. If training is delayed two turns, connectivity ends entirely. All options incur some loss of model freshness or mission risk. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Start a full federated training round immediately on eMBB at turn 9, using the current 820 Mbps throughput and 0.37 edge load to maximize freshness despite possible regression to 0.30 to 0.82 edge load.
options.B: Defer federated training to turn 10 on URLLC, accepting 115 Mbps throughput and about 0.41 edge load to avoid any chance of mMTC-level congestion.
options.C: Skip training this mission and upload data post-landing, avoiding all in-flight network risk but guaranteeing at least two turns of staleness.
options.D: Perform a partial federated update at turn 9 sized to tolerate a drop from 900 to 820 Mbps and bounded by the worst-case 0.82 edge load seen earlier.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV is executing a maneuver while network conditions have degraded on the mMTC slice with latency 22 ms, jitter 6 ms, loss 1.2 percent, throughput 0.8 Mbps, and edge load 0.82. The UAV is at altitude 15.0 m within the allowed 5.0 to 80.0 m bounds, moving at 18.0 mps with battery at 100.0 percent, and all sensors except radar are available. One option is to immediately re-enable all sensors with full RGB, thermal, and lidar fusion assuming recovery next turn. Another option is to keep only lidar and IMU fused locally while deferring RGB and thermal streams until edge load drops below earlier eMBB levels. A third option is to switch to URLLC and fuse RGB and lidar despite the lower throughput of 110 to 130 Mbps seen previously. A fourth option is to rely on GNSS and IMU only, accepting reduced perception but minimal bandwidth use. Considering worst case network metrics persisting for two more turns and minimizing maximum regret across those turns, which option should be selected?

options.A: Re-enable full RGB, thermal, and lidar fusion now, using 0.8 Mbps mMTC throughput and assuming latency returns toward 11 ms next turn.
options.B: Maintain only lidar and IMU local fusion while postponing RGB and thermal until edge load falls from 0.82 toward the prior 0.33 level.
options.C: Switch to URLLC and fuse RGB with lidar, accepting 110 to 130 Mbps throughput and edge load around 0.4 as seen earlier.
options.D: Disable all exteroceptive sensors except GNSS and IMU to minimize bandwidth under 1.2 percent loss conditions.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV is adapting to network degradation while operating inside a geofence of 200.0 by 150.0 meters and altitude bounds of 5.0 to 80.0 meters. During turns 6 and 7 the slice is mMTC with latency observed between 18 and 22 ms, jitter between 5 and 6 ms, loss between 0.8 and 1.2 percent, throughput between 1.2 and 0.8 Mbps, and edge load rising from 0.75 to 0.82. A coordination decision must balance safety now against regret if conditions do not recover in the next two turns. One option is to escalate to URLLC immediately, another is to remain on mMTC with reduced sensing, another is to switch back to eMBB with full sensing, and another is to hold position within current altitude. Each option has a downside within the next one to three turns. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Escalate to URLLC now using the observed 7 to 9 ms latency and accept the 110 to 130 Mbps throughput while keeping speed at 18.0 mps.
options.B: Remain on mMTC with reduced sensing given the current 18 to 22 ms latency and 0.8 to 1.2 percent loss to avoid increasing edge load beyond 0.82.
options.C: Switch back to eMBB with full sensing at 11 to 13 ms latency and 820 to 900 Mbps throughput despite prior edge load around 0.33 to 0.37.
options.D: Hold position within the 5.0 to 80.0 meter altitude bounds for one turn while keeping the current slice and reassessing next turn.

records.question: At turn 8 the operator considers granting a third party analytics agent access during the return sequence. The agent previously saw URLLC latency of 7 to 9 ms with jitter 0.6 to 1.1 ms and loss 0.01 to 0.04 during turns 5 and 10. During network stress at turns 6 and 7 the slice shifted to mMTC with latency 18 to 22 ms, jitter 5 to 6 ms, loss 0.8 to 1.2 and edge load 0.75 to 0.82. At turn 8 eMBB recovers with latency 11 ms, jitter 1.8 ms, loss 0.08, throughput 880 Mbps and edge load 0.33. Battery remains at 100 percent but return to base occurs over the next two turns using URLLC again. The third party offers four exposure modes that differ in data scope and compute calls and each would add incremental edge load in the next turns. Consent allows data sharing but policy requires avoiding cascading degradation if mMTC conditions reappear. Assume worst case that the mMTC degradation persists for one more turn after exposure. One option looks best now but risks pushing edge load past the stressed values seen earlier. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Grant full sensor data plus compute APIs immediately, assuming eMBB latency 11 ms and edge load 0.33 can absorb the added load this turn.

records.question: At turn 8 the UAV initiates inspection image capture while flying at 25 mps with battery still near 100 percent and sensors active except lidar and radar. records.question: The UAV is returning to base under URLLC slice with 4ms latency, 0.6ms jitter, 0.04% loss, 47Mbps throughput, and 0.35 edge load. A third-party analytics firm requests 300ms of compute time on the edge node to process lidar scans, which would increase edge load to 0.85 and degrade latency to 12ms with 5% packet loss under worst-case weather. The SLA guarantees latency <10ms and loss <1% for URLLC. If the request is denied, the firm will switch to a competitor’s cloud with 50ms latency. If accepted, the UAV’s return path may experience 200ms delay if edge load exceeds 0.8. The mission must complete within 120s or risk battery depletion below 10%. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Accept the request; edge load will peak at 0.85 but return to 0.35 within 2 turns, and the firm’s cloud alternative has 50ms latency which violates SLA.
options.B: Reject the request; worst-case latency of 12ms exceeds SLA, and the 200ms delay risk during return path could cause battery depletion below 10%.
options.C: Accept with throttling; limit compute to 150ms to keep edge load at 0.65, ensuring latency stays under 8ms and loss under 0.5%.
options.D: Defer the request; queue it for execution after UAV lands, accepting 50ms cloud latency for now to preserve SLA and battery safety.

records.question: At turn 9, the UAV is adapting its inspection strategy under deteriorating network conditions: URLLC slice latency is 6ms with 1.0ms jitter and 0.1% loss, while edge load is 0.45. The mission requires RAG-augmented decision-making for sensor fusion, with a policy SLA of 10ms max latency and 1% max loss. Historical data shows eMBB slice latency increased from 12ms to 18ms over two turns, and mMTC slice loss reached 2.5%. If the next turn projects edge load to rise to 0.55 under URLLC, and thermal support requires 15ms latency tolerance, which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next two turns while preserving mission continuity?

options.A: Continue using URLLC with current parameters; latency and loss are within SLA, and edge load is projected to remain below 0.6.
options.B: Switch to eMBB for thermal support; it offers 80Mbps throughput and previously handled sensor data, despite 18ms latency and 3% loss at turn 8.
options.C: Fallback to mMTC for minimal bandwidth; it has 5Mbps throughput but 25ms latency and 2.5% loss, which exceeds SLA but may suffice for low-priority metadata.
options.D: Hybrid mode: use URLLC for control and eMBB for thermal data; accept 12ms average latency and 1.5% loss, with edge load projected to hit 0.7 next turn.

records.question: An AI agent operating a UAV in icing conditions must decide whether to onboard a thermal support agent for redundancy. Current network slice is URLLC with 6ms latency, 1.0ms jitter, 0.1% loss, and 35Mbps throughput. Edge load is 0.45. The thermal agent requires 10ms latency, 2ms jitter, and 50Mbps throughput to function. Historical data shows edge load increases by 0.15 per turn under URLLC when additional agents are onboarded. If the thermal agent is onboarded, projected edge load next turn is 0.60. If not, the UAV must rely on lidar alone, which has a 15% failure rate per turn under icing. The mission SLA requires 99.9% reliability over 3 turns. What is the optimal identity onboarding decision given worst-case network degradation and sensor failure probabilities? Which option should be selected?

options.A: Onboard thermal agent immediately; edge load will remain under 0.7 and SLA is met with 99.95% confidence.
options.B: Delay onboarding; current URLLC slice can handle lidar alone with 98.5% reliability over 3 turns.
options.C: Switch to eMBB slice before onboarding; it offers 120Mbps throughput but latency may exceed 15ms, risking control loss.
options.D: Onboard thermal agent only if edge load drops below 0.4; otherwise, accept 15% per-turn failure risk.

records.question: At turn 9, the agent activates lidar gain adjustment and requests thermal support from a swarm agent under URLLC slice with 6ms latency, 1.0ms jitter, 0.1% loss, 35Mbps throughput, and 0.45 edge load. The thermal support agent responds with acknowledgment but operates under eMBB slice with 18ms latency, 4.0ms jitter, 3.0% loss, 80Mbps throughput, and 0.85 edge load. Historical data shows edge load increases by 0.05 per turn under eMBB and 0.03 under URLLC. If thermal data must arrive within 20ms latency and 5% loss to be actionable, and the mission requires two more communication turns before abort, which option minimizes maximum regret under worst-case jitter and loss projection? A: Maintain URLLC for both agents despite lower throughput. B: Switch thermal support to URLLC even if edge load exceeds 0.9. C: Accept eMBB for thermal support with current metrics. D: Delay thermal request until edge load drops below 0.7.

options.A: Maintain URLLC for both agents despite lower throughput.
options.B: Switch thermal support to URLLC even if edge load exceeds 0.9.
options.C: Accept eMBB for thermal support with current metrics.
options.D: Delay thermal request until edge load drops below 0.7.

records.question: The UAV is operating under icing conditions with wind at 8.0 m/s from 270 degrees, currently at 5.0m altitude with 100% battery and multiple sensor failures. At turn 8, the RGB camera failed to capture defect images under eMBB slice with 18ms latency, 4.0ms jitter, 3.0% loss, and 80Mbps throughput while edge load is 0.85. The mission requires defect classification within 25ms SLA. URLLC slice offers 6ms latency, 1.0ms jitter, 0.1% loss, 35Mbps throughput, and 0.45 edge load at turn 9. mMTC slice has 25ms latency, 10ms jitter, 2.5% loss, 5Mbps throughput, and 0.9 edge load. If sensor fusion continues, the next turn may see edge load rise to 0.55 under URLLC or 0.92 under eMBB. Which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next two turns while respecting SLA and avoiding overload?

options.A: Offload defect classification to edge via URLLC slice now, accepting 35Mbps throughput but ensuring latency under 10ms with 0.45 edge load, projected to rise to 0.55 next turn.
options.B: Retry RGB capture under eMBB slice, leveraging 80Mbps throughput despite 18ms latency and 3.0% loss, with edge load at 0.85 projected to hit 0.92 next turn.
options.C: Switch to mMTC slice for classification, accepting 25ms latency and 10ms jitter with 5Mbps throughput, edge load already at 0.9 and projected to exceed 0.95 next turn.
options.D: Run classification locally on UAV, consuming 15% battery per inference, risking 30ms latency due to thermal throttling, with no network dependency.

records.question: The UAV is operating under icing conditions with wind at 8.0 m/s from 270 degrees, and its thermal and radar sensors remain offline. At turn 9, the edge load is 0.45, latency is 6 ms, and throughput is 35 Mbps on URLLC. The mission requires federated model updates to compensate for sensor fusion drift, with a policy limit of edge_load ≤ 0.8 and latency ≤ 10 ms. If the next turn projects edge_load to increase by 0.15 under current slice, or by 0.05 if switching to eMBB, and latency may degrade by 2 ms under URLLC or 8 ms under eMBB due to weather-induced jitter, which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next two turns while preserving model convergence?

options.A: Stay on URLLC: current latency 6 ms is under SLA, edge_load 0.45 is safe, and model updates can proceed without reconfiguration.
options.B: Switch to eMBB: throughput increases to 80 Mbps, enabling faster model aggregation, despite higher jitter and projected latency of 14 ms.
options.C: Delay federated update for one turn: wait for edge_load to stabilize, accepting 100% model drift risk but avoiding SLA violation.
options.D: Initiate partial model sync on URLLC with 50% data volume: reduces edge_load impact to +0.07, latency remains under 8 ms, but model accuracy degrades by 15%.

records.question: At turn 9, the agent adapts its inspection strategy by adjusting lidar intensity and requesting thermal support from a third-party UAV swarm agent. The current network slice is URLLC with latency 6ms, jitter 1.0ms, loss 0.1%, throughput 35Mbps, and edge load 0.45. The thermal sensor remains offline locally, and the swarm agent’s last known reliability was 87% with a 15% variance in response latency. The mission SLA requires sub-10ms latency for critical control and allows up to 2% packet loss. If the swarm agent’s latency degrades by 50% next turn and edge load rises to 0.6, which exposure level should be granted to the third-party agent to minimize maximum regret over the next two turns while preserving mission integrity? A) Full API access with real-time telemetry streaming. B) Read-only sensor status with 500ms polling interval. C) Compute-only access to fusion pipeline with no data egress. D) No exposure; rely on local lidar with adjusted gain.

options.A: Full API access with real-time telemetry streaming.
options.B: Read-only sensor status with 500ms polling interval.
options.C: Compute-only access to fusion pipeline with no data egress.
options.D: No exposure; rely on local lidar with adjusted gain.

records.question: The UAV agent is returning to home at 25 m/s with 100% battery, but network slice URLLC is experiencing latency of 4 ms, jitter 0.6 ms, loss 0.04%, throughput 47 Mbps, and edge load 0.35. The mission SLA requires latency < 10 ms and edge load < 0.8 for critical control. A new inspection request arrives with 30% probability of thermal sensor recovery in 2 turns. If the agent continues return, it will land in 120 seconds with 92% battery. If it reorients for the new task, edge load will rise to 0.75, latency may spike to 8 ms under worst-case jitter, and battery will drop to 78% in 180 seconds. The policy allows one mission extension if SLA margins remain above 20%. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue return to home; battery and SLA margins are sufficient for safe landing.
options.B: Reorient for new inspection; thermal recovery probability justifies edge load increase to 0.75.
options.C: Migrate agent to backup edge node; latency will stabilize at 5 ms but throughput drops to 30 Mbps.
options.D: Retire agent and instantiate new one; ensures SLA compliance but incurs 90s setup delay.

records.question: The UAV is returning to base with 41% edge load and 47 Mbps throughput on URLLC, but a customer requests immediate LLM fine-tuning using 80 Mbps sustained throughput for 3 turns, which would raise edge load to 0.92 with 1.5% packet loss uncertainty. The mission SLA allows max 2% loss and 20 ms latency, but current latency is 4 ms with 0.6 ms jitter. If the UAV’s battery drops below 20% in 2 turns under current load, and thermal sensor recovery is uncertain, accepting the task risks violating SLA in turn 13 under worst-case jitter growth of 0.3 ms/turn. Declining preserves current QoS but forfeits $1200 revenue. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Accept the task: edge load 0.92 is under 1.0, and 1.5% loss is below SLA 2% with 0.5% safety margin.
options.B: Decline the task: battery will drop below 20% in 2 turns, and thermal sensor recovery uncertainty makes fusion unreliable for training.
options.C: Accept with throttling: reduce throughput to 60 Mbps to cap edge load at 0.75, accepting 10% revenue loss to avoid SLA violation.
options.D: Delay 1 turn: monitor battery and sensor recovery; if battery >25% and thermal online, accept; else decline.

records.question: The UAV is conducting an immersive inspection under icing conditions with wind at 8 m/s. At turn 8, the RGB camera failed to capture defect images due to eMBB slice degradation: latency 18 ms, jitter 4.0 ms, loss 3.0%, throughput 80 Mbps, edge load 0.85. The mission requires high-fidelity visual feedback within 20 ms latency and under 2% loss for AR overlay. URLLC slice offers 6 ms latency, 1.0 ms jitter, 0.1% loss, 35 Mbps throughput, edge load 0.45 at turn 9. mMTC slice has 25 ms latency, 10 ms jitter, 2.5% loss, 5 Mbps throughput, edge load 0.9. If edge load exceeds 0.9 in the next turn, the system will throttle all slices by 30%. The UAV battery is at 100% but descending at 25 m/s. Which option should be selected to ensure mission continuity while minimizing future regret over the next two turns?

options.A: Switch to URLLC slice immediately; accept reduced throughput (35 Mbps) but guarantee latency < 20 ms and loss < 0.1% for AR overlay.
options.B: Stay on eMBB slice; throughput 80 Mbps supports high-res images, and loss may improve if edge load drops below 0.8 in turn 9.
options.C: Switch to mMTC slice; it has 2.5% loss which is near the 2% SLA, and latency 25 ms may be acceptable if jitter stabilizes.
options.D: Request edge load reduction from network; delay image capture for one turn to allow edge load to fall from 0.85 to 0.75, then retry eMBB.

records.question: At turn 8, the UAV’s RGB camera fails to capture defect images while operating on eMBB slice with 18ms latency, 4.0ms jitter, 3.0% loss, and 80Mbps throughput under 0.85 edge load. The policy mandates SLA of <20ms latency and <2% loss for critical imaging. Historical data shows eMBB degrades further under wind gusts (8m/s) with 15% probability of 5ms latency spike and 1% loss increase per turn. URLLC slice offers 6ms latency, 1.0ms jitter, 0.1% loss, 35Mbps throughput, and 0.45 edge load but cannot support high-res RGB. mMTC slice has 25ms latency, 10ms jitter, 2.5% loss, 5Mbps throughput, and 0.9 edge load. If the mission must complete within 3 turns and battery depletes 5% per turn, which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret under worst-case degradation?

options.A: Stay on eMBB: current latency and loss are within SLA; throughput supports RGB; edge load is manageable at 0.85.
options.B: Switch to URLLC: latency and loss are well below SLA; jitter is low; but throughput may limit image resolution.
options.C: Switch to mMTC: edge load is near capacity; latency exceeds SLA; loss is borderline; throughput is insufficient for RGB.
options.D: Delay imaging for 1 turn: wait for wind to subside; risk battery drop to 95%; eMBB may degrade further under gusts.

records.question: At turn 9 the operator evaluates whether the original mission intent remains feasible after network degradation. The UAV is inside the geofence with altitude constrained by policy to 30.0–150.0 and still has battery_pct 100.0 and speed_mps 35.0. The current network slice is mMTC with latency observed at 120 ms in turn 8 and 110 ms in turn 9, jitter between 45 and 50 ms, loss between 4.5 and 5.0 pct, throughput between 1.5 and 2.0 Mbps, and edge_load between 0.88 and 0.9. Earlier safe operation used URLLC with latency 4–7 ms, jitter 1–2 ms, loss 0.05–0.3 pct, throughput 40–55 Mbps, and edge_load 0.25–0.5. Weather includes hail and lightning risk, making collision avoidance and command reliability relevant over the next two turns. Assume the degraded mMTC conditions could persist for up to two more turns before recovery. Switching slices or aborting imposes overhead and opportunity cost even if safety improves. Continuing without adjustment risks accumulating control delay under worst observed conditions. Considering worst-case latency and loss, projected edge load trends, and regret if degradation persists for two turns, which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue the mission on mMTC since battery_pct 100.0 and speed_mps 35.0 provide buffer and the observed 110 ms latency is acceptable in the current turn.
options.B: Immediately switch back to URLLC despite edge_load around 0.5 because worst-case latency would drop from 120 ms to below 7 ms over the next turns.
options.C: Hold position within the geofence and alt_bounds 30.0–150.0 for one turn to wait for recovery since throughput may rise from 1.5 Mbps without incurring slice switch cost.
options.D: Initiate return-to-base now using URLLC as in turn 10, accepting mission loss but bounding worst-case network delay and weather risk over the next two turns.

records.question: At turn 9 the UAV is mid mission with battery at 100 percent, speed 35 mps, altitude constrained between 30 and 150 meters, and lightning risk still present. Network telemetry over the last two turns shows mMTC latency increasing from 120 ms to 110 ms, jitter from 50 ms to 45 ms, loss between 5.0 and 4.5 percent, throughput near 1.5 to 2.0 Mbps, and edge load around 0.9 to 0.88. Earlier safety maneuvers relied on URLLC with latency 4 to 7 ms and edge load 0.25 to 0.5, but recovery is uncertain because hail persists. The mission intent is to continue sensing, while network policy favors minimizing congestion and avoiding unreliable control. If degradation persists one more turn, worst case control latency remains at the higher observed bound and loss does not improve. Returning now reduces exposure time but costs mission data, while continuing risks delayed avoidance commands. Switching slices may relieve congestion but can spike edge load temporarily. Over the next two turns, each option incurs regret either from safety risk or mission failure. Considering worst case network behavior and future regret rather than current averages, which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue mission on mMTC since current latency dropped to 110 ms and loss to 4.5 percent, accepting short term sensing gains despite high edge load 0.88.
options.B: Immediately switch back to URLLC to regain 5 to 7 ms latency even if edge load rises toward 0.5 and throughput falls near 40 Mbps.
options.C: Initiate return to base now using URLLC, accepting mission abort but limiting exposure to worst case 120 ms latency and 5.0 percent loss over the next two turns.
options.D: Loiter at minimum altitude 30 m for one turn on eMBB with latency around 25 to 35 ms, assuming network recovers before further action.

records.question: At turn 8 the user reports degraded connectivity while earlier turns emphasized sensing and weather avoidance within the 30 to 150 altitude bounds. Network telemetry shifted from URLLC at 5 to 7 latency to mMTC at 110 to 120 latency with jitter 45 to 50 and loss 4.5 to 5.0 while edge load rose from 0.3 to 0.9. Throughput simultaneously collapsed from 40 to 55 down to 1.5 to 2.0 even though the UAV still has 100 battery and speed 35. At turn 9 the agent adapts to degradation rather than executing new sensing actions. At turn 10 the user issues a return waypoint under URLLC again with latency 7 and edge load 0.5. The apparent goal may have shifted from anomaly sensing to early recovery or abort. If the mMTC condition persists one more turn the worst case latency remains 120 and loss 5.0 which could invalidate high rate sensing intent. If the recovery is transient the prior sensing intent could resume but edge load trends suggest congestion risk. Each detection option below has future regret either from false alarm or delayed response over the next two turns. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Declare intent drift immediately at turn 8 because worst case latency 120 and loss 5.0 exceed the needs of sensing even though URLLC briefly returns at turn 10.
options.B: Wait one turn and require two consecutive mMTC readings since current battery 100 and speed 35 allow patience despite edge load 0.9.
options.C: Do not flag drift and assume transient congestion because URLLC at turn 10 shows latency 7 and edge load 0.5 within earlier norms.
options.D: Flag provisional drift only if projected edge load stays above 0.75 next turn while maintaining altitude within 30 to 150.

records.question: At turn nine the UAV is flying in hail with lightning risk while lidar and radar remain offline and only RGB and thermal are available. The network slice is mMTC with latency 110 ms, jitter 45 ms, loss 4.5 percent, throughput 2.0 Mbps, and edge load 0.88. One turn earlier the same slice showed 120 ms latency, 50 ms jitter, 5.0 percent loss, throughput 1.5 Mbps, and edge load 0.9, indicating volatility rather than recovery. Policy altitude bounds remain 30 to 150 m and the UAV is already at the lower bound after a weather-driven descent. Battery is still 100 percent so endurance is not yet limiting. URLLC performance in earlier turns showed latency between 4 and 7 ms with edge load between 0.25 and 0.5, but slice switching has previously coincided with control actions. The next two turns may either stay on mMTC with similar degradation or briefly recover then degrade again. High autonomy requires timely state updates despite missing lidar and radar. A downgrade too late risks loss under worst-case latency plus jitter, while a downgrade too early incurs mission regret. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Maintain full autonomy on mMTC because 110 ms latency and 2.0 Mbps throughput are acceptable now and battery is 100 percent.
options.B: Immediately switch to URLLC and keep full autonomy since past URLLC latency of 4 to 7 ms and edge load up to 0.5 look safe.
options.C: Preemptively downgrade autonomy to supervised return mode while remaining on the current slice, accepting reduced throughput of 2.0 Mbps.
options.D: Delay downgrade for one more turn and only act if loss exceeds the prior 5.0 percent level or edge load exceeds 0.9.

records.question: At turn 9 the UAV is mid mission inside the geofence with battery at 100 percent and speed 35 mps while flying at the minimum allowed altitude of 30 m under hail and lightning risk. Network telemetry over the last two turns shows mMTC latency fluctuating between 110 and 120 ms with jitter between 45 and 50 ms and loss between 4.5 and 5.0 percent as edge load stays near 0.88 to 0.9. Earlier in the mission URLLC latency was as low as 4 to 7 ms but recent adaptation has not yet restored that slice. The next waypoint adjustment or return decision must be issued within the next one to three turns while weather and network conditions may persist. Continuing the mission yields coverage benefits but increases exposure to control lag if degradation persists another turn. Immediate return reduces exposure but incurs mission failure regret if the network recovers as it did previously. A brief hold to continue on the current path for one turn could allow observation of recovery while keeping altitude constant at 30 m. Worst case reasoning must assume latency remains at the upper observed bound and jitter does not improve. Considering maximum regret across the next three turns under worst case network behavior and current mission parameters, which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue full mission progression now assuming mean latency of about 110 ms and relying on prior URLLC recovery despite current loss near 4.5 percent.
options.B: Abort immediately and return to base now to avoid operating with up to 120 ms latency and 50 ms jitter even though battery is still 100 percent.
options.C: Hold course and continue conservatively for one more turn at 30 m altitude while monitoring whether latency stays near 120 ms before deciding next turn.
options.D: Climb toward 150 m to improve link margin and continue despite edge load around 0.9 and current throughput near 2.0 Mbps.

records.question: At turn 9 the AI scheduler must be reconfigured after the network slice shifted to mMTC with latency 110 ms, jitter 45 ms, loss 4.5 pct, throughput 2.0 Mbps, and edge load 0.88. In the prior turn 8 the same slice showed latency 120 ms, jitter 50 ms, loss 5.0 pct, throughput 1.5 Mbps, and edge load 0.9, indicating uncertainty that spans those values. The UAV is flying at speed 35.0 mps, battery 100.0 pct, and altitude constrained by bounds 30.0 to 150.0 while weather includes hail and lightning risk. Earlier URLLC turns showed latency 4 to 7 ms with edge load between 0.25 and 0.5, but that recovery only occurred after a user command at turn 10. The scheduler must decide now assuming the degraded mMTC conditions could persist for the next two turns before any recovery. One option prioritizes immediate telemetry freshness despite low throughput. Another option throttles tasks to protect edge load but risks delayed collision avoidance coordination. A third option defers noncritical sensing while maintaining consistent waypoint execution within altitude bounds. A fourth option aggressively switches back to URLLC despite recent congestion history. Considering worst case latency and jitter over the next two turns and minimizing maximum regret rather than current performance, which option should be selected?

options.A: Keep high rate telemetry on mMTC at 2.0 Mbps and 110 ms latency to optimize the current turn despite edge load 0.88.
options.B: Throttle all tasks to reduce edge load from 0.88 toward 0.5 even if waypoint updates at speed 35.0 mps are delayed under 120 ms latency.
options.C: Defer noncritical sensing and keep waypoint execution within 30.0 to 150.0 altitude bounds while tolerating 45 to 50 ms jitter for two turns.
options.D: Force immediate URLLC switching aiming for 5 to 7 ms latency even though prior congestion showed edge load up to 0.5 only after turn 10.

records.question: At turn 9 the UAV is adapting to degraded connectivity while already having executed altitude adjustment and collision avoidance earlier. The current network slice is mMTC with latency 110 ms, jitter 45 ms, loss 4.5 percent, throughput 2.0 Mbps, and edge load 0.88, following a prior report of 120 ms latency and 5.0 percent loss at turn 8. Earlier safety critical actions at turns 6 and 7 relied on URLLC with latency between 4 and 6 ms and loss between 0.05 and 0.2 percent. The user is likely to confirm return within the next one to two turns as later happened at turn 10. Battery is still 100 percent and speed is 35.0 mps, so endurance is not the binding constraint. Policy altitude bounds of 30.0 to 150.0 meters remain unchanged, so replanning should not contradict the recent avoidance and return intent. Assume worst case that the mMTC degradation persists one more turn at the higher loss and latency observed. A consistent decision should minimize maximum regret if another avoidance or control command is needed before landing. Choosing a slice now also affects projected edge load next turn if traffic increases. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Stay on mMTC because throughput of 2.0 Mbps is sufficient and accept 110 to 120 ms latency since return is imminent, keeping edge load near 0.88.
options.B: Switch immediately back to URLLC with 5 to 7 ms latency and 0.1 to 0.3 percent loss even though edge load was previously 0.3 to 0.5, accepting possible congestion next turn.
options.C: Switch to eMBB with 25 to 35 ms latency, 0.5 to 1.5 percent loss, and throughput 90 to 120 Mbps to balance sensing and control during return.
options.D: Delay any switch for one turn to observe whether mMTC recovers from 4.5 to 5.0 percent loss, then decide at the return confirmation.

records.question: At turn 9 the UAV agent must federate telemetry and imagery with a swarm agent and a ground analytics agent under degraded networking. The current slice is mMTC with latency 110 ms, jitter 45 ms, loss 4.5 percent, throughput 2.0 Mbps, and edge_load 0.88. In the immediately prior turn the same slice showed latency 120 ms, jitter 50 ms, loss 5.0 percent, throughput 1.5 Mbps, and edge_load 0.9, indicating uncertainty across the next turn. The UAV speed is 35.0 mps at altitude 30.0 within the 30.0 to 150.0 policy bounds, and battery is 100.0 percent so flight constraints are not yet binding. Interoperability options differ in schema verbosity and synchronization cadence and therefore change effective throughput consumption and retransmission sensitivity. A lightweight schema reduces required throughput but increases sensitivity to loss, while a verbose schema tolerates loss but needs higher throughput and edge capacity. A hybrid gateway buffers for one extra turn to smooth jitter but increases edge_load further before recovery. The operator expects the degraded condition could persist for up to two more turns before a possible return to URLLC as seen at turn 10. The decision must minimize worst case regret across the next two turns rather than optimize the current turn. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Federate immediately using the verbose loss tolerant schema that assumes throughput 2.0 Mbps is sufficient despite edge_load 0.88 and jitter 45 ms.
options.B: Federate immediately using the lightweight schema optimized for low throughput at 1.5 to 2.0 Mbps while accepting loss around 4.5 to 5.0 percent.
options.C: Delay federation for one turn using a hybrid gateway buffer that raises edge_load toward 0.9 while waiting for a possible return to URLLC latency near 7 ms.
options.D: Downsample and federate only critical telemetry at the current turn while deferring imagery until loss drops below the 4.5 to 5.0 percent range.

records.question: At turn 9 the agent must choose how to route horizontal messages to a nearby swarm agent while the network shows mMTC latency oscillating between 110 ms and 120 ms with jitter between 45 ms and 50 ms. Recent turns show loss between 4.5 percent and 5.0 percent, throughput between 1.5 Mbps and 2.0 Mbps, and edge load between 0.88 and 0.9. Earlier URLLC turns delivered 4 to 7 ms latency, 1 to 2 ms jitter, loss below 0.3 percent, throughput between 40 and 55 Mbps, and edge load between 0.25 and 0.5. Agent to agent collision avoidance messages must remain timely over the next two to three turns if lightning avoidance persists. Assume the next turn may remain degraded like turn 9 before possibly recovering to URLLC as in turn 10. Routing choices include staying on mMTC, forcing URLLC with reduced capacity, using eMBB relay paths seen at 25 to 35 ms latency with 8 to 12 ms jitter, or deferring noncritical traffic. The decision must consider worst case latency and loss if degradation persists one more turn. Each option increases future regret either by risking stale avoidance data, congesting the edge load above recent values, or starving throughput needed for coordination. A myopic single turn view would favor the lowest current latency, but multi turn safety may differ. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Keep all agent to agent traffic on mMTC accepting 110 to 120 ms latency, 45 to 50 ms jitter, 4.5 to 5.0 percent loss, and edge load near 0.9 to preserve capacity.
options.B: Force URLLC for all agent to agent traffic using 4 to 7 ms latency and 40 to 55 Mbps throughput despite edge load rising from 0.25 to 0.5 if degradation persists.
options.C: Route agent to agent traffic through eMBB relays with 25 to 35 ms latency, 8 to 12 ms jitter, 0.5 to 1.5 percent loss, and edge load around 0.6 to 0.75.
options.D: Defer noncritical agent to agent messages and send only collision avoidance on URLLC while the rest wait through the degraded turn.

records.question: At turn 9 the digital twin must stay coherent while the UAV is still inside the geofence and between the policy altitude bounds of 30.0 and 150.0. Over turns 8 and 9 the network degraded to the mMTC slice with latency observed between 110 and 120 ms and jitter between 45 and 50 ms, loss between 4.5 and 5.0 percent, throughput between 1.5 and 2.0 Mbps, and edge_load between 0.88 and 0.9. Earlier in the episode, URLLC showed latency between 4 and 7 ms, jitter between 1 and 2 ms, loss between 0.05 and 0.3 percent, throughput between 40 and 55 Mbps, and edge_load between 0.25 and 0.5. eMBB previously provided throughput between 90 and 120 Mbps but with latency between 25 and 35 ms and jitter between 8 and 12 ms. The UAV is moving at 35.0 mps with battery_pct at 100.0, and lightning risk means command delays can cause altitude violations across the next two turns if the degradation persists. The digital twin requires both timely command channels and enough sensing to detect anomalies like those seen at turn 5. Assume the worst case that mMTC conditions persist for two more turns and URLLC edge_load could rise back toward 0.5 if reused. A single turn recovery to URLLC is possible but not guaranteed. Each choice below trades command safety against telemetry fidelity and future regret. Considering worst case latency, loss, and edge load over the next two turns, which option should be selected?

options.A: Keep all telemetry and commands on mMTC at 110 to 120 ms latency and 1.5 to 2.0 Mbps to avoid increasing edge_load beyond 0.9.
options.B: Move all traffic back to URLLC with 4 to 7 ms latency and 40 to 55 Mbps throughput even if edge_load returns toward 0.5.

The UAV is at 25 m altitude within policy bounds of 10 to 120 m and flying at 25 mps, so perception errors can propagate quickly. Thermal, RGB, and lidar sensors are available, while radar is offline. Fusing all three streams centrally increases throughput demand and edge load, while reducing streams lowers perception richness. If degradation persists into the next turn, worst case latency must consider jitter accumulation rather than mean latency alone. If recovery occurs, over-constraining sensing may cause regret by missing thermal anomalies already observed at turn 5. The decision must balance near-term safety and multi-turn robustness under uncertainty. Which sensing and fusion option should be selected?

options.A: Maintain full RGB plus thermal plus lidar fusion on the current eMBB slice, accepting 110 ms latency and 25 ms jitter because throughput is still 200 Mbps.
options.B: Switch to URLLC and fuse lidar and RGB only, dropping thermal to cut load, relying on 6 to 10 ms latency seen earlier.
options.C: Use edge-side fusion of thermal and lidar only, suppressing RGB, to reduce throughput while tolerating mMTC-like latency of 50 to 60 ms.
options.D: Keep thermal only with local processing, minimizing throughput under edge load 0.9 but accepting loss up to 5.0 percent.

records.question: At turn 9 the UAV is resuming navigation after network degradation while coordinating with a backup UAV for public safety monitoring. Recent telemetry shows latency rising from 60 ms to 110 ms across turns 8 and 9, jitter from 15 ms to 25 ms, loss fluctuating between 4.0 and 5.0 percent, and edge load peaking between 0.85 and 0.9. Throughput simultaneously dropped from 200 Mbps earlier to 0.8 Mbps on the mMTC slice. The mission is expected to continue for at least two more turns under similar weather and load conditions. If degradation persists one more turn, coordination messages to the backup UAV may queue behind sensing traffic. If recovery occurs, URLLC performance similar to turn 10 could return but is not guaranteed. Escalating coordination too early risks saturating edge resources again. Deferring coordination risks delayed anomaly sharing during the next navigation phase. Considering worst case network behavior over the next two turns, which option should be selected?

options.A: Immediately switch all coordination and control back to URLLC now, accepting 0.15 to 0.25 edge load seen earlier for lowest current latency.
options.B: Maintain mMTC with reduced sensor frequency as at 0.8 Mbps throughput and 0.85 edge load, relying on average 60 ms latency improving next turn.
options.C: Split coordination so critical messages use URLLC while bulk sensing stays on mMTC, limiting edge load growth near the observed 0.9 peak.
options.D: Defer any coordination changes until after delivery, assuming the 110 ms latency spike was transient despite 5.0 percent loss.

records.question: The UAV is returning with 100% battery and operating under URLLC slice with 8ms latency, 1.1ms jitter, 0.05% loss, 60Mbps throughput, and 0.3 edge load. A customer requests immediate LLM fine-tuning using 45Mbps sustained throughput for 3 turns, which would increase edge load to 0.75 and latency to 18ms. The policy allows edge load up to 0.9 and latency up to 30ms. If wind persists at 8m/s from 225°, the UAV’s optimized return path will consume 12% battery per turn. Accepting the task now risks exceeding 0.85 edge load by turn 13 under worst-case jitter growth of +2ms/turn. Declining preserves battery and QoS but forfeits $1200 revenue. What should be selected?

options.A: Accept immediately: edge load 0.75 < 0.9, latency 18ms < 30ms, and revenue justifies risk.
options.B: Delay until turn 14: battery will be 64%, edge load drops to 0.35, but customer may cancel and lose $1200.
options.C: Accept with throttling: cap throughput at 30Mbps to keep edge load at 0.6, latency at 12ms, but training takes 5 turns and revenue drops to $800.
options.D: Reject outright: preserve 100% battery and URLLC QoS, accept $0 revenue, avoid any SLA violation risk.

records.question: The UAV is returning with critical AR-rendered terrain data under icing conditions, wind at 8 m/s from 225°, and battery at 100%. Current network slice is URLLC with 8ms latency, 1.1ms jitter, 0.05% loss, 60 Mbps throughput, and 0.3 edge load. Projected next turn: wind may increase to 10 m/s, edge load may rise to 0.45, and battery consumption rate may increase by 15% if altitude is maintained. If the UAV switches to eMBB, throughput rises to 120 Mbps but latency jumps to 30ms, jitter to 6ms, loss to 1.0%, and edge load to 0.7. If it switches to mMTC, latency balloons to 150ms, throughput drops to 0.8 Mbps, but edge load falls to 0.2. The mission requires AR rendering to complete within 2 turns with <15ms latency and >50 Mbps throughput to avoid data corruption. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Stay on URLLC: latency and throughput meet current SLA, edge load is low, and no immediate risk of violation.
options.B: Switch to eMBB: higher throughput supports AR rendering, acceptable latency for non-critical frames, and edge load remains under 0.8.
options.C: Switch to mMTC: minimizes edge load and conserves battery, suitable for low-priority telemetry if AR rendering is deferred.
options.D: Switch to eMBB only if edge load exceeds 0.4: balances throughput and latency while monitoring load to avoid overload.

records.question: At turn 5, the UAV experiences severe network degradation: latency spikes to 95ms, jitter to 25ms, loss to 8.5%, throughput drops to 45Mbps, and edge load reaches 0.88. The mission requires 120MB of sensor data to be uploaded within 3 turns to meet SLA, with a maximum allowable latency of 50ms and loss under 1%. A customer requests immediate initiation of a 6G model training task requiring 800MB upload over 4 turns with 99.9% reliability. The UAV battery is at 100% but will deplete 12% per turn if active. URLLC slice offers 110Mbps throughput with 9ms latency and 0.1% loss but caps total upload at 500MB per session. eMBB slice offers 870Mbps but is currently degraded and may recover in 1 turn with 60% probability. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Accept the training task on eMBB now, assuming recovery in 1 turn; projected upload completes in 2.5 turns with 95% confidence if recovery occurs.
options.B: Reject the training task and prioritize mission data upload on URLLC; mission data completes in 1.1 turns with 100% reliability, preserving SLA.
options.C: Accept the training task on URLLC; upload 500MB in 4.5 turns, then switch to eMBB for remaining 300MB; total time exceeds SLA by 1.5 turns.
options.D: Delay decision for 1 turn to observe network recovery; if eMBB recovers, accept task; else reject; worst-case delay risks mission SLA violation by 0.8 turns.

records.question: At turn 5, the UAV experiences severe network degradation: latency spikes to 95 ms, jitter to 25 ms, loss to 8.5%, throughput drops to 45 Mbps, and edge load reaches 0.88. The mission requires continuous AR overlay rendering at 60 fps, which demands at least 70 Mbps throughput and sub-20 ms latency. If the degradation persists for two more turns, eMBB will violate SLA thresholds, while URLLC may cause edge overload if three or more UAVs join. The mission must complete within 10 minutes. options.A: Stay on eMBB for one more turn to avoid edge load spike; throughput may recover to 80 Mbps with 15 ms latency based on prior trend.

options.C: Switch to URLLC but throttle transmission to 80 Mbps to reduce edge load to 0.35, accepting 12 ms latency and 0.08% loss.
options.D: Delay switching until turn 7; if latency drops below 50 ms by then, remain on eMBB; otherwise, switch to URLLC.

records.question: At turn 7 the agent monitors progress while the user intent remains continued navigation with possible altitude adjustments. Across turns 6 to 10 the URLLC slice shows latency values of 9, 8, 7 and 6 ms with jitter between 1.1 and 0.7 ms and loss between 0.2 and 0.05 pct. One option optimizes the current turn only while another fails only if the worst case repeats. No option avoids some downside over the next three turns. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Keep all control and coordination on URLLC since latency stayed between 6 and 9 ms and edge_load peaked only at 0.42.
options.B: Shift navigation commands to eMBB because throughput was 120 Mbps earlier even though latency reached 200 ms and edge_load hit 0.9.
options.C: Move noncritical coordination to mMTC while keeping control on URLLC, accepting 15 to 25 ms latency for mMTC and URLLC edge_load around 0.38.
options.D: Use mMTC exclusively since its loss stayed at or below 3.0 pct and it avoids URLLC congestion risk.

records.question: The mission began with navigation under GNSS outage using URLLC at 8 ms latency and 0.1 percent loss while the battery was 100 percent and altitude was within the 0.5 to 15.0 meter policy band. By turn 5, image capture occurred over eMBB with 200 ms latency, 8.0 percent loss, and edge load 0.9, which contrasted with earlier low latency control traffic. Swarm coordination at turn 6 reverted to URLLC with 9 ms latency and edge load 0.35, suggesting control intent still dominated. However, subsequent checks at turn 9 used mMTC with 25 ms latency, 3.0 percent loss, and edge load 0.8, which is inconsistent with tight navigation monitoring. Wind-driven altitude adjustment at turn 8 remained compliant but pushed closer to the lower bound of 0.5 meters, increasing sensitivity to delay. The final user command at turn 10 requested return to home with URLLC at 6 ms latency and edge load 0.3. Over the last three turns, edge load fluctuated from 0.38 to 0.8 to 0.3, indicating instability rather than steady recovery. If the higher mMTC load recurs for one more turn, monitoring traffic could again dominate control signaling. Under worst-case interpretation of the altitude bound and network variability, safety margins depend on whether intent has shifted from mission execution to termination. options.A: Declare no intent drift because URLLC latency returned to 6 ms at turn 10 and edge load dropped to 0.3, prioritizing current control performance.
options.B: Flag a transient anomaly only, citing that altitude remained within 0.5 to 15.0 meters and battery stayed at 100 percent despite the mMTC spike.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV is coordinating a swarm while returning telemetry, flying at 18.0 mps with battery at 100.0 pct under rain and gusty wind. Recent URLLC measurements show latency fluctuating between 6 and 9 ms and jitter between 0.7 and 1.3 ms across turns 7 to 10. Under worst case latency and edge load, control safety must be preserved with minimal future regret. All options incur risk either in latency spikes or throughput loss over the next three turns. Which slice should be selected?

options.A: Select URLLC, accepting 45 to 60 Mbps throughput with 6 to 9 ms latency while edge load may rise toward 0.5.
options.B: Select eMBB, exploiting 120 Mbps throughput at 12 ms latency assuming loss remains near 0.5 pct.
options.C: Select hybrid slicing, splitting control and data to hold latency near 12 ms with throughput around 55 Mbps under rising load.

records.question: During swarm area coverage, three UAVs contend for network slices while returning toward home over the next three turns. Telemetry shows URLLC latency between 6 and 9 ms with jitter between 0.7 and 1.3 ms and loss between 0.05 and 0.2 percent, while eMBB has shown latency of 12 ms earlier and a spike to 200 ms with jitter 50 ms and loss 8.0 percent under edge_load 0.9. The mMTC slice shows latency between 15 and 25 ms with jitter between 5.0 and 8.0 ms and loss between 1.2 and 3.0 percent as edge_load rises to 0.8. Policy requires altitude to remain within 0.5 to 15.0 m and collision avoidance messages must stay below 20 ms worst case to remain safe in rain and 3.0 mps wind. Battery is currently 100 percent but projected coordination lasts two more turns before landing. Fairness policy asks that no slice exceed an average edge_load of 0.5 across the next two turns. If one UAV takes URLLC exclusively, others must downgrade to eMBB or mMTC. Assuming worst case observed network conditions repeat for one additional turn, which slice assignment minimizes maximum regret across safety violation and fairness breach over the next three turns. Option A gives all UAVs URLLC now with edge_load 0.42 to 0.38. Option B keeps one UAV on URLLC and two on eMBB despite the 200 ms spike history. Option C assigns one URLLC, one eMBB, and one mMTC to balance load near 0.5. Option D moves all UAVs to mMTC to equalize access under higher jitter. Which option should be selected?

options.A: All UAVs remain on URLLC using observed latency 6 to 9 ms and edge_load around 0.38 to 0.42, risking fairness limits over two turns.
options.B: One UAV on URLLC and two on eMBB accepting possible 200 ms latency with loss 8.0 percent under edge_load 0.9.
options.C: One UAV on URLLC, one on eMBB, and one on mMTC keeping average edge_load near 0.5 while tolerating 15 to 25 ms latency on mMTC.
options.D: All UAVs on mMTC with latency up to 25 ms and jitter 8.0 ms to fully satisfy fairness.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV is navigating without GNSS while wind is present at 3.0 mps and altitude must remain within 0.5 to 15.0. Recent network observations include URLLC latency of 8 ms with jitter 1.3 and loss 0.15, mMTC latency of 25 ms with jitter 8.0 and loss 3.0, and an earlier eMBB spike at turn 5 with latency 200 ms, jitter 50, loss 8.0, throughput 10, and edge load 0.9. Over the next one to three turns the system must minimize the maximum regret between control instability and mission degradation. options.A: Maintain full autonomy on URLLC since latency is 8 ms and loss is 0.15, accepting the risk that edge load could rise again toward 0.8 or higher.

records.question: At turn 7 the scheduler observes stable URLLC telemetry with latency 8 ms, jitter 1.3 ms, loss 0.15 percent, throughput 48 Mbps, and edge load 0.42 while the UAV flies at 18.0 mps with battery at 100.0 percent. The previous turn 5 showed eMBB degradation with latency 200 ms, jitter 50 ms, loss 8.0 percent, throughput 10 Mbps, and edge load 0.9. URLLC has shown low latency at turns 1, 3, 6, 7, and 8 with edge load between 0.3 and 0.42, but mMTC showed higher latency 25 ms and loss 3.0 percent at turn 9. eMBB offers higher throughput 120 Mbps at turn 2 but has shown extreme congestion risk at turn 5.
