D) Delay offloading until turn 9, accepting 25 ms latency and 0.75 edge load for one more turn.

options.A: Stay on URLLC, accepting 100 Mbps throughput and projected edge load 0.45.
options.B: Revert to eMBB, risking 30 ms latency and 0.8 edge load next turn.
options.C: Switch to mMTC, accepting 10 Mbps throughput and 0.15 edge load, but risking 12 ms latency under wind.
options.D: Delay offloading until turn 9, accepting 25 ms latency and 0.75 edge load for one more turn.

records.question: At turn 6, the UAV is ascending under thermal updrafts with wind at 6.5 m/s, and network telemetry shows eMBB slice latency at 25 ms, jitter at 15 ms, packet loss at 1.2%, throughput at 400 Mbps, and edge load at 0.75. The SLA mandates latency under 20 ms and loss under 0.5% for critical control. Historical data shows latency increases by 30% per turn under updrafts, and edge load rises by 0.1 per turn. If the UAV continues ascending for two more turns, the worst-case latency could reach 42.25 ms and loss 2.076%, violating SLA. Switching to URLLC now yields latency 6 ms, loss 0.02%, but throughput drops to 100 Mbps, risking sensor data loss. Continuing eMBB risks SLA breach in turn 8. Switching to mMTC offers 8 ms latency and 0.05% loss but only 10 Mbps throughput, insufficient for thermal imaging. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue eMBB for two more turns, accepting SLA violation risk in turn 8 to preserve throughput for thermal imaging.
options.B: Switch to URLLC immediately to guarantee latency and loss SLA compliance, accepting reduced throughput for sensor data.
options.C: Switch to mMTC immediately for moderate latency and loss, accepting throughput limitation but avoiding SLA breach.
options.D: Wait one turn to reassess; if latency exceeds 30 ms, switch to URLLC, otherwise continue eMBB.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is operating under degraded eMBB conditions with latency 25ms, jitter 15ms, loss 1.2%, throughput 400Mbps, and edge_load 0.75. The operator must decide whether to expose compute capacity to third parties under URLLC, which currently has latency 6ms, jitter 2ms, loss 0.02%, throughput 100Mbps, and edge_load 0.3. The SLA requires latency <10ms and edge_load <0.8 for compute exposure. A third-party request arrives offering $120/hour for 50% of available compute, but the UAV must maintain 30% reserve for mission-critical tasks. If edge_load increases by 0.1 per turn under current conditions, and URLLC throughput may degrade by 10% per turn due to thermal interference, which option should be selected?

options.A: Expose compute under URLLC now, accepting $120/hour, since current edge_load 0.3 is below SLA and latency 6ms is acceptable.
options.B: Delay exposure until turn 9, when edge_load is projected to drop to 0.15 and latency stabilizes at 8ms under mMTC, despite lower throughput.
options.C: Expose under eMBB now, accepting $120/hour, since throughput 400Mbps exceeds mission needs and edge_load 0.75 is below SLA threshold 0.8.
options.D: Reject exposure entirely for next 3 turns, preserving compute for mission-critical tasks, as worst-case edge_load may reach 0.85 by turn 9 under current degradation trend.

records.question: At turn 6, the UAV is ascending under thermal updrafts with wind at 6.5 m/s from 145 degrees, battery at 100%, and all sensors operational. Network telemetry shows eMBB slice with 25 ms latency, 15 ms jitter, 1.2% loss, 400 Mbps throughput, and 0.75 edge load. Policy requires latency under 30 ms and loss under 2% for RAG augmentation. If degradation persists for two more turns, edge load may reach 0.9, increasing jitter to 25 ms and loss to 2.5%. URLLC offers 6 ms latency, 2 ms jitter, 0.02% loss, 100 Mbps throughput, and 0.3 edge load but cannot support high-throughput sensor streams. mMTC offers 8 ms latency, 3 ms jitter, 0.05% loss, 10 Mbps throughput, and 0.15 edge load but lacks real-time guarantees. Which option should be selected for RAG augmentation to minimize maximum regret over the next three turns?

options.A: Stay on eMBB: current latency 25 ms is under 30 ms SLA, and throughput supports sensor streaming; edge load 0.75 is manageable for one more turn.
options.B: Switch to URLLC: latency 6 ms and loss 0.02% are well under SLA; throughput 100 Mbps may limit thermal imaging but ensures reliability.
options.C: Switch to mMTC: latency 8 ms and loss 0.05% are under SLA; throughput 10 Mbps is insufficient for thermal imaging but minimizes edge load.
options.D: Wait one turn: if degradation reverses, eMBB may recover to 15 ms latency and 0.5% loss; if not, switch to URLLC at turn 7.

records.question: At turn 7, the agent switches to URLLC due to network degradation, observing latency of 6ms, jitter of 2ms, loss of 0.02%, throughput of 100Mbps, and edge load of 0.3. The mission policy requires latency under 10ms and loss under 0.1% for critical control, with a 20% safety margin for edge load. Thermal updrafts are increasing wind speed to 8.5m/s by turn 9, which may raise edge load by 0.15 per turn. If the agent must maintain identity registration for swarm coordination over the next 3 turns, and eMBB’s projected edge load at turn 9 is 0.9 (exceeding 0.8 threshold), while URLLC’s throughput may drop to 80Mbps under worst-case wind-induced interference, which option should be selected to ensure continuous identity validation and avoid SLA violation?

options.A: Remain on URLLC: latency and loss are within SLA, edge load is 0.3 (below 0.8), and even with 20% margin, worst-case throughput drop to 80Mbps still supports identity heartbeat at 50Mbps.
options.B: Switch back to eMBB: current latency 10ms is borderline, but throughput 800Mbps supports sensor fusion; edge load 0.4 is safe now, and projected 0.9 at turn 9 is acceptable if wind stabilizes.
options.C: Hybrid mode: use URLLC for control (latency 6ms) and eMBB for telemetry (throughput 800Mbps), accepting 0.05% loss on eMBB; edge load splits to 0.25 each, staying under 0.8.
options.D: Fallback to mMTC: latency 8ms is acceptable, loss 0.05% is within SLA, edge load 0.15 is safe, and throughput 10Mbps suffices for identity ping every 5 seconds.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is ascending under thermal updrafts with battery at 85%, edge load at 0.75, and eMBB slice showing 25ms latency, 15ms jitter, and 1.2% loss. Switching to URLLC reduces latency to 6ms and loss to 0.02% but caps throughput at 100Mbps and edge load to 0.3. The swarm requires federated model updates every 3 turns with 500MB payload, and the next update is due in 1 turn. If network degradation persists, eMBB throughput may drop to 300Mbps with 3% loss, while URLLC remains stable. The mission policy allows a maximum 10% model staleness and 200ms cumulative latency per update. Which option should be selected to minimize regret over the next 2 turns while ensuring model convergence and battery conservation?

options.A: Stay on eMBB: current throughput 400Mbps supports 500MB update in 10s, but risk 3% loss may cause retransmission delays and exceed 200ms latency if degradation continues.
options.B: Switch to URLLC: stable 6ms latency and 0.02% loss ensure timely delivery, but 100Mbps throughput requires 40s for 500MB, risking staleness if next update is delayed.
options.C: Delay update by 1 turn: wait for descent to reduce edge load, but battery drops to 70% and model staleness may hit 15% if no update occurs.
options.D: Split update: send 250MB on eMBB and 250MB on URLLC concurrently, but coordination overhead may increase latency to 30ms and edge load to 0.85, risking violation.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is ascending under thermal updrafts with wind at 6.5 m/s and battery at 100%, but network latency has spiked to 25 ms with 1.2% loss on eMBB, forcing a switch to URLLC with 6 ms latency and 100 Mbps throughput. The swarm agent requests full telemetry exposure for collision avoidance, while the thermal imaging payload is active and edge load is at 0.75. Under SLA, latency must stay under 10 ms for safety-critical control, and exposure must not exceed 70% of sensor data unless edge load drops below 0.4. If edge load remains above 0.6 for two more turns, the system will violate SLA. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Grant full telemetry exposure to swarm agent; edge load is 0.3 after switch, latency is 6 ms, and SLA is satisfied for now.
options.B: Grant partial exposure (only GNSS and IMU) with 50% data; latency is 6 ms, edge load 0.3, but thermal data is withheld despite active payload.
options.C: Deny all exposure; maintain URLLC slice, latency 6 ms, edge load 0.3, but risk swarm coordination failure if updrafts persist.
options.D: Switch back to eMBB for higher throughput; latency 25 ms, loss 1.2%, edge load 0.75, but enable full exposure to swarm agent.

records.question: At turn 6, network telemetry shows eMBB slice latency spiked to 25ms with 15ms jitter and 1.2% packet loss under thermal updrafts, while edge load reached 0.75. The UAV is ascending at 22m/s with 100% battery, and policy allows altitudes between 20m and 150m. A security anomaly detection system flags this as a potential jamming or spoofing event with 70% confidence, and the next 3 turns may see continued degradation or partial recovery. Switching to URLLC would reduce latency to 6ms but cap throughput at 100Mbps, while staying on eMBB risks violating SLA if latency exceeds 30ms or loss exceeds 2%. The swarm formation requires 80Mbps minimum for coordination, and thermal imaging consumes 200Mbps. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Stay on eMBB; current degradation is within SLA bounds and may recover by turn 8.
options.B: Switch to URLLC immediately; latency and jitter are guaranteed under 10ms, ensuring control integrity despite throughput loss.
options.C: Switch to mMTC; it has lowest edge load (0.15) and can handle telemetry at 10Mbps, preserving battery and reducing attack surface.
options.D: Request manual override; wait for turn 7 telemetry before deciding, accepting risk of SLA violation if degradation worsens.

records.question: At turn 6, the UAV is streaming live video over eMBB with latency 25ms, jitter 8ms, loss 1.5%, throughput 750Mbps, and edge load 0.75. The mission requires continuous object detection with latency under 10ms and loss under 0.1% for the next 3 turns. URLLC offers 9ms latency, 1.2ms jitter, 0.08% loss, 110Mbps throughput, and 0.35 edge load. mMTC offers 50ms latency, 15ms jitter, 2.0% loss, 1.2Mbps throughput, and 0.15 edge load. The radar remains offline, and sensor fusion is active. If edge load increases by 0.1 per turn under eMBB, and URLLC throughput may drop to 90Mbps under wind gusts, which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next 3 turns while maintaining mission-critical detection?

options.A: Stay on eMBB: current throughput supports video, and edge load may stabilize.
options.B: Switch to URLLC: meets latency and loss SLAs, but throughput may drop to 90Mbps under wind gusts.
options.C: Switch to mMTC: lowest edge load and guaranteed delivery, but latency exceeds 10ms.
options.D: Switch to eMBB with reduced resolution: cuts throughput demand by 30%, but latency and loss remain high.

records.question: The UAV is returning to base under rain with wind at 3.0 mps from 180 degrees, currently at 1.5m altitude with 100% battery, and must negotiate slice allocation for the next 3 turns. Current slice is URLLC with 7ms latency, 1.0ms jitter, 0.05% loss, 135Mbps throughput, and 0.3 edge load. Historical data shows eMBB degrades to 25ms latency and 1.5% loss under video streaming, while mMTC has 50ms latency and 2.0% loss. The swarm policy requires latency under 10ms for navigation and loss under 0.1% for sensor fusion. If edge load exceeds 0.8, the network may drop connections. Projecting worst-case degradation over 3 turns, which slice should be selected to minimize maximum regret while ensuring mission continuity?

options.A: Maintain URLLC: latency 7ms, jitter 1.0ms, loss 0.05%, throughput 135Mbps, edge load 0.3 — sufficient for navigation but may not support future video if needed.
options.B: Switch to eMBB: latency 12ms (mean), 25ms (worst), loss 0.1% (mean), 1.5% (worst), throughput 850Mbps, edge load 0.75 — high throughput but violates latency and loss SLAs under worst-case.
options.C: Switch to mMTC: latency 50ms, loss 2.0%, throughput 1.2Mbps, edge load 0.15 — low load but violates all SLAs for navigation and fusion.
options.D: Negotiate hybrid slice: latency 10ms (projected), loss 0.08% (projected), throughput 200Mbps, edge load 0.45 — meets SLAs but risks exceeding edge load if degradation persists.

records.question: At turn 6, the UAV is streaming live video at 750 Mbps with 25 ms latency and 1.5% packet loss under eMBB slice, while edge load is 75%. The mission requires real-time object detection with <10 ms latency SLA and <0.5% loss. Radar is offline, forcing reliance on lidar-thermal fusion which consumes 18% battery per minute. URLCC slice offers 9 ms latency, 0.08% loss, and 110 Mbps throughput but increases edge load to 35%. mMTC slice has 50 ms latency and 2% loss but only 1.2 Mbps throughput. If the video stream continues for 2 more turns, battery will drop to 64% and edge load may rise to 85%, risking SLA violation. What should be selected to maintain mission integrity while minimizing future regret?

options.A: Continue eMBB streaming: maintains throughput but risks SLA violation if edge load exceeds 80% in next turn.
options.B: Switch to URLCC: meets latency and loss SLA but throughput drops to 110 Mbps, risking video quality degradation.
options.C: Switch to mMTC: preserves battery and edge load but violates latency and throughput SLA by 5x and 600x respectively.
options.D: Terminate streaming and offload detection to edge: reduces battery drain to 5% per minute but increases latency to 12 ms with 0.3% loss.

records.question: The UAV agent is returning to base under URLLC slice with latency 7ms, jitter 1.0ms, loss 0.05%, throughput 135Mbps, and edge load 0.3. Battery is at 68% and decreasing at 3% per turn. The next turn may see edge load rise to 0.45 if no action is taken, and SLA requires latency under 10ms with loss under 0.1%. A new mission request arrives with 80% probability of requiring eMBB slice, which would increase latency to 25ms and edge load to 0.75. If the agent retires now, it avoids risk but forfeits future mission credit worth 120 units. If it scales down to half power, battery lasts 3 more turns but latency may rise to 9ms under load. If it migrates to a backup edge node, edge load drops to 0.2 but migration latency adds 15ms once. If it continues unchanged, edge load may hit 0.5 in two turns, violating SLA. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Retire agent immediately to avoid SLA violation risk and preserve battery for future use.
options.B: Scale down to half power to extend battery life by 3 turns while accepting 9ms latency under load.
options.C: Migrate to backup edge node to reduce edge load to 0.2, accepting 15ms one-time migration latency.
options.D: Continue unchanged and monitor, accepting 0.5 edge load in two turns with 10% SLA violation risk.

records.question: At turn 8 the operator requests a high priority data downlink while the UAV is inside a geofence defined by points from x 100.0 to 400.0 and y 100.0 to 300.0. The UAV pose remains near x 120.0 and y 120.0 at altitude z 10.0, which is within the policy altitude bounds of 5.0 to 120.0. The recent network history shows mMTC latency varying between 50 and 55 ms with jitter up to 12 ms, loss up to 2.0 percent, throughput down to 0.9 Mbps, and edge load peaking at 0.91. Earlier URLLC turns showed latency between 7 and 10 ms, jitter up to 2 ms, loss below 0.05 percent, throughput between 100 and 130 Mbps, and edge load up to 0.65. eMBB previously provided throughput around 800 to 870 Mbps but with latency rising to 15 ms and loss up to 0.2 percent when thermal data was active. The intent is to complete downlink and continue return to home over the next two turns without violating geofence or altitude policy and without queue growth at the edge. If mMTC degradation persists one more turn, worst case latency and loss remain at their observed maxima. If URLLC is selected, capacity limits may increase future congestion under sustained load. If eMBB is selected, latency and loss may increase again under thermal activation. Considering worst case network behavior over the next two turns and minimizing maximum regret rather than optimizing the current turn, which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue with mMTC despite 55 ms latency and 0.9 Mbps throughput because it is already queued and avoids switching overhead under edge load 0.91.
options.B: Switch to URLLC with 8 to 10 ms latency and up to 130 Mbps throughput, accepting higher future congestion risk at edge load 0.65.
options.C: Switch to eMBB with 800 Mbps throughput, tolerating 15 ms latency and 0.2 percent loss observed during thermal activity.
options.D: Delay transmission until after return to home to avoid current network uncertainty while staying within altitude bounds 5.0 to 120.0.

records.question: At turn 8 the operator requests a data downlink while the UAV is navigating after swarm coordination. The active network slice is mMTC with latency 55 ms, jitter 12 ms, loss 2.0 pct, throughput 0.9 Mbps, and edge load 0.91. One turn earlier mMTC showed latency 50 ms, jitter 10 ms, loss 1.5 pct, throughput 1.2 Mbps, and edge load 0.85. Earlier URLLC conditions included latency 9 ms, jitter 1.8 ms, loss 0.02 pct, throughput 115 Mbps, and edge load 0.58. The UAV battery is 100 pct and speed is 35.0 mps, so energy is not yet a binding constraint. Policy requires operation within altitude bounds of 5.0 to 120.0 m, which the current waypoint already satisfies. The mission intent prioritizes timely thermal data delivery, but network policy discourages actions that risk congestion collapse when edge load exceeds observed highs. Assume the next two turns may keep edge load at the worst previously observed level rather than recovering. Assume that if transmission is delayed one turn, conditions may revert to those seen at turn 9 under URLLC. Each option below causes some regret either in delay, congestion risk, or future maneuver constraints. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Transmit immediately on mMTC at 0.9 Mbps despite edge load 0.91 to satisfy immediacy of mission intent.
options.B: Switch to URLLC now and transmit at about 115 Mbps even though URLLC previously carried control traffic with edge load 0.58.
options.C: Delay transmission one turn while maintaining altitude within 5.0 to 120.0 m and wait for conditions similar to URLLC at latency 10 ms and edge load 0.65.
options.D: Abort downlink and continue navigation at 35.0 mps to avoid any network load increase until return to home.

records.question: The mission began as a survey with ascent and thermal activation, then progressed through waypoint navigation and data downlink over several turns. Network slices shifted from eMBB with 12 to 15 ms latency to URLLC with 7 to 10 ms latency, and briefly to mMTC with 50 to 55 ms latency and jitter rising from 10 to 12 ms. Edge load increased from 0.4 early to 0.85 and 0.91 during navigation and queued downlink, then dropped back to 0.5 to 0.65 after compression and approval. Loss also ranged from 0.01 to 2.0 percent across these turns, creating uncertainty about sustained reliability if congestion persists one more turn. Battery remained at 100 percent and speed stayed at 35 mps, so platform constraints did not force an early return. The final agent action set a return to home waypoint while the network recovered to 8 ms latency and 0.5 edge load. One interpretation is that the intent remained survey focused with a temporary retreat due to mMTC congestion. Another interpretation is that the intent drifted toward mission termination once data delivery succeeded under URLLC. A third view is that intent is ambiguous because short term network recovery could support continued survey if congestion was transient. Considering worst case persistence of the 50 to 55 ms latency regime for one more turn and the regret of misclassifying intent, which option should be selected?

options.A: Flag no intent drift because URLLC latency returned to 8 to 10 ms and edge load fell below 0.65, assuming the mMTC spike was transient.
options.B: Flag definite intent drift to return home because the last explicit action was return_to_home and loss had earlier reached 2.0 percent.
options.C: Flag probable intent drift toward termination because after data approval the agent switched goals despite battery at 100 percent, minimizing worst case regret if congestion at 55 ms and 0.91 edge load recurs next turn.
options.D: Defer judgment because current latency of 8 ms meets prior performance and ignore the earlier 10 to 12 ms jitter range.

records.question: At turn 8 the swarm experiences contention after waypoint navigation and a queued downlink, while weather includes snow and wind at 6.0 mps. The local UAV is moving at 35.0 mps at altitude 10.0 within bounds 5.0 to 120.0 and battery is 100.0 percent. Network telemetry shows mMTC latency rising from 50 to 55 ms, jitter from 10 to 12 ms, loss from 1.5 to 2.0 percent, throughput falling from 1.2 to 0.9 Mbps, and edge load rising from 0.85 to 0.91 across turns 7 and 8. Other swarm members rely on URLLC links that recently showed latency between 8 and 10 ms with edge load between 0.5 and 0.65 in turns 9 to 11. The operator must choose a slice action that balances fairness so other UAVs are not starved while maintaining safety if congestion persists one or two more turns. Assume the worst case that mMTC loss stays at 2.0 percent and edge load remains at 0.91 for the next two turns. One option prioritizes immediate downlink completion this turn, another shifts slices to protect collision avoidance traffic, another delays all noncritical traffic, and another alternates slices turn by turn. Each option reduces one risk but increases another over the next three turns. Considering worst case projections and minimizing maximum regret across the swarm, which option should be selected?

options.A: Keep mMTC for the queued downlink because throughput was 1.2 Mbps recently and accept edge load 0.91 this turn.
options.B: Force URLLC for all swarm traffic now since latency has been as low as 7 to 9 ms with edge load near 0.58.
options.C: Delay the downlink and reassign the local UAV to URLLC only for coordination while others share eMBB next turn given edge load previously 0.55.
options.D: Alternate mMTC this turn and URLLC next turn because average loss between 1.5 and 2.0 percent appears tolerable.

records.question: At turn 7 the network shifts to mMTC with latency 50 ms, jitter 10 ms, loss 1.5 percent, throughput 1.2 Mbps, and edge load 0.85. At turn 8 the same slice worsens to latency 55 ms, jitter 12 ms, loss 2.0 percent, throughput 0.9 Mbps, and edge load 0.91 while data downlink is queued. Earlier turns on URLLC showed latency between 7 and 10 ms, loss between 0.01 and 0.05 percent, throughput between 100 and 130 Mbps, and edge load between 0.38 and 0.65. The environment remains snowy with wind at 6.0 mps and the UAV speed stays at 35.0 mps, so mobility stress is unchanged across turns. Assume no immediate recovery trend because edge load increased from 0.85 to 0.91 over one turn. Consider the next two turns where edge load could remain at its worst observed level and loss could stay at its maximum observed value. A violation is defined operationally as sustained high latency and loss that prevents timely completion of queued transmissions. One option is to predict no violation based only on current success history. Another option is to predict a violation only if URLLC also degrades beyond its past range. Another option is to predict a violation if the mMTC degradation persists one more turn. The final option is to predict a violation immediately due to current conditions and worst case persistence. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Predict no SLA violation because prior URLLC latency stayed below 10 ms and throughput stayed above 100 Mbps.
options.B: Predict an SLA violation only if URLLC later exceeds 10 ms latency and 0.05 percent loss.
options.C: Predict an SLA violation if mMTC conditions like 55 ms latency, 2.0 percent loss, and 0.9 Mbps throughput persist for one more turn.
options.D: Predict an SLA violation immediately because mMTC already shows 55 ms latency, 12 ms jitter, 2.0 percent loss, and edge load 0.91.

records.question: At turn 8 the UAV is en route after waypoint navigation while using the mMTC slice with latency observed at 50 ms in the prior turn and 55 ms now, jitter rising from 10 ms to 12 ms, loss increasing from 1.5 pct to 2.0 pct, throughput dropping from 1.2 to 0.9 Mbps, and edge load climbing from 0.85 to 0.91. The vehicle is at altitude 10 m within policy bounds of 5 to 120 m, moving at 35 mps, with battery at 100 pct and lidar and radar offline in snowy weather. The return to home command is planned for the next turns, which will require stable control and collision avoidance under wind of 6.0 mps. One option is to continue full autonomy on mMTC to finish queued data downlink quickly this turn. Another option is to switch back to URLLC immediately, accepting lower throughput around 110 to 125 Mbps but lower latency near 8 to 10 ms and edge load around 0.5 to 0.65 as previously observed. A third option is to reduce speed while staying on mMTC, betting that lower dynamics offset the 50 to 55 ms latency and 2.0 pct loss. A fourth option is to loiter at current altitude to wait for network recovery, which delays return but avoids immediate control stress. Considering worst case network behavior persisting for the next one to three turns, the lack of lidar and radar, and minimizing maximum future regret rather than current performance, which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue full autonomy on mMTC with 0.9 Mbps throughput and edge load 0.91 to complete downlink this turn despite 55 ms latency and 2.0 pct loss.
options.B: Switch immediately to URLLC with observed 8 to 10 ms latency and edge load near 0.5 to 0.65, accepting reduced throughput for the next turns.
options.C: Reduce speed below 35 mps but remain on mMTC, assuming 50 to 55 ms latency and 1.5 to 2.0 pct loss remain manageable.
options.D: Enter a loiter at 10 m altitude within the 5 to 120 m policy bounds to wait for mMTC recovery before returning home.

records.question: During coordinated swarm operations, three network slices are observed across recent turns with changing loads and performance. At turn 6 URLLC shows latency 9 ms, jitter 1.5 ms, loss 0.03 pct, throughput 130 Mbps, and edge_load 0.41 during collision avoidance. At turns 7 and 8 mMTC shows latency increasing from 50 to 55 ms, jitter from 10 to 12 ms, loss from 1.5 to 2.0 pct, throughput falling from 1.2 to 0.9 Mbps, and edge_load rising from 0.85 to 0.91 during waypoint navigation and queued downlink. At turn 5 eMBB shows latency 15 ms, jitter 4 ms, loss 0.2 pct, throughput 800 Mbps, and edge_load 0.55 during thermal survey. The swarm must negotiate a slice for the next two turns assuming edge_load may remain at its worst observed value. Collision avoidance traffic similar to turn 6 is expected to persist for at least one more turn. Data downlink demand similar to turn 8 may or may not clear in the next turn. Choosing a slice now affects regret if congestion persists into the following turn. A myopic choice favors immediate throughput, while a conservative choice limits worst case degradation. Considering worst case latency and loss under sustained load and the need to coordinate multiple agents, which option should be selected?

options.A: Keep mMTC for all swarm traffic because its latency of 50 to 55 ms and throughput near 1.2 to 0.9 Mbps already match queued downlink behavior even with edge_load up to 0.91.
options.B: Switch the swarm to eMBB since throughput around 800 Mbps at edge_load 0.55 can absorb downlink bursts and its 15 ms latency is acceptable in the current turn.
options.C: Allocate URLLC to coordination traffic and leave bulk data on eMBB, accepting URLLC throughput near 125 to 130 Mbps with edge_load up to 0.65 to bound worst case latency.
options.D: Move all traffic to URLLC because its latency of 7 to 10 ms and loss below 0.05 pct look safest regardless of rising edge_load.

records.question: At turn 7 the AI scheduler shifted the UAV from URLLC to mMTC while navigation completed and data tasks queued. The mMTC slice shows latency of 50 ms with jitter of 10 ms, loss of 1.5 percent, throughput of 1.2 Mbps, and edge load of 0.85. One turn later the same slice shows latency of 55 ms, jitter of 12 ms, loss of 2.0 percent, throughput of 0.9 Mbps, and edge load of 0.91, indicating a range rather than a point value. The policy altitude bounds remain 5 to 120 m and the UAV is already compliant, but scheduler consistency must be maintained for the next two turns. URLLC previously showed latencies between 7 and 10 ms with jitter between 1 and 2 ms but throughput near 100 to 130 Mbps and edge load rising to 0.65. eMBB earlier provided throughput near 800 to 870 Mbps with latency between 11 and 15 ms and edge load up to 0.55. Assume worst case that the higher mMTC edge load of 0.91 persists for two more turns and that loss increases to the observed maximum. The scheduler must minimize future regret if another transmission or coordination action occurs before return to home. A myopic choice would only optimize the current turn, while a robust choice must survive the worst case over two turns. No option avoids all downsides because any slice change affects either latency, throughput, or load. Which scheduler reconfiguration option should be selected?

options.A: Keep mMTC for the next two turns because 50 to 55 ms latency is acceptable now and changing slices could increase edge load beyond 0.91.
options.B: Immediately switch back to URLLC despite throughput near 100 to 130 Mbps because its latency of 7 to 10 ms minimizes coordination risk even if edge load stays around 0.65.
options.C: Reconfigure to eMBB for the next two turns, accepting 11 to 15 ms latency to gain 800 to 870 Mbps throughput while keeping edge load below 0.55.
options.D: Alternate between mMTC and URLLC each turn to balance 50 to 55 ms latency against higher throughput while assuming loss does not exceed 1.5 percent.

records.question: At turn 8 the primary UAV must federate data with a swarm collision avoidance agent and a ground analytics agent while weather remains snowy and wind is 6.0 mps. The UAV is within an altitude policy range of 5.0 to 120.0 meters and currently operates near 10.0 meters after ascent. Recent networking shows URLLC latency between 7 and 10 ms with edge load around 0.38 to 0.65, eMBB latency around 11 to 15 ms with edge load up to 0.55, and mMTC latency rising to 50 to 55 ms with edge load from 0.85 to 0.91. The queued downlink at turn 8 uses mMTC throughput of 0.9 to 1.2 Mbps with loss up to 2.0 percent, while swarm coordination previously succeeded on URLLC at 9 ms latency. Over the next one to three turns the UAV must still return to home while maintaining collision avoidance and completing data sharing. If edge load follows the worst observed mMTC value again, interoperability failures could cascade across agents. A single turn view favors immediate throughput, but a multi turn view must consider regret if retransmissions block collision avoidance. Assume no sensor recovery and no improvement in network conditions beyond observed ranges. Which interoperability and federation option should be selected?

options.A: Federate all agents on URLLC now, accepting 120 to 130 Mbps throughput limits and edge load up to 0.65 to minimize current latency.
options.B: Keep data on mMTC for all agents because 0.9 to 1.2 Mbps is sufficient now despite 50 to 55 ms latency and edge load near 0.91.
options.C: Split federation by keeping swarm collision avoidance on URLLC at 9 to 10 ms while deferring bulk analytics to eMBB with 800 to 870 Mbps despite 0.55 edge load.
options.D: Use eMBB for all agents since 11 to 15 ms latency and 850 Mbps throughput appear balanced under average conditions.

records.question: At turn 9 the UAV must decide where to offload a thermal image inference task while returning home over the next two turns. The device battery is at 100 and onboard compute would avoid network use but slows navigation feedback. Recent network observations show URLLC latency between 8 and 10 with jitter between 1 and 2 and loss between 0.01 and 0.05 while throughput stays between 100 and 125 and edge_load ranges from 0.5 to 0.65. eMBB previously provided latency of 11 to 15 with jitter of 2 to 4 loss of 0.05 to 0.2 throughput of 800 to 870 and edge_load up to 0.55. mMTC showed latency of 50 to 55 jitter of 10 to 12 loss of 1.5 to 2.0 throughput below 1.2 and edge_load as high as 0.91 during turns 7 and 8. The task output is needed within the next two turns to assist safe return but missing one update is tolerable while persistent delay is not. Assume worst case metrics persist for the next two turns and that switching slices adds one extra turn of exposure to that slice conditions. Offloading reduces onboard energy draw but increases exposure to network delay. Each option below incurs some downside either in delay risk energy use or congestion contribution. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Offload immediately to URLLC now accepting throughput near 100 and edge_load up to 0.65 to minimize current latency.
options.B: Delay one turn and offload to eMBB where throughput 800 to 870 is higher but latency can reach 15 and loss 0.2.
options.C: Keep computation onboard for the next two turns to avoid loss rates up to 0.05 at the cost of local processing delay.
options.D: Attempt offload over mMTC after compression since throughput near 1.2 is sufficient and edge_load may drop from 0.91.

records.question: The UAV is currently operating under URLLC slice with 7ms latency, 1.5ms jitter, 0.04% loss, 110Mbps throughput, and 0.32 edge load. A customer requests immediate LLM fine-tuning requiring 150Mbps sustained throughput and <10ms latency for 3 turns, with SLA penalty if violated. Historical data shows URLLC throughput degrades by 5–15% per turn under sustained load, and edge load increases by 0.03–0.07 per turn. eMBB offers 800Mbps but latency spikes to 15ms with 0.3% loss and edge load 0.55, risking mission-critical telemetry. mMTC is saturated at 1.2Mbps and 0.75 edge load. If the UAV must also maintain 95% telemetry reliability for safety over the next 3 turns, which option should be selected?

options.A: Accept training on URLLC: current throughput 110Mbps exceeds 150Mbps requirement by 40Mbps margin, latency 7ms is under 10ms SLA, and edge load 0.32 allows 0.48 headroom before saturation.
options.B: Reject training: URLLC throughput will drop below 150Mbps in 2 turns under worst-case 15% degradation, and edge load may hit 0.53 by turn 13, risking telemetry loss.
options.C: Switch to eMBB: 800Mbps exceeds requirement, but 15ms latency violates SLA, and 0.55 edge load may spike to 0.7+ under load, risking telemetry failure during critical landing phase.
options.D: Accept on mMTC: 1.2Mbps is below requirement, but edge load 0.75 is already saturated; however, it avoids URLLC degradation and preserves telemetry on separate slice.

records.question: The UAV is executing a final approach under URLCC slice with 7ms latency, 1.5ms jitter, 0.04% loss, 110Mbps throughput, and 0.32 edge load. Weather remains rainy with 6m/s wind from 240°, and the geofence boundary is 200m east. Mission policy requires latency <10ms and throughput >100Mbps for AR rendering. If wind gusts increase uncertainty to ±2m/s and edge load rises 0.05 per turn, and the next turn may require 150Mbps for stereo depth rendering, which option minimizes maximum regret over the next two turns while maintaining safety? A: Stay on URLLC with current settings. B: Switch to eMBB despite 15ms latency risk. C: Throttle AR rendering to 80Mbps to reduce edge load. D: Request edge node scaling with 200ms setup delay.

options.A: Stay on URLLC with current settings.
options.B: Switch to eMBB despite 15ms latency risk.
options.C: Throttle AR rendering to 80Mbps to reduce edge load.
options.D: Request edge node scaling with 200ms setup delay.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is preparing for delivery approach with eMBB slice active, latency 25ms, jitter 5ms, loss 1.2%, throughput 700Mbps, and edge load 0.65. The SLA requires inference latency under 15ms with 99.9% reliability over the next 3 turns. Edge inference would consume 12ms processing time with 0.5ms jitter, while onboard inference takes 18ms with 2ms jitter. The edge load is projected to rise to 0.75 by turn 8 under current trends, and network loss may increase to 2.5% if weather worsens. If the UAV proceeds with edge inference now, it risks SLA violation by turn 8 under worst-case jitter and loss. If it switches to onboard, it accepts higher current latency but avoids edge congestion. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Use edge inference now; current latency is 25ms but edge processing adds only 12ms, total 37ms, which is acceptable under SLA if jitter remains under 5ms.
options.B: Switch to onboard inference; current total latency would be 18ms + 25ms = 43ms, but avoids future edge load spike to 0.75 and potential loss increase to 2.5%.
options.C: Wait one turn to re-evaluate; edge load may drop to 0.55 if mMTC slice is released, reducing latency to 20ms and making edge inference viable with 32ms total.
options.D: Use edge inference with fallback to onboard if latency exceeds 30ms; this balances current performance with future risk, assuming edge load stabilizes at 0.65.

records.question: At turn 8, edge load is 0.85, latency is 60 ms, jitter is 15 ms, and packet loss is 2.0%, all under mMTC slice. The SLA requires latency ≤ 50 ms and loss ≤ 1.5% for critical operations. The UAV is at 25m altitude with 100% battery, and weather risk persists. If edge load increases by 0.1 per turn under current conditions, and latency degrades by 5 ms per 0.1 edge load increase, then by turn 10, latency will exceed 70 ms. Option A maintains mMTC with no action, risking SLA violation by turn 9. Option B switches to URLLC now, which has 12 ms latency and 0.1% loss but only 95 Mbps throughput, risking sensor data loss during return. Option C reduces autonomy to manual override, consuming 0.05 edge load per turn but requiring 20 ms latency tolerance. Option D delays return by one turn to wait for edge load to drop, risking battery depletion if wind speed increases. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Maintain mMTC slice with no action, accepting SLA violation risk by turn 9.
options.B: Switch to URLLC slice immediately, accepting reduced throughput risk during return.
options.C: Reduce autonomy to manual override, accepting 20 ms latency tolerance and 0.05 edge load per turn.
options.D: Delay return by one turn, accepting battery risk if wind speed increases beyond 6.5 mps.

records.question: The UAV is returning from delivery under deteriorating network conditions with edge_load at 0.85 and loss_pct at 2.0 under mMTC slice, while policy mandates SLA compliance for safety-critical telemetry with max_lat_ms=15 and max_loss_pct=0.5. The next turn may see edge_load rise to 0.92 under worst-case weather-induced congestion, and the UAV’s battery is at 68% with 12km to base at 15m/s. Offloading telemetry to edge would reduce local compute load but risks violating SLA if latency exceeds 15ms or loss exceeds 0.5%. The alternative is to retain telemetry locally, consuming 12% battery per km but guaranteeing SLA compliance. A third option is to switch to URLLC slice with current lat_ms=12 and loss_pct=0.1, but edge_load may spike to 0.75 next turn, risking congestion-induced latency degradation. The fourth option is to request emergency bandwidth from the swarm, which has 30% spare capacity but requires 500ms coordination latency and may fail if swarm is already overloaded. Given the uncertainty in edge_load growth and the criticality of telemetry integrity over the next two turns, which option should be selected?

options.A: Offload telemetry to edge under current mMTC slice, accepting 2.0% loss and 60ms latency as acceptable for non-critical data.
options.B: Retain telemetry locally, consuming 12% battery per km, ensuring SLA compliance despite higher energy cost.
options.C: Switch to URLLC slice immediately, accepting potential edge_load spike to 0.75 next turn and possible latency degradation to 20ms.
options.D: Request emergency bandwidth from swarm, accepting 500ms coordination delay and 30% chance of failure due to swarm overload.

records.question: At turn 8, the UAV is returning from delivery under mMTC slice with latency 60ms, jitter 15ms, loss 2.0%, throughput 0.8Mbps, and edge load 0.85. The SLA requires latency <50ms, loss <1.5%, and throughput >1Mbps for critical control. Weather risk persists with wind 6.5m/s. If the UAV continues on current path, latency may rise to 70±5ms next turn due to edge congestion, and loss may reach 3.0±0.5% if lightning strikes. The URLLC slice offers latency 12ms, loss 0.1%, throughput 95Mbps, but is capacity-constrained with only 3 slots left. The eMBB slice offers throughput 700Mbps but latency 25ms and loss 1.2% — both within SLA now but projected to degrade to 35ms and 2.5% loss next turn. Which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next two turns under worst-case weather and congestion?

options.A: Stay on mMTC: current metrics are acceptable under SLA if we ignore jitter, and edge load may drop to 0.75 next turn.
options.B: Switch to URLLC: latency and loss are guaranteed within SLA, but if two more UAVs join, capacity may be exceeded, forcing fallback to mMTC with 75ms latency.
options.C: Switch to eMBB: throughput is sufficient and latency is currently acceptable; projected 35ms latency next turn is still under 50ms SLA bound.
options.D: Request emergency reroute to lower altitude: reduces wind impact but increases edge load to 0.95 and may trigger SLA violation on latency if congestion persists.

records.question: The UAV is returning from a medical delivery under deteriorating network conditions with edge load at 0.85 and mMTC slice latency at 60ms, exceeding the SLA of 50ms. The next turn may see edge load rise to 0.92 under worst-case weather-induced congestion, and the UAV’s battery is at 65% with 12km remaining. Exposing compute to third parties now could generate $120 in revenue but risks increasing edge load by 0.08 and latency by 15ms, potentially violating SLA in turn 9. Alternatively, deferring exposure until turn 10 may yield only $80 due to reduced demand, but edge load is projected to drop to 0.45. A third option is to expose compute at 50% capacity, generating $90 while adding only 0.04 to edge load and 7ms latency. The fourth option is to reserve all compute for mission-critical functions, forgoing revenue but ensuring SLA compliance. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Expose full compute now for $120, accepting 0.08 edge load increase and 15ms latency penalty, assuming weather stabilizes by turn 9.
options.B: Defer exposure to turn 10 for $80, accepting lower revenue but benefiting from projected edge load of 0.45 and SLA-safe latency.
options.C: Expose compute at 50% capacity for $90, accepting 0.04 edge load increase and 7ms latency, balancing revenue and SLA risk.
options.D: Reserve all compute for mission-critical functions, forgoing revenue to guarantee SLA compliance under worst-case edge load of 0.92.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is preparing for delivery approach under eMBB slice with 25ms latency, 5ms jitter, 1.2% loss, 700Mbps throughput, and 0.65 edge load. Policy requires SLA latency <30ms and loss <2%. Weather risk persists with wind at 6.5m/s. The next turn may degrade to mMTC with 60ms latency and 2% loss. RAG augmentation must select one telemetry subset for prompt context: A) full telemetry including battery and sensor status, B) only latency and loss metrics, C) only edge load and throughput, D) only jitter and wind speed. Which option should be selected to ensure RAG can recover from worst-case degradation in turn 8 while maintaining SLA compliance and minimizing regret over the next two turns?

options.A: Full telemetry including battery and sensor status
options.B: Only latency and loss metrics
options.C: Only edge load and throughput
options.D: Only jitter and wind speed

records.question: The UAV agent has completed delivery and is initiating return with swarm dismissal under URLLC slice, latency 9ms, jitter 1ms, loss 0.06%, throughput 115Mbps, edge_load 0.3. Historical data shows eMBB slice degraded to 25ms latency and 1.2% loss at turn 7, and mMTC slice peaked at 60ms latency and 2.0% loss at turn 8. Wind remains at 6.5m/s from 210°, and battery is at 78% after delivery. If the agent must onboard a new identity for a secondary payload mission within 3 turns, and policy mandates identity registration only if edge_load < 0.4 and latency < 15ms for 2 consecutive turns, which option should be selected to ensure compliance while minimizing future regret under worst-case network drift?

options.A: Proceed with identity registration now under current URLLC parameters, assuming edge_load will remain below 0.4 and latency under 15ms for next 2 turns.
options.B: Delay registration until turn 13, monitoring edge_load and latency; if either exceeds threshold, switch to eMBB and retry, accepting 25ms latency and 1.2% loss as acceptable for registration.
options.C: Immediately switch to eMBB slice to register identity, leveraging higher throughput (800Mbps) despite 20ms latency and 0.1% loss, assuming wind will not degrade performance further.
options.D: Register identity under mMTC slice to conserve edge resources, accepting 60ms latency and 2.0% loss, with plan to re-register under URLLC if network recovers within 2 turns.

records.question: The UAV has completed delivery and is returning with 87% battery, operating under URLLC slice with 11ms latency, 2ms jitter, 0.09% loss, 105Mbps throughput, and 0.45 edge load. The next federated learning round requires 150Mbps throughput for 30 seconds to upload model updates, but the edge load must not exceed 0.7 for safety. Historical data shows edge load increases by 0.1 per turn under URLLC and 0.2 under eMBB. If the UAV switches to eMBB now, throughput jumps to 750Mbps but latency rises to 25ms and edge load climbs to 0.65. If it waits one turn under URLLC, edge load becomes 0.55 and throughput remains 105Mbps. If it waits two turns, edge load hits 0.65 and throughput drops to 90Mbps due to congestion. Which option should be selected to ensure federated learning completes without violating edge load limits while minimizing regret over the next two turns?

options.A: Switch to eMBB immediately: throughput 750Mbps > 150Mbps required, edge load 0.65 < 0.7 limit, latency 25ms acceptable for non-critical update.
options.B: Wait one turn under URLLC: edge load 0.55 < 0.7, throughput 105Mbps < 150Mbps, so learning fails unless throughput recovers — but recovery is uncertain.
options.C: Wait two turns under URLLC: edge load 0.65 < 0.7, throughput 90Mbps < 150Mbps, guaranteed failure with no recovery path.
options.D: Initiate federated learning now under URLLC: throughput 105Mbps < 150Mbps, edge load 0.45 < 0.7, but update will time out and waste battery.

records.question: The UAV has just completed a medical delivery under degraded eMBB conditions with 1.2% packet loss and 700 Mbps throughput, while the swarm agent remains active with 0.38 edge load and 9 ms latency. Weather risk persists with 6.5 m/s winds and lightning potential, and the UAV’s thermal and radar sensors remain offline. The next turn requires exposing telemetry to a third-party logistics agent for route optimization, but policy restricts exposure if edge load exceeds 0.7 or latency exceeds 15 ms under uncertainty. URLLC slice offers 12 ms latency with 0.1% loss but only 95 Mbps throughput, while mMTC offers 60 ms latency with 2.0% loss and 0.8 Mbps throughput. If the swarm agent’s edge load increases by 0.1 per turn under sustained weather stress, and the logistics agent requires at least 50 Mbps to function, which option should be selected?

options.A: Expose telemetry via URLLC slice with 12 ms latency and 95 Mbps throughput, accepting 0.1% loss, since edge load is 0.38 and within policy limit of 0.7.
options.B: Expose telemetry via mMTC slice with 60 ms latency and 0.8 Mbps throughput, accepting 2.0% loss, since it is the only slice available if URLLC fails.
options.C: Delay exposure until next turn when edge load may drop to 0.28 under improved weather, risking mission delay but preserving policy compliance.
options.D: Expose telemetry via eMBB slice with 25 ms latency and 700 Mbps throughput, accepting 1.2% loss, since throughput exceeds 50 Mbps and edge load is 0.65 below 0.7.

records.question: At turn 8, network telemetry shows mMTC slice with 60ms latency, 15ms jitter, 2.0% loss, 0.8Mbps throughput, and 0.85 edge load under lightning risk. Historical data from turn 5 shows URLLC slice degraded to 10ms latency, 2ms jitter, 0.08% loss, 100Mbps throughput, 0.4 edge load after weather adaptation. If lightning risk persists, edge load may increase by 0.1 per turn, and loss may rise by 0.5% per turn under worst-case. The mission requires at least 95% packet delivery success over next 2 turns for safe return. Option A switches to URLLC now despite 115Mbps throughput cap. Option B stays on mMTC with 0.8Mbps throughput but risks 3.0% loss next turn. Option C switches to eMBB with 700Mbps throughput but 25ms latency and 1.2% loss, which may exceed SLA if jitter spikes. Option D waits one turn to reassess, risking 0.95 edge load and 2.5% loss. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Switch to URLLC immediately: latency 12ms, jitter 3ms, loss 0.1%, throughput 95Mbps, edge load 0.5 — meets SLA under worst-case if loss stays below 0.5%.
options.B: Remain on mMTC: latency 60ms, jitter 15ms, loss 2.0%, throughput 0.8Mbps, edge load 0.85 — throughput may suffice for telemetry but loss exceeds 95% success threshold next turn.
options.C: Switch to eMBB: latency 25ms, jitter 5ms, loss 1.2%, throughput 700Mbps, edge load 0.65 — high throughput but loss may exceed 2.0% next turn under worst-case, violating SLA.
options.D: Delay decision one turn: mMTC degrades to latency 65ms, jitter 18ms, loss 2.5%, throughput 0.7Mbps, edge load 0.95 — violates SLA with 97.5% delivery success, risking mission failure.

records.question: The mission began as surveillance with eMBB at 12 ms latency and 850 Mbps throughput while the UAV flew at 35 mps at 1500 m altitude. By turn 3 to 5 the slice shifted to URLLC with latencies between 7 and 9 ms and throughput near 105 to 120 Mbps while the agent still reported data collection. At turn 6 the network degraded to eMBB with 45 ms latency, 12 ms jitter, 2.3 percent loss, and edge load 0.78. In response at turn 7 the agent switched back to URLLC with 10 ms latency and 0.43 edge load and stated safety adaptation. Two turns later at turn 9 the agent initiated return and data offload planning despite battery still at 100 percent and altitude within the 1000 to 3000 policy band. At turn 10 the user confirmed safe return over mMTC with 150 ms latency and 25 ms jitter, indicating tolerance of low throughput. Across turns 6 to 10 the observed latency spans from 7 to 150 ms, forming an uncertainty range that makes worst case communication critical. The original user intent focused on surveillance and imaging, including thermal and high resolution RGB capture completed at turn 8. A detector must decide whether the agent intent drifted from surveillance to early termination due to network risk rather than mission completion. Considering regret over the next one to three turns if degradation persists or recurs, which option should be selected?

options.A: Flag no intent drift because URLLC latency returned to 10 ms at turn 7 and imaging finished at turn 8, so the return at turn 9 aligns with completion despite the 45 ms spike being transient.
options.B: Flag intent drift immediately at turn 6 because the 45 ms latency and 0.78 edge load alone exceed prior values, regardless of later recovery to 10 ms and edge load 0.43.
options.C: Flag subtle intent drift at turn 9 because return and offload were initiated while surveillance tasks had just stabilized under URLLC at 9 to 10 ms and worst case latency uncertainty up to 150 ms makes early termination a risk minimizing shift.
options.D: Delay flagging intent drift until after turn 10 since mMTC at 150 ms latency was user requested for integrity checks and edge load 0.85 reflects backend load not mission intent.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV has switched back to URLLC after an eMBB degradation at turn 6 during icing and high wind. Recent observations show latency varying between 8 ms and 45 ms, jitter between 0.7 ms and 12 ms, loss between 0.01 percent and 2.3 percent, and edge load between 0.36 and 0.78 across the last three turns. Throughput has ranged from 105 to 130 Mbps on URLLC and from 300 to 900 Mbps on eMBB, while battery remains at 100 percent and speed is 35 mps. The next two turns are expected to include continued return flight and queued data handoff to the relay. If degradation similar to turn 6 recurs for one more turn, worst case latency and edge load must be tolerated without losing control or stalling data transfer. URLLC offers low latency but limited throughput and risks congestion if edge load spikes again. eMBB offers high throughput but showed a sharp latency and jitter spike under load. A hybrid slice would split control and data but inherits partial risk from both paths. The operator must minimize maximum regret over the next two turns rather than optimize the current snapshot. Which slice should be selected now?

options.A: Remain on URLLC, accepting throughput around 120 Mbps and edge load near 0.43 to guarantee sub 10 ms latency even if conditions persist.
options.B: Switch to eMBB to exploit 300 to 900 Mbps throughput, assuming the turn 6 spike to 45 ms latency and 12 ms jitter was transient.
options.C: Adopt a hybrid slice, keeping URLLC for control at roughly 8 to 10 ms latency while offloading data toward eMBB capacity under edge load up to 0.78.
options.D: Delay switching and stay adaptive turn by turn, tolerating mMTC like behavior with latency up to 150 ms if congestion worsens.

records.question: At turn 6 the operator reports a network fluctuation while the UAV is mid-mission under icing weather and 8.0 mps wind. Across turns 3 to 5 on URLLC the latency varies between 7 ms and 9 ms with jitter between 0.7 ms and 1.1 ms and edge_load between 0.36 and 0.41. At turn 6 on eMBB the latency jumps to 45 ms with jitter 12 ms, loss 2.3 percent, throughput 300 Mbps, and edge_load 0.78. Battery is still 100.0 percent and speed is 35.0 mps, so energy margin is high for the next two turns. The mission over the next one to three turns consists of RGB capture, perimeter coordination, and return planning that already succeeded on URLLC at throughput between 105 and 130 Mbps. The observed URLLC throughput is lower than eMBB but has remained within 105 to 130 Mbps across four consecutive turns. Edge load on URLLC has fluctuated but stayed below 0.43, while eMBB showed a spike to 0.78 that could persist one more turn. If the fluctuation persists, switching again may incur additional control overhead during return. If recovery does not occur, a poor choice could increase control latency during the next waypoint set. Given these observations and worst-case continuation of the current trends for the next two turns, which option should be selected?

options.A: Switch immediately back to eMBB because 300 Mbps throughput at turn 6 exceeds the 105 to 130 Mbps seen on URLLC, accepting 45 ms latency and 12 ms jitter for the next turn.
options.B: Stay on URLLC despite lower throughput because worst-case latency remains under 10 ms with edge_load at or below 0.43 across recent turns, minimizing control risk if degradation persists.
options.C: Switch to mMTC preemptively since it verified data integrity at turn 10 with loss 0.5 percent and could reduce edge_load pressure from 0.78 seen on eMBB.
options.D: Delay the decision for one turn and then switch if eMBB latency drops below the earlier 11 to 12 ms range seen at turns 1 and 2.

records.question: At turn 6 the UAV is cruising at 35.0 mps at an altitude of 1500.0 with battery_pct at 100.0 during icing and 8.0 mps crosswind conditions. The network has just degraded on eMBB to 45 ms latency with 12 ms jitter, 2.3 percent loss, 300 Mbps throughput, and edge_load of 0.78. Earlier turns showed URLLC latencies of 7 to 10 ms with jitter near 1 ms and edge_load between 0.36 and 0.43, so recovery is possible but not guaranteed next turn. Mission completion requires safe return within the geofence and altitude bounds of 1000.0 to 3000.0 over the next two turns. High resolution RGB and thermal capture increase reliance on timely control updates even though lidar is already offline. If degradation persists for one more turn, autonomy margins tighten because speed remains 35.0 mps and icing increases control sensitivity. Four downgrade actions are considered, each incurring some cost in the next one to three turns. The objective is to safely degrade before failure while minimizing worst case regret if the bad network state repeats. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Remain on eMBB and continue full autonomy since 300 Mbps throughput is still available and battery_pct is 100.0, accepting the current 45 ms latency as transient.
options.B: Immediately force URLLC and reduce speed below 35.0 mps, accepting lower throughput near 120 Mbps and potential edge_load rebound toward 0.43.
options.C: Switch to mMTC for robustness against loss, tolerating 150 ms latency and 25 ms jitter for the next two turns while keeping speed at 35.0 mps.
options.D: Maintain URLLC but preemptively drop high resolution RGB capture to lower edge_load from around 0.4 and accept reduced sensing quality.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV has switched back to URLLC after a degradation where latency spiked to 45 ms and jitter to 12 ms on eMBB. Current URLLC telemetry shows latency 10 ms, jitter 1.3 ms, loss 0.04 percent, throughput 130 Mbps, and edge load 0.43. Earlier in the mission URLLC latency ranged between 7 ms and 10 ms, while eMBB ranged between 11 ms and 45 ms. The UAV is at altitude 1500 within the allowed 1000 to 3000 band, flying at 35 mps with battery at 100 percent. Weather includes icing and 8.0 mps wind from 270 degrees, and lidar remains offline. Over the next two turns the operator must decide whether to continue surveillance or take a conservative action assuming network volatility may persist. If degradation returns, the worst case is a repeat of 45 ms latency and 0.78 edge load as previously observed. A decision must minimize maximum regret over the next two turns rather than optimize the current snapshot. Stopping early risks losing high resolution RGB data already requested, while continuing risks compounding network instability during icing. The question is which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue for two more turns on URLLC since current latency is 10 ms and edge load 0.43, accepting risk if it returns to 45 ms.
options.B: Immediately abort and return because eMBB previously showed 45 ms latency and 0.78 edge load under similar conditions.
options.C: Continue for one turn only on URLLC while preparing return, since latency has stayed between 7 and 10 ms on URLLC even when eMBB degraded.
options.D: Switch back to eMBB to gain 300 Mbps throughput despite the prior 45 ms latency and 12 ms jitter spike.

records.question: At turn 6 the swarm observes a sudden network degradation with eMBB latency of 45 ms, jitter of 12 ms, loss of 2.3 percent, throughput of 300 Mbps, and edge load of 0.78. In earlier turns the same swarm operated URLLC with latencies between 7 and 10 ms, jitter below 1.3 ms, throughput near 110 to 130 Mbps, and edge load around 0.36 to 0.43. A background mMTC slice is also available, but at turn 10 it showed 150 ms latency, 25 ms jitter, 0.5 percent loss, throughput of 1.2 Mbps, and edge load of 0.85. The mission remains within altitude bounds of 1000 to 3000 meters and must coordinate perimeter scan agents and a data offload agent over the next two turns. Edge load has shown volatility, rising from 0.45 to 0.78 and later peaking at 0.85, so worst case saturation must be considered. If degradation persists for two more turns, the swarm must avoid a slice that appears acceptable now but causes coordination failure later. Allocating URLLC to all agents risks capacity stress, while reverting all agents to eMBB risks latency spikes under load. A mixed allocation can reduce regret but may constrain throughput for imaging agents. The decision must minimize the maximum regret across the next one to three turns rather than optimize the current snapshot. Which slice allocation should the swarm select?

options.A: Assign URLLC to all swarm agents because current latency of 10 ms and edge load of 0.43 are well below the degraded eMBB values of 45 ms and 0.78.
options.B: Assign eMBB to all swarm agents because throughput of 300 to 900 Mbps exceeds URLLC throughput of about 110 to 130 Mbps despite higher latency.
options.C: Assign URLLC only to perimeter coordination agents and keep imaging and offload agents on eMBB, accepting 45 ms latency but lower projected edge load than full URLLC.
options.D: Shift most agents to mMTC since loss is only 0.5 percent and latency of 150 ms is acceptable for noncritical traffic.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV has just switched back to URLLC with latency 10 ms, jitter 1.3 ms, loss 0.04 percent, throughput 130 Mbps, and edge load 0.43 while flying at 1500 m altitude and 35 mps speed in 8 mps wind. Two turns earlier the same area experienced an eMBB degradation with latency 45 ms, jitter 12 ms, loss 2.3 percent, throughput 300 Mbps, and edge load 0.78. The mission requires coordinated perimeter scanning with a swarm agent and reliable data handoff over the next two turns during potential network relapse. The policy altitude bounds remain 1000 m to 3000 m and the UAV battery is still near its initial 100 percent state. Observed network metrics therefore span a latency range from 8 ms to 45 ms and an edge load range from 0.36 to 0.78 within the last three turns. If congestion returns to the worst observed case, control stability and coordination timeliness become the dominant risk rather than raw throughput. However, URLLC has shown lower throughput near 120 Mbps, which can delay bulk data offload if sustained for multiple turns. A myopic choice would optimize the current turn only, while a conservative choice must minimize maximum regret if degradation persists one or two more turns. The swarm perimeter scan requires consistent command latency across both upcoming turns to avoid desynchronization under wind. Given these constraints and uncertainties, which option should be selected?

options.A: Remain on URLLC for both next turns, accept 115 to 130 Mbps throughput, and prioritize keeping latency near 9 to 10 ms even if edge load rises again toward 0.78.
options.B: Switch back to eMBB immediately to exploit 300 Mbps throughput, assuming latency stays near the recent 11 to 12 ms values rather than returning to 45 ms.
options.C: Use URLLC for the next turn only and then revert to eMBB for data offload, betting that congestion will not persist beyond one turn.
options.D: Move to mMTC for coordination and data integrity, tolerating 150 ms latency and 0.5 percent loss while relying on lower control demand.

records.question: A mission began with an initiate_mission intent on a URLLC slice at 5 ms latency and 0.01 percent loss while flying at 25.0 mps with battery at 100.0 percent. By turn 3 the agent requested swarm formation on eMBB with latency 12 ms and edge_load 0.6, which still aligned with mission expansion. At turn 4 the user adjusted altitude due to icing within the 50.0 to 200.0 bound, preserving safety intent. By turn 6 the user reported network degradation on eMBB with latency 45 ms, jitter 12 ms, loss 2.3 percent, throughput 60 mbps, and edge_load 0.88. At turn 7 the agent switched back to URLLC and reduced sensor sampling, restoring latency to 7 ms and edge_load to 0.55. At turn 8 the user initiated a return sequence even though battery remained at 100.0 percent and the UAV was still within the geofence. Observed latency over the episode ranged from 5 ms to 45 ms, creating uncertainty about whether degradation would persist another turn. If degradation persisted for one to two more turns, projected edge_load could rebound toward 0.88 under eMBB but remain near 0.55 under URLLC. The intent could either be mission continuation with adaptation or a subtle drift toward early termination. Which option best detects an intent drift while minimizing worst case regret over the next two turns?

options.A: Treat the return initiation as intent drift because battery is 100.0 percent and prior URLLC latency recovered to 7 ms, flagging early termination risk if edge_load stays below 0.6.
options.B: Assume no intent drift because worst case latency of 45 ms already justified return, ignoring that URLLC restored loss to 0.03 percent.
options.C: Delay intent classification for one turn, accepting current URLLC latency 6 to 7 ms but risking regret if edge_load rebounds from 0.55 to 0.88.
options.D: Confirm intent drift only if two more turns show latency above 12 ms, relying on eMBB throughput of 60 to 120 mbps.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV is flying at 70.0 m altitude within the 50.0 to 200.0 m policy band and at 25.0 mps with battery at 100.0 percent while icing conditions persist. The network was degraded on eMBB at turn 6 with latency 45 ms jitter 12 ms loss 2.3 percent throughput 60 Mbps and edge load 0.88. After adaptation the slice is URLLC with latency 7 ms jitter 1.5 ms loss 0.03 percent throughput 40 Mbps and edge load 0.55. Historical turns show URLLC latency fluctuating between 4 and 8 ms and edge load between 0.3 and 0.6. The mission objective can continue if command latency stays below prior degraded levels and collision avoidance remains active for the next two turns. A return path has been planned at turn 8 but not yet executed. If degradation persists one more turn eMBB edge load is expected to rise again while URLLC may lose throughput margin. Lidar was offline earlier and only reactivates reliably when link loss stays below prior worst levels. Continuing risks future regret if the slice fails while aborting now incurs mission loss. Considering worst case network behavior over the next two turns which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue the mission on URLLC accepting 40 Mbps throughput and edge load 0.55 because latency stays under 8 ms even if jitter rises.
options.B: Switch back to eMBB to regain 60 Mbps throughput despite prior 45 ms latency and 0.88 edge load since current loss was only 2.3 percent.
options.C: Initiate immediate return because URLLC throughput is 40 Mbps and edge load could rise to 0.6 within one turn.
options.D: Hold position for one turn to observe recovery since current latency is 7 ms and battery is 100 percent.

records.question: At turn 7 the swarm has just switched the focal UAV back to URLLC with latency 7 ms, jitter 1.5 ms, loss 0.03 pct, throughput 40 Mbps, and edge load 0.55. Other swarm members are still exchanging formation and collision data after observing eMBB degradation at turn 6 with latency 45 ms, jitter 12 ms, loss 2.3 pct, throughput 60 Mbps, and edge load 0.88. Across earlier turns, URLLC latency has ranged from 4 to 8 ms while eMBB latency has ranged from 12 to 45 ms, indicating uncertainty if degradation persists. The swarm expects at least two more coordination turns before landing, during which collision checks similar to turn 9 are required. If edge load increases by reverting any agent to eMBB, the observed pattern suggests edge load can move from 0.55 toward 0.6 or higher within one turn. Allocating URLLC to all agents reduces throughput relative to the 120 Mbps seen at turn 3 but stabilizes latency and loss. Keeping eMBB for all agents maximizes throughput but risks repeating the worst case seen at turn 6. A mixed allocation could isolate high risk traffic but may push shared edge load toward prior peaks. Considering worst case latency, edge load trends, and regret over the next two turns, which slice allocation should the swarm select?

options.A: Assign URLLC to all swarm agents, accepting throughput around 40 to 55 Mbps and edge load near 0.55 to 0.6.
options.B: Assign eMBB to all swarm agents to regain throughput near 100 to 120 Mbps while edge load is currently below 0.6.
options.C: Keep the focal UAV on URLLC and move the rest of the swarm to eMBB, assuming edge load stays near 0.6.
options.D: Alternate slices per turn so agents use eMBB next turn and URLLC after, targeting average latency near 12 ms.

records.question: At turn 7 the system considers onboarding a returning UAV agent identity for continued coordination during degraded network conditions. Across turns 5 to 7 the network slice alternated between eMBB and URLLC with latency values of 15 ms, 45 ms, and 7 ms and loss values observed between 0.5 pct and 2.3 pct before stabilizing at 0.03 pct. Edge load rose as high as 0.88 on eMBB and later reduced to 0.55 on URLLC while throughput dropped from 100 Mbps to 40 Mbps. The agent must be registered under an identity policy that remains valid if degradation persists for one to three more turns. Policy constraints require operation within altitude bounds of 50.0 to 200.0 while maintaining control responsiveness during landing preparation. Identity Option A binds the agent to a persistent URLLC-scoped identity assuming latency remains near 7 ms. Identity Option B assigns a dual-slice identity that can authenticate on both eMBB and URLLC but incurs revalidation overhead when edge load exceeds prior peaks. Identity Option C delays full onboarding and uses a provisional identity optimized for high throughput near 100 Mbps. Identity Option D reuses the earlier eMBB swarm identity that performed adequately before loss reached 2.3 pct. Considering worst-case recurrence of 45 ms latency and 0.88 edge load within the next three turns, which option should be selected?

options.A: Select a persistent URLLC-only identity anchored to 7 ms latency and 0.55 edge load, accepting reduced throughput of 40 Mbps.
options.B: Select a dual-slice identity spanning URLLC and eMBB that tolerates latency between 7 ms and 45 ms but adds revalidation when edge load exceeds 0.6.
options.C: Select a provisional high-throughput identity favoring eMBB at 100 Mbps and accepting loss up to 2.3 pct.
options.D: Reuse the prior eMBB swarm identity that previously handled 15 ms latency before degradation.

records.question: The UAV is returning to base under URLLC slice with 6ms latency, 1.5ms jitter, 0.03% loss, 40Mbps throughput, and 0.42 edge load. A customer requests immediate LLM fine-tuning requiring 100Mbps sustained throughput and <5ms latency for 3 turns, with SLA penalty if violated. Current battery is 85%, and wind may increase edge load by 0.1 per turn. If network degrades to mMTC again, latency could spike to 55ms with 2% loss. Option A accepts the task now under URLLC with 40Mbps, risking SLA breach. Option B delays until next turn, projecting edge load at 0.52 and throughput at 35Mbps. Option C switches to eMBB now, offering 120Mbps but 15ms latency, violating SLA immediately. Option D rejects the task entirely to preserve battery and avoid SLA penalty. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Accept now under URLLC: 40Mbps throughput, 6ms latency, 0.42 edge load, 85% battery.
options.B: Delay one turn: projected 35Mbps, 7ms latency, 0.52 edge load, 80% battery.
options.C: Switch to eMBB now: 120Mbps, 15ms latency, 0.55 edge load, 85% battery.
options.D: Reject task: preserve 85% battery, avoid SLA penalty, maintain current QoS.

records.question: The UAV is returning to base under deteriorating network conditions with edge load at 0.42 and URLLC slice latency at 6ms, jitter 1.5ms, loss 0.03%, throughput 40Mbps. Historical data shows eMBB slice degraded from 120Mbps to 100Mbps over two turns with jitter rising from 2.1ms to 3.0ms and loss from 0.05% to 0.1%. mMTC slice is currently at 0.9Mbps with 52ms latency and 1.6% loss, edge load 0.82. Wind remains at 8m/s from 240°, and battery is at 100%. If the UAV must transmit a 500MB AR overlay update within the next 3 turns, and SLA requires latency under 10ms with loss under 0.1%, which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret under worst-case projection? C) Switch to eMBB immediately despite 15ms latency and 0.1% loss, leveraging 100Mbps throughput. D) Use mMTC slice for low priority, accepting 52ms latency and 1.6% loss with 0.9Mbps throughput.

options.A: Use URLLC slice now, accepting 40Mbps throughput and 6ms latency.
options.B: Wait 1 turn for potential eMBB recovery, risking 3.0ms jitter and 0.1% loss.
options.C: Switch to eMBB immediately despite 15ms latency and 0.1% loss, leveraging 100Mbps throughput.
options.D: Use mMTC slice for low priority, accepting 52ms latency and 1.6% loss with 0.9Mbps throughput.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV agent must choose how to federate data with a swarm agent and a weather agent for the next coordination window. Recent turns show URLLC latency of 10 to 12 ms with jitter from 1 to 2 ms and loss from 0.05 to 0.1 while edge_load ranges from 0.35 to 0.55. Earlier eMBB turns showed latency of 18 to 25 ms with jitter of 3 to 6 ms, loss of 0.1 to 0.3, throughput of 90 to 120 Mbps, and edge_load rising to 0.65. A brief mMTC degradation at turn 5 reached 120 ms latency, 25 ms jitter, 2.5 loss, 1.2 Mbps throughput, and 0.85 edge_load, showing a plausible worst case. If the next two turns mirror the worst observed edge_load while weather remains snowy with 8.5 mps wind, coordination delays can amplify path divergence. A single turn optimization would favor highest throughput, but multi turn regret depends on avoiding another mMTC like collapse. The agent must pick a federation mode that remains acceptable if edge_load spikes again and latency variance persists for two more turns. Each option degrades either imagery fidelity or coordination reliability within that horizon. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Federate all agents over eMBB to maximize 90 to 120 Mbps imagery throughput despite 18 to 25 ms latency and edge_load up to 0.65.
options.B: Federate all agents over URLLC with reduced imagery at 45 to 70 Mbps accepting tighter capacity and edge_load up to 0.55.
options.C: Split federation by keeping swarm coordination on URLLC at 10 to 12 ms latency while routing imagery to eMBB at 90 Mbps.
options.D: Defer cross agent federation for one turn and retry after confirming edge_load returns to 0.35.

records.question: At turn 7 the agent must choose a routing and QoS policy for continued agent to agent coordination during the next three turns of return planning. Recent turns show URLLC latency fluctuating between 9 and 12 ms with jitter between 1 and 2 ms and edge load between 0.35 and 0.55. Assume the worst case that current URLLC metrics regress to their highest recently observed values and that recovery does not improve in the next two turns. Also assume that any slice change incurs at least one full turn before stabilization. Each available option has a downside within the next three turns due to load, latency, or instability risk. options.A: Keep URLLC for all agent to agent traffic, accepting possible regression to 12 ms latency, 2 ms jitter, throughput 60 Mbps, and edge load 0.55.
options.B: Switch to eMBB to gain 90 to 110 Mbps throughput while tolerating 20 to 25 ms latency, 4 to 6 ms jitter, and edge load near 0.65.
options.C: Fall back to mMTC for robustness, accepting 1.2 Mbps throughput with potential latency spikes up to 120 ms and edge load 0.85.
options.D: Alternate between URLLC and eMBB each turn to balance load, accepting one turn of transition instability with metrics similar to the degraded slice.

records.question: At turn 6 the UAV is executing low bandwidth mode while returning to base with battery_pct at 100.0 and speed_mps at 22.0. The onboard model can process frames locally with zero network latency but consumes energy continuously over the next 3 turns. The edge currently reports edge_load at 0.55 but has recently fluctuated between 0.3 and 0.85 across turns. The task requires sustained inference for the next 2 turns with tolerance only if worst case latency stays below the highest previously observed safe URLLC value of 12 ms. If degradation persists one more turn the slice could revert to mMTC characteristics. Energy regret is proportional to time spent computing locally while mission regret is proportional to delayed inference during return. All options incur risk either from energy draw, congestion or latency spikes. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Offload to edge over URLLC accepting 12 ms latency and 0.55 edge_load despite possible rise toward 0.85 in the next turn.
options.B: Offload to cloud over eMBB using 25 ms latency and 90 Mbps throughput assuming conditions recover as in turn 4.
options.C: Process fully onboard at altitude 150.0 and speed 22.0 to avoid network loss while drawing energy over 2 turns.
options.D: Delay inference for one turn and reassess if URLLC latency remains near 10 ms and edge_load near 0.4.

records.question: At turn 7 the digital twin must stay synchronized while the UAV resumes survey with adaptations after prior degradation. Recent telemetry shows URLLC latency of 10 ms with jitter of 1.5 ms and loss of 0.08 percent at edge load 0.4, while earlier turns showed URLLC latency of 12 ms with jitter of 2 ms and eMBB latency up to 25 ms with jitter of 6 ms.
