options.D: Request network upgrade to eMBB+ with 20ms latency cap and 0.5% loss, but it may not be available until turn 10.

records.question: An AI agent operating in a dynamic 5G network must be onboarded with identity mapping policies that account for fluctuating slice performance and mission-critical latency bounds. At turn 10, the agent is logging an incident over mMTC with 30ms latency, 8ms jitter, 1.2% loss, and 0.8Mbps throughput under 85% edge load. Historical data shows URLLC slice latency dropped from 10ms to 7ms over two turns while edge load rose from 0.4 to 0.55. The mission SLA requires latency <15ms for critical commands and throughput >100Mbps for data streaming. If the agent must remain active for 3 more turns and edge load is projected to increase by 0.05 per turn, which identity mapping policy should be selected to minimize worst-case regret? A: Assign to URLLC with 7ms latency and 100Mbps throughput, accepting 0.41 edge load. B: Assign to eMBB with 16ms latency and 720Mbps throughput, accepting 0.78 edge load. C: Assign to mMTC with 30ms latency and 0.8Mbps throughput, accepting 0.85 edge load. D: Assign to URLLC but cap throughput at 50Mbps to reduce edge load by 0.1 per turn.

options.A: Assign to URLLC with 7ms latency and 100Mbps throughput, accepting 0.41 edge load.
options.B: Assign to eMBB with 16ms latency and 720Mbps throughput, accepting 0.78 edge load.
options.C: Assign to mMTC with 30ms latency and 0.8Mbps throughput, accepting 0.85 edge load.
options.D: Assign to URLLC but cap throughput at 50Mbps to reduce edge load by 0.1 per turn.

records.question: The UAV is currently streaming thermal data over eMBB with 720 Mbps throughput and 0.8% loss, while edge load is at 0.78 and rising. The next federated model update requires 1.2 Gbps sustained for 30 seconds to aggregate from 5 edge nodes, each with 15% battery remaining. URLLC offers 105 Mbps with 0.03% loss but only 0.48 edge load, while mMTC has 0.8 Mbps and 1.2% loss with 0.85 edge load. If the edge load exceeds 0.9 in the next turn, the system will throttle all slices, and battery decay accelerates by 2% per minute under high load. The anomaly detection model must be updated before the next survey leg in 2 turns or accuracy degrades by 15%. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Proceed with eMBB now: throughput is sufficient for 30s, edge load is 0.78, and battery decay is acceptable at 2% per minute.
options.B: Switch to URLLC: lower throughput but guaranteed low latency and jitter, edge load is 0.48, and battery decay is halved under low load.
options.C: Delay update until next turn: edge load may drop to 0.65 if mMTC traffic clears, and battery will be at 13% with 1.5% decay rate.
options.D: Split update across slices: use eMBB for 15s and URLLC for 15s, balancing load and throughput while keeping edge load under 0.85.

records.question: At turn 8, the UAV is streaming thermal data over eMBB with 16ms latency, 4ms jitter, 0.8% loss, and 720Mbps throughput while edge load is 0.78. The third-party analytics agent requests full sensor API access for anomaly detection, citing a 95% confidence interval on detection latency under 12ms. However, historical data shows URLLC slice latency can spike to 10ms with 1.5ms jitter under edge load >0.55, and mMTC has 30ms latency with 8ms jitter at 0.85 edge load. Regulatory policy mandates that any third-party access must maintain SLA compliance for mission-critical functions for at least 3 turns, with maximum allowable latency of 15ms and loss under 1%. If the UAV continues streaming, edge load will rise to 0.82 next turn, risking URLLC degradation. Which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret across plausible futures while preserving trust and compliance?

options.A: Grant full API access immediately; current eMBB metrics are within SLA and the agent’s 95% confidence interval suggests low risk.
options.B: Delay access until turn 10; by then, edge load will drop to 0.41 and URLLC will be available, ensuring compliance even under worst-case jitter.
options.C: Grant limited read-only access to thermal data only; this reduces exposure while allowing partial analysis, though throughput may drop to 500Mbps under URLLC.
options.D: Deny access entirely; the risk of SLA violation under projected edge load and uncertain jitter exceeds acceptable trust thresholds for third-party agents.

records.question: At turn 10, the UAV is streaming thermal anomaly data over mMTC with 30ms latency, 8ms jitter, 1.2% loss, and 0.8Mbps throughput under 85% edge load. The SLA requires latency <20ms, loss <0.5%, and throughput >1Mbps for critical data. The next turn may see edge load rise to 90% with 15% probability or drop to 75% with 85% probability. URLLC offers 7ms latency, 0.7ms jitter, 0.01% loss, and 100Mbps throughput at 41% edge load but cannot carry thermal streams exceeding 50Mbps. eMBB offers 16ms latency, 4ms jitter, 0.8% loss, and 720Mbps throughput at 78% edge load but risks violating SLA if edge load exceeds 80%. The UAV must complete anomaly logging within 2 turns or abort. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Switch to URLLC immediately; it meets all SLA bounds and has low edge load, though it cannot carry full thermal stream.
options.B: Stay on mMTC; edge load may drop to 75% next turn, restoring SLA compliance with 85% probability.
options.C: Switch to eMBB; it currently meets SLA with 78% edge load and can carry full thermal stream, though it risks violation if load rises.
options.D: Abort mission; no slice guarantees SLA compliance over the next 2 turns under worst-case edge load projections.

records.question: The UAV is operating under icing conditions with wind at 6.0 m/s and is currently at 50m altitude with 100% battery. Network telemetry at turn 7 shows URLLC slice with 3.8ms latency, 1.0ms jitter, 0.15% loss, 52Mbps throughput, and 0.38 edge load. The mission requires real-time inference with SLA of <5ms latency and <1% packet loss. Thermal sensor is degraded, and next turn may see edge load rise to 0.45 under worst-case traffic. If inference is placed on edge, projected latency under worst-case jitter and load could reach 5.2ms. Onboard inference consumes 12% battery per turn and adds 2ms processing delay. Which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next two turns while maintaining SLA compliance?

options.A: Place inference on edge; current latency 3.8ms is under SLA and edge load 0.38 is low, so risk is acceptable.
options.B: Place inference onboard; onboard adds 2ms delay but avoids network jitter and ensures SLA even if edge load rises to 0.45.
options.C: Wait one turn to re-evaluate; edge load may drop to 0.35 and latency may improve to 3.5ms, reducing risk.
options.D: Switch to eMBB slice; throughput is higher at 120Mbps and latency is 12ms, which is acceptable for non-critical inference.

records.question: At turn 4, the UAV is operating under eMBB slice with latency 15.0 ms, jitter 5.0 ms, loss 1.0%, throughput 100 Mbps, and edge load 0.75, while the SLA requires latency under 12.0 ms and edge load under 0.8. The thermal sensor is degraded, and the user requests thermal imaging. The next turn may see edge load rise to 0.82 under worst-case weather persistence. If the UAV continues eMBB, latency may spike to 18.0 ms with 2.0% loss. Switching to URLLC now would cap latency at 4.5 ms but reduce throughput to 48 Mbps, risking incomplete thermal capture. Continuing eMBB risks SLA violation in turn 5 with 70% probability. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue eMBB with current settings; throughput is sufficient and SLA violation is not guaranteed.
options.B: Switch to URLLC immediately; latency will stay under SLA and edge load will drop to 0.35, even if throughput falls below 50 Mbps.
options.C: Reduce thermal resolution to 50% to lower data load; this may keep edge load under 0.78 and latency under 14.0 ms.
options.D: Delay thermal capture until turn 6; edge load may naturally drop to 0.65 if wind decreases, but risk of missed inspection window is 40%.

records.question: The UAV is operating under icing conditions with wind at 6.0 m/s from 270 degrees, currently at 50m altitude and 100% battery. At turn 4, the network slice is eMBB with 15.0ms latency, 5.0ms jitter, 1.0% loss, 100Mbps throughput, and 0.75 edge load. The thermal sensor is degraded, and lidar is nonfunctional, requiring offloading of image processing. Policy restricts altitude to 300m max. If edge load exceeds 0.85, offloading fails; if latency exceeds 20ms, mission-critical tasks degrade. Projected edge load in turn 5 is 0.82 with 90% confidence, and jitter may spike to 7.0ms under icing. Which option should be selected to ensure trust-aware offloading while minimizing future regret over the next two turns?

options.A: Offload thermal image processing now via eMBB; accept 15.0ms latency and 0.75 edge load, assuming edge load stays under 0.85 next turn.
options.B: Switch to URLLC slice for offloading; latency drops to 4.1ms but throughput is only 45Mbps, risking incomplete image transmission if resolution exceeds 1080p.
options.C: Delay offloading until turn 5; projected edge load is 0.82 with 90% confidence, but if it exceeds 0.85, offloading fails and thermal data is lost.
options.D: Abort offloading and use onboard processing; battery is 100% but thermal sensor is degraded, risking inaccurate analysis and potential mission failure.

records.question: The UAV is returning to base under URLLC slice with latency 4.0ms, jitter 1.1ms, loss 0.2%, throughput 50Mbps, and edge load 0.42. Historical data shows jitter increased from 0.8ms to 1.1ms over 3 turns, and edge load rose from 0.3 to 0.42. The SLA mandates latency <5ms and loss <0.5% for 3 consecutive turns. If wind persists at 6m/s and battery depletes at 2% per turn, the next turn may see jitter up to 1.5ms and edge load to 0.5. Under worst-case jitter and edge load, which option minimizes maximum regret over the next 2 turns? A) Stay on URLLC with current settings. B) Switch to eMBB with 12ms latency and 0.5% loss. C) Switch to mMTC with 8ms latency and 0.8% loss. D) Initiate emergency descent with 20% battery penalty.

options.A: Stay on URLLC with current settings.
options.B: Switch to eMBB with 12ms latency and 0.5% loss.
options.C: Switch to mMTC with 8ms latency and 0.8% loss.
options.D: Initiate emergency descent with 20% battery penalty.

records.question: The UAV is returning to base under URLCC slice with latency 3.3ms, jitter 0.85ms, loss 0.05%, throughput 56Mbps, and edge_load 0.32. A third-party analytics firm requests compute access for real-time anomaly detection, requiring 40Mbps throughput and latency under 5ms, with a 10% SLA buffer for jitter. The edge node currently has 0.32 load, but projected load increases by 0.08 per turn if two additional UAVs join the swarm. The policy allows exposing compute only if edge_load remains under 0.8 and latency stays under 6ms for the next 3 turns. One UAV may experience a 20% throughput drop due to icing, and jitter may spike to 1.5ms in worst case. Given these constraints and the need to maintain mission safety, which option should be selected to expose compute while minimizing future regret?

options.A: Expose compute immediately with 40Mbps allocation; edge_load will rise to 0.40, within 0.8 limit, and latency remains under 5ms even with 1.5ms jitter worst case.
options.B: Delay exposure for 2 turns; projected edge_load will be 0.48, still under 0.8, and latency will remain under 5ms if no additional UAVs join.
options.C: Expose compute with 30Mbps allocation to leave 10Mbps buffer; edge_load rises to 0.38, but throughput may drop to 32Mbps under icing, violating SLA.
options.D: Reject exposure; current edge_load is safe, but worst-case jitter and throughput drop may violate SLA within 1 turn, risking mission integrity.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is executing a return-to-base maneuver under icing conditions with battery at 100% and sensor suite degraded. Network telemetry shows URLLC slice with latency 3.8ms, jitter 1.0ms, loss 0.15%, throughput 52Mbps, and edge load 0.38. Policy requires latency <5ms and loss <0.5% for critical control. If jitter increases by 0.5ms next turn and edge load rises to 0.45, while throughput drops to 48Mbps, which telemetry subset should be augmented into the RAG prompt to ensure mission continuity under worst-case bounds? Option A includes full telemetry with jitter and edge load projections. Option B includes only latency and loss with current values. Option C includes throughput and battery with no projections. Option D includes only slice type and geofence status. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Full telemetry with jitter and edge load projections
options.B: Only latency and loss with current values
options.C: Throughput and battery with no projections
options.D: Only slice type and geofence status

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV reports battery at 85%, network slice is URLLC with latency 3.8ms, jitter 1.0ms, loss 0.15%, throughput 52Mbps, and edge load 0.38. The mission requires continuous sensor telemetry with SLA of max 5ms latency and 0.5% loss. Wind remains at 6.0m/s from 270°, and icing conditions persist. The agent must onboard a new swarm node with identity 'SwarmNode-7' that will increase edge load by 0.15 and add 1.2ms latency under worst-case jitter. If the new node is onboarded, projected edge load becomes 0.53 and worst-case latency becomes 5.0ms. If not onboarded, the current node must handle all telemetry alone, risking overload if wind increases to 8.0m/s next turn, which would raise jitter to 2.0ms and latency to 5.8ms. The policy allows identity mapping only if SLA is projected to hold for the next 3 turns under worst-case conditions. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Onboard SwarmNode-7 immediately; projected worst-case latency is exactly at SLA limit (5.0ms) and edge load remains under 0.6, satisfying policy for next 3 turns.
options.B: Delay onboarding until turn 9; current node can handle telemetry for 2 more turns, and wind may subside, reducing jitter to 0.8ms and latency to 4.6ms.
options.C: Onboard SwarmNode-7 but throttle its telemetry to 25Mbps; this reduces edge load to 0.48 and worst-case latency to 4.7ms, but violates the 50Mbps minimum throughput requirement for sensor fusion.
options.D: Reject onboarding; current node’s latency under wind increase (5.8ms) exceeds SLA, and adding SwarmNode-7 pushes latency to 5.0ms which is unsafe under jitter uncertainty.

records.question: The UAV swarm is currently operating under URLCC slice with latency 3.8ms, jitter 1.0ms, loss 0.15%, throughput 52Mbps, and edge load 0.38. Battery is at 100% but degrading at 0.8% per minute due to icing conditions. The next federated model update window opens in 2 turns, requiring at least 40Mbps throughput and latency under 5ms for 30 seconds. Edge load is projected to rise to 0.65 if eMBB is activated for high-res sensor fusion. If the swarm continues current URLCC operation, edge load may spike to 0.55 under worst-case jitter accumulation. A competing swarm in sector B reports 0.7 edge load and 18ms latency on eMBB. The mission requires federated learning to complete before battery drops below 70%. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Proceed with URLCC slice now; current latency and throughput meet thresholds, and edge load is below 0.5.
options.B: Switch to eMBB slice for higher throughput; accept 15ms latency and 0.75 edge load to ensure model update completes before battery depletion.
options.C: Delay federated update by one turn; wait for edge load to drop below 0.4 and battery to stabilize, risking 10% battery loss and potential SLA violation.
options.D: Initiate partial model sync over URLCC now, then switch to eMBB for final aggregation; accept 0.55 edge load and 4.5ms latency for first phase, 18ms for second.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is operating under URLLC slice with latency 3.8ms, jitter 1.0ms, loss 0.15%, throughput 52Mbps, and edge load 0.38. Battery is at 100% but sensor diagnostics show thermal and lidar are degraded. A third-party analytics agent requests full telemetry access and compute offload for predictive path correction, citing SLA of 5ms latency and 99.9% reliability. The agent’s trust score is 0.72, below the 0.80 threshold for unrestricted access. Network edge load is projected to rise to 0.65 if compute offload is granted, risking SLA violation under worst-case jitter of +2.0ms. If the agent is denied, the UAV must rely on onboard processing, which increases latency by 12ms and reduces maneuver accuracy by 15%. If granted partial access with throttled throughput, edge load rises to 0.50 and latency margin shrinks to 0.5ms. If granted full access, edge load hits 0.65 and worst-case latency reaches 5.8ms, exceeding SLA. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Deny all access: retain full control, accept 12ms latency penalty and 15% accuracy loss, avoid edge load risk.
options.B: Grant partial access with throttled throughput: edge load 0.50, latency margin 0.5ms, trust score 0.72 still below threshold.
options.C: Grant full access: edge load 0.65, worst-case latency 5.8ms, exceeds SLA but agent claims 99.9% reliability.
options.D: Delay decision until turn 8: monitor if edge load drops below 0.40, but risk missing critical path correction window.

records.question: At turn 7, telemetry indicates the UAV is operating under URLCC slice with latency 3.8ms, jitter 1.0ms, packet loss 0.15%, throughput 52Mbps, and edge load 0.38. Historical data shows jitter has increased from 0.8ms at turn 1 to 1.0ms at turn 7, and edge load has risen from 0.35 to 0.38. The SLA requires latency <5ms, jitter <1.5ms, loss <0.5%, and edge load <0.8. A security anomaly detection system flags a potential DDoS probe targeting the edge node, with 90% confidence, and projects edge load could spike to 0.92 in the next turn if unmitigated. If the UAV continues on current path, it will reach 80% battery in 2 turns and require 30Mbps throughput for safe return. Option A isolates the UAV to a dedicated slice with fixed latency 6ms, jitter 2ms, loss 0.3%, throughput 40Mbps, edge load 0.2. Option B maintains URLCC but throttles throughput to 30Mbps, reducing edge load to 0.32 but increasing jitter to 1.8ms. Option C switches to mMTC with latency 8ms, jitter 2.5ms, loss 0.8%, throughput 10Mbps, edge load 0.55. Option D initiates immediate return with current slice, risking edge overload in turn 8. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Isolate to dedicated slice: latency 6ms (exceeds SLA), jitter 2ms (exceeds SLA), throughput 40Mbps (sufficient), edge load 0.2 (safe)
options.B: Maintain URLCC with throttled throughput: latency 3.8ms (SLA), jitter 1.8ms (exceeds SLA), throughput 30Mbps (minimum required), edge load 0.32 (safe)
options.C: Switch to mMTC: latency 8ms (exceeds SLA), jitter 2.5ms (exceeds SLA), throughput 10Mbps (insufficient), edge load 0.55 (safe)
options.D: Continue current path: latency 3.8ms (SLA), jitter 1.0ms (SLA), throughput 52Mbps (excess), edge load 0.38 (rising to 0.92 projected)

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV is streaming data on eMBB while the network shows latency 35 ms, jitter 15 ms, loss 2.1 percent, throughput 300 Mbps, and edge load 0.88. Earlier on eMBB the latency ranged from 18 to 25 ms with edge load between 0.45 and 0.65, while URLLC showed latency from 7 to 10 ms but throughput only 100 to 130 Mbps. The operator receives an advice to switch slices immediately, but the data stream initiated at turn 6 was already reduced once at turn 9 after a prior switch. Over the last three turns, edge load increased by 0.23 and latency increased by 10 ms on eMBB, indicating uncertain but worsening congestion. If congestion persists one more turn, the worst observed latency of 35 ms and edge load of 0.88 may repeat or slightly worsen. Switching to URLLC would stabilize latency but constrain throughput for the queued upload requested at turn 10, which historically used 780 to 820 Mbps on eMBB. Remaining on eMBB risks further loss beyond 2.1 percent, while switching risks multi turn backlog and delayed mission completion. The decision must minimize maximum regret over the next two turns assuming worst case persistence of current conditions. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Stay on eMBB despite 35 ms latency and 0.88 edge load, accepting possible loss above 2.1 percent to preserve 300 Mbps throughput for the upcoming upload.
options.B: Switch immediately to URLLC with 9 ms latency and 110 Mbps throughput to minimize control risk this turn.
options.C: Defer switching for one turn while reducing stream load again, using the fact that eMBB previously operated at 25 ms latency and 0.65 edge load.
options.D: Switch to mMTC based on its prior availability despite its 45 ms latency, 1.2 percent loss, and 1.5 Mbps throughput.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV reports eMBB latency of 35 ms, jitter of 15 ms, loss of 2.1 percent, throughput of 300 Mbps, and edge load of 0.88 while streaming video. The same episode shows that URLLC at nearby turns delivers latency between 7 and 10 ms, jitter of 1 to 2 ms, loss below 0.1 percent, throughput between 100 and 130 Mbps, and edge load around 0.3 to 0.4. Policy altitude bounds span from 10.0 to 450.0 meters, so loss of control during maneuvering is safety critical. Battery is still at 100 percent, so mission time is not yet constrained, but network contention is expected to persist for the next two to three turns. The operator must choose a slice and streaming posture that is fair to other swarm traffic while minimizing worst case safety risk. If degradation persists one more turn, edge load above 0.85 is known to trigger scheduler backoff for non safety traffic. A myopic choice would optimize current throughput, but future regret must be considered if safety traffic is preempted. Another option appears acceptable at mean values but fails if jitter remains near its observed peak. No option avoids all downsides over the next turns. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Remain on eMBB at 300 Mbps despite edge load 0.88 to preserve fairness, accepting 35 ms latency and 15 ms jitter for the next turns.
options.B: Switch fully to URLLC with throughput capped near 110 Mbps and edge load near 0.35, prioritizing low latency even if other swarm uploads are delayed.
options.C: Alternate slices each turn, using eMBB now and URLLC next, assuming jitter drops back toward 5 ms and edge load falls below 0.75.
options.D: Stay on eMBB but further reduce stream bitrate so edge load falls just under 0.85 while keeping latency near 35 ms.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV is flying at 22.0 mps with battery at 100.0 percent and altitude within the policy bounds of 10.0 to 450.0 meters. Network telemetry shows eMBB latency at 35 ms with jitter 15 ms, loss 2.1 percent, throughput 300 Mbps, and edge load 0.88. One turn earlier the stream was active at high bitrate, and one turn later a switch to URLLC produced latency 9 ms with edge load 0.35 but throughput only 110 Mbps. The mission must consider the next two turns where dust and wind at 8.5 mps may persist and thermal and radar sensors remain offline. If degradation persists for one more turn, worst case latency must be assumed as latency plus jitter and edge load may increase toward saturation. A preemptive autonomy downgrade is allowed if it reduces the chance of violating policy bounds or losing control authority. Four downgrade options trade sensing quality, network robustness, and maneuver aggressiveness. Each option carries some downside within the next one to three turns. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Maintain current autonomy and speed at 22.0 mps on eMBB despite edge load 0.88 and loss 2.1 percent to maximize throughput 300 Mbps this turn.
options.B: Immediately switch to URLLC and keep full autonomy and speed 22.0 mps accepting throughput 110 Mbps and edge load 0.35.
options.C: Downgrade autonomy to reduced mode, cap speed below 22.0 mps, and accept URLLC characteristics with latency 9 ms and edge load 0.35.
options.D: Descend toward the lower policy bound near 10.0 meters to reduce wind impact while staying on eMBB with latency 35 ms.

records.question: At turn 8 the operator has authorized a switch to URLLC after degradation, and the UAV is at 25.0 m altitude moving at 22.0 mps with battery at 100.0 percent. The airspace policy allows altitude between 10.0 and 450.0 m, creating a bounded safety range under dusty weather and 8.5 mps wind. Network telemetry now shows URLLC latency of 9 ms with jitter 1 ms, loss 0.08 percent, throughput 110 Mbps, and edge load 0.35, but earlier eMBB reached edge load 0.88 with loss 2.1 percent. The mission plan requires continuing for the next two turns to finish navigation before return, with reduced streaming already applied. If edge load rebounds toward the prior peak, URLLC capacity may tighten while eMBB may again degrade. A conservative continuation must minimize worst case regret over the next one to three turns rather than maximize current throughput. One option is to continue on URLLC with reduced stream at the current altitude. Another is to climb toward mid band altitude to gain link margin while staying on URLLC. A third is to switch back to eMBB immediately to upload more data now. A fourth is to pause the mission despite having full battery and being inside altitude bounds. Considering altitude limits, observed edge load volatility, and multi turn network risk, which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue on URLLC at 25.0 m with reduced stream, accepting 110 Mbps throughput and 0.35 edge load as a buffer against a rebound toward 0.88 over the next two turns.
options.B: Climb toward higher altitude within the 10.0 to 450.0 m bounds to improve link conditions while remaining on URLLC despite the added maneuver risk.
options.C: Switch back to eMBB now to exploit 780 to 820 Mbps throughput seen earlier, assuming the 0.88 edge load spike was transient.
options.D: Pause the mission and hold position even with 100.0 percent battery and acceptable URLLC latency of 9 ms to avoid any future degradation.

records.question: During turn 8 the operator must finalize identity onboarding for a UAV agent that has switched slices multiple times. Across turns 1 to 9 the observed one way latency values include 7, 8, 9, 18, 20, 25 and 35 ms while jitter spans from 1 to 15 ms and loss ranges from 0.05 to 2.1 percent. Edge load peaked at 0.88 on eMBB in turn 7 and dropped to 0.3 to 0.35 on URLLC in turns 8 and 9. Throughput simultaneously fell from 850 and 800 Mbps on early eMBB turns to 110 to 130 Mbps on URLLC. Battery remains at 100 percent so power is not the limiting factor over the next three turns. The identity service can be bound either to a persistent device identity or to a session scoped network identity tied to a slice. A persistent binding reduces reauthentication cost next turn but amplifies risk if worst case latency or loss recurs. A session scoped identity increases reauth frequency but limits blast radius under degradation. Assume the worst case repeats for one more turn and recovery is uncertain. Which onboarding option should be selected?

options.A: Bind a persistent device identity over URLLC since current latency is 9 ms and edge load is 0.35, accepting future risk if loss rises again.
options.B: Bind a persistent device identity over eMBB because throughput was 820 Mbps at 22 ms in turn 10, assuming conditions revert.
options.C: Use a session scoped network identity on URLLC to cap impact if latency returns to 35 ms and loss to 2.1 percent despite added reauth cost.
options.D: Delay onboarding for one turn to observe whether jitter stabilizes below 3 ms and edge load stays under 0.5.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV must federate data between the planning agent, network orchestrator, and base analytics while network quality degrades. The eMBB slice shows latency 35 ms, jitter 15 ms, loss 2.1 percent, throughput 300 Mbps, and edge load 0.88 at this turn. Earlier turns show URLLC latency values of 7 to 10 ms with jitter 1 to 2 ms, loss between 0.05 and 0.1 percent, throughput from 100 to 130 Mbps, and edge load from 0.3 to 0.4. The base analytics requires sustained throughput above 120 Mbps, while the planning agent requires worst case latency below 40 ms to avoid compounding route error. Battery remains at 100 percent so energy is not the immediate constraint, but policy requires the mission to continue for at least two more turns. There is uncertainty that eMBB loss could persist at the observed 2.1 percent for the next two turns if edge load remains above 0.85. There is also uncertainty that URLLC throughput could dip to the observed 100 Mbps in the next turn if contention rises. If federation fails, the regret is a forced abort in turn 9 or 10 rather than graceful completion. Considering worst case bounds over the next two turns, the agent must choose one federation and slice strategy. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Federate all agents on eMBB now because 300 Mbps throughput exceeds the 120 Mbps requirement despite 35 ms latency and 0.88 edge load.
options.B: Federate planning and control on URLLC and defer base analytics to the queued upload on eMBB because URLLC latency stays under 10 ms with edge load near 0.3.
options.C: Federate everything on URLLC because loss is 0.1 percent or lower and latency is under 10 ms even if throughput drops toward 100 Mbps.
options.D: Pause federation for one turn to wait for recovery since earlier eMBB turns had latency near 20 ms and loss below 0.3 percent.

records.question: The UAV is operating under snow conditions with wind at 8.0 m/s and is currently using URLLC with 7 ms latency, 1 ms jitter, 0.01% loss, 115 Mbps throughput, and 0.30 edge load. The mission requires real-time obstacle avoidance with a maximum allowable latency of 15 ms and a minimum throughput of 100 Mbps. Thermal and radar sensors are offline; lidar is primary with GNSS and IMU as backups. The next waypoint is 1200 meters away at 15 m/s speed, requiring 80 seconds of continuous inference. Edge load is projected to increase by 0.05 per turn due to swarm coordination. If network degradation recurs, latency may spike to 45 ms with 2.1% loss. Which compute placement option should be selected to ensure mission completion under worst-case conditions over the next two turns?

options.A: Onboard inference only: uses local GPU, consumes 12% battery per minute, latency 3 ms, no network dependency, but cannot fuse thermal data if restored.
options.B: Edge inference via URLLC: current latency 7 ms, throughput 115 Mbps, edge load 0.30, but projected edge load 0.40 next turn may cause queuing delay exceeding 15 ms SLA.
options.C: Hybrid inference: onboard handles collision avoidance (latency 3 ms), edge handles path planning (URLLC, 7 ms), but edge load 0.30 + 0.05 per turn risks SLA violation by turn 12 if degradation recurs.

options.C: Shift the imaging UAV to mMTC because 50 to 60 ms latency and 10 Mbps throughput reduce contention and edge load near 0.3 to 0.75.
options.D: Rotate all members to URLLC despite throughput near 100 Mbps to equalize fairness and keep latency low.

records.question: At turn 7 the swarm detects a potential obstacle while flying at 15.0 mps and coordinating collision avoidance under icing and 6.0 mps wind. records.question: At turn 8 the UAV is inspecting an anomaly after de icing with lidar and RGB available while thermal and radar remain offline.
