Under the worst observed mMTC loss of 6.5 percent and edge_load of 0.91, telemetry gaps compound over multiple turns. If the next two turns resemble the last two rather than the earlier URLLC phase, which scheduler reconfiguration should be selected?

options.A: Force URLLC immediately, accepting throughput around 95 Mbps and edge_load near 0.5 to minimize current latency.
options.B: Maintain reduced telemetry on mMTC, tolerating 130 ms latency and loss up to 6.5 percent while edge_load stays near 0.91.
options.C: Revert to eMBB assuming recovery to 13 ms latency, 0.1 percent loss, and edge_load around 0.38.

records.question: At turn 10 the route is resumed after a weather hold and the network is on URLLC with latency 8 ms, jitter 0.9 ms, loss 0.01 percent, throughput 105 Mbps, and edge load 0.44. Earlier degradation at turns 6 and 7 showed mMTC latency 120 to 130 ms, jitter 25 to 30 ms, loss 5.0 to 6.5 percent, throughput 1.2 to 0.9 Mbps, and edge load 0.88 to 0.91. Each option below has a downside in either capacity, observability, or future reversals. options.A: Keep URLLC and restore high rate telemetry now because latency 8 ms and loss 0.01 percent are currently best, accepting possible capacity stress if edge load rises from 0.44 toward 0.91.
options.B: Switch back to eMBB for consistency with turn 11 conditions since latency 13 ms and throughput 800 Mbps allow richer data even if loss returns to 0.1 percent.

records.question: At turn 7 the primary agent must decide how to route horizontal messages to a swarm agent for collision avoidance while the network has degraded. Recent turns show URLLC latency between 7 and 10 ms with jitter between 0.8 and 1.2 ms and loss between 0.01 and 0.04 pct, while mMTC latency has risen from 120 to 130 ms with jitter from 25 to 30 ms and loss from 5.0 to 6.5 pct. Routing over mMTC risks excessive delay if the worst observed loss and jitter persist. A relay via the edge can smooth jitter but adds one extra hop equivalent to the higher observed URLLC latency. A hybrid policy can duplicate messages across slices but consumes throughput under high edge_load. Assuming no option avoids all risk, which routing and QoS policy should be selected?

options.A: Send all agent-to-agent traffic directly over URLLC at observed 8 to 10 ms latency and accept edge_load up to 0.5.
options.B: Switch all agent-to-agent traffic to mMTC since throughput demand is low despite 120 to 130 ms latency and 5.0 to 6.5 pct loss.
options.C: Route agent-to-agent traffic via an edge relay over URLLC accepting an extra hop roughly equal to 10 ms while avoiding mMTC conditions.
options.D: Duplicate agent-to-agent messages over both URLLC and mMTC to hedge against loss while using available 95 to 105 Mbps throughput.

records.question: At turn 7 the digital twin is being updated under mMTC with latency at 130 ms, jitter at 30 ms, loss at 6.5 percent, throughput at 0.9 Mbps, and edge load at 0.91. Earlier in turn 6 the same slice showed 120 ms latency, 25 ms jitter, 5.0 percent loss, 1.2 Mbps throughput, and edge load 0.88. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Keep mMTC for both telemetry and commands because 0.9 Mbps throughput still exceeds reduced telemetry needs and latency only rose from 120 to 130 ms.
options.B: Switch fully to URLLC since latency stays near 8 to 10 ms even if jitter varies from 0.9 to 1.2 ms and loss remains below 0.04 percent.

records.question: During turns 6 and 7 the UAV experienced degraded mMTC conditions with latency rising from 120 to 130 ms, jitter increasing from 25 to 30 ms, loss from 5.0 to 6.5 percent, throughput dropping from 1.2 to 0.9 Mbps, and edge load climbing from 0.88 to 0.91. At the same time the vehicle is flying at 35.0 mps inside an altitude band of 10.0 to 120.0 m with icing weather and wind of 6.5 mps. A hybrid strategy may trade some immediacy for robustness under loss and jitter. All options risk either perception gaps or network saturation within one to three turns. options.A: Stream full RGB and LiDAR to the edge over mMTC and perform edge-centric fusion, accepting 130 ms latency and 6.5 percent loss to maximize shared awareness.
options.B: Switch to URLLC and stream RGB only for edge fusion while suppressing LiDAR to stay within 95 to 110 Mbps throughput and current 0.5 edge load.

options.D: Use hybrid fusion with onboard RGB plus LiDAR for immediate avoidance and opportunistic URLLC bursts for shared features, tolerating 7 to 10 ms latency when available and falling back to mMTC otherwise.

records.question: At turn 6 the UAV is en route in icing weather with wind at 6.5 mps and battery at 100 percent while the network shifts to mMTC with latency 120 ms, jitter 25 ms, loss 5.0 percent, throughput 1.2 Mbps, and edge load 0.88. records.question: At turn 7 the mission is en route while the network slice is mMTC with latency between 120 and 130 ms, jitter between 25 and 30 ms, loss between 5.0 and 6.5 percent, throughput between 1.2 and 0.9 Mbps, and edge_load between 0.88 and 0.91. options.D: Migrate only the core navigation agent to URLLC while keeping telemetry and coordination agents on mMTC to balance edge_load near 0.88 and latency exposure.

records.question: At turn 6 the operator requests an inspection capture while the UAV is airborne in rain with wind at 6.0 mps. The UAV is at altitude 30.0 within policy bounds of 10.0 to 120.0 and is flying at 15.0 mps with battery at 100.0 percent. Network performance has recently varied across turns with URLLC latency observed at 5, 6, and 7 ms and jitter at 1, 1.1, and 1.5 ms while eMBB earlier showed latency of 25 and 30 ms with jitter of 5 and 8 ms. Edge load has ranged from 0.3 to 0.4 on URLLC and reached 0.75 on eMBB. The intent message asks to continue inspection for the next two turns and then return to home without changing altitude. If latency degrades again similar to turn 4 while the UAV maintains 30.0 altitude, collision avoidance messages must still be exchanged as in turn 5. Battery drain is not quantified per turn but higher edge load and throughput swings between 45 and 120 Mbps imply processing variability. A single turn view would favor the highest throughput slice for image capture, but a multi turn view must consider worst observed latency and jitter. Under worst case assumptions using only observed values, one option minimizes maximum regret if degradation persists for two more turns. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Keep eMBB for the next two turns to use 120 Mbps throughput despite latency reaching 30 ms and edge load 0.75.
options.B: Switch to URLLC and hold altitude at 30.0 accepting throughput around 45 to 50 Mbps with latency between 5 and 7 ms and edge load below 0.4.
options.C: Switch to mMTC to reduce edge load to 0.2 even though latency may reach 100 ms and throughput drops to 1 Mbps.
options.D: Alternate between eMBB and URLLC each turn to balance throughput 120 Mbps and latency 6 ms assuming degradation will not repeat.

records.question: At turn 4 the UAV is executing a maneuver while inspection intent is pending and network conditions have degraded. Latency on the active eMBB slice has varied between 25 ms and 30 ms across turns 3 and 4, jitter increased from 5 ms to 8 ms, and loss rose from 0.3 percent to 1.2 percent. Throughput dropped from 120 Mbps to 90 Mbps while edge load climbed from 0.6 to 0.75 over the same window. The mission intent requires timely control for the next two turns because capture and collision avoidance are expected to continue. Network policy allows switching slices but URLLC has lower throughput of 45 to 50 Mbps and edge load around 0.38 to 0.4 as seen later. Battery remains at 100 percent so endurance is not immediately limiting, but wind is 6.0 mps and recovery uncertainty exists if degradation persists one more turn. If latency stays at the worst observed value and loss increases proportionally with edge load next turn, control stability risk increases. If a switch is made now, throughput may constrain imagery but latency margin improves immediately. Delaying a switch optimizes current throughput but risks compounding loss if the trend continues. Which option should be selected to minimize worst case regret over the next two turns given mission intent and network policy?

options.A: Remain on eMBB to preserve 90 Mbps throughput since current latency is only 30 ms and battery is 100 percent.
options.B: Switch immediately to URLLC accepting 45 to 50 Mbps throughput to reduce latency to about 7 ms and stabilize loss near 0.2 percent.
options.C: Delay one turn on eMBB and switch only if edge load exceeds 0.75 to avoid unnecessary slice changes.
options.D: Switch to mMTC to minimize edge load to about 0.2 despite latency near 100 ms.

records.question: The mission began with navigation and inspection under URLLC and eMBB slices with latency values between 5 and 30 and edge load rising from 0.3 to 0.75. At turn 7 the agent reports completion and battery while the network slice shifts to mMTC with latency 100, jitter 20, loss 2.0 and throughput 1. The UAV altitude remains 30 within policy bounds of 10 to 120 and battery was initially 100 with no depletion reported yet. The user intent at turn 6 was initiate inspection and at turn 8 becomes request return, but turn 7 precedes that change. Over the last three turns edge load drops from 0.75 to 0.4 to 0.38 suggesting recovery rather than emergency. Under worst case reasoning the mMTC latency of 100 must be treated as persistent for the next one to three turns. If intent has not drifted, continued safety critical control would favor URLLC despite capacity limits, but if intent has drifted to reporting or telemetry then mMTC is acceptable. A single turn view might treat turn 7 as benign reporting, but a multi turn view risks missing a subtle shift away from mission execution. The quantitative question is whether the combination of slice change, latency jump, and timing before return indicates an unintended intent change. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Flag intent drift because latency increased from 6 to 100 and throughput fell from 50 to 1, implying a shift from control to telemetry despite altitude 30 remaining within 10 to 120.
options.B: Do not flag intent drift because battery reporting is consistent with mission completion and edge load decreased from 0.75 to 0.38 indicating normal recovery.
options.C: Defer judgment for one more turn since mMTC edge load is only 0.2 and worst case latency of 100 does not violate any explicit policy bound.
options.D: Flag intent drift only if the slice remains mMTC after the return command at turn 8, treating the current turn as noise.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV has completed inspection and reports telemetry while flying at 30.0 m altitude and 15.0 mps in rain with 6.0 mps wind. The network slice has shifted to mMTC with 100 ms latency, 20 ms jitter, 2.0 percent loss, 1 Mbps throughput, and 0.2 edge load. Earlier turns showed URLLC latency between 4 and 7 ms with loss between 0.02 and 0.2 percent and edge load between 0.28 and 0.4. The geofence is a 200 by 200 area and the UAV is returning from inside it with starting battery previously at 100 percent and no recharge opportunity. Thermal, lidar, and radar sensors remain offline, so continuation relies on GNSS and IMU only. If the degraded mMTC conditions persist for one more turn, command delays could accumulate while wind remains constant. If the system switches slices again, edge load may rise toward previously observed 0.75 under eMBB. A conservative decision must minimize worst case regret over the next two turns rather than optimize this instant. All options have downsides either in latency risk, load risk, or mission delay. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue on mMTC for the next two turns because edge load is only 0.2 even though latency is 100 ms and loss is 2.0 percent.
options.B: Switch immediately to URLLC with 6 to 7 ms latency and 0.1 to 0.2 percent loss despite edge load rising toward 0.4.
options.C: Switch to eMBB to gain 90 to 120 Mbps throughput accepting 25 to 30 ms latency and edge load that previously reached 0.75.
options.D: Pause maneuvering for one turn to wait for recovery since latency earlier dropped from 30 ms to 7 ms.

records.question: At turn 5 the swarm has just switched back to URLLC while edge load has fluctuated between 0.3 and 0.75 in recent turns and the UAV is flying at 30.0 m altitude within policy bounds of 10.0 to 120.0. Battery is still 100.0 percent and speed is 15.0 mps so there is no immediate energy pressure. Recent network history shows eMBB latency rising from 25 to 30 ms with loss up to 1.2 percent while URLLC stayed between 5 and 7 ms with loss at or below 0.2 percent. mMTC showed 100 ms latency with 2.0 percent loss but low edge load of 0.2. The swarm plans to coordinate collision avoidance and return maneuvers over the next two turns where latency spikes would compound regret if congestion persists. Weather is rainy with 6.0 mps wind so navigation errors amplify if control messages are delayed. Edge load uncertainty is represented by the observed spread up to 0.75 which could reoccur next turn. Allocating too much URLLC capacity risks future congestion while eMBB risks control instability under worst case loss. The decision must minimize maximum regret over the next three turns rather than optimize the current snapshot. Which slice allocation should the swarm select now?

options.A: Keep URLLC for all agents since latency has stayed between 5 and 7 ms and loss at 0.2 percent despite edge load around 0.4.
options.B: Move all agents to eMBB because throughput reached 120 Mbps earlier and current speed is only 15.0 mps.
options.C: Assign mMTC to all agents since edge load was as low as 0.2 and battery is 100.0 percent.
options.D: Split with control agents on URLLC and noncritical telemetry on eMBB to hedge against edge load rising again toward 0.75.

records.question: At turn 5 the agent must choose how to route agent to agent collision avoidance traffic while returning to home over the next three turns. Recent telemetry shows URLLC latency of 7 ms with jitter 1.5 ms, loss 0.2 percent, throughput 45 Mbps, and edge load 0.4 at turn 5. Earlier eMBB conditions reached latency 30 ms with jitter 8 ms, loss 1.2 percent, throughput 90 Mbps, and edge load 0.75 at turn 4. Later mMTC behavior showed latency 100 ms with jitter 20 ms, loss 2.0 percent, throughput 1 Mbps, and edge load 0.2 at turn 7. The return maneuver spans turns 5 to 9 and requires continuous low latency exchanges to avoid collision risk. Edge load has varied between 0.28 and 0.75 across turns, creating uncertainty for the next turn. Assume the worst case that the highest observed jitter and edge load can recur for any chosen slice. A single turn view would favor higher throughput for richer messages. Over multiple turns, message loss or delay compounds into higher regret if avoidance messages arrive late. Each option below changes routing or slice selection immediately and holds it for the next two turns. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Keep URLLC routing for agent to agent traffic despite throughput 45 to 55 Mbps and edge load around 0.4 to minimize latency risk.
options.B: Switch agent to agent traffic to eMBB to gain 90 to 120 Mbps throughput accepting latency around 25 to 30 ms and edge load up to 0.75.
options.C: Downgrade agent to agent traffic to mMTC since edge load can be as low as 0.2 despite latency reaching 100 ms and jitter 20 ms.
options.D: Alternate between URLLC and eMBB each turn to balance latency 6 to 30 ms and throughput 45 to 120 Mbps under varying edge load.

records.question: A UAV supporting disaster inspection has just switched back to URLLC at turn 5 after eMBB degradation, while rain and 6.0 mps wind persist. Across turns 1 to 6, URLLC latency varied between 5 and 7 ms, jitter between 1 and 1.5 ms, loss between 0.05 and 0.2 pct, and edge load between 0.3 and 0.4. The prior eMBB phase showed latency rising from 25 to 30 ms, jitter from 5 to 8 ms, loss up to 1.2 pct, and edge load up to 0.75. The UAV flies at 15.0 mps at 30.0 m altitude within the 10.0 to 120.0 m policy bounds and has 100.0 pct battery, but only the RGB sensor is operational. The operator must choose a coordination and network policy that will govern the next two turns during inspection and possible return. If congestion similar to turn 4 reappears, the worst case must be assumed rather than the mean. A single turn decision that looks safe may increase regret if degradation persists into turn 7 when mMTC previously showed 100 ms latency and 2.0 pct loss. All options incur some downside either in sensing quality, collision risk, or command latency. The goal is to minimize maximum regret over the next two turns rather than optimize current throughput. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Keep URLLC for both upcoming turns, limit coordination messages to collision avoidance only, and accept throughput around 45 to 50 Mbps with edge load near 0.4.
options.B: Switch back to eMBB to maximize 120 Mbps throughput for richer RGB streaming, assuming latency stays near 25 ms and edge load below 0.6.
options.C: Downgrade to mMTC to reduce edge load to about 0.2 immediately, tolerating latency near 100 ms and loss up to 2.0 pct for coordination.
options.D: Alternate URLLC this turn and eMBB next turn to balance load, expecting average latency around 15 ms and edge load near 0.5.

records.question: During an XR inspection stream, the operator must prioritize network slices and edge resources over the next three turns while conditions fluctuate. Across recent turns, eMBB showed latency rising from 25 ms to 30 ms with jitter increasing from 5 ms to 8 ms and edge load growing from 0.6 to 0.75. URLLC in nearby turns showed latency between 5 ms and 7 ms with jitter from 1 ms to 1.5 ms and throughput between 45 Mbps and 55 Mbps while edge load ranged from 0.3 to 0.4. The XR feed requires both stable frame timing and enough throughput to avoid rebuffering, and battery remains at 100 percent so energy is not the immediate constraint. Assume the degradation seen on eMBB may persist one more turn before recovery, but URLLC capacity may tighten if edge load exceeds 0.4. mMTC previously exhibited 100 ms latency, 20 ms jitter, and only 1 Mbps throughput despite low edge load. The operator must choose a slice strategy now and accept that no option is perfect. One option optimizes the current turn visuals, another barely misses stability under worst case jitter, another ignores uncertainty, and one minimizes worst case regret over the next three turns. Considering worst case latency and jitter over the next three turns and projected edge load, which option should be selected?

options.A: Stay on eMBB to exploit 90 to 120 Mbps throughput despite latency possibly reaching 30 ms and edge load rising to 0.75 next turn.
options.B: Switch to URLLC with 45 to 55 Mbps throughput and accept tighter capacity as edge load approaches 0.4 while latency stays under 7 ms.
options.C: Drop to mMTC to minimize edge load at 0.2 even though latency can reach 100 ms and throughput is 1 Mbps.
options.D: Alternate eMBB this turn and URLLC next turn to balance 25 ms latency now and 7 ms later assuming recovery occurs.

records.question: At turn 7 the monitoring system flags a potential network anomaly after an unexpected switch to mMTC with latency 100 ms, jitter 20 ms, loss 2.0 pct, throughput 1 Mbps, and edge_load 0.2. Earlier turns show URLLC latency between 4 and 7 ms, jitter between 0.8 and 1.5 ms, loss between 0.02 and 0.2 pct, and edge_load between 0.28 and 0.4. The anomaly detector reports uncertainty because similar spikes have previously either cleared within one turn or persisted for two more turns. Automated response must consider the next one to three turns during return and landing operations. Full isolation of the node reduces edge_load growth but forces continued use of mMTC characteristics. Staying on URLLC without action risks recurrence if the anomaly represents a slow attack ramp rather than a transient fault. A rate limit and enhanced inspection can reduce throughput temporarily while preserving low latency. The worst case assumes the anomaly persists and edge_load increases toward previously observed peaks. The best case assumes recovery to URLLC baselines next turn. Which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret across these futures?

options.A: Immediately isolate the affected network node, accept mMTC latency 100 ms and loss 2.0 pct, and keep edge_load near 0.2 for the next turns.
options.B: Do nothing and continue normal operations, assuming return to URLLC latency 4 to 7 ms and edge_load around 0.3 next turn.
options.C: Force a permanent switch to URLLC now, targeting latency 5 to 7 ms and throughput above 50 Mbps despite prior anomaly uncertainty.
options.D: Apply rate limiting and enhanced inspection while remaining on URLLC, tolerating temporary throughput reduction from 50 Mbps toward 45 Mbps and edge_load rising from 0.3 toward 0.4.

records.question: The UAV has completed its delivery mission and is now preparing for return, with battery at 100% and thermal sensor still offline. Network slice is currently eMBB with 750 Mbps throughput, 13 ms latency, 2.5 ms jitter, 0.15% loss, and 0.35 edge load. A customer requests immediate LLM fine-tuning via 6G Model Training-as-a-Service, requiring 500 Mbps sustained throughput for 3 turns, with SLA latency under 15 ms and edge load under 0.6. Historical data shows eMBB degrades to 600 Mbps and 18 ms latency under wind gusts above 7 m/s, which are forecasted for the next 2 turns. URLLC slice offers 100 Mbps, 5 ms latency, 0.02% loss, and 0.1 edge load but cannot meet throughput requirements. mMTC slice offers 1 Mbps, 50 ms latency, 1.5% loss, and 0.8 edge load, violating all SLAs. If training begins now, the UAV must maintain eMBB for 3 turns, risking SLA violation if degradation persists. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Accept training on eMBB now; current metrics meet SLA and wind may not worsen.
options.B: Reject training; eMBB may degrade to 600 Mbps and 18 ms latency, violating SLA in turn 11.
options.C: Switch to URLLC and throttle training; accept 100 Mbps throughput with 5 ms latency, risking training failure.
options.D: Delay training for 2 turns; wait for wind to subside and re-evaluate eMBB stability.

records.question: The UAV is returning under eMBB slice with 750 Mbps throughput, 13 ms latency, 2.5 ms jitter, 0.15% loss, and 0.35 edge load. Weather risk persists with 8 m/s wind from 240°, and thermal sensor remains offline. The next 3 turns require AR-guided obstacle avoidance with 100 Mbps minimum throughput and 15 ms max latency. URLLC slice offers 100 Mbps, 5 ms latency, 0.5 ms jitter, 0.02% loss, and 0.1 edge load but is reserved for emergency telemetry. mMTC slice has 1 Mbps, 50 ms latency, 10 ms jitter, 1.5% loss, and 0.8 edge load. If wind degrades latency by up to 3 ms per turn and edge load increases by 0.1 per turn, which option minimizes maximum regret over the next 3 turns while maintaining AR session integrity?

options.A: Stay on eMBB; current latency 13 ms is under 15 ms SLA, and throughput 750 Mbps exceeds 100 Mbps requirement.
options.B: Switch to URLLC; latency 5 ms is safe, throughput 100 Mbps meets minimum, and edge load 0.1 is low, but may block emergency telemetry.
options.C: Switch to mMTC; edge load 0.8 is high but acceptable, latency 50 ms exceeds SLA by 35 ms, and throughput 1 Mbps is below requirement.
options.D: Wait 1 turn for weather to clear; projected latency under eMBB will be 16 ms (exceeding SLA) and edge load 0.45, risking session failure.

records.question: The UAV has completed its mission and is now idle with 100% battery, but a customer requests immediate LLM fine-tuning over the current eMBB slice with 800 Mbps throughput and 13 ms latency. The edge load is 0.35 and rising, and historical data shows edge load increases by 0.05 per turn under eMBB. The SLA requires latency under 20 ms and throughput above 500 Mbps for 3 consecutive turns. Under worst-case jitter of +2 ms and loss of +0.2%, the projected latency in turn 12 would be 17 ms with 750 Mbps throughput. URLLC offers 135 Mbps and 7.5 ms latency but cannot support model training due to bandwidth constraints. mMTC has 1.2 Mbps and 55 ms latency, violating SLA. Which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next 3 turns while preserving mission readiness?

options.A: Accept the training request on eMBB now, accepting the risk of SLA violation in turn 12 if edge load continues rising.
options.B: Reject the request and wait for URLLC to become available, even though it cannot support training, preserving SLA compliance for future tasks.
options.C: Switch to mMTC to free up eMBB for future high-priority tasks, accepting immediate SLA violation but reducing edge load pressure.
options.D: Delay the request for 2 turns to allow edge load to stabilize, risking customer churn but ensuring SLA compliance through turn 12.

records.question: The UAV is at target with eMBB slice active, latency 13ms, jitter 2.1ms, loss 0.2%, throughput 800Mbps, edge load 0.35. Thermal sensor remains offline. Battery is 100% but threshold set at 20% for emergency return. Next turn requires AR overlay rendering (min 500Mbps, max 20ms latency) and telemetry sync (min 100Mbps, max 50ms latency). URLLC slice offers 135Mbps throughput, 7.5ms latency, 0.17 edge load. mMTC slice offers 1.2Mbps, 55ms latency, 0.9 edge load. Worst-case jitter may increase by 20% next turn. If edge load exceeds 0.95, system degrades to emergency mode. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Use eMBB slice for AR rendering and telemetry; accept 13ms latency and 0.35 edge load; projected edge load next turn 0.4 under worst-case jitter.
options.B: Switch to URLLC for AR rendering; accept 135Mbps throughput; telemetry will fail due to bandwidth; edge load 0.17; latency 7.5ms.
options.C: Use mMTC for telemetry only; AR rendering deferred; edge load 0.9; latency 55ms; risk of emergency mode if load exceeds 0.95 next turn.
options.D: Split AR rendering over eMBB and telemetry over URLLC; total edge load 0.52; worst-case latency 15ms for AR; telemetry latency 7.5ms.

records.question: The UAV has completed its mission and is now idle with 100% battery, but the network slice is currently URLLC with 58 Mbps throughput and 0.42 edge load. A customer requests immediate LLM fine-tuning requiring 70 Mbps sustained throughput for 3 turns, with SLA latency capped at 10 ms and edge load not exceeding 0.8. Historical data shows eMBB slice offers 100–120 Mbps but latency spikes to 30 ms under wind shear, while URLLC degrades to 40 Mbps if edge load exceeds 0.6. The next 3 turns may see wind gusts increasing to 12 m/s, potentially forcing a switch to eMBB. If the training starts now on URLLC, projected edge load will hit 0.75 by turn 13. If deferred to turn 14, eMBB may be available but with 35% chance of 40 ms latency violation. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Accept training now on URLLC: current throughput 58 Mbps is below 70 Mbps requirement but edge load 0.42 allows headroom; latency 7 ms is within SLA.
options.B: Defer training to turn 14 on eMBB: projected throughput 110 Mbps exceeds 70 Mbps, but 35% risk of 40 ms latency violation exceeds SLA tolerance.
options.C: Accept training now on URLLC with throttling: reduce training batch size to fit 58 Mbps, accepting 20% slower convergence but preserving latency and edge load under 0.5.
options.D: Reject training: no slice can guarantee 70 Mbps + 10 ms SLA under projected wind conditions and edge load growth.

records.question: The UAV has completed payload release and is initiating return under poor weather with wind at 8.5 m/s from 270°. Current network slice is URLLC with 7ms latency, 0.6ms jitter, 0.03% loss, 58 Mbps throughput, and 0.42 edge load. Policy mandates max 10ms latency and 1% loss for AR streaming. Wind shear may persist for 2 more turns, increasing jitter by up to 50% and edge load by 0.15. Battery is at 78% and descending at 2% per turn. If the UAV switches to eMBB for higher throughput, latency jumps to 30ms and edge load to 0.75, risking SLA violation. If it stays on URLLC, throughput may drop to 40 Mbps under sustained wind, degrading AR quality. If it switches to mMTC, latency exceeds 120ms, making AR unusable. If it throttles payload data to 30 Mbps, edge load drops to 0.25 but AR resolution suffers. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Stay on URLLC; accept 40 Mbps throughput under wind shear; edge load remains below 0.6; latency stays under 10ms.
options.B: Switch to eMBB; gain 100 Mbps throughput; tolerate 30ms latency and 0.75 edge load; risk SLA violation if jitter increases.
options.C: Switch to mMTC; reduce edge load to 0.3; accept 120ms latency; AR becomes non-interactive but data logs survive.
options.D: Throttle payload to 30 Mbps; reduce edge load to 0.25; latency stays at 7ms; sacrifice AR resolution for stability.

records.question: At turn 11 the operator intends to finalize a safe return while keeping the UAV within the policy altitude bounds of 10.0 to 120.0 meters. The UAV is currently at altitude 25.0 meters with speed 15.0 mps and full battery at 100.0 percent under icing and 6.0 mps wind. The network slice has shifted to mMTC with latency 50 ms, jitter 20 ms, loss 1.8 percent, throughput 1.2 Mbps, and edge load 0.18. In earlier return-related turns on URLLC the latency ranged from 5 to 9 ms with edge load between 0.27 and 0.32, while eMBB degraded to latency 45 ms with edge load 0.85 during video. The intent assumes that the current mMTC conditions may persist for the next two turns or revert to URLLC levels observed before. Collision avoidance and navigation commands require timely delivery but not high throughput. Under worst-case assumptions the UAV must avoid altitude corrections that could drift outside 10.0 meters due to delayed control. Each slice choice carries regret either from latency risk or from capacity stress if conditions degrade again. The feasibility decision must minimize maximum regret over the next two turns rather than optimize the current snapshot. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Remain on mMTC since the edge load is only 0.18 and throughput needs are low, accepting 50 ms latency for the next two turns.
options.B: Switch immediately to URLLC as used in turns 8 to 10 with latency between 5 and 9 ms and edge load up to 0.32 to protect altitude control.
options.C: Switch to eMBB because it previously delivered up to 780 Mbps throughput and can handle control and monitoring together despite 45 ms latency.
options.D: Defer any slice change for one turn to observe whether mMTC jitter of 20 ms reduces, then decide before the following turn.

records.question: The mission began with navigation and sensing under icing weather with the UAV at altitude 25.0 m, speed 15.0 mps, and battery at 100.0 percent. Early turns used eMBB with latency 12 to 14 ms, jitter 2 to 3 ms, loss 0.1 to 0.2 percent, and edge load rising from 0.35 to 0.4. Mid-mission the agent switched to URLLC for collision avoidance and waypoint execution with latency between 7 and 9 ms, jitter 1.0 to 1.5 ms, and edge load up to 0.32. At turn 6 the user requested real time video and the slice reverted to eMBB with latency 25 ms, jitter 8 ms, loss 0.5 percent, throughput 780 Mbps, and edge load 0.65. At turn 7 the agent adapted video but latency worsened to 45 ms, jitter 15 ms, loss 2.1 percent, throughput 320 Mbps, and edge load 0.85. The stated mission intent earlier emphasized safe navigation and payload delivery rather than persistent video streaming. Over the next two turns the user then aborted video and prepared for payload drop, returning to URLLC with latency 6 ms and edge load 0.3. Considering worst case network conditions observed so far as a bound on uncertainty, the system must decide whether an intent drift occurred that could jeopardize future actions. A myopic interpretation would focus only on the recovery after video abort, while a longer horizon must consider regret if high load recurs. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Flag intent drift at turn 6 to 7 because the switch back to eMBB caused worst case latency 45 ms and edge load 0.85 that contradict the earlier navigation focused intent over the next two turns.
options.B: Do not flag intent drift because URLLC metrics at turn 8 show latency 6 ms and edge load 0.3 which restores compliance in the immediate next turn.
options.C: Flag intent drift only if battery drops below 100.0 percent or altitude exceeds 120.0 m, since mission parameters stayed constant despite network changes.
options.D: Defer drift detection until turn 11 because mMTC latency 50 ms and jitter 20 ms indicate a clearer intent change after return is initiated.

records.question: At turn 7 the swarm experiences contention while transitioning from video streaming to safety critical coordination. Recent telemetry shows URLLC latency observed at 5 ms, 6 ms, 7 ms, and 9 ms across turns 3, 8, 10, and 5, while eMBB latency rose from 25 ms to 45 ms between turns 6 and 7. Edge load on eMBB increased from 0.65 to 0.85 over one turn, while URLLC edge load varied between 0.25 and 0.32. Jitter on eMBB climbed from 8 ms to 15 ms, and loss rose from 0.5 pct to 2.1 pct, while URLLC jitter stayed between 0.5 ms and 1.5 ms with loss between 0.01 pct and 0.07 pct. The radar is offline and collision avoidance depends on timely lidar fusion messages shared among swarm members. Battery remains at 100 pct, speed is 15 mps, and altitude 25 m is within the 10 to 120 m policy bounds. The operator plans coordinated return maneuvers over the next two turns, requiring fair access for peers and avoidance of worst case congestion. If degradation persists one more turn, eMBB metrics may worsen further while URLLC remains variable within its observed range. Each slice choice trades immediate throughput against multi turn safety and fairness. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Keep eMBB for all swarm traffic because throughput is still 320 mbps at turn 7 and battery and altitude margins are ample.
options.B: Switch all swarm members to URLLC because latency has been as low as 5 ms and loss as low as 0.01 pct in recent turns.
options.C: Allocate URLLC only for collision avoidance and coordination while throttling eMBB to non swarm video given edge load already reached 0.85.
options.D: Move swarm traffic to mMTC since edge load there was only 0.18 at turn 11 and latency was acceptable earlier.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV is operating in icing conditions with wind at 6.0 mps while flying at 25.0 m altitude inside policy alt bounds of 10.0 to 120.0. The network has shifted to eMBB with latency at 45 ms, jitter at 15 ms, loss at 2.1 percent, throughput at 320 Mbps, and edge load at 0.85. Earlier at turn 6 the same slice showed latency at 25 ms, jitter at 8 ms, loss at 0.5 percent, throughput at 780 Mbps, and edge load at 0.65, indicating rapid degradation. The video stream was already reduced once, but autonomy still relies on timely edge inference for navigation because radar is offline. Historical URLLC turns showed latency between 5 and 9 ms with edge load between 0.25 and 0.32, but there is uncertainty whether that recovery will persist if load remains high. If degradation persists for one to two more turns, delayed control could cause altitude oscillations that risk breaching the 10.0 m lower bound during descent corrections. A graceful degradation choice must reduce autonomy before such a violation while considering that switching slices or autonomy modes has its own cost. One option optimizes current video quality, another narrowly meets present metrics, another ignores worst case uncertainty, and another reduces autonomy despite reduced throughput. Considering worst case latency and loss over the next two turns and minimizing maximum regret, which option should be selected?

options.A: Maintain current autonomy and keep reduced video on eMBB since throughput is still 320 Mbps and altitude is safely between 10.0 and 120.0 m.
options.B: Further lower video bitrate on eMBB to push edge load below the earlier 0.65 level while keeping full autonomy despite 45 ms latency.
options.C: Immediately switch back to URLLC and maintain full autonomy assuming latency returns to the prior 7 to 9 ms range.
options.D: Reduce autonomy level to a safer mode and pause nonessential streaming, accepting URLLC throughput near 95 to 115 Mbps to stabilize control.

records.question: At turn 11 the UAV is returning with battery at 100 percent, speed 15.0 mps, altitude 25.0 m, and icing conditions with 6.0 mps wind. Network telemetry has shifted to mMTC with latency 50 ms, jitter 20 ms, loss 1.8 percent, throughput 1.2 Mbps, and edge load 0.18. Earlier in the same flight the network experienced eMBB degradation with latency 45 ms, jitter 15 ms, loss 2.1 percent, and edge load peaking at 0.85. URLLC performance across turns showed latency between 5 and 9 ms, jitter between 0.5 and 1.5 ms, loss between 0.01 and 0.07 percent, and edge load between 0.25 and 0.32. The policy altitude bounds are 10.0 to 120.0 m and the current altitude margin is therefore limited but compliant. Assume worst case that icing persists and network conditions revert for one more turn to the highest previously observed loss and edge load. Also assume autonomy must remain safe even if throughput drops to the minimum previously observed value. records.question: At turn 6 the system must decide which network telemetry to expose to a Retrieval-Augmented Generation prompt while the link degrades. Across turns 1 to 6 observed latency ranges from 3.2 to 100.0 ms and jitter ranges from 0.5 to 15.0 ms depending on slice. Throughput varies between 1.0 and 120 Mbps and edge load rises as high as 0.9 on the mMTC slice. Loss also varies from 0.0 to 5.0 percent over the same horizon. The agent expects the next one to three turns to alternate between URLLC and mMTC as previously observed rather than stabilizing immediately. Exposing more telemetry improves reasoning quality but increases prompt size and processing time on high edge load. Exposing less telemetry reduces latency risk but may cause incorrect future decisions during return to base. A worst case must assume the highest observed latency, jitter, loss, and edge load persist for another turn. Considering regret over the next three turns rather than only the current turn, which augmentation option should be selected?

options.A: Expose full per-turn telemetry including latency, jitter, loss, throughput, and edge load from all slices, accepting up to 100.0 ms latency and 0.9 edge load for maximal context.
options.B: Expose only URLLC telemetry with latency between 3.0 and 6.0 ms and loss below 0.3 percent, ignoring mMTC conditions seen at 100.0 ms and 5.0 percent loss.
options.C: Expose aggregated ranges for latency from 3.2 to 100.0 ms and jitter from 0.5 to 15.0 ms plus current edge load up to 0.9, omitting raw per-slice throughput values of 1.0 to 120 Mbps.
options.D: Expose minimal status flags and current throughput only, relying on values from 40 to 70 Mbps and excluding latency and loss metrics.

records.question: The UAV is currently operating under URLCC slice with 9ms latency, 1.2ms jitter, 0.03% loss, 150Mbps throughput, and 0.35 edge load after recovering from mMTC degradation. The mission requires inference with 12ms SLA latency and 0.1% max loss. Onboard inference consumes 15W and adds 2ms processing delay. Edge inference under current URLLC has 9ms network latency but may degrade to 15ms with 0.1% loss in next turn due to edge load rising to 0.45. If the UAV continues at 18m/s, it will reach the next waypoint in 3 turns. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Use onboard inference: adds 2ms delay but avoids network risk; total latency 2ms, within 12ms SLA; battery drain 15W over 3 turns.
options.B: Use edge inference now: 9ms latency, 0.03% loss, within SLA; but next turn may hit 15ms latency and 0.1% loss, violating SLA.
options.C: Switch to eMBB: 12ms latency, 0.1% loss, exactly at SLA boundary; edge load 0.6 may cause 18ms latency next turn.
options.D: Wait for edge load to drop: current edge load 0.35 may fall to 0.25 in 2 turns, reducing latency to 6ms; but mission delay risks collision.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV experiences severe network degradation with mMTC slice latency at 120ms, jitter at 25ms, packet loss at 5.0%, and edge load at 0.85, while the SLA mandates latency under 50ms and loss under 1.0%. The UAV is 1.2km from goal, traveling at 18m/s, with battery at 82% and thermal sensor offline. If edge load increases by 0.03 per turn under current conditions, and URLLC slice offers 9ms latency with 0.03% loss but only 150Mbps throughput, while eMBB offers 15ms latency with 0.5% loss and 700Mbps throughput but edge load already at 0.6, which option should be selected to avoid SLA violation over the next two turns while minimizing regret?

options.A: Switch to URLLC immediately; latency and loss meet SLA, and edge load drops to 0.35, though throughput is limited to 150Mbps.
options.B: Stay on mMTC and reduce speed to 9m/s to lower edge load by 0.05 per turn; latency remains 120ms, violating SLA now and next turn.
options.C: Switch to eMBB; latency 15ms and loss 0.5% are within SLA, but edge load will reach 0.66 next turn and 0.69 in two turns, risking overload.
options.D: Initiate fail-safe and hover; edge load drops to 0.2, latency drops to 10ms, but mission delay incurs 120s penalty and battery drains 5% per minute.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV experiences severe network degradation with mMTC slice latency at 120 ms, jitter at 25 ms, packet loss at 5.0%, and edge load at 0.85, while policy mandates sub-50 ms latency for safety-critical control. The UAV is 1.2 km from goal, moving at 18 m/s, with 100% battery and thermal sensor offline. Switching to URLLC slice reduces latency to 9 ms but caps throughput at 150 Mbps, insufficient for full sensor fusion. Continuing on mMTC risks control failure, while switching may delay mission completion by 2 turns due to reinitialization. If edge load exceeds 0.9 next turn, offloading becomes unreliable. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Switch to URLLC immediately despite throughput limit, accepting 2-turn delay to ensure sub-50 ms latency compliance and avoid control failure.
options.B: Remain on mMTC for one more turn to complete sensor fusion, accepting 5.0% packet loss and 120 ms latency, then switch if edge load stays below 0.9.
options.C: Switch to eMBB for higher throughput (850 Mbps) despite 15 ms latency, assuming jitter and loss will improve in next turn based on historical trend.
options.D: Initiate fail-safe landing immediately, abandoning mission, to eliminate all network risk and preserve UAV integrity under hail conditions.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is operating under hail with wind at 8.5 m/s, and telemetry reveals network degradation: latency spiked to 120 ms, jitter at 25 ms, packet loss at 5.0%, throughput collapsed to 1.2 Mbps, and edge load reached 0.85. The SLA mandates latency under 20 ms, jitter under 5 ms, loss under 1%, and throughput above 10 Mbps for mission-critical control. Historical data shows that mMTC slice degradation persists for 2–4 turns unless manually switched, and edge load above 0.8 risks cascading failure. If the UAV continues on mMTC for one more turn, projected latency could hit 150 ms with 7% loss, violating SLA by 7.5x. Switching to URLLC now guarantees latency under 10 ms and loss under 0.05%, but reduces throughput to 150 Mbps, which may delay payload processing by 1.5 turns. Continuing on mMTC risks immediate SLA breach and potential mission abort, while switching incurs throughput penalty but preserves control integrity. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue on mMTC for one more turn; historical recovery suggests degradation may reverse by turn 9 with 60% probability.
options.B: Switch to URLLC immediately; guarantees SLA compliance for control with throughput 150 Mbps, accepting 1.5-turn payload delay.
options.C: Switch to eMBB; offers 800 Mbps throughput but latency 15 ms and loss 0.5%, risking SLA violation if jitter spikes to 6 ms next turn.
options.D: Initiate fail-safe and land immediately; avoids SLA violation but forfeits mission completion and incurs 3-turn operational cost.

records.question: The UAV is operating under hail with wind at 8.5 m/s and has just switched from mMTC to URLLC after experiencing 130 ms latency and 6% packet loss. Current edge load is 0.35, and URLLC offers 150 Mbps throughput with 9 ms latency. A third-party request arrives to offload compute for a swarm coordination task requiring 120 Mbps sustained throughput and 10 ms max latency over the next 3 turns. The edge load is projected to increase by 0.08 per turn if the request is accepted. The SLA mandates latency under 15 ms and throughput above 100 Mbps. One option risks exceeding latency SLA by turn 11 under worst-case jitter growth of 0.5 ms/turn. Another option accepts the request but caps throughput at 110 Mbps to preserve margin. A third option rejects the request to maintain current 140 Mbps throughput and 8 ms latency. The fourth option accepts but throttles to 100 Mbps to guarantee SLA under worst-case jitter. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Accept request with no throttling; current 150 Mbps and 9 ms latency exceeds SLA margin and supports 120 Mbps requirement.
options.B: Accept request but throttle to 110 Mbps to preserve 40 Mbps buffer against edge load growth and jitter uncertainty.
options.C: Reject request to maintain 140 Mbps throughput and 8 ms latency, avoiding any risk of SLA violation over next 3 turns.
options.D: Accept request but throttle to 100 Mbps to guarantee SLA under worst-case jitter growth of 0.5 ms/turn and edge load increase to 0.59 by turn 11.

records.question: At turn 9, the UAV has just switched from mMTC to URLLC after experiencing 130ms latency and 6% packet loss, with edge load at 0.88. The mission requires telemetry augmentation for RAG within 10ms latency and under 0.1% loss, while maintaining edge load below 0.4. URLLC currently shows 9ms latency, 0.03% loss, and 0.35 edge load, but throughput is only 150Mbps. eMBB offers 850Mbps throughput but 15ms latency and 0.5% loss at 0.6 edge load. mMTC is degraded and unusable. If wind speed increases by 20% next turn, URLLC latency may rise to 12ms and loss to 0.05%, while eMBB latency may jump to 20ms and loss to 1.0%. Which network slice should be selected for RAG augmentation to ensure compliance over the next two turns under worst-case wind escalation?

options.A: URLLC: meets current SLA with 9ms latency and 0.03% loss, edge load 0.35, and projected worst-case 12ms latency and 0.05% loss next turn.
options.B: eMBB: higher throughput (850Mbps) supports richer RAG context, current latency 15ms exceeds SLA but may be acceptable if loss stays below 0.5%.
options.C: mMTC: currently degraded with 130ms latency and 6% loss, but may recover if wind stabilizes; edge load 0.88 exceeds policy limit.
options.D: Hybrid: split RAG queries between URLLC for control and eMBB for data, assuming 50% load per slice; URLLC handles 12ms worst-case, eMBB 20ms.

records.question: At turn 9, the agent reestablishes a reliable link by switching to URLLC with latency 9ms, jitter 1.2ms, loss 0.03%, throughput 150Mbps, and edge load 0.35. The mission requires continuous identity validation every 3 turns with a SLA of max 10ms latency and 0.1% loss. Historical data shows edge load increases by 0.05 per turn under URLLC during active flight. The next identity validation is due at turn 12. If the agent continues using URLLC, projected edge load at turn 12 will be 0.50, exceeding the safe threshold of 0.45. Switching to eMBB at turn 10 would yield 140Mbps throughput and 0.33 edge load but with 8ms latency and 0.02% loss, risking SLA violation if jitter spikes to 3ms. mMTC offers 1.0Mbps and 0.88 edge load but violates SLA by 120ms latency. Which option should be selected to ensure identity validation compliance across turns 10–12 while minimizing maximum regret under worst-case jitter and edge load growth?

options.A: Continue URLLC: latency 9ms, jitter 1.2ms, loss 0.03%, edge load 0.35 — projected edge load 0.50 at turn 12, exceeding safe threshold 0.45.
options.B: Switch to eMBB: latency 8ms, jitter 2ms (mean), loss 0.02%, edge load 0.33 — risk of 11ms latency under worst-case jitter 3ms, violating SLA.
options.C: Switch to mMTC: latency 130ms, loss 6.0%, edge load 0.88 — violates SLA by 120ms and 5.9% loss, unacceptable for identity validation.
options.D: Maintain current slice until turn 11, then switch to eMBB: edge load grows to 0.40 at turn 11, then drops to 0.33 at turn 12 — but jitter may spike to 3ms at turn 12, risking 11ms latency.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV experiences severe network degradation with mMTC slice latency at 120ms, jitter at 25ms, loss at 5.0%, throughput at 1.2Mbps, and edge load at 0.85. The mission requires federated model updates every 3 turns with a latency SLA of 20ms and minimum throughput of 5Mbps. The next update is due in 1 turn, and the UAV has 100% battery but thermal and radar sensors are offline. The edge load is projected to increase by 0.03 per turn if no action is taken. Under worst-case jitter and loss, the effective throughput drops by 40%. Option A schedules the update now over mMTC with 100% risk of SLA violation. Option B delays the update by 2 turns, risking model staleness but allowing edge load to peak at 0.91. Option C switches to URLLC now, which has 9ms latency and 150Mbps throughput but only 0.35 edge load, though it may not sustain the load if another UAV joins. Option D initiates local model caching and defers federated sync until turn 10, accepting 3-turn staleness but guaranteeing no SLA breach. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Schedule federated update immediately over mMTC despite SLA violation risk.
options.B: Delay update by 2 turns to allow edge load to stabilize, accepting 0.91 peak load.
options.C: Switch to URLLC slice now and proceed with update, assuming no additional UAV load.
options.D: Cache locally and defer sync until turn 10, accepting 3-turn model staleness.

records.question: At turn 9, the UAV has just switched from mMTC to URLLC after experiencing 130ms latency and 6% packet loss, with edge load at 0.88. The mission requires coordination with a third-party swarm agent that demands 95% reliability over the next 2 turns, but URLLC offers only 150 Mbps throughput and 0.03% loss. The swarm agent’s SLA permits up to 10ms latency but requires 200 Mbps for full telemetry. Historical data shows URLLC degrades to 120 Mbps and 0.05% loss under sustained load. eMBB offers 850 Mbps but 15ms latency and 0.5% loss, which violates the SLA. If the swarm agent is untrusted and may exfiltrate data, and the UAV’s battery will drop to 70% by turn 11, which exposure level should be selected to minimize regret under worst-case network degradation and trust risk? A) Full API and telemetry exposure over URLLC with 150 Mbps cap. B) Partial telemetry over URLLC with 100 Mbps reserved for control, accepting 0.05% loss. C) Full exposure over eMBB despite 15ms latency, assuming swarm agent is trustworthy. D) No exposure, abort coordination, and land immediately with 70% battery remaining.

options.A: Full API and telemetry exposure over URLLC with 150 Mbps cap.
options.B: Partial telemetry over URLLC with 100 Mbps reserved for control, accepting 0.05% loss.
options.C: Full exposure over eMBB despite 15ms latency, assuming swarm agent is trustworthy.
options.D: No exposure, abort coordination, and land immediately with 70% battery remaining.

records.question: At turn 8, the network slice is mMTC with latency 130ms, jitter 30ms, packet loss 6.0%, throughput 1.0Mbps, and edge load 0.88, exceeding SLA thresholds for mission-critical control. The UAV is at 10m altitude, battery 100%, and speed 18m/s, with thermal and radar sensors offline. A fail-safe is engaged, but the next 2 turns may see continued degradation or partial recovery. Option A switches to URLLC immediately, accepting 150Mbps throughput but risking edge load increase to 0.4 under worst-case jitter. Option B remains on mMTC with a 20% chance of recovery to 100ms latency next turn, but if degradation persists, latency may hit 160ms by turn 10. Option C switches to eMBB, offering 800Mbps throughput but latency 18ms and jitter 6ms, which violates control SLA if jitter exceeds 5ms. Option D initiates emergency landing now, sacrificing mission completion but guaranteeing safety with zero network dependency. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Switch to URLLC immediately, accepting 150Mbps throughput and projected edge load 0.4 under worst-case jitter.
options.B: Remain on mMTC with 20% recovery chance; if degradation persists, latency may reach 160ms by turn 10.
options.C: Switch to eMBB, accepting 18ms latency and 6ms jitter, which violates control SLA if jitter exceeds 5ms.
options.D: Initiate emergency landing now, sacrificing mission completion but guaranteeing safety with zero network dependency.

records.question: At turn 8 the UAV is executing a survey pattern inside a geofence with altitude bounds of 10.0 to 150.0 while flying at 22.0 mps and battery at 100.0 percent. Network telemetry over recent turns shows latency values of 25 ms and 28 ms on eMBB with jitter rising from 8 ms to 10 ms and loss_pct increasing from 2.0 to 3.5. Edge_load has climbed from 0.85 to 0.9 on eMBB while throughput has dropped from 400 Mbps to 300 Mbps. Earlier URLLC operation showed latency values of 7 ms to 9 ms with jitter at or below 1.5 ms and loss_pct no higher than 0.03 but throughput only between 90 and 110 Mbps. The mission intent assumes continued image capture while remaining within the same altitude band and geofence for at least the next two turns. Wind is steady at 18.0 mps with thermal updrafts, implying control traffic sensitivity if packet loss spikes. If degradation persists one more turn, the worst observed latency and loss values must be assumed rather than the mean. Switching slices or aborting now both incur regret because data quality or mission completion is affected. A single turn view favors higher throughput, but a two turn view must consider edge_load saturation risk. Which option should be selected to make the intent feasible with minimum worst case regret over the next two turns?

options.A: Continue on eMBB at 300 Mbps despite 28 ms latency and 3.5 loss_pct to maximize survey data this turn.
options.B: Immediately switch to URLLC with 90 to 110 Mbps throughput accepting lower data rate but latency near 7 ms and edge_load around 0.35.
options.C: Descend toward the 10.0 m altitude bound to reduce wind impact while staying on eMBB at 0.9 edge_load.
options.D: Abort the survey and initiate return to base now using URLLC with 5 to 6 ms latency and 0.3 edge_load.

records.question: At turn 8 the UAV is executing a survey mission inside a geofence while network conditions have degraded on the eMBB slice. Telemetry shows latency rising from 25 ms at turn 7 to 28 ms at turn 8 with jitter increasing from 8 ms to 10 ms and loss reaching 3.5 percent. Throughput has fallen from 400 Mbps to 300 Mbps while edge load has increased from 0.85 to 0.9. The mission intent is to continue image capture, but network policy favors stable control and telemetry delivery. The UAV speed remains 22 mps and battery is at 100 percent, so energy is not the immediate constraint. The airspace and policy altitude bounds remain 10 to 150 m and are not violated. Historical behavior shows that degradation persisted for at least one full turn before recovery in earlier phases. If degradation persists for one or two more turns, worst case jitter can be assumed anywhere between 8 ms and 10 ms with loss up to 3.5 percent. Switching slices reduces throughput to around 90 Mbps but lowers latency to about 6 ms and edge load to about 0.35. Which option should be selected to minimize worst case regret over the next two turns?

options.A: Continue the survey on eMBB because 300 Mbps throughput exceeds prior 100 Mbps levels and battery is 100 percent despite 28 ms latency and 0.9 edge load.
options.B: Pause the survey and switch to URLLC because latency drops to about 6 ms with jitter around 0.5 ms and edge load near 0.35 even though throughput falls to about 90 Mbps.
options.C: Continue the survey for one more turn on eMBB assuming jitter stabilizes near 8 ms and loss remains below 3.5 percent.
options.D: Abort the mission immediately and return to base using URLLC because loss is 3.5 percent and speed is 22 mps.

records.question: At turn 9, the agent has just switched from eMBB to URLLC after degradation during survey execution. Recent telemetry shows latency moved from 25 ms with jitter 8 ms and loss 2.0 percent at turn 7 to latency 28 ms with jitter 10 ms and loss 3.5 percent at turn 8, then down to latency 6 ms with jitter 0.5 ms and loss 0.01 percent at turn 9. Throughput simultaneously dropped from 400 Mbps to 300 Mbps while edge load rose from 0.85 to 0.9 before falling to 0.35 on URLLC. The mission intent before turn 8 was to execute a survey pattern inside the geofence while maintaining altitude between 10.0 and 150.0 m. A new user request to return to base arrives at turn 10, but intent drift detection must decide earlier whether behavior already shifted due to network adaptation rather than explicit mission change. Assume jitter could remain anywhere between 0.5 ms and 10 ms for the next two turns and edge load could rebound up to 0.9 if URLLC demand spikes. If survey execution continues for two more turns under worst case network conditions, image capture depends on throughput above 300 Mbps which was only met on eMBB. If return preparation begins one turn early, survey coverage is lost but network risk is reduced. A myopic single turn view favors the improved 6 ms latency, but a multi turn view must weigh regret if degradation recurs and intent silently changes from survey to safe return. Which option should be selected to best detect intent drift while minimizing worst case regret over the next two turns?

options.A: Defer drift detection and treat the 6 ms latency and 0.35 edge load on URLLC as confirmation that survey intent remains unchanged.
options.B: Flag probable intent drift at turn 9 because the switch from 400 Mbps to 90–110 Mbps throughput implies preparatory behavior for return despite lower latency.
options.C: Wait one more turn for confirmation since current loss is only 0.01 percent and jitter may stay near 0.5 ms.
options.D: Assume no drift until the explicit return command at turn 10 because altitude and geofence constraints are still satisfied.

records.question: At turn 8 the UAV is executing a survey with eMBB while network metrics have degraded over the last two turns. Latency rose from 25 ms to 28 ms and jitter from 8 ms to 10 ms while loss increased from 2.0 pct to 3.5 pct. Throughput simultaneously dropped from 400 Mbps to 300 Mbps and edge load climbed from 0.85 to 0.9. In earlier turns URLLC showed latency between 6 and 9 ms with throughput between 90 and 110 Mbps and edge load between 0.35 and 0.42. The survey is expected to continue for at least two more turns before return to base. Battery remains at 100 pct so endurance is not the immediate constraint. Network behavior is uncertain because the last two turns show a worsening trend that could persist one more turn. Switching slices itself consumes one turn and may face capacity limits if edge load spikes. If the degradation persists into the next two turns which option minimizes maximum regret across these futures. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Remain on eMBB despite current 28 ms latency and 0.9 edge load, accepting possible further degradation next turn.
options.B: Switch immediately to URLLC with 6 to 9 ms latency but accept 90 to 110 Mbps throughput limits under a 0.35 to 0.42 edge load.
options.C: Delay the decision for one turn on eMBB to see if metrics recover, then switch if latency exceeds the current 28 ms.
options.D: Switch to URLLC now because loss of 3.5 pct on eMBB exceeds the recent 0.01 to 0.03 pct seen earlier.

records.question: At turn 9 the swarm has just switched one UAV to URLLC with latency 6 ms, jitter 0.5 ms, loss 0.01 percent, throughput 90 Mbps, and edge load 0.35. In the prior two turns the same UAV on eMBB saw latency rise from 25 ms to 28 ms, jitter from 8 ms to 10 ms, loss from 2.0 percent to 3.5 percent, throughput fall from 400 Mbps to 300 Mbps, and edge load increase from 0.85 to 0.9. Other swarm members are still surveying and depend on eMBB capacity while operating within the policy altitude bounds of 10 to 150 m under 18 mps wind. The mission plan requires another two turns of coordination before return to base is executed. URLLC offers lower latency but much lower throughput than eMBB, and its edge load has previously increased to 0.42 when multiple agents used it. Assume the worst case that eMBB degradation persists for one more turn and URLLC edge load rebounds to its recent high. Safety requires collision avoidance and command links to stay reliable, while fairness requires not starving the rest of the swarm. A single turn decision that looks optimal may increase regret over the next two turns if contention worsens. No option avoids some downside in the next three turns. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Keep this UAV on URLLC at 90 to 100 Mbps to guarantee low latency even if edge load returns toward 0.42, accepting reduced throughput for the swarm over the next two turns.
options.B: Switch this UAV back to eMBB at 300 to 400 Mbps to restore fairness now despite 28 ms latency and 3.5 percent loss if edge load stays near 0.9.
options.C: Alternate slices every turn, using URLLC on odd turns and eMBB on even turns to average latency and throughput across the next two turns.
options.D: Keep URLLC for one more turn and then force all swarm members onto eMBB assuming edge load will drop below 0.6.

records.question: At turn 8 the UAV is executing a survey at 22.0 mps with battery at 100.0 percent inside an altitude policy band of 10.0 to 150.0 meters. Network telemetry on eMBB shows latency of 28 ms, jitter of 10 ms, loss of 3.5 percent, throughput of 300 Mbps, and edge load of 0.9. In earlier turns eMBB latency rose from 25 ms with jitter 8 ms and loss 2.0 percent, indicating a worsening trend. A fallback to URLLC previously delivered latency between 6 and 9 ms with jitter between 0.5 and 1.5 ms but throughput between 90 and 110 Mbps. The mission plan requires continuous image capture, and losing images for two consecutive turns would invalidate coverage even if the UAV remains airborne. Wind is 18.0 mps from 270 degrees, so holding heading corrections over multiple turns is expected. The operator asks whether to continue the mission rather than return to base, assuming the next two turns could resemble the worst observed conditions so far. Continuing on eMBB risks further congestion if edge load stays near 0.9, while switching slices risks insufficient throughput for imagery. Returning now guarantees mission failure but avoids further degradation. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue on eMBB because 300 Mbps throughput still exceeds URLLC throughput and latency of 28 ms has not yet caused a failure.
options.B: Switch to URLLC and continue because latency near 6 to 9 ms and jitter below 1.5 ms reduce control risk despite throughput near 90 to 110 Mbps.
options.C: Continue on eMBB for one more turn and reassess because battery is 100.0 percent and altitude remains within 10.0 to 150.0 meters.
options.D: Abort the mission and return to base now because network loss has reached 3.5 percent and edge load is 0.9.

records.question: At turn 9 the agent has just switched the network slice to URLLC with latency 6 ms, jitter 0.5 ms, loss 0.01 pct, throughput 90 mbps, and edge load 0.35 after eMBB degraded to 28 ms latency, 10 ms jitter, 3.5 pct loss, 300 mbps throughput, and 0.9 edge load at turn 8. The UAV is flying at 22.0 mps within altitude bounds 10.0 to 150.0 with battery at 100.0 pct and the survey mission was started at turn 7. The return to base request arrives at turn 10 using the same URLLC slice with latency 5 ms and throughput 100 mbps. Replanning must avoid contradicting the turn 9 adaptation if degradation persists for one to three more turns. The policy does not mandate throughput but requires reliable control within altitude bounds. Assume worst case that eMBB metrics remain at turn 8 levels for the next two turns and URLLC edge load can rise back to 0.4 as seen at turn 3. Any choice incurs regret because URLLC limits data and eMBB risks control loss. A single turn view would favor higher throughput, but multi turn consistency penalizes oscillation. Which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next three turns?

options.A: Immediately switch back to eMBB to regain 300 mbps throughput despite 28 ms latency and 3.5 pct loss.
options.B: Stay on URLLC for the return despite 90 to 100 mbps throughput and possible edge load increase to 0.4.
options.C: Alternate slices each turn to balance 6 ms latency now and 300 mbps later.
options.D: Delay the return one turn on eMBB assuming edge load drops from 0.9 to 0.6.

records.question: At turn 9 the operator considers exposing onboard edge compute to third parties during return operations. Recent telemetry shows edge_load rose from 0.6 at turn 6 to 0.85 at turn 7 and 0.9 at turn 8 on eMBB, then dropped to 0.35 after switching to URLLC. Latency peaked at 28 ms with jitter 10 ms and loss 3.5 percent on eMBB, while URLLC stabilized at 6 ms latency with 0.5 ms jitter and 0.01 percent loss. Throughput concurrently fell from 300 to 90 Mbps after the slice switch. Battery remains at 100 percent but the mission is ending with return and land expected within the next two turns. Third parties request short term compute bursts that would increase edge_load by an estimated fraction of current usage without guarantees of release timing. If degradation persists for one more turn, eMBB conditions could repeat while URLLC capacity remains limited. The operator must choose an exposure and allocation policy that minimizes worst case regret over the next one to three turns. All options reduce some risk but impose opportunity cost or service degradation. Under these constraints and uncertainties, which option should be selected?

options.A: Expose full compute on URLLC now because latency is 6 ms and edge_load is only 0.35, accepting the 90 Mbps throughput limit.
options.B: Expose compute only on eMBB at current conditions since throughput is higher at 300 Mbps despite recent edge_load of 0.9.
options.C: Defer all third party exposure until landing, keeping current URLLC metrics of 6 ms latency and 0.35 edge_load unchanged.
options.D: Expose a capped fraction of compute on URLLC sized to keep projected edge_load below the earlier 0.6 level observed at turn 6.

records.question: At turn 8 the UAV is executing a survey while network conditions have degraded on eMBB with latency 28 ms, jitter 10 ms, loss 3.5 percent, throughput 300 Mbps, and edge load 0.9. Earlier in the mission eMBB latency ranged from 10 ms to 28 ms and jitter ranged from 1 ms to 10 ms, while URLLC showed latency from 4 ms to 9 ms and throughput from 90 Mbps to 110 Mbps. The UAV speed is 22 mps, altitude is within 20 m to 150 m, and battery is at 100 percent so energy cost is secondary to timing risk. The perception model can run on device with no network delay but reduced accuracy, or be offloaded to edge over URLLC or eMBB, or to cloud over eMBB only. If degradation persists for the next two turns, edge load is expected to remain near 0.85 to 0.9 on eMBB but around 0.35 on URLLC based on the previous switch. Worst case end to end latency must consider latency plus jitter rather than mean values. A single turn view favors eMBB offload due to 300 Mbps throughput, but multi turn regret depends on loss accumulation and edge saturation. URLLC has lower throughput but much lower and more stable latency and loss across observed turns. On device inference avoids network loss but consumes time that increases with speed induced motion blur during the survey. Considering the next one to three turns and worst case network conditions, which option should be selected?

options.A: Offload to cloud over eMBB now since 300 Mbps throughput can absorb the model and current 28 ms latency is acceptable this turn.
options.B: Offload to edge over URLLC despite 90 to 110 Mbps throughput because latency stays between 4 ms and 9 ms with loss near 0.01 percent and lower edge load.
options.C: Keep inference on device to avoid 3.5 percent packet loss and jitter up to 10 ms even though accuracy drops at 22 mps.
options.D: Delay inference one turn hoping eMBB recovers toward earlier 10 ms latency and 1 ms jitter while edge load falls from 0.9.

records.question: At turn 8 the survey agent reports network degradation while executing a mission with battery at 100.0 percent and speed 22.0 mps. Recent telemetry shows eMBB latency rising from 25 to 28 ms with jitter observed at 8 to 10 ms and loss increasing from 2.0 to 3.5 percent while edge_load climbed from 0.85 to 0.9. Earlier turns showed URLLC latency between 4 and 9 ms with jitter between 0.3 and 1.5 ms and edge_load between 0.25 and 0.42 but throughput only 90 to 110 Mbps. The operator policy enforces altitude bounds of 10.0 to 150.0 which the agent currently satisfies, so lifecycle choice is driven by compute and network risk rather than flight safety. The next two turns may either repeat eMBB congestion at edge_load 0.9 or revert to URLLC conditions at edge_load 0.35 as seen at turn 9. Instantiating a parallel processing agent increases edge_load by 0.1 next turn, while migrating the agent to URLLC reduces edge_load by 0.5 but caps throughput at 100 Mbps. Retiring the agent ends data capture immediately but avoids any further network exposure over the next two turns. Keeping the agent unchanged assumes mean conditions and risks another eMBB turn with jitter near 10 ms. Under worst case assumptions the decision must minimize maximum regret over the next two turns rather than optimize the current snapshot. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Instantiate a parallel agent on eMBB accepting edge_load rising from 0.9 to 1.0 to preserve 300 Mbps throughput this turn.
options.B: Migrate the agent to URLLC with expected latency near 6 ms and throughput capped at 100 Mbps while reducing edge_load toward 0.35.
options.C: Retire the agent immediately to eliminate exposure to 28 ms latency and 3.5 percent loss at the cost of zero throughput.
options.D: Keep the agent unchanged on eMBB assuming jitter returns from 10 ms to the earlier 8 ms level.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV is executing the mission in icing weather with wind 7.5 mps while flying at speed 45.0 mps and altitude 40.0 within policy bounds of 30.0 to 300.0. The battery is still at 100.0 percent but lidar is offline, increasing reliance on networked coordination. Network telemetry has shifted from eMBB at latency 30 and jitter 10 in turn 6 to mMTC at latency 60 and jitter 25 with loss 2.1 and edge load 0.92 in turn 7. Earlier URLLC turns showed latency between 5 and 8 with edge load between 0.3 and 0.5. The user intent implies continuing area coverage and collision avoidance coordination for at least one to three more turns before return. If the edge load trend from 0.78 to 0.92 persists one more turn, congestion risk increases even if latency briefly improves. If the network instead recovers to URLLC characteristics, capacity limits may still bind during swarm coordination. All options violate at least one constraint either in altitude margin, sensing robustness, or network stability over the next turns. The decision must minimize worst case regret if degradation persists and collision avoidance remains active. Assume policy altitude bounds are strict and cannot be violated under any contingency. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue on URLLC immediately because latency 8 and loss 0.05 in turn 8 are lower than mMTC and keep speed at 45.0 within altitude 40.0.
options.B: Stay on mMTC for coordination because throughput 0.8 and edge load 0.92 already reflect worst congestion and altitude 40.0 is policy compliant.
options.C: Delay coordination and switch back to eMBB since throughput 100 to 120 supports sensing while accepting latency 25 to 30 and edge load up to 0.78.
options.D: Proceed with URLLC but throttle coordination frequency anticipating edge load returning toward 0.5 while maintaining altitude between 30.0 and 300.0.

records.question: The mission begins with a safety focused flight under icing conditions while maintaining stable URLLC connectivity at 5 to 7 ms latency and edge load near 0.3 to 0.4. Over subsequent turns the network slice alternates across eMBB and mMTC with latency rising to 25 ms and then 50 ms while edge load peaks at 0.85. At turn 7 the agent explicitly notes network degradation when mMTC latency reaches 60 ms with jitter 25 ms, loss 2.1 percent, throughput 0.8 Mbps, and edge load 0.92. Immediately after, the user switches back to collision avoidance and then requests return to base at turn 10 while URLLC metrics recover to 5 ms latency and 0.3 edge load. The altitude policy remains between 30.0 and 300.0 meters and the UAV speed stays at 45.0 mps with battery at 100.0 percent, so platform constraints do not force termination. The implicit intent can be either continued area coverage despite degradation or a subtle shift toward risk minimization and early termination. Because edge load has shown rapid swings between 0.3 and 0.92, a worst case assumption is that high load could recur in the next one to two turns. If high load recurs, coordination or imaging intents would again rely on mMTC or eMBB behavior rather than URLLC. A single turn view suggests recovery and normal completion, but a multi turn view must consider regret if congestion returns. Which option best identifies the correct moment and nature of intent drift to minimize worst case future regret?

options.A: No intent drift occurred because URLLC latency returned to 5 ms and edge load fell back to 0.3 by turn 10, indicating stable execution.
options.B: Intent drift begins at turn 4 when mMTC latency hits 50 ms and edge load 0.85, implying immediate abandonment of the original flight intent.
options.C: Intent drift emerges at turn 7 where degradation to 60 ms latency and 0.92 edge load shifts intent from area coverage toward conservative continuation under uncertainty.
options.D: Intent drift only occurs at turn 10 when return to base is commanded with URLLC metrics of 5 ms latency and 0.3 edge load.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV detects degradation while operating in icing weather with wind 7.5 mps and flying at speed 45.0 mps at altitude 40.0 within policy bounds 30.0 to 300.0. The current slice is mMTC with latency 60 ms, jitter 25 ms, loss 2.1 pct, throughput 0.8 mbps, and edge load 0.92. In earlier turns URLLC showed latency between 5 and 8 ms, jitter between 1 and 2 ms, loss between 0.01 and 0.05 pct, throughput between 45 and 55 mbps, and edge load between 0.3 and 0.5. eMBB previously showed latency 25 to 30 ms, jitter 8 to 10 ms, loss 0.5 to 0.8 pct, throughput 100 to 120 mbps, and edge load 0.7 to 0.78. A single turn improvement in throughput would help thermal imaging but increases control risk during collision avoidance. A myopic switch could look acceptable if only the current turn is considered. options.A: Switch immediately to eMBB to regain 100 to 120 mbps throughput despite latency of 25 to 30 ms and edge load up to 0.78.
options.B: Switch to URLLC and remain there even if edge load rises from 0.5 back toward 0.92 while accepting 45 to 55 mbps throughput.
options.C: Remain on mMTC because 0.8 mbps is sufficient and avoid any switching overhead despite 60 ms latency and 2.1 pct loss.
options.D: Delay a decision for one turn on mMTC to see if latency falls below 50 ms before switching.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV is flying at 45.0 mps at altitude 40.0 with battery at 100.0 while operating in icing and 7.5 mps wind. Maintaining current autonomy preserves throughput but risks abrupt failure if loss spikes again toward 2.1 pct. options.A: Maintain full autonomy at 45.0 mps because current URLLC shows 8 ms latency and 0.05 pct loss, accepting the prior 0.92 edge_load as transient.
options.B: Preemptively downgrade autonomy to a lower mode while holding altitude 40.0, accepting reduced mission performance to tolerate loss up to 2.1 pct if edge_load continues rising.

records.question: At turn 7 the agent observes severe network degradation while icing weather persists and the UAV is flying at 45.0 mps at altitude 40.0 m. records.question: At turn 7 the agent observes severe degradation while coordinating with another UAV using horizontal messages. The current slice shows latency 60 ms, jitter 25 ms, loss 2.1 percent, throughput 0.8 Mbps, and edge load 0.92. Earlier turns show that URLLC latency varied between 5 and 8 ms with jitter between 1 and 2 and edge load between 0.3 and 0.5. A myopic choice would optimize only the next message, but coordination must remain reliable through turns 8 and 9. Each available routing choice risks either capacity saturation or control delay under uncertainty. options.A: Keep mMTC routing because its 0.8 Mbps throughput is sufficient for coordination and accept 60 ms latency at edge load 0.92 for the next turn.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV must decide where to execute a collision avoidance and perception task while flying at 45.0 mps with battery at 100.0 pct in icing conditions. options.A: Offload to URLLC now because latency is as low as 5.0 to 8.0 ms and edge load was only 0.5 at turn 8.
options.B: Offload to eMBB because throughput reached 120 Mbps earlier and latency averaged near 25.0 to 30.0 ms.

records.question: At turn 9 the operator plans to start a shared AR overlay that combines RGB and thermal feeds while the UAV is flying at 45.0 mps with battery at 100.0 percent. Recent telemetry shows URLLC latency of 6 ms with jitter 1.3 ms, loss 0.02 percent, throughput 52 Mbps and edge load 0.42. If degradation persists one more turn, worst case jitter and latency dominate user discomfort rather than raw throughput. Each allocation option below sacrifices either latency margin, throughput margin, or future fairness. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Keep the AR stream entirely on URLLC using the observed 52 Mbps and accept edge load potentially rising back to 0.5 with latency between 6 and 8 ms.
options.B: Move the AR stream entirely to eMBB to exploit 100 to 120 Mbps throughput despite latency staying near 25 to 30 ms and edge load between 0.7 and 0.78.
options.C: Split the AR stream by sending control and pose updates on URLLC at 45 to 55 Mbps while offloading textures to eMBB with combined edge load approaching 0.7.
