options.D: Grant access on mMTC slice; current load 90%, add 0.2 units to reach 92%, which is under 95% threshold; latency 115ms exceeds SLA but may recover next turn.

records.question: At turn 8, network slice degrades to mMTC with latency 120ms, jitter 25ms, loss 8%, throughput 1.2Mbps, and edge load 0.85. The UAV is at 25m altitude, 28m/s speed, and must return to base within 3 turns under policy altitude bounds [20,120]. The RAG system must select which telemetry subset to augment the prompt: A) full sensor status + current slice metrics, B) only latency and loss with 10% uncertainty margin, C) projected edge load next turn assuming 5% degradation per turn, D) battery and speed with worst-case latency bound of 150ms. The system must ensure prompt generation completes within 50ms and avoid exceeding edge load 0.95. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Full sensor status + current slice metrics
options.B: Only latency and loss with 10% uncertainty margin
options.C: Projected edge load next turn assuming 5% degradation per turn
options.D: Battery and speed with worst-case latency bound of 150ms

records.question: At turn 9, the UAV agent detects network degradation to mMTC slice with 10.0% packet loss and 0.8 Mbps throughput, while edge load is at 0.9. The agent must decide whether to onboard a backup UAV agent for handover, cache 3 waypoints locally, or switch to eMBB slice despite its higher latency. The backup agent requires 120ms round-trip authentication latency and consumes 0.15 edge load, but guarantees 99.9% mission continuity. Caching 3 waypoints consumes 0.05 edge load and tolerates up to 15% loss, but fails if degradation persists beyond 2 turns. Switching to eMBB offers 750 Mbps throughput but increases latency to 15ms and jitter to 4ms, risking control instability if wind gusts exceed 10 m/s. The current wind is 8.5 m/s with 240° direction, and the UAV is at 25m altitude with 100% battery. If the degradation continues for one more turn, the mission will violate SLA if control latency exceeds 20ms or loss exceeds 12%. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Onboard backup UAV agent: accepts 120ms authentication latency and 0.15 edge load to guarantee 99.9% continuity under 10% loss.
options.B: Cache 3 waypoints: uses 0.05 edge load and tolerates 15% loss, but fails if degradation persists beyond 2 turns.
options.C: Switch to eMBB slice: gains 750 Mbps throughput but risks 15ms latency and 4ms jitter, which may exceed 20ms SLA under wind gusts >10 m/s.
options.D: Maintain current mMTC slice: accepts 10% loss and 0.8 Mbps throughput, but edge load is already at 0.9 and may exceed 1.0 next turn.

records.question: The UAV is experiencing severe network degradation with 10.0% packet loss and 0.8 Mbps throughput under mMTC slice, while edge load is at 0.9. The mission requires federated model updates to be synchronized across three edge nodes before returning to base, each requiring 50 MB of data transfer. The next 2 turns may see either recovery to URLLC (latency 9ms, throughput 130 Mbps) or continued mMTC degradation (loss up to 12%, throughput as low as 0.5 Mbps). Battery is at 65% and descending at 3% per turn. The SLA mandates model sync completion within 3 turns or risk mission failure. Option A schedules sync immediately over mMTC with 50% success probability per node. Option B delays sync until turn 11, assuming URLLC recovery, but risks 15% battery depletion before sync. Option C splits sync across turns 10 and 11, using cached waypoints to reduce latency, but incurs 20% data loss per segment. Option D aborts sync and returns to base, preserving battery but violating SLA. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Schedule immediate sync over mMTC with 50% success probability per node.
options.B: Delay sync until turn 11 assuming URLLC recovery, risking 15% battery depletion.
options.C: Split sync across turns 10 and 11 using cached waypoints, accepting 20% data loss per segment.
options.D: Abort sync and return to base, preserving battery but violating SLA.

records.question: At turn 9, the UAV is operating under mMTC slice with 10.0% packet loss, 115ms latency, and 0.9 edge load while executing a survey mission. A third-party analytics agent requests full telemetry access including GNSS, IMU, and radar data for real-time anomaly detection. The policy allows exposure only if latency remains under 50ms and loss under 2.0% for the next 2 turns. Historical data shows mMTC degrades further by 15% loss and 20ms latency per turn under dust conditions. URLCC slice is available but has only 150Mbps throughput, insufficient for full telemetry streaming. The UAV must decide whether to grant full, partial, or no access, or defer until return to base. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Grant full access now; current latency is 115ms but will drop to 95ms next turn per trend.
options.B: Grant partial access (GNSS and IMU only); radar requires 120Mbps and exceeds URLLC capacity.
options.C: Deny all access; worst-case loss in 2 turns exceeds 2.0% and violates policy.
options.D: Defer access until return to base; network will stabilize and policy limits will be met.

records.question: At turn 9, the network has degraded to mMTC slice with 115ms latency, 30ms jitter, 10% packet loss, and 0.8Mbps throughput under 0.9 edge load. The UAV is mid-survey at 25m altitude with 100% battery, but thermal and lidar sensors remain offline. A security anomaly detection system flags potential spoofing of GNSS signals with 70% confidence, and the policy mandates maintaining at least 95% control reliability for 3 more turns. If the anomaly persists, latency may increase by 20ms per turn and loss may rise by 2% per turn. The edge load is projected to hit 0.95 next turn. Option A isolates GNSS and switches to IMU-only navigation with 85% reliability but reduces speed to 15mps. Option B maintains current configuration with 90% reliability but risks SLA violation if loss exceeds 12%. Option C initiates immediate return to base using cached waypoints, consuming 15% battery per turn and guaranteeing 98% reliability. Option D requests handover to backup UAV with 92% reliability but requires 500ms handover latency and 10% throughput overhead. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Isolate GNSS, switch to IMU-only, reduce speed to 15mps (reliability 85%, latency 10ms, throughput 100Mbps)
options.B: Maintain current config (reliability 90%, latency 115ms, loss 10%, edge load 0.9)
options.C: Initiate immediate return to base (reliability 98%, battery drain 15%/turn, throughput 130Mbps)
options.D: Handover to backup UAV (reliability 92%, handover latency 500ms, throughput overhead 10%)

records.question: At turn 8 the operator requests thermal imagery while the UAV is flying in icing conditions with 8.5 mps wind and active wind drift compensation. In the immediately preceding turns the network alternated between URLLC with latency values of 8.2 ms and 7.8 ms and eMBB with 14 ms latency. Jitter has fluctuated between 0.8 ms and 3 ms and loss between 0.01 percent and 0.2 percent across those same turns. Throughput demand for thermal imagery matches prior eMBB observations near 800 Mbps while URLLC has only delivered between 110 and 135 Mbps. Edge load has shown variability from 0.39 to 0.5, indicating nonstationary congestion. Assume the next two turns may resemble the worst previously observed metrics rather than the mean. Autonomous navigation has just been enabled earlier with mMTC showing 50 ms latency and 1.2 percent loss, so control sensitivity remains high. The UAV is expected to continue maneuvering for at least two more turns before return. A hybrid slice would split control and payload traffic across URLLC and eMBB using the same observed characteristics. Given worst case network behavior over the next two turns, which slice selection minimizes maximum regret across control safety and imagery completion?

options.A: Select pure URLLC, accepting 110 to 135 Mbps throughput with 8 to 9 ms latency and edge load around 0.4 to guarantee control stability.
options.B: Select pure eMBB, accepting 14 ms latency and up to 3 ms jitter with 0.2 percent loss to guarantee 800 Mbps imagery throughput.
options.C: Select a hybrid slice, using URLLC metrics near 8 ms latency for control and eMBB metrics near 800 Mbps throughput for payload under edge load up to 0.5.
options.D: Remain on the previously used slice without change, assuming recent averages of 11 to 12 ms latency and jitter under 2 ms will persist.

records.question: At turn 6 the user enables autonomous navigation while the network slice shifts to mMTC with latency 50 ms, jitter 15 ms, loss 1.2 percent, throughput 1.5 Mbps, and edge load 0.75. In earlier turns the same mission alternated between URLLC at about 8 ms latency and eMBB at about 14 ms latency, showing volatility across turns. The policy altitude bounds remain 10.0 to 120.0 meters and the UAV speed is 18.0 mps with battery at 100 percent. Assume the autonomy SLA requires latency below 40 ms and loss below 1.0 percent to avoid control instability. Edge load has previously ranged from 0.33 to 0.5 and now spikes to 0.75, so worst case assume it increases by another 0.05 next turn. If overload persists for the next two turns, projected contention can further increase latency proportionally to edge load. Reducing autonomy one level cuts throughput demand by half but increases operator latency sensitivity, while full autonomy maximizes local compute usage. Switching slices back to URLLC reduces latency but is capacity limited when edge load exceeds 0.7. Maintaining full autonomy risks compounding SLA violations over multiple turns, while immediate manual control increases pilot workload under icing and wind of 8.5 mps. Considering worst case bounds and minimizing maximum regret over the next two turns, which option should be selected?

options.A: Maintain full autonomy on mMTC despite 50 ms latency and 1.2 percent loss, accepting edge load 0.75 because battery is 100 percent and speed is stable at 18.0 mps.
options.B: Immediately switch back to URLLC with observed 8 to 9 ms latency, even though edge load above 0.7 risks capacity saturation next turn.
options.C: Gracefully degrade autonomy by one level to halve throughput demand from 1.5 Mbps while staying on mMTC, accepting higher latency now to avoid future overload escalation.
options.D: Drop to full manual control and eMBB with 14 ms latency and 800 Mbps throughput, relying on operator input despite wind 8.5 mps and icing.

records.question: At turn 6 the UAV has just enabled autonomous navigation while flying at 18.0 mps and 20.0 m altitude in icing conditions with wind at 8.5 mps. The policy altitude bounds remain a range from 10.0 to 120.0 m, and the geofence has not changed. Network conditions on the current turn show the mMTC slice with 50 ms latency, 15 ms jitter, 1.2 percent loss, 1.5 Mbps throughput, and 0.75 edge load. In prior turns URLLC showed latency between 7.5 and 9 ms with edge load between 0.38 and 0.45, while eMBB showed latency between 11 and 14 ms with edge load up to 0.5. The mission objective requires continuing for at least the next two turns unless the worst case risks exceed conservative limits. If the high edge load on mMTC persists for one more turn, command responsiveness may degrade further under worst case assumptions. Switching immediately to URLLC reduces latency but risks capacity stress if edge load rises toward previously observed peaks. Staying on eMBB improves throughput but increases latency relative to URLLC while keeping edge load moderate. Given uncertainty across the next two turns and the need to minimize maximum regret rather than optimize the current turn, which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue on mMTC at 50 ms latency and 0.75 edge load to avoid a slice switch during autonomous navigation.
options.B: Switch to URLLC with 7.5 to 9 ms latency despite edge load around 0.38 to 0.45 to prioritize control immediacy.
options.C: Switch to eMBB with 11 to 14 ms latency and edge load up to 0.5 to balance capacity and responsiveness.
options.D: Pause continuation and hold altitude at 20.0 m within the 10.0 to 120.0 m bounds until network conditions stabilize.

records.question: During autonomous navigation, the UAV must federate data among the mission control agent, a timing agent, and a swarm collision avoidance agent while GPS jamming risk persists. Recent turns show URLLC latency between 7.5 and 9 ms with jitter up to 1.2 ms and loss up to 0.04, while eMBB shows latency between 11 and 14 ms with jitter up to 3 ms and loss up to 0.2. The mMTC slice used at turn 6 shows 50 ms latency, 15 ms jitter, 1.2 loss, and edge load of 0.75, which risks delayed coordination if reused. Policy altitude bounds are 10 to 120, and the UAV is operating near 20 altitude while rerouting around obstacles over multiple turns. The federation choice must remain safe if current network conditions persist for the next three turns without recovery. A worst case must assume the highest observed jitter and loss on each slice. Mission control requires timely state sharing, while swarm collision avoidance requires low worst case latency margins. Edge load above 0.5 is expected to increase contention in the next turn. A single turn improvement is insufficient if future regret grows under sustained degradation. The decision must minimize maximum regret across the next three turns rather than optimize the current one. Which interoperability and federation option should be selected?

options.A: Federate all agents over URLLC despite edge load around 0.45 to 0.42, accepting 9 ms latency and 1.2 ms jitter for the next turns.
options.B: Use eMBB for mission control and URLLC for swarm coordination, tolerating up to 14 ms latency and 3 ms jitter on eMBB.
options.C: Switch all federation to mMTC to reduce edge load pressure, accepting 50 ms latency and 15 ms jitter.
options.D: Keep current turn on URLLC but plan to migrate all agents to eMBB next turn if edge load exceeds 0.5.

records.question: At turn 7 the agent must choose how to route horizontal messages to the uav_swarm_agent for collision avoidance and follow up coordination. Recent telemetry shows URLLC latency values of 7.5 ms at turn 4, 9 ms at turn 5, and 8.2 ms at turn 7 with jitter of 1.0 ms and loss of 0.04 percent. eMBB earlier provided latency of 12 ms at turn 1 and 14 ms at turn 8 with jitter up to 3 ms and loss of 0.2 percent but throughput near 800 Mbps. mMTC at turn 6 showed 50 ms latency, 15 ms jitter, 1.2 percent loss, throughput 1.5 Mbps, and edge load of 0.75. Edge load on URLLC has varied between 0.38 and 0.45 across recent turns, indicating possible congestion if the trend persists for the next two turns. The UAV is flying at 18 mps in 8.5 mps wind, so delayed peer updates compound positional error over time rather than in a single turn. If congestion worsens, jitter can add to effective latency even if the mean stays low. A myopic choice optimizes only the current turn, but the agent must minimize maximum regret if degradation persists into turns 8 and 9. Security requirements are unchanged and all slices are permitted. Which communication policy should be selected?

options.A: Continue direct URLLC routing with current parameters because mean latency is 8.2 ms and loss is only 0.04 percent despite edge load around 0.42.
options.B: Switch to eMBB relay routing since 800 Mbps throughput can absorb retries and earlier latency of 12 to 14 ms is acceptable at current speed.
options.C: Fallback to mMTC for robustness because its edge load of 0.75 is already saturated and unlikely to worsen further over the next turn.
options.D: Use URLLC but rate limit peer messages to account for jitter of 1.0 ms and rising edge load from 0.38 to 0.45 over recent turns.

records.question: During post-mission analysis at turn 8, the operator considers scheduling a federated model update between the UAV and the edge. Recent network slices oscillated between eMBB with latency 11 to 14 ms and URLLC with latency 7.5 to 9 ms, while mMTC previously spiked to 50 ms. Edge load has ranged from 0.33 to 0.75, and throughput has varied from 1.5 to 870 Mbps depending on slice. The UAV battery was initially 100 percent but a return was triggered by turn 9, implying limited remaining energy for compute. Policy altitude bounds remain between 10.0 and 120.0, constraining flight but not compute. A federated round would require sustained uplink and downlink over at least the next two turns. If congestion persists one more turn, the worst observed edge load of 0.75 may recur. If instead conditions recover to recent URLLC levels, capacity remains limited to about 130 Mbps. Considering regret over the next three turns and worst-case network conditions, which scheduling option should be selected?

options.A: Start a full federated update immediately on eMBB at turn 8, using 800 Mbps throughput despite edge load near 0.5.
options.B: Delay all federated updates until after landing, avoiding current edge load between 0.35 and 0.75 but forgoing any in-flight learning.
options.C: Run a single lightweight federated round only if URLLC persists, accepting 120 to 135 Mbps throughput and edge load around 0.38 to 0.42.
options.D: Attempt federated updates opportunistically across any slice each turn, assuming average latency near 12 ms and ignoring the prior 50 ms spike.

records.question: At turn 6 the digital twin must support autonomous navigation while compensating for icing winds and recent GPS jamming. The network slice at that turn is mMTC with latency 50 ms, jitter 15 ms, loss 1.2 percent, throughput 1.5 Mbps, and edge load 0.75. Earlier and later URLLC turns show latency between 7.2 ms and 9 ms, jitter between 0.7 ms and 1.2 ms, loss up to 0.04 percent, throughput between 110 and 140 Mbps, and edge load between 0.35 and 0.45. eMBB turns show latency 11 to 14 ms, jitter 1.8 to 3 ms, loss up to 0.2 percent, throughput 800 to 870 Mbps, and edge load up to 0.5. The digital twin requires continuous telemetry and command updates over the next two turns to safely maintain control in 8.5 mps wind while the UAV remains within altitude bounds of 10 to 120. If edge load increases toward the previously observed 0.75 again, worst case scheduling delay must be considered rather than mean performance. If GPS jamming persists for one more turn, higher jitter directly degrades state estimation even if throughput is ample. Switching slices incurs at least one turn of adaptation during which metrics resemble the first observed values of the new slice. No slice can satisfy all needs perfectly, so the choice must minimize worst case regret over the next two turns. Which network slice option should be selected now?

options.A: Remain on mMTC to keep load isolation, accepting 50 ms latency and 15 ms jitter with 1.5 Mbps throughput if edge load stays near 0.75.
options.B: Switch to eMBB to gain 800 Mbps throughput at about 14 ms latency and 3 ms jitter while tolerating edge load up to 0.5.
options.C: Switch to URLLC to obtain 7.2 to 9 ms latency and 0.7 to 1.2 ms jitter even if throughput is limited to 110 to 140 Mbps and edge load may reach 0.45.
options.D: Delay switching for one turn, assuming mMTC metrics improve toward earlier eMBB-like values while keeping current autonomous mode.

records.question: At turn 9 the agent must choose how to route agent to agent coordination traffic for the next three turns while approaching the final inspection point. Recent slices show URLLC latency between 7 and 11 ms with jitter from 1.0 to 2.0 ms, loss between 0.005 and 0.02 percent, throughput from 40 to 55 Mbps, and edge load from 0.3 to 0.42. eMBB previously showed 25 to 30 ms latency, 5.0 to 6.0 ms jitter, 0.1 to 0.15 percent loss, throughput from 110 to 120 Mbps, and edge load from 0.65 to 0.7. mMTC at turn 9 degraded to 50 ms latency, 15.0 ms jitter, 0.5 percent loss, 1 Mbps throughput, and 0.85 edge load. The UAV is flying at 22.0 mps with battery at 100.0 percent and wind at 8.5 mps, so extra retransmissions increase future energy cost. Assume link conditions may stay at the worst observed values for the next two turns and that telemetry must tolerate no more than 20 ms end to end latency to remain useful. High resolution imaging traffic is bursty and can be deferred but coordination messages cannot. If congestion rises by the same edge load deltas seen previously, URLLC could reach 0.42 edge load again while eMBB could reach 0.7. Each option below changes routing for all agent to agent messages starting now. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Route all agent to agent traffic over URLLC only, accepting throughput of 40 to 55 Mbps and edge load up to 0.42 to minimize current latency of 7 to 11 ms.
options.B: Switch all agent to agent traffic to eMBB to gain 110 to 120 Mbps throughput despite 25 to 30 ms latency and edge load up to 0.7.
options.C: Keep mMTC for coordination since it already carries traffic at 50 ms latency and 1 Mbps throughput with edge load 0.85.
options.D: Split traffic so coordination stays on URLLC while noncritical bursts opportunistically spill to eMBB when edge load is below 0.65.

records.question: At turn 9 the UAV reaches the final inspection point while the network slice shifts to mMTC with latency 50 ms, jitter 15.0 ms, loss 0.5 percent, throughput 1 Mbps, and edge load 0.85. Earlier turns on URLLC showed latency between 7 and 11 ms, jitter between 1.0 and 2.0 ms, throughput between 40 and 55 Mbps, and edge load between 0.30 and 0.42. The UAV speed is 22.0 mps and altitude must remain within 10.0 to 120.0 m while icing and wind persist. Battery started at 100 percent and has been under wind load since turn 7 with no recovery observed. A federated learning round would exchange model updates during the next two turns while the UAV is returning. One option is to schedule training immediately on the current slice, another is to wait one turn hoping URLLC conditions return, another is to downscale to partial updates on URLLC, and another is to defer all training until after landing. Assume worst case that mMTC conditions persist for one extra turn and URLLC recovers only to its worst observed jitter. Regret is defined as the maximum loss of model freshness or mission risk over the next two turns. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Schedule a full federated round immediately on mMTC using 1 Mbps throughput despite 50 ms latency and 0.85 edge load to avoid freshness loss this turn.
options.B: Wait one turn and schedule a full federated round on URLLC assuming latency near 8 ms and throughput near 50 Mbps return.
options.C: Schedule a downscaled federated round on URLLC next turn that fits within 40 to 45 Mbps throughput and tolerates up to 2.0 ms jitter.
options.D: Defer all federated training until after landing, accepting two turns of model staleness but zero network load in flight.

records.question: At turn 10 the operator must decide how the network supplies telemetry and commands to keep the digital twin synchronized while the UAV approaches completion. Recent links showed URLLC latency values of 9, 10, and 11 ms with jitter observed between 1.6 and 2.0 ms and loss between 0.01 and 0.02. A prior fallback to mMTC at turn 9 had 50 ms latency, 15.0 ms jitter, 0.5 loss, throughput of 1 Mbps, and edge load of 0.85. eMBB earlier provided 25 to 30 ms latency with jitter of 5.0 to 6.0 ms and edge load rising to 0.7. Throughput demand is modest for telemetry at 50 to 52 Mbps but imaging can spike beyond 45 Mbps. The digital twin control loop tolerates short bursts of jitter but drifts if worst case latency exceeds the recent envelope for more than two turns. There is uncertainty whether the current fluctuation will persist into the next two turns or recover as seen before. If degradation persists, battery and wind loads make delayed commands more costly than deferred imaging. Each option below trades present fidelity against future regret under worst case network behavior. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Lock all channels to URLLC at 50 Mbps accepting edge load around 0.42 and potential jitter up to 2.0 ms for the next two turns.
options.B: Switch telemetry and commands to eMBB at 120 Mbps with 25 to 30 ms latency to preserve imaging throughput this turn.
options.C: Fall back to mMTC for telemetry only with 50 ms latency and 0.5 loss while buffering commands locally for one turn.
options.D: Split traffic by keeping telemetry on URLLC and deferring imaging entirely for up to two turns to reduce contention.

records.question: At turn 9 the UAV approaches the final inspection point while the network briefly shifts to mMTC with latency 50 ms, jitter 15.0 ms, loss 0.5 percent, throughput 1 Mbps, and edge load 0.85. In prior and subsequent turns the link recovers to URLLC with latency between 7 and 11 ms, jitter between 1.0 and 2.0 ms, loss between 0.005 and 0.02 percent, throughput between 40 and 55 Mbps, and edge load between 0.3 and 0.42. The weather remains icing with wind 8.5 mps and the UAV maintains speed 22.0 mps at altitude within the 10.0 to 120.0 meter policy bounds. The agent must choose which sensing streams and fusion strategy to provide for time sensitive perception over the next two turns while returning telemetry reliably. High resolution RGB and lidar together require far more throughput than thermal and radar, but they provide finer detail for obstacle discrimination. GNSS, IMU, and barometer are already active and assumed negligible bandwidth. If the degraded condition persists one more turn, worst case throughput could again be 1 Mbps with high jitter. If recovery occurs, URLLC capacity is sufficient but edge load variability remains. Each option trades immediate perception quality against robustness to worst case network behavior. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Stream fused RGB plus lidar at full rate over URLLC assuming recovery to 40–55 Mbps, accepting the risk that a repeat of 1 Mbps throughput would drop frames.
options.B: Stream thermal plus radar with edge fusion and downsampled telemetry, fitting within 1 Mbps throughput and tolerating 50 ms latency and 15.0 ms jitter if mMTC recurs.
options.C: Stream RGB only with cloud fusion using the observed 8–11 ms latency, ignoring the prior 0.5 percent loss spike as transient.
options.D: Pause all imaging and send only telemetry over URLLC at 50 Mbps to minimize loss and jitter regardless of sensing needs.

records.question: At turn 9 the UAV enters a degraded link state while approaching the final inspection point and a third party planning agent requests access. The current slice is mMTC with latency 50 ms, jitter 15.0 ms, loss 0.5 percent, throughput 1 Mbps, and edge load 0.85. Earlier turns on URLLC showed latency between 7 and 11 ms, loss between 0.005 and 0.02 percent, throughput between 40 and 55 Mbps, and edge load between 0.3 and 0.42. The mission is expected to complete in the next two turns but recovery to URLLC is uncertain. The third party asks for live sensor data, path planning APIs, and limited onboard compute to optimize the return. Battery is still 100 percent and speed is 22.0 mps, so immediate energy constraints are low. However icing conditions persist and wind is 8.5 mps, increasing sensitivity to control latency. Granting exposure now could reduce future regret if the link improves but could also amplify risk if degradation persists for another turn. You must choose an exposure level that remains acceptable under the worst case of continued mMTC conditions. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Grant full data streams and compute APIs now because battery is 100 percent and any optimization benefit outweighs the current 1 Mbps throughput limit.
options.B: Grant read only telemetry and path suggestion APIs without raw sensor data because this caps exposure under 50 ms latency and 0.85 edge load if mMTC persists.
options.C: Delay all third party access until URLLC returns since earlier latency of 7 to 11 ms and loss below 0.02 percent would then support safe sharing.
options.D: Grant live imaging data only for the next turn because loss is just 0.5 percent and recovery is likely based on prior URLLC stability.

records.question: The UAV is descending under URLLC slice with 9ms latency, 1.6ms jitter, 0.15% loss, 48Mbps throughput, and 0.42 edge load. Battery is at 85% and decreasing at 3% per turn. The next two turns require collision avoidance inference with SLA of ≤10ms latency and ≤0.2% loss. Edge load is projected to rise to 0.55 by turn 10 under current trajectory. Onboard inference consumes 12ms latency and 5% battery per turn. If edge load exceeds 0.6, latency spikes to 25ms. Wind gusts may increase jitter by ±2ms. Which placement minimizes maximum regret over turns 9–10 under worst-case jitter and edge load?

options.A: Use edge inference: current latency 9ms < SLA 10ms, and edge load 0.42 < 0.6 threshold.
options.B: Use onboard inference: avoids edge load risk, latency 12ms exceeds SLA but battery allows 2 turns.
options.C: Hybrid: edge for turn 9, onboard for turn 10 if edge load > 0.55, accepting 12ms latency in worst case.
options.D: Wait for edge load to drop: delay inference until turn 10 when load projected at 0.33, risking SLA violation in turn 9.

records.question: At turn 4, edge load is 0.85, latency is 200 ms, jitter is 50 ms, and loss is 2.1%, while the SLA mandates latency under 100 ms and edge load under 0.8. The UAV is at 30 m altitude with 100% battery and must complete a mission requiring sensor fusion within 3 turns. URLLC slice offers 9 ms latency but only 45 Mbps throughput, while eMBB offers 100 Mbps but 15 ms latency and 0.7 edge load. If edge load increases by 0.05 per turn under current slice and latency degrades by 10% per turn, which option minimizes maximum regret over the next 3 turns? A: Stay on mMTC and accept SLA violation risk. B: Switch to URLLC immediately despite throughput constraint. C: Switch to eMBB and accept 15 ms latency. D: Delay action for one turn to observe recovery.

options.A: Stay on mMTC and accept SLA violation risk.
options.B: Switch to URLLC immediately despite throughput constraint.
options.C: Switch to eMBB and accept 15 ms latency.
options.D: Delay action for one turn to observe recovery.

records.question: At turn 4, the UAV is operating under lightning risk with wind at 6.5 m/s and is attempting to diagnose a sensor failure via mMTC slice with 200 ms latency, 50 ms jitter, 2.1% loss, and 1.2 Mbps throughput while edge load is at 0.85. The policy mandates altitude between 30 and 120 meters, and the UAV is currently at 30 meters with 100% battery. The next two turns require either offloading diagnostics to edge (risking SLA violation if edge load exceeds 0.9) or switching to URLLC (which has 9 ms latency but only 45 Mbps throughput and may not support diagnostic data size). If edge load increases by 0.1 per turn under current mMTC usage, and URLLC can only handle 80% of diagnostic payload, which option should be selected to avoid trust violation and ensure mission continuity over the next three turns?

options.A: Offload to edge via mMTC; edge load will reach 0.95 in two turns, exceeding SLA but maintaining diagnostic fidelity.
options.B: Switch to URLLC; latency drops to 9 ms but payload is truncated, risking incomplete diagnosis and potential mid-air failure.
options.C: Delay diagnostics for one turn; edge load may drop to 0.75 if no new tasks arrive, but lightning risk increases probability of sensor degradation.
options.D: Use eMBB slice; throughput is 120 Mbps but latency is 12 ms and jitter 3.0 ms, which may violate real-time trust constraints for diagnostics.

records.question: At turn 8, the UAV is descending under URLLC slice with latency 9ms, jitter 1.6ms, loss 0.15%, throughput 48Mbps, and edge load 0.42. The SLA mandates latency ≤10ms, jitter ≤2ms, loss ≤0.2%, and edge load ≤0.5. Historical trends show latency increases by 1ms per turn under URLLC during descent, jitter grows by 0.3ms per turn, and edge load rises by 0.05 per turn. If lightning risk persists, worst-case latency could spike by +3ms, jitter by +1ms, and edge load by +0.1. Over the next two turns, which option minimizes maximum regret under worst-case degradation? Option A: Stay on URLLC, accepting 10.6ms latency and 0.52 edge load by turn 10. Option B: Switch to eMBB now, accepting 15ms latency and 0.7 edge load, but with no projected degradation. Option C: Switch to mMTC now, accepting 200ms latency and 0.85 edge load, but with 90% probability of recovery to eMBB by turn 10. Option D: Delay descent for one turn to allow edge load to drop to 0.37, then proceed on URLLC with 9.5ms latency and 0.47 edge load by turn 10. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Stay on URLLC, accepting 10.6ms latency and 0.52 edge load by turn 10.
options.B: Switch to eMBB now, accepting 15ms latency and 0.7 edge load, but with no projected degradation.
options.C: Switch to mMTC now, accepting 200ms latency and 0.85 edge load, but with 90% probability of recovery to eMBB by turn 10.
options.D: Delay descent for one turn to allow edge load to drop to 0.37, then proceed on URLLC with 9.5ms latency and 0.47 edge load by turn 10.

records.question: The UAV has completed its mission with 28% edge compute load remaining and is now idle. A third-party client requests compute allocation for a latency-sensitive application requiring 95% SLA compliance with max 10ms latency and 0.5% packet loss over the next 3 turns. Current network slice is URLLC with 6ms latency, 0.9ms jitter, 0.05% loss, and 60Mbps throughput. Historical edge load trend shows 0.05 increase per turn under eMBB and 0.03 under URLLC. Worst-case jitter could spike to 3ms under lightning risk. If the client pays 1.5x premium for URLLC, but eMBB offers 2x throughput at 0.8x cost, which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next 3 turns while preserving safety margins?

options.A: Allocate URLLC slice with 1.5x premium; current latency 6ms is under 10ms SLA and jitter 0.9ms is within tolerance, edge load will rise to 0.37 by turn 13.
options.B: Switch to eMBB slice at 0.8x cost; throughput doubles to 120Mbps, latency 15ms exceeds SLA by 5ms, but client may accept degraded QoS for cost savings.
options.C: Reject the request; edge load would exceed 0.8 under eMBB by turn 13, risking system instability, and URLLC cannot guarantee SLA under worst-case jitter of 3ms.
options.D: Allocate URLLC but throttle throughput to 30Mbps to reduce edge load growth; latency remains 6ms, but client may experience 50% throughput reduction, violating SLA on bandwidth.

records.question: At turn 8, the UAV is descending under URLLC slice with latency 9ms, jitter 1.6ms, loss 0.15%, throughput 48Mbps, and edge load 0.42. Policy requires latency ≤10ms and loss ≤0.2% for critical control. Historical data shows jitter may spike to 3.0ms under wind gusts, and edge load may rise to 0.65 if two more UAVs join. The RAG system must decide which telemetry subset to expose: Option A includes full telemetry but risks exceeding 10ms latency if jitter spikes; Option B omits jitter and loss, reducing payload but risking undetected SLA violation; Option C includes only latency and throughput, ignoring jitter and edge load, which may mask future overload; Option D includes latency, jitter, and edge load but excludes loss, which may hide packet loss trends. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Expose full telemetry: latency, jitter, loss, throughput, edge load — despite risk of exceeding 10ms if jitter spikes to 3.0ms.
options.B: Expose only latency and throughput — omitting jitter and loss to reduce payload, accepting risk of undetected SLA violation if loss exceeds 0.2%.
options.C: Expose only latency and throughput — ignoring jitter and edge load, assuming current 0.42 load won’t rise to 0.65 under wind gusts.
options.D: Expose latency, jitter, and edge load — excluding loss, assuming 0.15% loss is stable and won’t exceed 0.2% even if edge load rises to 0.65.

records.question: An AI agent operating a UAV must be onboarded under dynamic network slicing conditions with fluctuating latency, jitter, and edge load. options.B: Register under eMBB with 0.7 edge load and 15ms latency

records.question: The UAV has completed its mission and is now grounded with battery at 100 percent and all sensors offline except RGB and GNSS. The edge network load is currently 0.28 with URLLC slice latency at 6 ms and jitter at 0.9 ms. Historical data shows that edge load increases by 0.05 per turn during federated training and that URLLC slice throughput degrades by 5 Mbps per turn under sustained load. The SLA requires latency under 15 ms and edge load under 0.9 for any federated training session. If training begins now, it will require 3 turns and consume 15 Mbps throughput per turn. If delayed by one turn, edge load will rise to 0.33 and latency may increase to 8 ms under worst-case jitter. If training is split across two edge nodes, each node’s load increases by 0.03 per turn but throughput per node is capped at 25 Mbps. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Begin federated training immediately on the current URLLC slice, accepting the risk of throughput degradation over 3 turns.
options.B: Delay training by one turn to allow edge load to stabilize, accepting potential latency increase to 8 ms.
options.C: Split training across two edge nodes to distribute load, accepting reduced per-node throughput and increased coordination latency.
options.D: Abort federated training and defer to next mission cycle, preserving network headroom for critical operations.

records.question: The UAV has completed landing under URLLC with 6ms latency, 0.05% loss, and 0.28 edge load. options.A: Grant full telemetry access now; edge load will remain under 0.8 and analytics can optimize future thermal activation.
options.B: Grant read-only access to non-sensor telemetry; restrict API calls to 1 per 5 seconds to cap edge load at 0.45.
options.C: Deny all access until thermal sensor is confirmed online; delay analytics until post-mission review in 3 turns.
options.D: Grant temporary access with 100ms latency tolerance; allow 20Mbps throughput cap to preserve URLLC for thermal activation.

records.question: At turn 4, the network slice switched to mMTC with latency spiking to 200ms, jitter at 50ms, packet loss at 2.1%, and edge load at 0.85, while the UAV remains at 30m altitude with 100% battery and thermal/lidar/radar sensors offline. options.A: Isolate UAV and switch to local autonomy with 10ms internal latency, losing remote telemetry.

options.C: Revert to URLLC with 9ms latency but accept 0.5% packet loss and 0.4 edge load.
options.D: Delay action for one turn to confirm recovery, risking 30% command loss if degradation continues.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV is hovering at altitude 25 within an allowed band from 10 to 120 while the network has degraded on an mMTC slice. Latency has risen from 25 to 30 with jitter from 10 to 12 and loss from 0.5 to 1.2 while throughput has fallen to 0.8 and edge load has increased to 0.9. The user intent in the next turns is to return to base under snowy weather with wind at 8.5 while conserving energy. Earlier URLLC operation showed latency between 3 and 6 with jitter below 1.5 and edge load between 0.32 and 0.45. Battery is still at 100 but prolonged hover or retransmissions will increase consumption over the next one to three turns. Policy requires staying within altitude bounds at all times and avoiding loss spikes during command execution. If the mMTC degradation persists one more turn the worst case latency and loss may delay waypoint adherence. If the system switches too aggressively to URLLC there is a risk of edge load saturation seen earlier at 0.45 under movement. A hybrid adjustment can change slice selection and speed without violating altitude constraints. Considering worst case bounds and regret over the next three turns, which option should be selected?

options.A: Remain on mMTC with latency 30 jitter 12 loss 1.2 and edge load 0.9 to avoid slice switching overhead while holding altitude 25.
options.B: Immediately switch to URLLC at latency 6 jitter 1.5 and edge load 0.45 and maintain current speed despite wind 8.5.
options.C: Switch to URLLC but reduce speed to limit edge load near 0.4 and keep altitude at 25 within the 10 to 120 bound.
options.D: Delay return one turn to wait for mMTC recovery since throughput may rise above 0.8 while hovering at altitude 25.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV is hovering in snow with wind at 8.5 mps and speed capability of 15 mps while battery remains at 100 percent. Network telemetry has shown URLLC latency between 3 and 6 ms across turns 1 to 11 with jitter up to 1.5 ms, throughput between 50 and 70 Mbps, and edge load between 0.3 and 0.45. eMBB has shown latency between 12 and 15 ms with jitter up to 3.2 ms, throughput between 100 and 120 Mbps, and edge load between 0.5 and 0.6. mMTC at turns 6 and 7 degraded to 25 to 30 ms latency, 10 to 12 ms jitter, throughput below 1 Mbps, and edge load between 0.8 and 0.9. The operator expects at least two more turns of control and telemetry during return to base after weather deterioration. Assume worst case that the next two turns follow the highest observed edge load and latency for any selected slice so far. Control commands are small but safety critical, while video payload is currently inactive due to thermal sensor failure. Switching slices incurs no immediate cost but choosing a congested slice risks compounding delay if degradation persists for another turn. A myopic choice would optimize only the next turn while ignoring persistence of edge load. options.A: Stay on URLLC to minimize current latency at 3 to 6 ms even if edge load could rise again toward 0.45.
options.B: Switch to eMBB to gain 100 to 120 Mbps throughput despite latency up to 15 ms and edge load up to 0.6.
options.C: Adopt a hybrid slice to balance control on URLLC and telemetry on eMBB while assuming edge load averages rather than peaks.
options.D: Remain on the current degraded profile similar to mMTC since control traffic is light and hover reduces demand.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV is hovering at 25.0 m altitude with battery at 100.0 percent while snow and 8.5 mps wind persist. The active slice is mMTC with latency observed rising from 25 ms at turn 6 to 30 ms at turn 7 and jitter increasing from 10 ms to 12 ms. Loss also increased from 0.5 percent to 1.2 percent while throughput dropped from 1 Mbps to 0.8 Mbps and edge load rose from 0.8 to 0.9. Staying on mMTC risks another increase matching the last observed step while switching risks transient instability during return. Over a two turn horizon no option avoids some performance loss. options.A: Immediately switch to URLLC now since its prior latency of 6 ms and jitter of 1.5 ms are far below the current 30 ms and 12 ms even if edge load reaches 0.45.

options.D: Switch to eMBB to balance higher throughput of 100 to 120 Mbps with moderate latency of 12 to 15 ms and edge load near 0.6.

records.question: At turn 7 the scheduler has shifted tasks across network slices after degradation during hover and scan. Telemetry shows mMTC latency fluctuating between 25 and 30 ms with jitter between 10 and 12 ms and loss rising from 0.5 to 1.2 percent while edge load increased from 0.8 to 0.9. options.B: Reconfigure scheduler to prioritize URLLC control at 3 to 5 ms latency and edge load near 0.4 while deferring scans for two turns.

records.question: At turn 8 the operator requests return to base due to weather after earlier hovering and scanning under degraded mMTC conditions. Telemetry across turns shows mMTC latency rising from 25 to 30 ms with jitter from 10 to 12 ms and edge_load from 0.8 to 0.9, while URLLC latency stays between 3 and 6 ms with edge_load between 0.3 and 0.45. options.B: Pause return and hover for one more turn to reattempt scanning on mMTC despite latency up to 30 ms and edge_load up to 0.9.

options.D: Switch back to mMTC during return to reduce URLLC congestion even if loss reaches 1.2 percent and jitter 12 ms.

records.question: At turn 7 the agent observes sustained degradation on the mMTC slice while coordinating sensor coverage with another UAV agent. Recent turns show mMTC latency increasing from 25 to 30 ms with jitter rising from 10 to 12 ms and loss from 0.5 to 1.2 percent, while throughput fell from 1 to 0.8 Mbps and edge load rose from 0.8 to 0.9. The agent must choose a routing and QoS policy for agent to agent messages that minimizes worst case regret over the next two turns. One option favors immediate reliability, one favors capacity, one ignores uncertainty, and one balances margins. Which option should be selected?

options.B: Keep agent to agent traffic on mMTC since current latency of 30 ms and throughput of 0.8 Mbps are acceptable for non video messages.
options.C: Switch agent to agent traffic to eMBB with latency up to 15 ms and edge load up to 0.6 to preserve URLLC headroom.
options.D: Split agent to agent traffic by sending control messages on URLLC and bulk state on eMBB, avoiding mMTC while monitoring edge load trends.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV is hovering in snow with wind_mps 8.5 and battery_pct 100 while network conditions have degraded compared to earlier turns. Across turns 1 to 7 the observed latency ranges from 3 to 30 ms, jitter ranges from 0.7 to 12 ms, throughput ranges from 0.8 to 120 Mbps, and edge_load ranges from 0.3 to 0.9 depending on slice. options.B: Offload to eMBB accepting lat_ms 12 to 15 and edge_load 0.5 to 0.6 to gain higher throughput_mbps up to 120.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV experiences degraded connectivity while hovering, with latency rising from 25 ms at turn 6 to 30 ms, jitter from 10 ms to 12 ms, loss increasing from 0.5 pct to 1.2 pct, throughput dropping from 1 Mbps to 0.8 Mbps, and edge load climbing from 0.8 to 0.9. options.D: Force a switch to URLLC slice now and run a compressed federated round tolerating up to 1.2 pct loss and 12 ms jitter.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV is hovering in snow with wind 8.5 and has rgb and lidar available while thermal and radar are offline. Network telemetry over recent turns shows URLLC latency between 3 and 6 with jitter between 0.7 and 1.5 and loss at or below 0.02, while mMTC shows latency 25 to 30 with jitter 10 to 12 and loss 0.5 to 1.2. A myopic choice that works only for the current URLLC turn may fail if the next turn reverts to mMTC. options.A: Select high rate rgb only over URLLC at 58 to 70 throughput assuming latency stays near 3 to 6 and ignoring the 12 jitter seen on mMTC.

options.C: Select fused rgb plus lidar with adaptive downsampling over URLLC sized to tolerate 30 latency and 12 jitter using recent edge load 0.45.
options.D: Select mMTC friendly sparse lidar beacons only assuming 25 latency and 0.5 loss will not worsen beyond the current turn.

records.question: A snowstorm mission is underway with a UAV inside a geofenced area and altitude bounds of 10.0 to 120.0 meters. By turn 7 the UAV is hovering at 25.0 meters with battery at 100.0 percent initially and thermal and radar sensors offline, requiring swarm coordination. A policy breach would occur if control responsiveness risks loss of safe navigation inside the geofence during return. Switching slices or escalating coordination has tradeoffs because URLLC capacity rises with edge load while mMTC risks further loss. The agent must choose an action that minimizes maximum regret over the next two turns rather than optimizing the current hover. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Remain on mMTC for the next two turns since 0.8 Mbps throughput is sufficient for low-rate coordination despite 30 ms latency and 12 ms jitter.
options.B: Immediately switch back to URLLC at edge load around 0.45 to reduce latency to about 5 to 6 ms even if capacity tightens.
options.C: Stay on eMBB because prior latency of 12 to 15 ms with edge load 0.5 to 0.6 balances throughput and stability.
options.D: Delay any slice change for one turn to observe recovery since prior URLLC loss was only 0.01 to 0.02 percent.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV is returning to base while a third party swarm agent remains available after earlier coordination. Recent network telemetry shows latency rising from 25 to 30 ms, jitter from 10 to 12 ms, loss increasing from 0.5 to 1.2 percent, throughput dropping from 1 to 0.8 Mbps, and edge load climbing from 0.8 to 0.9. Over the next three turns, excessive exposure could increase retries and delay landing, while too little exposure could reduce coordination benefits. Each option below limits or expands exposure differently and none avoids all risk. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Grant full data, API, and compute access now because current latency of 30 ms and throughput of 0.8 Mbps are still usable for coordination this turn.
options.B: Grant read-only telemetry access only, limiting compute calls, because loss at 1.2 percent and edge load at 0.9 indicate high congestion.

options.D: Grant telemetry and limited APIs for two turns but revoke compute access if latency stays above 25 ms or loss exceeds 0.5 percent.

records.question: At turn 7 an immersive AR inspection feed must be maintained while the UAV is hovering and preparing to return, and three network slices are available for allocation over the next two turns. Recent telemetry shows mMTC latency rising from 25 ms at turn 6 to 30 ms at turn 7 with jitter increasing from 10 ms to 12 ms and edge load from 0.8 to 0.9. URLLC capacity is lower but historically stable across turns. eMBB offers higher peak throughput but shows moderate and rising edge load. Considering worst case metrics across the next two turns and minimizing maximum regret if conditions do not improve, which allocation should be selected?

options.A: Prioritize URLLC for the AR feed, accepting 55 to 70 Mbps throughput with latency under 6 ms and edge load staying below 0.45 over the next two turns.
options.B: Switch fully to eMBB to exploit 100 to 120 Mbps throughput despite 12 to 15 ms latency and edge load around 0.6.

records.question: At turn 9 the operator issues an intent to resume normal operations and proceed to the goal while maintaining collision avoidance and geofence checks. The UAV is at speed 18.0 mps with battery at 100.0 percent and altitude constrained between 1.0 and 40.0. Recent network observations show URLLC latency values of 3.2, 4.1, 5.0 and 4.5 ms with edge_load up to 0.6, while mMTC degraded to 30.0 ms latency, 8.0 ms jitter, 1.2 percent loss and edge_load 0.8. Throughput has ranged from 0.5 to 55.0 Mbps depending on slice. Weather icing persists and at least one more turn of degraded telemetry is plausible. The intent requires feasibility over the next two turns without violating geofence or losing collision avoidance. If worst case network conditions repeat from turn 9, some adaptations may fail only in the second turn rather than immediately. Each option below makes a different adjustment while proceeding to the goal. Considering worst case latency and load persistence over the next two turns, which option should be selected?

options.A: Proceed immediately on URLLC with unchanged telemetry assuming latency stays near 3.5 ms and edge_load near 0.38 as in turn 10.
options.B: Proceed using mMTC with reduced telemetry rate since throughput 0.5 Mbps is sufficient and edge_load 0.8 is acceptable for one turn.
