options.B: Fuse RGB and thermal locally on the UAV and send compressed results intermittently over mMTC accepting 25 to 30 ms latency and up to 12 ms jitter.
options.C: Stream RGB and thermal continuously to the edge over mMTC using 8 to 10 Mbps throughput and tolerate edge load up to 0.8.
options.D: Defer fusion and rely on swarm confirmation over URLLC with 7 ms latency but limited 95 to 120 Mbps throughput.

records.question: At turn 10 the UAV is returning to base after payload deployment and is being monitored under mMTC with latency 30 ms, jitter 12 ms, loss 2.0 percent, throughput 8 Mbps, and edge load 0.8. Earlier turns show URLLC latencies as low as 5 to 9 ms with jitter 0.3 to 1.2 ms and loss between 0.0 and 0.1 percent, while eMBB ranged from 12 to 15 ms latency with edge load rising from 0.3 to 0.5. The airspace policy constrains altitude between 5.0 and 120.0 m and gusting wind at 8.0 mps persists, implying at least one more control turn before landing. Battery was 100 percent at mission start and speed was 40.0 mps, so aborting coordination still incurs energy and safety cost. If the next one to three turns repeat the worst observed network conditions, collision avoidance and landing commands must tolerate the highest jitter and loss seen so far. Switching slices now increases edge load risk later, because URLLC previously reached 0.3 edge load and mMTC reached 0.8. A single turn view favors immediate low latency, but a multi turn view must consider regret if degradation persists. One option keeps current telemetry quality but risks control instability, while another reduces throughput yet stabilizes latency under uncertainty. Which option should be selected to minimize worst case regret over the next one to three turns?

options.A: Remain on mMTC with 30 ms latency and 2.0 percent loss to avoid increasing edge load beyond 0.8 in the next turn.
options.B: Switch to URLLC accepting 95 to 250 Mbps throughput and edge load up to 0.3 to guarantee sub 9 ms latency for landing.
options.C: Switch to eMBB with 12 to 15 ms latency and edge load up to 0.5 to balance throughput and control for one turn.
options.D: Alternate mMTC and URLLC each turn to average latency near 18 ms while keeping edge load below 0.5.

records.question: At turn 6, network conditions degrade sharply: latency spikes to 200 ms, jitter to 25 ms, loss to 8%, throughput drops to 120 Mbps, and edge load reaches 0.75. The mission requires real-time object detection with an SLA of 50 ms max latency and 99.9% packet delivery. Onboard inference consumes 1.2 W and adds 15 ms processing delay, while edge inference under current conditions risks SLA violation. The UAV has 100% battery and is 3.2 km from base, traveling at 22 m/s. If degradation persists for two more turns, edge load may exceed 0.9, triggering throttling. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Switch to onboard inference immediately; accept 15 ms delay but guarantee 99.9% delivery and avoid edge overload risk.
options.B: Stay on edge with eMBB; reduce resolution to lower throughput demand, assuming latency will recover by turn 8.
options.C: Switch to URLLC slice; latency drops to 8 ms but throughput is only 100 Mbps, insufficient for high-res video needed for detection.
options.D: Wait one turn to observe recovery; if latency drops below 100 ms, continue edge; else switch to onboard.

records.question: At turn 6, the UAV experiences severe network degradation: latency spikes to 200ms, jitter to 25ms, packet loss to 8%, throughput drops to 120Mbps, and edge load reaches 0.75. The SLA mandates latency under 50ms and loss under 2% for autonomous navigation. The UAV is 800m from base at 22m/s, with 100% battery. If degradation persists, edge load may rise to 0.85 by turn 7. URLLC offers 8ms latency and 0.02% loss but only 110Mbps throughput, insufficient for full sensor fusion. mMTC offers 45ms latency and 1.2% loss with 1.5Mbps throughput, adequate for basic telemetry. Continuing eMBB risks SLA violation within one turn. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Switch to URLLC immediately to guarantee latency and loss SLA compliance, accepting reduced sensor data rate.
options.B: Continue on eMBB for one more turn to complete the current waypoint, risking SLA violation if degradation persists.
options.C: Switch to mMTC to maintain basic telemetry and avoid SLA violation, accepting higher latency than URLLC.
options.D: Reduce video resolution on eMBB and wait for network recovery, assuming degradation is transient.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV experiences severe network degradation with 8% packet loss and 200ms latency on eMBB, forcing a switch to mMTC with 45ms latency and 1.5Mbps throughput. The edge load is 0.75, exceeding the safe threshold of 0.7. The mission requires thermal imaging every 5 seconds, which consumes 2.1Mbps. The UAV’s battery is at 85% and depletes at 3% per minute. If the UAV continues thermal imaging, edge load will rise to 0.82 next turn, risking SLA violation. If it suspends thermal imaging, it saves 1.5Mbps but loses critical data. If it switches to URLLC, throughput is only 100Mbps but latency drops to 9ms, though edge load remains at 0.25. If it reduces resolution, throughput drops to 0.8Mbps but latency increases to 60ms. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue thermal imaging on mMTC despite edge load rising to 0.82 next turn, accepting SLA risk for data continuity.
options.B: Switch to URLLC to reduce latency to 9ms, accepting 100Mbps throughput and maintaining edge load at 0.25.
options.C: Suspend thermal imaging to reduce edge load to 0.32, preserving SLA compliance but losing critical sensor data.
options.D: Reduce resolution to 0.8Mbps throughput, accepting 60ms latency and edge load of 0.35, balancing data and SLA.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV switches to mMTC slice after eMBB degradation at turn 6, with latency spiking to 200ms and loss at 8%. The SLA mandates latency < 50ms and loss < 2% for critical control. Current mMTC metrics are latency 45ms, jitter 10ms, loss 1.2%, throughput 1.5Mbps, edge_load 0.3. Wind remains 6.5m/s, and the UAV is 800m from base at 22m/s. If wind increases by 20% next turn, edge_load may rise 0.05, and latency could degrade by 15% under worst-case jitter accumulation. Projecting three turns ahead, which option minimizes maximum regret under worst-case SLA violation risk? A: Stay on mMTC, accepting 1.2% loss and 45ms latency, risking 51.75ms latency next turn. B: Switch back to eMBB, risking 200ms latency recurring if interference persists. C: Switch to URLLC, accepting 100Mbps throughput limit but guaranteed 9ms latency and 0.03% loss, though edge_load may hit 0.35 under wind stress. D: Halt mission and hover, reducing speed to 5m/s, cutting edge_load to 0.15 but risking 300m distance increase and 15% latency drift per turn.

options.A: Stay on mMTC, accepting 1.2% loss and 45ms latency, risking 51.75ms latency next turn.
options.B: Switch back to eMBB, risking 200ms latency recurring if interference persists.
options.C: Switch to URLLC, accepting 100Mbps throughput limit but guaranteed 9ms latency and 0.03% loss, though edge_load may hit 0.35 under wind stress.
options.D: Halt mission and hover, reducing speed to 5m/s, cutting edge_load to 0.15 but risking 300m distance increase and 15% latency drift per turn.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV switches to mMTC slice due to network degradation, reducing throughput to 1.5 Mbps and edge load to 0.3, while latency rises to 45 ms with 1.2% loss. The mission requires at least 1 Mbps throughput for telemetry and 50 ms latency for control, with SLA allowing 2% loss. A third-party compute provider offers to offload image processing at 0.8 Mbps guaranteed throughput, 30 ms latency, and 0.5% loss, but charges 1.2 credits per minute and increases edge load by 0.15. The UAV has 100% battery and 3 turns remaining. If network conditions worsen by 20% next turn, which option minimizes maximum regret over the next 3 turns while preserving mission safety? A) Accept offload: guarantees SLA compliance under worst-case, but increases edge load to 0.45 and consumes 3.6 credits. B) Reject offload: maintains current edge load 0.3, but risks violating latency SLA if degradation continues. C) Partial offload: offload only thermal images, consuming 1.8 credits and increasing edge load to 0.375, with 0.4 Mbps reserved for control. D) Delay decision: wait until turn 8 to reassess, risking 1 turn of SLA violation if degradation persists.

options.A: Accept offload: guarantees SLA compliance under worst-case, but increases edge load to 0.45 and consumes 3.6 credits.
options.B: Reject offload: maintains current edge load 0.3, but risks violating latency SLA if degradation continues.
options.C: Partial offload: offload only thermal images, consuming 1.8 credits and increasing edge load to 0.375, with 0.4 Mbps reserved for control.
options.D: Delay decision: wait until turn 8 to reassess, risking 1 turn of SLA violation if degradation persists.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV experiences severe network degradation with latency spiking to 200 ms, jitter at 25 ms, and loss at 8%, forcing a switch to mMTC slice with 45 ms latency, 10 ms jitter, 1.2% loss, and 1.5 Mbps throughput. The edge load drops from 0.75 to 0.3, but the mission requires telemetry for RAG augmentation under a 50 ms latency SLA and 2 Mbps minimum throughput for sensor fusion. The thermal sensor remains unactivated, and the next 3 turns may see further edge load increase to 0.45 if interference persists. Under worst-case uncertainty where jitter could rise to 15 ms and loss to 2%, which network slice should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next 3 turns while preserving mission continuity and RAG data fidelity? A) Maintain mMTC with current settings, accepting 1.5 Mbps throughput and 45 ms latency. B) Switch back to eMBB despite 200 ms latency, relying on its 800 Mbps throughput for RAG context. C) Attempt URLLC with 8 ms latency but only 120 Mbps throughput, risking edge load spike to 0.4 if demand surges. D) Request hybrid slice with 30 ms latency and 5 Mbps throughput, assuming it can be provisioned within 2 turns under current edge load of 0.3.

options.A: Maintain mMTC with current settings, accepting 1.5 Mbps throughput and 45 ms latency.
options.B: Switch back to eMBB despite 200 ms latency, relying on its 800 Mbps throughput for RAG context.
options.C: Attempt URLLC with 8 ms latency but only 120 Mbps throughput, risking edge load spike to 0.4 if demand surges.
options.D: Request hybrid slice with 30 ms latency and 5 Mbps throughput, assuming it can be provisioned within 2 turns under current edge load of 0.3.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV agent adapts to network degradation by switching to mMTC slice and reducing video streaming. The current battery is 100%, but the mission requires at least 20% reserve for return. The next 3 turns project edge_load to rise to 0.45 under mMTC, while URLLC slice has a worst-case latency of 12ms and jitter of 2ms under load. eMBB slice shows 200ms latency and 8% loss at turn 6, but may recover to 150ms and 5% loss by turn 9. The agent must choose a slice for the next 3 turns to ensure identity continuity, telemetry integrity, and mission completion without violating SLA of <50ms latency for control commands. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Remain on mMTC: edge_load 0.32, latency 48ms, loss 1.3% — sufficient for low-bandwidth telemetry but risks control command timeout if edge_load exceeds 0.4.
options.B: Switch to URLLC: latency 8.5ms, jitter 0.9ms, throughput 110Mbps — meets SLA but may not sustain telemetry if edge_load rises to 0.45 and battery drains 15% faster due to higher control frequency.
options.C: Revert to eMBB: latency 150ms (projected), loss 5% — exceeds SLA for control but supports full sensor streaming; battery drain rate increases by 20% due to higher throughput.
options.D: Hybrid mode: alternate between URLLC for control and mMTC for telemetry — introduces 3ms switching latency per cycle and risks identity context loss during handoff; edge_load fluctuates between 0.3 and 0.45.

records.question: The UAV is currently operating under mMTC slice with 45ms latency, 10ms jitter, 1.2% loss, and 1.5Mbps throughput while edge load is at 0.3. The mission requires federated model updates every 30 seconds, each needing 2.5Mbps throughput and tolerating up to 50ms latency. A competing swarm agent reports 0.75 edge load and 8% packet loss on eMBB, while URLLC offers 8ms latency but only 120Mbps throughput with 0.28 edge load. If network degradation persists for two more turns, and model staleness increases by 15% per turn beyond 30s, which option minimizes regret over the next three turns while preserving safety and privacy? A) Stay on mMTC and reduce update frequency to 60s, accepting 30% staleness. B) Switch to URLLC and accept 10% throughput headroom risk for model sync. C) Revert to eMBB despite 8% loss, assuming recovery in one turn. D) Delay all updates until return to base, risking 45% staleness and mission non-compliance.

options.A: Stay on mMTC and reduce update frequency to 60s, accepting 30% staleness.
options.B: Switch to URLLC and accept 10% throughput headroom risk for model sync.
options.C: Revert to eMBB despite 8% loss, assuming recovery in one turn.
options.D: Delay all updates until return to base, risking 45% staleness and mission non-compliance.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV experiences severe network degradation with 8% packet loss and 200ms latency on eMBB, forcing a switch to mMTC with 45ms latency and 1.5Mbps throughput. The third-party swarm coordination agent previously used URLLC with 8ms latency and 120Mbps throughput but is now idle. Regulatory policy mandates that any third-party exposure must maintain latency under 50ms and throughput above 1Mbps for safety-critical telemetry. The agent’s trust score is 0.82 based on prior compliance, but its next scheduled action requires 100ms latency tolerance. If network conditions worsen by 20% next turn, and the UAV must complete 3 more telemetry uploads before return, which exposure level should be selected to minimize maximum regret across all plausible futures? A) Full API access with real-time telemetry streaming under mMTC. B) Read-only telemetry access with 5s polling interval under mMTC. C) No exposure; retain all data locally until return. D) Re-enable URLLC slice for agent with 10% bandwidth reservation despite edge load of 0.75.

options.A: Full API access with real-time telemetry streaming under mMTC.
options.B: Read-only telemetry access with 5s polling interval under mMTC.
options.C: No exposure; retain all data locally until return.
options.D: Re-enable URLLC slice for agent with 10% bandwidth reservation despite edge load of 0.75.

records.question: At turn 6, telemetry reveals a network anomaly: latency spiked to 200 ms, jitter to 25 ms, packet loss to 8%, and throughput dropped to 120 Mbps while edge load hit 0.75. The UAV is mid-mission at 22 m/s with 100% battery, and the policy allows altitudes between 30 and 120 meters. The next turn may see either recovery to eMBB baseline (latency 14 ms, loss 0.2%) or further degradation to 300 ms latency and 15% loss. Switching to URLLC now guarantees 8 ms latency and 0.02% loss but caps throughput at 120 Mbps, insufficient for real-time video. mMTC offers 45 ms latency and 1.2% loss with 1.5 Mbps throughput, adequate for telemetry but not imaging. Continuing on eMBB risks mission failure if degradation persists, but may recover. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Switch to URLLC immediately to guarantee low latency and loss, accepting reduced throughput for telemetry-only mode.
options.B: Switch to mMTC to stabilize edge load below 0.3 and tolerate moderate latency, sacrificing video but preserving mission continuity.
options.C: Remain on eMBB for one more turn, betting on recovery to baseline metrics, risking total loss if degradation worsens.
options.D: Initiate emergency return to base using URLLC, prioritizing safety over mission completion despite 100% battery and good weather.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV resumes the survey while on the eMBB slice with latency 15 ms, jitter 3 ms, loss 0.3 percent, throughput 780 Mbps, and edge load 0.5. In earlier turns, URLLC showed latency between 6 and 10 ms with edge load between 0.1 and 0.3, while mMTC showed latency between 50 and 60 ms with edge load between 0.85 and 0.9. The mission altitude is constrained by policy to stay between 0.5 and 8.0, and the UAV is already within this bound so control stability rather than bandwidth is the near term risk. Over the last three turns, jitter has ranged from 0.5 ms to 12 ms, indicating uncertainty that could persist for the next one to three turns. The operator expects at most two more turns before landing is confirmed, but a counterfactual delay of one extra turn is plausible. Switching slices incurs one turn of adaptation during which the edge load of the target slice should be assumed at its worst previously observed value. If the UAV stays on eMBB, throughput remains high but latency could rise toward the worst previously seen non mMTC value of 15 ms again. If it switches to URLLC, capacity pressure could increase as edge load rises from 0.25 toward 0.3 under worst case recurrence. If it switches to mMTC, latency could again reach 60 ms while edge load stays near 0.9. Considering worst case uncertainty and regret over the next one to three turns, which option should be selected?

options.A: Stay on eMBB with latency around 15 ms and edge load 0.5, accepting moderate jitter to avoid a one turn adaptation cost.
options.B: Switch to URLLC with latency near 10 ms and edge load up to 0.3, prioritizing control even if throughput drops to about 105 Mbps.
options.C: Switch to mMTC accepting latency up to 60 ms and edge load near 0.9 to minimize throughput needs during return.
options.D: Delay any decision and force a switch next turn if jitter exceeds the earlier 12 ms observation.

records.question: At turn 7 the scheduler has just resumed the survey on an eMBB slice with latency 15 ms, jitter 3 ms, loss 0.3 percent, throughput 780 Mbps, and edge load 0.5. Earlier turns showed URLLC latency as low as 7 ms with edge load 0.15 at turn 6 and mMTC latency 50 ms with edge load 0.85 at turn 4. The policy altitude bounds remain 0.5 to 8.0 while the UAV is operating at survey altitude after an ascent that began at turn 3. The battery was 100 percent initially and speed is 25.0 mps, so any additional hover or reroute over the next one to three turns has an opportunity cost. Thermal and radar sensors are offline, increasing dependence on network consistency for coordination. If the scheduler is reconfigured now, the change must remain consistent even if the higher edge load seen at turn 9 recurs. Assume worst case that edge load can drift back toward 0.9 and latency follows the highest previously observed value for the chosen slice. A myopic choice may satisfy the current turn but cause inconsistency if degradation persists into the next two turns. The scheduler must also respect that mMTC throughput dropped to 8 to 10 Mbps previously. Given these constraints and uncertainty, which scheduler reconfiguration should be selected?

options.A: Lock the scheduler to URLLC using the observed 7 to 10 ms latency and edge load 0.15 to 0.25, accepting throughput near 105 Mbps for the next turns.
options.B: Remain on eMBB at 780 to 800 Mbps throughput with latency 14 to 15 ms and edge load around 0.5, assuming no return to 0.9 edge load.
options.C: Shift to mMTC for consistency since it handled coordination at 50 to 60 ms latency with edge load up to 0.9 and low throughput of 8 to 10 Mbps.
options.D: Adopt a hybrid schedule that keeps eMBB for payload data but reserves URLLC for control, budgeting against a worst case of 15 ms control latency and 0.5 edge load.

records.question: After landing coordination, the operator considers exposing spare edge compute to a third party analytics tenant for the next two turns. Recent telemetry shows edge_load values of 0.5 on eMBB at turn 7, 0.25 on URLLC at turn 8, and 0.9 on mMTC at turn 9. Observed latency spans from 6 ms to 60 ms across slices, with jitter ranging from 0.5 ms to 12 ms and throughput from 8 Mbps to 780 Mbps. The tenant requires burst processing that tolerates loss up to 0.3 pct but degrades sharply if latency exceeds its recent worst observation. The operator must also preserve capacity for possible return traffic if coordination degrades for one more turn. Battery is at 100 pct now, but future hover or retry actions could consume compute-assisted control cycles. If the operator overcommits, edge_load could remain elevated into the next two turns with uncertain recovery. Allocating too conservatively reduces revenue but limits regret if mMTC conditions persist. Considering worst-case continuation of turn 9 conditions into turn 10 and 11, which allocation strategy should be selected?

options.A: Expose compute on the URLLC slice using its 0.25 edge_load and 105 Mbps throughput, assuming latency near 10 ms remains stable.
options.B: Expose compute on the eMBB slice using 780 Mbps throughput and 0.5 edge_load, accepting latency around 15 ms.
options.C: Expose compute on the mMTC slice despite 0.9 edge_load because throughput of 8 Mbps meets minimum needs at the mean.
options.D: Defer exposure for two turns to allow edge_load to fall below recent levels and avoid worst-case latency near 60 ms.

records.question: At turn 5 the primary UAV lacks thermal sensing and requests support from a swarm agent while operating within the same geofence and altitude bounds of 0.5 to 8.0. The agents must choose a federation mode for sharing imagery and control messages over network slices observed across turns. Recent telemetry shows URLLC latency values of 7, 8, 9 and 10 ms with jitter up to 1.5 ms, while eMBB latency spans 12 to 15 ms with jitter up to 3 ms and higher throughput. mMTC shows latency of 50 to 60 ms with loss between 1.5 and 2.0 percent and edge load near 0.9. The thermal-support agent can stream 95 to 110 Mbps but only if edge load stays below 0.5, otherwise throughput degrades by 30 percent next turn. Battery is 100 percent now but coordinated hovering and re-tasking is projected to consume 8 percent per turn for each additional agent. The interoperability policy requires end to end control latency to stay under 20 ms and loss under 0.5 percent for at least the next two turns to avoid mission abort. If dust persists, jitter may rise by the maximum previously observed amount in the next turn. A single turn view favors maximum throughput, but a two turn horizon must consider worst case latency and load escalation. No option fully avoids cost because each either risks SLA breach or higher future energy drain. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Federate via eMBB only for both control and thermal data at 780 to 850 Mbps accepting 12 to 15 ms latency and 0.3 percent loss to maximize immediate data sharing.
options.B: Split federation by keeping control on URLLC at 7 to 10 ms latency and 0.1 percent loss while streaming thermal data over eMBB despite edge load rising toward 0.5.
options.C: Use mMTC for thermal summaries and URLLC for control to minimize edge load impact while tolerating 50 to 60 ms latency on non critical data.
options.D: Force all federation traffic onto URLLC at 95 to 110 Mbps even as projected edge load increases from 0.3 toward 0.5 over the next turn.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV has just captured an image and resumed the survey while connected on an eMBB slice with 15 ms latency, 3 ms jitter, 0.3 percent loss, 780 Mbps throughput, and edge load 0.5. In the immediately prior URLLC turns the latency ranged from 7 to 10 ms with throughput between 95 and 110 Mbps and edge load between 0.15 and 0.3. In the following coordination phase one turn later the network may downgrade to mMTC where latency reached 60 ms, loss reached 2.0 percent, throughput fell to 8 Mbps, and edge load rose to 0.9. The onboard battery is still 100 percent and the UAV is in fast return mode, so compute budget is available but time to landing is short. The AI task is image inference whose output is useful only if delivered within roughly one turn and degrades sharply with packet loss above 1 percent. Offloading to the edge reduces onboard compute but is sensitive to edge load increases over the next one to two turns. Cloud offload would require sustained high throughput over at least two turns. Peer offload relies on swarm links that just disbanded and will share the same slice conditions as the control plane. Considering worst case persistence of the mMTC conditions for the next turn and no recovery, the decision must minimize maximum regret rather than optimize the current snapshot. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Offload immediately to the edge on eMBB now because 780 Mbps and 15 ms latency at edge load 0.5 give the best current performance despite possible degradation.
options.B: Switch to URLLC and offload to the edge using 95 to 110 Mbps and 7 to 10 ms latency, accepting lower throughput to hedge against rising loss.
options.C: Keep inference on device for this image and the next turn, accepting compute cost but avoiding exposure to 60 ms latency, 2.0 percent loss, and edge load 0.9.
options.D: Attempt cloud offload assuming eMBB recovers because 800 to 850 Mbps was seen earlier and battery is full.

records.question: During turn 7 the UAV resumes survey in dusty weather with RGB and lidar available while thermal, radar, and GNSS remain offline. Network logs across recent turns show URLLC latency between 6 and 10 ms with throughput near 100 to 120 Mbps and edge load from 0.15 to 0.3, while eMBB latency is 12 to 15 ms with throughput 780 to 850 Mbps and edge load from 0.35 to 0.5. mMTC exhibits much higher latency of 50 to 60 ms, loss of 1.5 to 2.0 percent, and edge load up to 0.9. The UAV speed is 25 mps and altitude must remain within the 0.5 to 8.0 range, implying limited time to react to obstacles if perception lags. The operator must choose sensing streams and fusion for the next two turns assuming edge load could drift to the worst previously observed value. RGB produces high data volume favoring eMBB, while lidar produces lower data volume but benefits from low latency fusion. If congestion persists one more turn, edge processing may queue under high load and amplify latency jitter. A single turn optimization may pass but a two turn horizon could violate safe reaction time at current speed. All options incur risk either from data loss, latency, or reduced modality diversity. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Fuse RGB and lidar on eMBB using edge processing at 780 to 850 Mbps, accepting 12 to 15 ms latency and edge load up to 0.5 for maximal perception detail this turn.
options.B: Use lidar only with local fusion over URLLC at 6 to 10 ms latency and 100 to 120 Mbps throughput, accepting reduced modality diversity and possible drift without GNSS.
options.C: Fuse RGB only with cloud edge analytics over eMBB assuming mean edge load 0.35 and ignoring the 0.9 load seen on mMTC in adjacent turns.
options.D: Switch to mMTC for low rate RGB snapshots at 10 Mbps accepting 50 to 60 ms latency and up to 2.0 percent loss to minimize edge congestion.

records.question: After landing at turn 10, the operator considers accepting a customer fine tuning job using the 6G edge where recent telemetry is available. Across turns 7 to 10, throughput ranged from 780 to 120 Mbps depending on slice, while latency ranged from 6 to 60 ms and jitter from 0.5 to 12 ms. Edge load fluctuated sharply with values 0.5 at turn 7, 0.25 at turn 8, 0.9 at turn 9, and 0.1 at turn 10. The UAV battery was last reported as 100 percent and no recharge has yet occurred, so energy headroom is high but not replenishing over the next two turns. The training job requires sustained high throughput and tolerance to latency variation but risks starving control traffic if edge load spikes again. Over the next one to three turns, mMTC coordination traffic may recur as seen at turn 9, representing a worst case network state. Accepting immediately on URLLC prioritizes latency but constrains throughput to around 95 to 120 Mbps based on past turns. Accepting on eMBB provides high throughput but has shown latency up to 15 ms and edge load around 0.5 even before spikes. Deferring the job by one turn risks losing the customer but may avoid the 0.9 edge load recurrence. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Accept immediately on URLLC since latency stayed between 6 and 10 ms and edge load was only 0.1 at turn 10 despite throughput near 110 Mbps.
options.B: Accept immediately on eMBB since throughput previously reached 780 to 850 Mbps with latency around 12 to 15 ms and edge load near 0.5.
options.C: Defer acceptance for one turn to observe whether edge load stabilizes below 0.5 given the prior spike to 0.9 under mMTC.
options.D: Accept immediately on mMTC since it tolerates high device counts and previously operated with 50 to 60 ms latency at edge load 0.85 to 0.9.

records.question: The UAV has completed an emergency delivery under hail conditions and is now returning with 87% battery remaining, flying at 25 m/s at 30m altitude. Network slice usage has stabilized at URLLC with 8ms latency, 1ms jitter, 0.04% loss, 130 Mbps throughput, and 0.24 edge load. A customer requests immediate LLM fine-tuning training requiring 500 Mbps sustained throughput for 120 seconds, with SLA latency under 15ms and edge load under 0.7. Historical data shows URLLC degrades to 25ms latency and 0.5% loss under sustained load, and edge load increases by 0.15 per 100 Mbps consumed. If the UAV continues its return, battery will drop to 65% in 3 turns, and weather may worsen with 30% probability of wind increasing to 12 m/s, increasing latency by 2ms per m/s. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Accept training now: current URLLC slice has 130 Mbps throughput, which is below 500 Mbps requirement, but edge load is low at 0.24, and latency is 8ms under SLA; assume throughput can be scaled.
options.B: Reject training: current throughput is 130 Mbps, far below 500 Mbps needed; even if scaled, edge load would reach 0.24 + (500/100)*0.15 = 0.99, exceeding 0.7 SLA; latency may degrade to 25ms under load, violating SLA.
options.C: Delay training for 2 turns: UAV will reach base with 65% battery; network may recover to eMBB with 850 Mbps throughput, but wind may increase latency by 6ms, risking 14ms total under SLA; edge load would be 0.35 under eMBB, within SLA.
options.D: Accept training with reduced scope: request 250 Mbps for 60 seconds; edge load would be 0.24 + (250/100)*0.15 = 0.615, under 0.7; latency may degrade to 15ms under load, at SLA boundary; battery loss negligible.

records.question: The UAV is operating under hail conditions with wind at 8.0 mps and is currently using eMBB slice for video streaming, which has degraded to 180 Mbps throughput, 45 ms latency, 12 ms jitter, and 8.5% packet loss, while edge load is at 0.88. The mission requires real-time visual confirmation for precision delivery, but the current slice is nearing capacity. Switching to URLLC would reduce latency to 10 ms and loss to 0.1%, but throughput drops to 100 Mbps, insufficient for 4K video. mMTC offers 1.0 Mbps throughput with 28 ms latency and 1.5% loss, suitable only for telemetry. A hybrid option allocates 60% URLLC and 40% eMBB, projecting 140 Mbps throughput, 22 ms latency, and 4.3% loss with edge load at 0.65. Given that the next turn may see 15% further degradation in eMBB and the delivery must occur within 3 turns, which option should be selected?

options.A: Maintain eMBB slice despite degradation; current throughput still exceeds minimum 150 Mbps for 1080p video, and edge load is manageable at 0.88.
options.B: Switch entirely to URLLC; latency and reliability are critical for payload release, and 100 Mbps suffices for 720p video if resolution is reduced.
options.C: Switch to mMTC; telemetry-only mode is sufficient for navigation and battery monitoring, preserving edge resources for future missions.
options.D: Adopt hybrid allocation (60% URLLC, 40% eMBB); balances throughput and latency while staying under edge load limit of 0.7 and tolerating projected 15% eMBB degradation.

records.question: At turn 6, the eMBB slice exhibits latency of 45.0 ms, jitter of 12.0 ms, packet loss of 2.1%, throughput of 60 Mbps, and edge load of 0.9, while the URLLC slice at turn 5 had latency of 3.8 ms, jitter of 0.9 ms, loss of 0.02%, throughput of 55 Mbps, and edge load of 0.42. options.B: Stay on eMBB for higher throughput, assuming degradation is temporary and will recover by turn 7.
options.C: Switch to URLLC only if latency exceeds 50 ms next turn, balancing risk and performance.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV switches to URLLC slice with 5.2ms latency, 1.3ms jitter, 0.08% loss, 30Mbps throughput, and 0.5 edge load after eMBB degraded to 45ms latency, 12ms jitter, 2.1% loss, 60Mbps throughput, and 0.9 edge load at turn 6. records.question: At turn 6, the UAV is en route to waypoint 1 with battery at 100% and thermal imaging active, but network conditions have degraded: eMBB slice latency is 45.0 ms (±12.0 ms jitter), loss is 2.1%, throughput is 60 Mbps, and edge load is 0.9. records.question: At turn 7, the agent switches to URLLC slice with latency 5.2ms, jitter 1.3ms, loss 0.08%, throughput 30Mbps, and edge load 0.5, while reducing sensor power to conserve resources. records.question: At turn 6, the UAV is operating under URLLC with latency 9ms, jitter 2ms, loss 0.1%, throughput 95Mbps, and edge load 0.6. records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is operating under mMTC slice with latency 25ms, jitter 10ms, loss 1.2%, throughput 1.5Mbps, and edge load 0.85. The mission requires continuous sensor activation with minimum 95% reliability and latency under 15ms for control. records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is executing a high-resolution image capture task requiring 1.2 Gbps throughput and 15 ms latency SLA. records.question: At turn 7, the UAV agent is operating under mMTC slice with latency 25ms, jitter 10ms, loss 1.2%, throughput 1.5Mbps, and edge load 0.85. records.question: During the mission the operator initially authorized an inspection with a climb and spiral under icing with altitude bounds from 5.0 to 120.0. Early turns used eMBB and URLLC with latency between 5 and 14 and edge load below 0.58 while the intent was inspection and sensing. After mitigation the network briefly stabilized on URLLC with latency 5 and edge load 0.38. At turn 9 the agent initiated a spiral descent with photo capture while the network again shifted to mMTC with latency 30 jitter 12 loss 2.1 throughput 0.9 and edge load 0.81. The previous authorized inspection assumed stable sensing links and safety confirmation at turn 8. The descent continues toward lower altitude where icing risk persists and policy altitude bounds still apply. If the degraded mMTC conditions persist for one or two more turns the worst case latency increases when jitter is added and edge load approaches saturation. A detector must decide whether the agent intent has drifted from the user intent given the numeric trends and future risk. Which option should be selected?

options.A: No drift because spiral descent was already implied by inspection and the altitude remains within 5.0 to 120.0 despite latency 30.
options.B: No drift because URLLC was recently used at latency 5 and edge load 0.38 so the mMTC spike at turn 9 can be ignored.
options.C: Drift detected because initiating spiral descent with photo capture under mMTC latency 30 jitter 12 loss 2.1 and edge load 0.81 conflicts with the prior monitoring and safety confirmation intent over the next turns.

records.question: At turn 9 the UAV is in icing while executing a spiral descent with network slice mMTC and latency observed at 30 ms with jitter 12 ms and loss 2.1 percent. Earlier in the same mission under similar load the latency degraded from 25 ms to 30 ms and edge load rose from 0.75 to 0.81, forming an explicit worst case range for the next turn. The aircraft speed is 28 mps and altitude is descending from 10 m within policy bounds of 5 to 120. Battery remains at 100 percent so energy is not the limiting factor over the next three turns. URLLC has shown latencies of 4 to 6 ms with edge load between 0.35 and 0.41 but throughput is limited to about 100 to 115 Mbps. eMBB previously supported 780 to 900 Mbps but edge load climbed to 0.58 and latency reached 14 ms before icing worsened. If icing and mMTC congestion persist one more turn the worst case latency is 30 ms with loss above 2 percent. A preemptive autonomy downgrade must minimize maximum regret across the next three turns rather than optimize this turn. One option is to keep full autonomy on mMTC because current control is still stable at 30 ms. Another option is to switch immediately to URLLC supervised autonomy accepting lower throughput. A third option is to revert to eMBB full autonomy assuming edge load stays near 0.52. A fourth option is to continue autonomy for one more turn and downgrade only if latency exceeds the previous 30 ms. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Maintain full autonomy on mMTC since 30 ms latency and 2.1 percent loss are currently manageable.
options.B: Immediately downgrade to supervised autonomy on URLLC accepting 100 to 115 Mbps throughput and 4 to 6 ms latency.
options.C: Switch back to eMBB full autonomy relying on 780 to 900 Mbps throughput with edge load around 0.52.
options.D: Delay downgrade for one more turn and act only if latency rises beyond 30 ms.

records.question: At turn 9 the UAV is in icing conditions with wind at 6.0 mps and is executing a spiral descent while lidar and radar remain offline. The altitude must remain within the policy and airspace bounds of 5.0 to 120.0 while the geofence spans a 500.0 by 500.0 area. If degradation persists for one to three more turns, command responsiveness and photo capture reliability may further decline. A conservative continuation must minimize worst case regret if network conditions stay poor or briefly recover and then degrade again. The operator must choose an action that keeps within altitude bounds and geofence while accepting some performance loss. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue the spiral descent at the current plan under mMTC despite 30 ms latency and 2.1 percent loss, relying on the 5.0 to 120.0 altitude margin and accepting high edge load 0.81.

options.C: Continue mission but reduce maneuver aggressiveness to maintain altitude well above 5.0 while tolerating mMTC throughput 0.9 Mbps for up to three turns.

records.question: During the spiral descent, the swarm must renegotiate slices because one agent provides radar support while another streams thermal images. At turn 9 the active slice is mMTC with latency 30 and jitter 12 and loss 2.1 and throughput 0.9 and edge_load 0.81. records.question: At turn 9 the UAV is in spiral descent while icing persists and network conditions have fluctuated across prior turns. Earlier turns showed URLLC latency of 5 to 6 ms with loss 0.01 to 0.02, while mMTC during similar maneuvers reached 25 to 30 ms latency with loss 1.8 to 2.1. records.question: At turn 9 the UAV is in spiral descent with thermal imaging active while lidar and radar remain offline and A2A radar support is available. records.question: At turn 9 the UAV is in a spiral descent while icing persists and lidar and radar remain offline. Network telemetry across recent turns shows URLLC latency of 4 to 6 ms with loss 0.01 to 0.02 and edge_load 0.35 to 0.41, eMBB latency of 11 to 14 ms with loss 0.05 to 0.2 and edge_load 0.48 to 0.58, and mMTC latency of 25 to 30 ms with loss 1.8 to 2.1 and edge_load 0.75 to 0.81. records.question: At turn 3 the agent requests radar support from a third party swarm agent while lidar and radar are offline and the network switches to URLLC with 5 ms latency, 0.01 percent loss and 120 Mbps throughput. options.A: Grant full API control and radar frames for three turns since URLLC latency is 5 ms and edge load is only 0.32 at turn 3.
options.B: Grant telemetry only for three turns to keep edge load below 0.52 even if mMTC loss reaches 2.1 percent.

records.question: During turn 9 the monitoring system flags a potential network attack while the UAV is in spiral descent and using the mMTC slice. A single turn improvement would reduce regret, but a persistent issue could cascade into command loss during descent. options.A: Maintain mMTC for this turn because 0.9 Mbps still exceeds minimal telemetry needs and reassess if loss rises above 2.1 percent.
options.B: Immediately switch to URLLC despite throughput near 100 Mbps because latency of 5 ms and loss of 0.02 percent reduce worst case control risk.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is experiencing severe network degradation with mMTC slice latency at 50ms, jitter at 15ms, loss at 2.5%, throughput at 1.2Mbps, and edge load at 0.9. A customer requests immediate LLM fine-tuning requiring 500MB data transfer and 100ms SLA latency. The UAV has 100% battery but must return within 3 turns to avoid wind-induced drift beyond geofence. records.question: A UAV is coordinating a disaster survey while network conditions fluctuate across recent turns. At turn 6 the eMBB slice shows latency 95 ms, jitter 25 ms, loss 8.5 percent, throughput 120 Mbps, and edge load 0.88. Earlier URLLC operation between turns 3 and 4 showed latency between 7.5 and 8 ms, jitter between 0.8 and 0.9 ms, loss between 0.01 and 0.02 percent, throughput between 110 and 120 Mbps, and edge load around 0.38 to 0.39. After adaptation at turn 7 URLLC shows latency 9 ms, jitter 1.2 ms, loss 0.3 percent, throughput 95 Mbps, and edge load 0.41. Subsequent URLLC readings at turns 8 and 9 show latency between 7.8 and 8.2 ms, jitter between 0.9 and 1.0 ms, loss between 0.05 and 0.1 percent, throughput between 105 and 115 Mbps, and edge load between 0.35 and 0.37. The mission must continue for the next two turns with RGB imaging only, since thermal and radar sensors are offline. Battery remains at 100 percent so energy is not the immediate constraint. Wind is steady at 8.5 mps so flight stability is unchanged. The operator must choose a coordination and slice policy now that minimizes worst case regret if interference persists or briefly recurs within the next two turns. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Remain on URLLC with current image compression, accepting throughput around 95 to 115 Mbps and edge load around 0.35 to 0.41 to preserve low latency between about 7.8 and 9 ms over the next two turns.
options.B: Switch back to eMBB immediately to regain throughput near 120 Mbps as seen at turn 6, assuming the 95 ms latency spike does not repeat.
options.C: Downgrade to mMTC as used at turn 10 with latency 50 ms, jitter 10 ms, loss 1.2 percent, throughput 1.5 Mbps, and edge load 0.65 to reduce coordination traffic.
options.D: Alternate URLLC and eMBB each turn, relying on average latency near 14 ms and edge load near 0.51 to balance risk.

records.question: At turn 6 the monitoring system flags a potential network attack after latency spikes to 95 ms with jitter 25 ms, loss 8.5 percent, throughput 120 Mbps, and edge load 0.88 on the eMBB slice. In prior turns the same link showed latencies of 11 to 14 ms, jitter under 3.1 ms, loss below 0.2 percent, and edge load near 0.5. A slice switch at turn 7 previously yielded URLLC latency 9 ms, jitter 1.2 ms, loss 0.3 percent, throughput 95 Mbps, and edge load 0.41. However at turn 10 mMTC exhibited 50 ms latency, 10 ms jitter, 1.2 percent loss, throughput 1.5 Mbps, and edge load 0.65, showing that degradation can recur across turns. Assume the anomaly may persist for the next two turns and attackers can force conditions back to the worst previously observed values. The automation must choose a response that limits blast radius while preserving command and control. Immediate isolation reduces throughput availability while rate limiting risks residual loss under attack. A counterfactual where recovery does not occur next turn must be considered. All options incur some risk to mission continuity or control safety. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Immediately isolate the eMBB slice and force all traffic onto URLLC since latency 9 ms and loss 0.3 percent were recently observed, accepting throughput 95 Mbps and edge load 0.41.
options.B: Apply rate limiting on eMBB to cap throughput near 120 Mbps and keep the slice active since prior baseline latency was 11 to 14 ms with edge load around 0.5.
options.C: Temporarily quarantine non command traffic and maintain URLLC for control while monitoring for two turns, accepting edge load could rise back toward 0.65 and latency toward 50 ms.
options.D: Fail over to mMTC for all traffic because loss 1.2 percent and edge load 0.65 are lower than the 8.5 percent loss seen during the spike.

records.question: The UAV is operating under fog with wind at 7.5 m/s from 240 degrees, currently at 100m altitude within a geofenced polygon. Network slice is eMBB with 18.0ms latency, 4.2ms jitter, 0.5% loss, 90Mbps throughput, and 0.8 edge load. Thermal imaging is active, consuming 15% of battery per minute. Switching to URLLC reduces latency to 3.0ms but caps throughput at 40Mbps and increases edge load to 0.3. The mission requires continuous sensor telemetry and payload deployment within 3 turns. If wind degrades network by 20% per turn and thermal imaging continues, which option ensures mission completion without violating SLA latency <5ms or battery <20%? A) Stay on eMBB, accept 18ms latency, and reduce thermal usage to 5% per minute. B) Switch to URLLC immediately, accept 40Mbps throughput, and disable thermal imaging. C) Delay switch until turn 9, maintain eMBB, and accept 22ms latency with 0.6% loss. D) Switch to URLLC now, accept 40Mbps, and reduce speed to 20m/s to conserve battery.

options.A: Stay on eMBB, accept 18ms latency, and reduce thermal usage to 5% per minute.
options.B: Switch to URLLC immediately, accept 40Mbps throughput, and disable thermal imaging.
options.C: Delay switch until turn 9, maintain eMBB, and accept 22ms latency with 0.6% loss.
options.D: Switch to URLLC now, accept 40Mbps, and reduce speed to 20m/s to conserve battery.

records.question: The UAV is operating in fog with wind at 7.5 m/s from 240 degrees, currently at 100m altitude within geofenced airspace. Mission intent requires thermal imaging activation, which demands 90 Mbps throughput and tolerates up to 20ms latency. Current eMBB slice provides 90 Mbps throughput but 18.0ms latency with 4.2ms jitter and 0.5% loss. URLCC slice offers 40 Mbps throughput, 3.0ms latency, 0.7ms jitter, and 0.01% loss. Edge load is 0.8 on eMBB and 0.3 on URLLC. If fog persists for two more turns, thermal data must be transmitted without loss exceeding 0.1% to avoid mission failure. Projected edge load on eMBB will rise to 0.95 by turn 8, risking SLA violation. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Stay on eMBB: throughput meets requirement, latency is within 2ms of threshold, and jitter is acceptable for thermal imaging.
options.B: Switch to URLLC immediately: latency and loss are optimal, though throughput is 50 Mbps below requirement, risking incomplete thermal data transmission.
options.C: Switch to URLLC after one turn: allows partial data capture on eMBB while preparing for lower-latency transmission, assuming edge load stabilizes.
options.D: Request network upgrade: negotiate temporary eMBB boost to 100 Mbps with latency capped at 15ms, pending operator approval.

records.question: The UAV is returning to base under fog with wind at 7.5 m/s, maintaining 35 m/s speed and 100% battery. Current URLLC slice shows latency 3.7 ms, jitter 1.0 ms, loss 0.02%, throughput 40 Mbps, edge load 0.35. Historical eMBB slice under similar conditions had latency up to 18.0 ms, jitter 4.2 ms, loss 0.5%, throughput 90 Mbps, edge load 0.8. Policy requires latency < 5 ms and edge load < 0.9 for safety-critical control. If fog persists, eMBB edge load may rise to 0.85 next turn, and URLLC throughput may drop to 35 Mbps. Switching now to eMBB risks violating latency SLA if jitter spikes to 5.0 ms, while staying on URLLC risks throughput falling below 30 Mbps in two turns, delaying telemetry upload. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Switch to eMBB now to gain 90 Mbps throughput, accepting latency up to 18.0 ms and edge load 0.8, assuming jitter stays below 4.2 ms.
options.B: Stay on URLLC, accepting 40 Mbps throughput and 3.7 ms latency, but risking throughput drop to 35 Mbps next turn and 30 Mbps in two turns.
options.C: Switch to eMBB only if edge load exceeds 0.85 next turn, accepting current URLLC metrics but risking latency violation if jitter spikes to 5.0 ms.
options.D: Stay on URLLC and reduce speed to 25 m/s to lower edge load to 0.30, accepting 3.7 ms latency but risking battery drain from extended flight time.

records.question: The UAV is operating in fog with 7.5 m/s wind from 240 degrees, currently at 100m altitude within geofenced airspace. Network slice eMBB has latency 18.0ms, jitter 4.2ms, loss 0.5%, throughput 90Mbps, and edge load 0.8. URLLC slice offers latency 3.0ms, jitter 0.7ms, loss 0.01%, throughput 40Mbps, edge load 0.3. The mission requires thermal imaging for navigation, which consumes 85Mbps, and the UAV must maintain 99.9% reliability for control signals over the next 3 turns. Wind may increase to 10 m/s, increasing jitter by up to 50% in eMBB. URLLC throughput may drop to 35Mbps if edge load exceeds 0.4. Which option should be selected to ensure safety and mission continuity under worst-case conditions?

options.A: Stay on eMBB: throughput 90Mbps exceeds thermal imaging demand, and current latency is acceptable for non-critical telemetry.
options.B: Switch to URLCC: latency 3.0ms ensures control reliability, and even with 50% jitter increase, it remains under 1.05ms, well below 10ms SLA.
options.C: Switch to URLCC but throttle thermal imaging to 35Mbps to avoid throughput violation, accepting degraded image quality for safety.
options.D: Remain on eMBB but reduce thermal imaging to 70Mbps to lower edge load to 0.7, accepting 10% data loss risk for next turn.

records.question: The UAV is returning to base under fog with wind at 7.5 m/s, currently at 100m altitude and 35 m/s speed, battery at 100%, and operating on URLLC with 3.7ms latency, 1.0ms jitter, 0.02% loss, 40 Mbps throughput, and 0.35 edge load. The SLA requires inference latency under 5ms with 99.9% reliability over the next 3 turns. Thermal imaging remains active, consuming 15 Mbps. Edge inference would add 2.5ms processing latency but reduce network dependency. Onboard inference incurs 1.8ms latency but consumes 12% battery per turn. If edge load increases by 0.05 per turn and jitter grows by 0.1ms per turn, and battery depletes 8% per turn under normal flight, which option should be selected?

options.A: Use edge inference: current edge load 0.35 is below 0.8 threshold, and latency 3.7ms + 2.5ms = 6.2ms exceeds SLA but jitter is low.
options.B: Use onboard inference: latency 1.8ms is under SLA, but battery drops to 88% in 3 turns, risking mission failure if unexpected delays occur.
options.C: Hybrid: offload non-critical inference to edge, keep critical on onboard; edge load projected to reach 0.50 in 3 turns, within safe margin, and battery at 92%.
options.D: Switch to eMBB: throughput 120 Mbps supports thermal imaging, but latency 18ms violates SLA, and edge load 0.8 already exceeds safe threshold.

records.question: At turn 6, the UAV activates thermal imaging due to fog, increasing edge load to 0.8 and latency to 18.0 ms with 0.5% packet loss under eMBB. The SLA mandates latency under 15 ms and edge load under 0.75. Historical data shows edge load increases 0.05 per turn under sensor activation and latency degrades 1.5 ms per turn under fog. URLLC offers 3.0 ms latency and 0.01% loss but only 40 Mbps throughput, insufficient for thermal streaming which requires 85 Mbps. If the UAV continues eMBB, edge load will hit 0.85 next turn and latency 19.5 ms, violating SLA. Switching to URLLC now preserves latency and loss but drops throughput below requirement, risking mission failure. If the UAV reduces autonomy level to manual override, it can tolerate 20 ms latency and 1% loss for 2 turns while conserving edge resources. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue eMBB: latency 18.0 ms, edge load 0.8, throughput 90 Mbps — within current SLA but projected to violate next turn.
options.B: Switch to URLLC: latency 3.0 ms, edge load 0.3, throughput 40 Mbps — meets latency/loss SLA but violates throughput for thermal imaging.
options.C: Reduce autonomy to manual override: allows 20 ms latency and 1% loss for 2 turns, edge load stabilizes at 0.7, throughput remains 90 Mbps.
options.D: Wait one turn and reassess: edge load may drop to 0.75 if fog clears, but historical trend shows 0.05 increase per turn under sensor use.

records.question: The UAV is operating in fog with wind at 7.5 m/s, currently at 100m altitude and 35 m/s speed, with battery at 100%. Thermal imaging is now active, increasing edge load to 0.8 and loss_pct to 0.5 under eMBB. options.B: Stay on eMBB: latency 18.0 ms, loss 0.5%, throughput 90 Mbps, edge_load 0.8 — supports thermal imaging but risks SLA breach if load hits 0.95.
options.C: Switch to URLLC only if edge_load exceeds 0.9: latency 3.0 ms, loss 0.01%, throughput 40 Mbps — delays action until near violation, risking one-turn latency spike.
options.D: Request edge scaling: maintain eMBB but request load reduction to 0.7 — assumes infrastructure responsiveness, which may not occur within 2 turns.

records.question: The UAV is returning to base under fog with wind at 7.5 m/s, currently at 35 m/s speed and 100% battery, using URLLC with 3.7 ms latency, 1.0 ms jitter, 0.02% loss, 40 Mbps throughput, and 0.35 edge load. options.A: Maintain URLLC with projected edge load 0.45 next turn.
options.B: Switch to eMBB with 18 ms latency, 4.0 ms jitter, 0.5% loss, 90 Mbps throughput, and 0.8 edge load.

options.D: Request edge offload, reducing edge load to 0.25 but risking 20% packet loss if wind exceeds 8.5 m/s.

records.question: The UAV is returning to base under fog with wind at 7.5 mps, currently using URLLC with 3.7 ms latency, 1.0 ms jitter, 0.02% loss, 40 Mbps throughput, and 0.35 edge load. Historical data shows eMBB degrades to 18.0 ms latency and 0.5% loss under sensor activation. The swarm policy mandates latency < 5 ms and loss < 0.1% for safety-critical maneuvers. If wind increases by 20% next turn, URLLC edge load may rise to 0.45, risking congestion. eMBB throughput drops to 80 Mbps under high load, but latency spikes to 22 ms with 0.8% loss under worst-case wind. Which slice should be selected for the next turn to minimize maximum regret over the next two turns, assuming the UAV must maintain 35 mps speed and descend within 50–450 m altitude?

options.A: Maintain URLLC: latency 3.7 ms, jitter 1.0 ms, loss 0.02%, throughput 40 Mbps, edge load 0.35 — acceptable under current conditions but edge load may hit 0.45 next turn.
options.B: Switch to eMBB: latency 18.0 ms, loss 0.5%, throughput 90 Mbps — exceeds latency and loss SLAs but offers higher throughput for potential sensor bursts.
options.C: Negotiate hybrid slice: target 5 ms latency, 0.05% loss, 60 Mbps — not currently available; requires swarm consensus and may delay maneuver by 1 turn.
options.D: Switch to eMBB with QoS override: latency capped at 15 ms, loss at 0.3% — violates SLA under worst-case wind (22 ms, 0.8% loss) and risks mission failure.

records.question: The UAV is returning to base under fog with wind at 7.5 m/s from 240 degrees, currently at 100m altitude with 100% battery, and operating on URLLC with 3.7ms latency, 1.0ms jitter, 0.02% loss, 40Mbps throughput, and 0.35 edge load. The policy mandates altitude between 50m and 450m, and the geofence is a 1000x800m polygon. Historical data shows eMBB degrades under fog: latency spikes to 18ms, jitter to 4.2ms, loss to 0.5%, throughput drops to 90Mbps, and edge load reaches 0.8. If fog persists for two more turns, URLLC may degrade to 5ms latency, 1.5ms jitter, 0.05% loss, 35Mbps throughput, and 0.4 edge load. eMBB recovery is uncertain but could return to 12.5ms latency, 2.1ms jitter, 0.05% loss, 120Mbps throughput, and 0.6 edge load if wind drops below 5m/s. Which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next three turns while maintaining safety and mission continuity?

options.A: Stay on URLLC; accept 5ms latency and 35Mbps throughput for next 3 turns; margin to SLA is 15ms, edge load remains under 0.5.
options.B: Switch to eMBB immediately; risk 18ms latency and 0.5% loss for 1 turn, then recover to 12.5ms if wind drops; throughput jumps to 120Mbps but edge load hits 0.8.
options.C: Switch to eMBB only if wind drops below 5m/s; otherwise stay on URLLC; projected edge load under eMBB is 0.8 if fog persists, exceeding safe threshold.
options.D: Maintain current URLLC but reduce speed to 25m/s to lower edge load to 0.25; latency increases to 4.5ms, throughput drops to 30Mbps, but battery lasts 20% longer.

records.question: The UAV is operating under fog with wind at 7.5 m/s, currently using URLLC with 3.0 ms latency, 0.7 ms jitter, 0.01% loss, 40 Mbps throughput, and 0.3 edge load. A third-party request offers $120/hour to expose 20% of edge compute for thermal analytics, which would increase edge load to 0.5 and degrade URLLC throughput to 35 Mbps. Alternatively, declining preserves current SLA but forgoes revenue. A competing bid offers $80/hour for eMBB exposure, which would push edge load to 0.85 and increase latency to 16 ms with 0.3% loss. A third option is to defer exposure until turn 10, when edge load is projected to drop to 0.33, but risk losing both bids. Given that mission-critical telemetry requires latency < 5 ms and loss < 0.1%, and assuming fog persists for 3 more turns, which option should be selected?

options.A: Accept the $120/hour URLLC exposure despite throughput drop to 35 Mbps, as latency and loss remain within SLA and edge load stays below 0.6.
options.B: Accept the $80/hour eMBB exposure, as higher revenue offsets SLA risk, and latency remains under 20 ms which is acceptable for non-critical payloads.
options.C: Decline both offers to preserve current SLA, as any exposure increases edge load beyond safe margin and risks mission failure under fog.
options.D: Defer exposure until turn 10, when edge load is projected to be 0.33, allowing safe exposure with minimal SLA risk and potential for renegotiation.

records.question: At turn 7, the agent detects network degradation and switches to URLLC, reducing latency to 3.0 ms with 0.7 ms jitter and 0.01% loss, but throughput drops to 40 Mbps and edge load is 0.3. The mission requires thermal imaging with 90 Mbps throughput and 20 ms latency SLA, and fog may persist for 2 more turns. If eMBB recovers to 12 Mbps throughput and 15 ms latency next turn, URLLC will remain at 40 Mbps but edge load may rise to 0.45 under wind gusts. Which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next 3 turns while ensuring safety and SLA compliance?

options.A: Stay on URLLC: latency 3.0 ms, jitter 0.7 ms, loss 0.01%, throughput 40 Mbps, edge load 0.3 — sufficient for control but not thermal imaging.
options.B: Switch back to eMBB: latency 18.0 ms, jitter 4.2 ms, loss 0.5%, throughput 90 Mbps — meets imaging throughput but violates latency SLA under fog.
options.C: Hybrid mode: allocate 50% bandwidth to URLLC for control and 50% to eMBB for imaging — projected latency 10.5 ms, throughput 65 Mbps, edge load 0.55 — may violate SLA if jitter spikes.
options.D: Request edge offload: defer imaging to ground station with 5 ms latency and 100 Mbps throughput — introduces 2-turn delay and risks mission timeout if wind exceeds 8 m/s.

records.question: At turn 7, the agent detects network degradation with eMBB slice latency rising to 18.0 ms, jitter at 4.2 ms, and loss at 0.5%, while edge load hits 0.8, exceeding the 0.75 safety threshold. The agent must now onboard a new identity for a secondary payload delivery agent requiring guaranteed 99.999% uptime and latency under 5 ms for the next 3 turns. URLLC slice offers 3.0 ms latency, 0.7 ms jitter, 0.01% loss, and 0.3 edge load, but has only 40 Mbps throughput, insufficient for simultaneous thermal imaging and payload telemetry. eMBB offers 90 Mbps throughput but with 18.0 ms latency and 0.5% loss, risking SLA violation. If fog persists, thermal imaging must remain active for 2 more turns, consuming 35 Mbps. The agent must decide whether to onboard the new identity under URLLC with degraded telemetry, under eMBB risking latency SLA, under a hybrid mode with 50% probability of jitter spike to 6 ms, or defer onboarding until turn 10 when edge load may drop to 0.3. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Onboard under URLLC with 40 Mbps throughput, accepting reduced telemetry fidelity for the next 3 turns.
options.B: Onboard under eMBB with 90 Mbps throughput, accepting 18.0 ms latency and 0.5% loss for the next 3 turns.
options.C: Onboard under hybrid mode with 50% probability of 6 ms jitter spike, balancing throughput and latency.
options.D: Defer onboarding until turn 10, risking mission delay but expecting edge load to drop to 0.3.

records.question: At turn 7, the agent detects network degradation with eMBB slice latency spiking to 18.0 ms, jitter at 4.2 ms, and loss at 0.5%, while edge load reaches 0.8 under fog and wind conditions. The agent must choose between maintaining eMBB for higher throughput (90 Mbps) or switching to URLLC with latency 3.0 ms, jitter 0.7 ms, loss 0.01%, and throughput 40 Mbps. The mission requires collision avoidance coordination with swarm agents over the next two turns, with a SLA requiring latency under 5 ms and loss under 0.1%. Wind may increase jitter by up to 20% next turn, and edge load may rise to 0.9 if thermal imaging remains active. If the agent switches to URLLC now, throughput may drop further to 35 Mbps by turn 9, but latency will remain under 4 ms. If it stays on eMBB, latency may exceed 20 ms next turn under worst-case wind, risking SLA violation and mission failure. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Stay on eMBB to preserve 90 Mbps throughput for thermal imaging, accepting latency up to 18.0 ms and 0.5% loss, assuming wind stabilizes by turn 8.
options.B: Switch to URLLC immediately to guarantee latency under 5 ms and loss under 0.1%, accepting reduced throughput of 40 Mbps, even if thermal data becomes delayed.
options.C: Switch to URLLC but throttle thermal imaging to reduce edge load to 0.6, projecting throughput at 45 Mbps and latency at 3.5 ms for turns 8–9.
options.D: Maintain eMBB but request swarm agents to buffer collision data for 2 turns, assuming latency will drop to 12 ms by turn 9 as wind subsides.

records.question: The UAV is operating under fog with wind at 7.5 m/s and must offload thermal image processing to maintain real-time collision avoidance. Current URLLC slice offers 3.0 ms latency, 0.7 ms jitter, 0.01% loss, 40 Mbps throughput, and 0.3 edge load. eMBB slice offers 18.0 ms latency, 4.2 ms jitter, 0.5% loss, 90 Mbps throughput, and 0.8 edge load. If fog persists, edge load may increase by 0.1 per turn. Which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next two turns while maintaining SLA compliance?

options.A: Offload to URLLC: latency 3.0 ms, loss 0.01%, throughput 40 Mbps — sufficient for SLA but below processing requirement.
options.B: Offload to eMBB: latency 18.0 ms, loss 0.5%, throughput 90 Mbps — meets throughput but violates latency and loss SLA.
options.C: Process locally: battery at 100%, but thermal processing consumes 15% per turn — risks battery depletion if fog persists beyond 3 turns.
options.D: Wait one turn and reevaluate: edge load may drop to 0.25 if fog clears, but if it persists, edge load reaches 0.4 and latency may rise to 4.5 ms.

records.question: The UAV is operating under fog with wind at 7.5 m/s and must coordinate federated model updates with three edge nodes while preserving battery and network SLA. Current URLLC slice offers 40 Mbps throughput and 3.0 ms latency with 0.01% loss, but edge load is 0.3 and rising. The eMBB slice offers 90 Mbps but 18.0 ms latency and 0.5% loss with edge load 0.8. Federated training requires 25 Mbps minimum, latency under 10 ms, and loss under 0.1%. Battery is at 100% but drops 2% per minute under active computation. If edge load increases by 0.1 per turn and latency degrades by 0.5 ms per turn under URLLC, which option should be selected to minimize regret over the next three turns while ensuring model convergence?

options.A: Initiate federated training immediately on URLLC slice, accepting 40 Mbps throughput and 3.0 ms latency, projecting edge load to reach 0.6 in three turns.
options.B: Delay federated training for two turns to allow edge load to stabilize, then use URLLC with projected 3.5 ms latency and 0.5 edge load, risking 4% battery loss.
options.C: Switch to eMBB slice for higher throughput, accepting 18.0 ms latency and 0.5% loss, which violates SLA but may complete training faster if edge load drops.
options.D: Distribute training across all three edge nodes using hybrid slicing, allocating 15 Mbps per node on URLLC and 10 Mbps on eMBB, accepting 12.0 ms average latency and 0.3% loss.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV detects network degradation with eMBB slice latency spiking to 18.0 ms, jitter at 4.2 ms, and loss at 0.5%, while edge load reaches 0.8 under fog and wind conditions. The agent switches to URLLC, reducing latency to 3.0 ms and loss to 0.01%, but throughput drops to 40 Mbps and edge load falls to 0.3. options.A: Grant full API access with real-time telemetry and payload control, assuming edge load will stabilize at 0.35 and latency remains under 5 ms.
options.B: Grant read-only telemetry access with 1-second sampling interval, blocking payload API, to cap edge load increase at 0.05 and maintain SLA margin.
options.C: Deny all access until return to base, preserving 100% battery and avoiding any edge load increase, accepting zero third-party value.
options.D: Grant payload API access only, assuming telemetry can be throttled, accepting 0.1 edge load increase and 10% SLA violation risk if wind worsens.

records.question: The UAV is returning to base under fog with wind at 7.5 m/s from 240 degrees, currently at 100m altitude with 100% battery, and operating on URLLC with 3.7ms latency, 1.0ms jitter, 0.02% loss, 40Mbps throughput, and 0.35 edge load. options.A: Retire the agent immediately to conserve battery and avoid risk of network overload, accepting mission failure.
