URLLC slice offers 6 ms latency, 0.7 ms jitter, 0.01% loss, 140 Mbps throughput, and 0.33 edge load, but switching now risks 1.2 seconds of transient disconnection. eMBB slice has 14 ms latency, 3.1 ms jitter, 0.3% loss, 780 Mbps throughput, and 0.62 edge load, but may degrade further under thermal updrafts. mMTC will degrade further next turn to latency 60 ms, jitter 22 ms, loss 3.5%, throughput 0.7 Mbps, edge load 0.95. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Switch to URLLC now despite 1.2s disconnection risk; worst-case latency 6ms + 1.2s = 1206ms exceeds SLA but recovers before landing.
options.B: Stay on mMTC; current latency 55ms exceeds SLA but may be acceptable if landing telemetry tolerates 55ms for 1 turn.
options.C: Switch to eMBB; latency 14ms is under SLA, throughput 780Mbps supports telemetry, and edge load 0.62 is sustainable for 1 turn.
options.D: Delay switch until next turn; mMTC degrades to 60ms latency, but URLLC will be available with 0.33 edge load and 6ms latency if no further degradation occurs.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is performing a close inspection under mMTC slice with latency 50ms, jitter 15ms, loss 2.1%, throughput 1.2Mbps, and edge load 0.88. The mission requires real-time anomaly confirmation within 3 turns, and the next turn’s edge load is projected to rise to 0.93 under mMTC. URLLC offers 7ms latency, 0.8ms jitter, 0.01% loss, 130Mbps throughput, but only 0.35 edge load capacity. eMBB provides 14ms latency, 3.1ms jitter, 0.3% loss, 780Mbps throughput, and 0.62 edge load. The SLA mandates latency under 20ms and loss under 0.5% for critical inspection. If wind gusts increase jitter by ±2ms next turn and edge load exceeds 0.95, the system will trigger a safety override. Which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next 3 turns while ensuring mission continuity?

options.A: Stay on mMTC: current latency is acceptable, and throughput is sufficient for image capture; edge load will peak at 0.93 next turn, below override threshold.
options.B: Switch to URLLC: latency and jitter are optimal, loss is negligible, and edge load is low; however, throughput may limit high-res image streaming if required.
options.C: Switch to eMBB: high throughput supports detailed imaging, latency is within SLA, but jitter may exceed 5ms next turn under wind uncertainty, risking SLA violation.
options.D: Delay inspection for 1 turn to wait for edge load to drop: projected edge load under mMTC will be 0.93 next turn, but if wind increases jitter by 2ms, latency may exceed 52ms, violating SLA.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is performing a close inspection with thermal anomaly detection, and the network has switched to mMTC slice with 50ms latency, 15ms jitter, 2.1% loss, and 1.2Mbps throughput, while edge load is at 0.88. The SLA requires inference latency under 30ms with ≤1% packet loss for safety-critical decisions. The next turn may see edge load rise to 0.95 if no action is taken, and jitter could spike to 25ms under thermal updrafts. Onboard inference takes 45ms but consumes 12% battery per inference, while edge inference under current conditions violates SLA. If the UAV continues to use edge inference, the probability of SLA violation in turn 8 increases to 87% under worst-case jitter and load. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Use edge inference now; current latency is 50ms but SLA allows 30ms, and edge load may drop next turn.
options.B: Switch to onboard inference; it exceeds SLA latency by 15ms but avoids 87% violation risk in turn 8 and preserves network for other UAVs.
options.C: Wait one turn; edge load is 0.88 now and may fall to 0.82 if traffic eases, reducing latency to 40ms with 1.5% loss.
options.D: Request URLCC slice; it offers 7ms latency and 0.01% loss but only 130Mbps throughput, which may not support video stream if reactivated.

records.question: At turn 10, the UAV is returning to home with edge load at 0.91, latency at 55 ms, jitter at 18 ms, and loss at 3.0%, operating on mMTC slice with throughput of 0.9 Mbps. The SLA mandates latency under 40 ms and edge load under 0.85 for autonomous navigation. Historical data shows edge load increased from 0.62 at turn 4 to 0.91 at turn 10, and latency rose from 14 ms to 55 ms. If the trend continues, edge load may reach 0.95 next turn, and latency may exceed 60 ms. The UAV must choose one of four autonomy modes: A) Maintain full autonomy with mMTC, accepting SLA violation risk; B) Switch to URLLC with 140 Mbps throughput, 6 ms latency, 0.7 ms jitter, 0.01% loss, and edge load 0.33, but risk sensor data loss due to low bandwidth; C) Reduce autonomy to manual override, using eMBB with 850 Mbps throughput, 12 ms latency, 2 ms jitter, 0.1% loss, and edge load 0.45, but delay mission completion by 2 turns; D) Enter safe hover with no autonomy, using no slice, consuming 0.5% battery per minute, and awaiting ground intervention. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Maintain full autonomy with mMTC, accepting SLA violation risk.
options.B: Switch to URLLC with 140 Mbps throughput, 6 ms latency, 0.7 ms jitter, 0.01% loss, and edge load 0.33, but risk sensor data loss due to low bandwidth.
options.C: Reduce autonomy to manual override, using eMBB with 850 Mbps throughput, 12 ms latency, 2 ms jitter, 0.1% loss, and edge load 0.45, but delay mission completion by 2 turns.
options.D: Enter safe hover with no autonomy, using no slice, consuming 0.5% battery per minute, and awaiting ground intervention.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is performing close inspection with thermal anomaly detection, and the network slice has switched to mMTC with latency 50ms, jitter 15ms, loss 2.1%, throughput 1.2Mbps, and edge load 0.88. The mission policy requires latency under 20ms for real-time control and loss under 0.5% for sensor integrity. The edge load is projected to increase by 0.05 per turn if mMTC persists, and the next turn’s latency could rise to 60ms under worst-case jitter. The UAV’s battery is at 85% and will deplete 3% per turn if offloading continues. Option A proposes switching to URLLC now, which has 9ms latency and 0.01% loss but only 110Mbps throughput, risking sensor data truncation. Option B continues mMTC, accepting 50ms latency and 2.1% loss, with edge load projected to hit 0.93 next turn, risking SLA violation. Option C delays offloading for one turn to collect more data, accepting 55ms latency and 3.0% loss next turn, with edge load at 0.91, but battery drops to 82%. Option D offloads to eMBB, which has 14ms latency and 0.3% loss but edge load 0.62, which may spike to 0.75 next turn under traffic, exceeding the 0.70 trust threshold. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Switch to URLLC now: latency 9ms, loss 0.01%, throughput 110Mbps, edge load 0.41 — ensures real-time control but risks data truncation.
options.B: Continue mMTC: latency 50ms, loss 2.1%, throughput 1.2Mbps, edge load 0.88 — violates latency and loss SLAs, edge load projected to 0.93 next turn.
options.C: Delay offloading one turn: latency 55ms, loss 3.0%, edge load 0.91, battery 82% — accepts higher risk now for potential future gain, but violates all SLAs.
options.D: Switch to eMBB: latency 14ms, loss 0.3%, edge load 0.62 — within SLA now, but edge load projected to 0.75 next turn, exceeding trust threshold of 0.70.

records.question: At turn 10, the UAV is returning to base with mMTC slice active, exhibiting latency 55ms, jitter 18ms, loss 3.0%, throughput 0.9Mbps, and edge load 0.91. The SLA requires latency ≤50ms, jitter ≤10ms, loss ≤1.0%, and throughput ≥1.0Mbps. Historical trends show edge load increased from 0.35 at turn 8 to 0.91 at turn 10, and jitter has risen 12% per turn since turn 7. If wind persists at 6.0m/s and thermal updrafts continue, worst-case jitter could increase by 15% next turn. The UAV must choose one of four actions: A) remain on mMTC with current settings, B) switch to URLLC immediately despite 125Mbps throughput cap, C) switch to eMBB with 780Mbps throughput but 14ms latency and 3.1ms jitter, or D) request emergency handoff to satellite with 200ms latency and 0.5% loss. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Remain on mMTC: current latency 55ms exceeds SLA by 5ms, but throughput 0.9Mbps is near threshold; edge load 0.91 suggests imminent congestion.
options.B: Switch to URLLC: latency 6ms and jitter 0.7ms meet SLA, but throughput capped at 125Mbps may limit telemetry upload during landing.
options.C: Switch to eMBB: throughput 780Mbps supports high-res video, but latency 14ms and jitter 3.1ms are within SLA; however, edge load may rise to 0.95 next turn.
options.D: Request satellite handoff: latency 200ms violates SLA, but loss 0.5% is acceptable; introduces 300ms round-trip delay for control commands.

records.question: At turn 7, the agent is performing a close inspection with thermal and RGB sensors active, requiring low latency for real-time control and moderate throughput for image capture. The current slice is mMTC with 50ms latency, 15ms jitter, 2.1% loss, and 1.2Mbps throughput, while edge load is 88%. URLLC offers 9ms latency, 1.1ms jitter, 0.01% loss, and 110Mbps throughput but is projected to reach 95% edge load by turn 9 if sustained. eMBB provides 14ms latency, 3.1ms jitter, 0.3% loss, and 780Mbps throughput but has 62% edge load now and may exceed 80% by turn 8. The mission requires at least 5Mbps throughput and under 20ms latency for the next two turns. If wind speed increases by 20% next turn, mMTC latency may spike to 70ms. Which slice should be selected to minimize maximum regret over turns 8–9?

options.A: Maintain mMTC: it is currently active and sufficient for basic telemetry, though throughput is below 5Mbps and latency may exceed 70ms if wind increases.
options.B: Switch to URLLC: latency and jitter are optimal, throughput exceeds 5Mbps, but edge load may hit 95% by turn 9, risking future slice preemption.
options.C: Switch to eMBB: throughput is abundant and latency is acceptable, but jitter and loss are higher, and edge load may exceed 80% by turn 8, risking SLA violation.
options.D: Negotiate hybrid slice: combine URLLC for control and eMBB for data, but no such slice exists in current policy and would require 3 turns to configure, delaying mission.

records.question: The UAV is returning to base under deteriorating network conditions with edge_load rising to 0.91 and latency spiking to 55ms on mMTC. The next turn requires initiating a final telemetry upload before landing, which demands at least 80Mbps throughput and latency under 20ms to avoid mission log corruption. URLLC offers 140Mbps and 6ms latency but is reserved for emergency landing commands. eMBB currently provides 850Mbps but latency has fluctuated between 11ms and 14ms with jitter up to 3.1ms. mMTC is overloaded with 0.9Mbps and 55ms latency. If edge_load increases by 0.05 per turn and latency degrades by 10% per turn under mMTC, which option should be selected to ensure log integrity while preserving landing safety?

options.A: Use eMBB with 850Mbps throughput and 14ms latency, accepting 3.1ms jitter as acceptable risk for log upload.
options.B: Switch to URLLC for 140Mbps and 6ms latency, overriding landing reserve to guarantee log integrity.
options.C: Wait one turn and retry on mMTC, projecting edge_load will reach 0.96 and latency 60.5ms, risking log corruption.
options.D: Use mMTC immediately with 0.9Mbps and 55ms latency, accepting 3.0% packet loss as tolerable for non-critical logs.

records.question: The UAV has completed its mission and is returning to base with 100% battery, but the edge compute load has risen to 0.91 under mMTC slice, with latency at 55ms and packet loss at 3.0%. A third-party analytics firm requests access to the thermal anomaly dataset for real-time processing, requiring at least 80Mbps throughput and latency under 20ms. The edge node can allocate compute resources to third parties only if the load remains below 0.95 and SLA latency is under 30ms. Historical data shows edge load increases by 0.03 per turn under mMTC and decreases by 0.08 per turn under URLLC. If the UAV switches to URLLC now, latency drops to 8ms but throughput falls to 125Mbps, and edge load drops to 0.39. If it remains on mMTC, edge load may exceed 0.95 in the next turn, risking SLA violation. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Expose compute under mMTC with current load 0.91, accepting 55ms latency and 3.0% loss, as throughput exceeds 80Mbps and load is still under 0.95.
options.B: Switch to URLLC immediately, accepting 125Mbps throughput and 8ms latency, which satisfies SLA and reduces edge load to 0.39, ensuring safety for next turn.
options.C: Delay exposure until next turn, assuming edge load will naturally drop under mMTC, and then expose under URLLC if load falls below 0.90.
options.D: Expose compute under URLLC but throttle throughput to 80Mbps to conserve edge resources, accepting 8ms latency and 0.39 load, while risking future load spikes.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is performing a close inspection under mMTC slice with latency 50ms, jitter 15ms, loss 2.1%, throughput 1.2Mbps, and edge load 0.88. The mission requires RAG-augmented decision-making for anomaly classification, which demands at least 10Mbps throughput and latency under 20ms to avoid cognitive degradation. The next turn may see edge load rise to 0.95 under worst-case thermal updrafts increasing compute demand. URLLC slice offers 130Mbps throughput and 7ms latency but is reserved for safety-critical commands and may be preempted if edge load exceeds 0.9. eMBB slice provides 870Mbps throughput but latency 14ms and jitter 3.1ms, with edge load already at 0.62 and projected to hit 0.75 next turn. Which network slice should be selected for RAG augmentation to minimize maximum regret over the next two turns?

options.A: mMTC: maintain current slice despite low throughput; edge load is already high but RAG can tolerate 1.2Mbps with local caching.
options.B: URLLC: switch immediately for guaranteed low latency; edge load is 0.88 now and may hit 0.95, risking preemption but ensuring RAG latency compliance.
options.C: eMBB: switch for high throughput; latency 14ms is under 20ms SLA, and projected edge load 0.75 is below 0.9 preemption threshold.
options.D: Hybrid: split RAG queries between URLLC for latency-critical parts and eMBB for bulk data; assumes no cross-slice coordination overhead.

records.question: At turn 7, the agent is performing close inspection with thermal anomaly detection, currently using mMTC slice with 50ms latency, 15ms jitter, 2.1% loss, and 1.2Mbps throughput under 88% edge load. The mission requires real-time sensor fusion within 20ms latency and <1% loss for identity validation. URLLC slice offers 9ms latency, 1.1ms jitter, 0.01% loss, and 110Mbps throughput at 41% edge load but may degrade to 12ms latency and 0.05% loss under wind gusts. eMBB slice provides 14ms latency, 3.1ms jitter, 0.3% loss, and 780Mbps throughput at 62% edge load but risks 25ms latency during congestion. If the next turn requires identity registration with SLA of 15ms latency and 0.5% loss, and edge load is projected to increase by 10% per turn, which option should be selected?

options.A: Stay on mMTC: current latency 50ms exceeds SLA by 35ms, but edge load is already high and migration may cause disruption.
options.B: Switch to URLLC: meets SLA with 9ms latency and 0.01% loss, but under worst-case wind gusts latency may reach 12ms and loss 0.05%, still within SLA; edge load will rise to 51% next turn.
options.C: Switch to eMBB: offers 14ms latency and 0.3% loss, meeting SLA marginally, but under congestion latency may spike to 25ms, violating SLA; edge load will reach 72% next turn.
options.D: Delay identity registration for one turn: allows edge load to stabilize, but mission SLA requires registration within current turn; risk of 100% mission failure if delayed.

records.question: At turn 7, the agent initiates a close inspection requiring high sensor fidelity, but the network slice has degraded to mMTC with 50ms latency, 15ms jitter, 2.1% loss, and 1.2Mbps throughput under 88% edge load. The next turn will involve transmitting a 12MB thermal image to the swarm agent, and the mission SLA requires latency under 20ms and loss under 0.5%. Wind conditions may increase edge load by 10% next turn. Option A routes via URLLC with 8ms latency but only 120Mbps throughput, risking buffer overflow if image size exceeds 10MB. Option B stays on mMTC, accepting 50ms latency and 2.1% loss, which violates SLA but avoids switching cost. Option C switches to eMBB with 14ms latency and 780Mbps throughput, but edge load is projected to hit 95% next turn, risking congestion. Option D queues the image for 2 turns, reducing edge load to 75% but delaying critical anomaly reporting. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Route via URLLC: 8ms latency, 120Mbps throughput, 0.02% loss, edge load 0.38 — sufficient for small images but risks overflow if image exceeds 10MB.
options.B: Stay on mMTC: 50ms latency, 1.2Mbps throughput, 2.1% loss, edge load 0.88 — violates SLA but avoids switching overhead.
options.C: Switch to eMBB: 14ms latency, 780Mbps throughput, 0.3% loss, projected edge load 0.95 — meets latency but risks congestion-induced failure next turn.
options.D: Queue for 2 turns: defers transmission, reduces edge load to 0.75, but delays anomaly report by 2 turns, risking mission failure if anomaly escalates.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is performing a close inspection with thermal anomaly detection, and the network has switched to mMTC slice with 50ms latency, 15ms jitter, 2.1% loss, and 1.2Mbps throughput, while edge load is at 0.88. The onboard AI model requires 45ms inference time and can tolerate up to 60ms total latency including network. The next turn may see edge load rise to 0.95 if no offload is performed, and jitter may increase to 20ms under thermal updrafts. Offloading to edge would add 12ms network latency but reduce inference time to 8ms; offloading to cloud adds 35ms latency but reduces inference to 3ms. The mission SLA allows up to 70ms total latency but penalizes loss above 1.5%. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Keep processing onboard: current latency 50ms + 45ms = 95ms exceeds SLA, but avoids network loss risk.
options.B: Offload to edge: 50ms + 12ms + 8ms = 70ms total, within SLA, but edge load may hit 0.95 next turn, risking 25% throughput drop.
options.C: Offload to cloud: 50ms + 35ms + 3ms = 88ms total, exceeds SLA, but cloud has 0.01% loss and infinite capacity.
options.D: Switch to URLLC slice: latency drops to 9ms, but throughput is only 110Mbps, insufficient for thermal stream, and edge load is 0.41, but may spike to 0.85 if others join.

records.question: The UAV is currently operating under mMTC slice with 50ms latency, 15ms jitter, 2.1% loss, and 1.2Mbps throughput while edge load is at 0.88. The federated learning model requires 100MB of data to be uploaded within 30 seconds to avoid staleness, and the next training window closes in 2 turns. The edge load is projected to increase by 0.05 per turn if no action is taken. URLLC slice offers 10ms latency and 130Mbps throughput but can only handle 3 concurrent uploads before exceeding its 0.5 edge load limit. eMBB slice has 800Mbps throughput but latency exceeds 10ms and jitter is unstable. If the UAV waits one more turn, edge load will reach 0.93, risking network collapse. Which option should be selected to ensure model update completion while minimizing regret over the next 2 turns?

options.A: Immediately switch to URLLC slice and upload the 100MB model update, accepting that edge load will rise to 0.44 and potentially block other critical control signals for 1 turn.
options.B: Wait one turn and attempt upload via eMBB slice, assuming jitter stabilizes to 2ms and throughput remains above 750Mbps, risking 30% data loss if conditions degrade.
options.C: Split the 100MB update into two 50MB chunks and upload sequentially via URLLC over the next 2 turns, accepting 20% latency penalty per chunk and risking edge load exceeding 0.5 by turn 9.
options.D: Abort federated update and log failure, preserving network stability for mission-critical telemetry, accepting model staleness penalty of 15% accuracy drop in next mission.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is performing a close inspection under mMTC slice with latency 50ms, jitter 15ms, loss 2.1%, throughput 1.2Mbps, and edge load 0.88. The thermal anomaly requires high-fidelity imaging, but the current slice cannot support real-time transmission. A third-party analytics agent requests full sensor API access to process images locally and return alerts. The policy allows exposure only if edge load remains below 0.9 for the next two turns and latency stays under 20ms. Historical data shows edge load increases by 0.03 per turn under mMTC and latency degrades by 5ms per turn. The URLLC slice is available but has only 130Mbps throughput, insufficient for raw video. The UAV battery is at 78% and will deplete 5% per turn if computation is offloaded. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Grant full API access under mMTC with a 2-turn SLA cap; accept 2.1% packet loss and 50ms latency as acceptable for image batch transfer.
options.B: Switch to URLLC slice and grant limited API access for metadata only; accept 130Mbps throughput limit and 8ms latency for alert transmission only.
options.C: Deny all exposure; retain local processing to avoid violating edge load >0.9 in turn 8 and latency >20ms in turn 9 under mMTC degradation.
options.D: Grant full API access under mMTC with a 1-turn extension; assume edge load stabilizes at 0.88 and latency degrades only 3ms per turn based on recent trend.

records.question: The UAV agent has completed its mission and is returning to base under deteriorating network conditions: edge_load has risen from 0.39 to 0.91 over the last two turns, latency has increased from 8ms to 55ms, and packet loss has climbed from 0.02% to 3.0%. The policy mandates that no agent may operate with edge_load above 0.95 or latency above 60ms for more than one consecutive turn. The agent’s battery is at 45% and descending at 5% per turn. If the agent remains active for one more turn, it risks violating SLA thresholds; if it retires now, it forfeits the ability to transmit final telemetry. A new agent can be instantiated at 10% battery cost but requires 2 turns to reach operational readiness. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Retire the current agent immediately to avoid SLA violation, accepting loss of final telemetry.
options.B: Keep the current agent active for one more turn to transmit telemetry, accepting 80% risk of SLA breach.
options.C: Instantiate a new agent now and keep the current agent active for one turn to bridge the gap.
options.D: Delay retirement until next turn, assuming edge_load will drop below 0.95 as it did previously.

records.question: The UAV has just completed a mission with telemetry showing edge_load peaked at 0.91 under mMTC during logging, while URLLC maintained lat_ms ≤ 8 and throughput_mbps ≥ 125. A customer requests LLM fine-tuning requiring 800 Mbps sustained throughput for 3 turns, with SLA allowing max 20 ms latency and 0.5% loss. Current edge_load is 0.91, and wind_mps=6.0 may cause 10% throughput degradation next turn. URLLC can support 140 Mbps max, eMBB supports 870 Mbps but has jitter_ms=3.1 and loss_pct=0.3. If edge_load exceeds 0.95, network stability degrades by 25% throughput per turn. Accepting now risks violating SLA in turn 12 if degradation persists. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Accept using eMBB now; current throughput 870 Mbps exceeds 800 Mbps, and jitter is acceptable for non-URLLC training.
options.B: Delay 1 turn; wait for edge_load to drop below 0.90, then accept using eMBB with projected throughput 783 Mbps (90% of 870) under wind degradation.
options.C: Accept using URLLC now; although throughput is only 140 Mbps, it guarantees latency < 8 ms and loss < 0.02%, meeting SLA strictly.
options.D: Reject outright; edge_load 0.91 is too high, and even eMBB cannot guarantee 800 Mbps for 3 turns under wind and load degradation.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is performing a close inspection with thermal anomaly detection, currently using mMTC slice with 50ms latency, 15ms jitter, 2.1% loss, and 1.2Mbps throughput, while edge load is at 0.88. The mission requires real-time AR overlay with <20ms latency and >50Mbps throughput for the next 3 turns. URLLC offers 7–10ms latency, 0.8–1.3ms jitter, 0.01–0.03% loss, and 105–130Mbps throughput but is projected to increase edge load to 0.95 by turn 9. eMBB offers 12–14ms latency, 1.8–3.1ms jitter, 0.05–0.3% loss, and 780–870Mbps throughput but may spike edge load to 0.97 under thermal updrafts. mMTC will degrade further to 60ms latency and 0.5Mbps throughput by turn 9 if not switched. Given the UAV’s battery is at 100% and wind speed is 6.0m/s, which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next 3 turns while ensuring AR overlay remains viable under worst-case network conditions?

options.A: Switch to URLLC immediately; it meets latency and throughput SLAs with edge load projected at 0.95 by turn 9, which is under the 0.98 safety threshold.
options.B: Stay on mMTC; it is currently active and avoids switching overhead, though throughput will drop to 0.5Mbps by turn 9, risking AR overlay failure.
options.C: Switch to eMBB; it provides 780Mbps throughput and 12ms latency, sufficient for AR, but edge load may hit 0.97 under wind-induced load spikes, nearing overload.
options.D: Delay decision until turn 8; monitor if edge load drops below 0.85, but risk AR overlay failure if mMTC degrades further before turn 9.

records.question: At turn 10, the UAV is returning to base with battery at 100%, but network slice has degraded to mMTC with latency 55ms, jitter 18ms, packet loss 3.0%, throughput 0.9Mbps, and edge load 0.91. The SLA requires latency < 20ms and loss < 1.0% for safe landing telemetry. Historical data shows URLLC slice recovers within 1 turn with 80% probability, but if not, edge load may spike to 0.98 next turn. If the UAV attempts landing now, there is a 15% chance of command loss; if it waits one turn, battery drops to 98% and wind may increase to 8.0m/s, risking instability. The mission policy allows aborting landing if risk exceeds 10%. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Initiate immediate landing using current mMTC slice, accepting 15% command loss risk and 0.91 edge load, since battery is full and wind is currently 6.0m/s.
options.B: Switch to URLLC slice immediately, even though it may not be available; if unavailable, wait one turn, accepting 2% battery loss and 8.0m/s wind risk, with 80% chance of SLA compliance.
options.C: Wait one turn without switching slices, relying on mMTC recovery; if edge load exceeds 0.95 next turn, abort landing; this preserves battery but risks 3.0% loss and 55ms latency persisting.
options.D: Abort mission and return to hover at 10m altitude, maintaining URLLC slice if available, consuming 1% battery per turn, until edge load drops below 0.85 or SLA is met, regardless of wind or time.

records.question: The UAV is currently operating under eMBB slice with 840 Mbps throughput, 13 ms latency, 2.0 ms jitter, 0.1% loss, and 0.5 edge load while executing lidar scans at 18 m/s with 100% battery. A customer requests immediate LLM fine-tuning via 6G Model Training-as-a-Service, requiring 500 Mbps sustained throughput, <10 ms latency, and <0.05% loss for 3 turns. The network may degrade to mMTC slice (1.2 Mbps, 130 ms, 1.5% loss) with 0.88 edge load in turn 12 if wind increases beyond 9 m/s, which has 30% probability. URLCC slice offers 115 Mbps, 8 ms, 0.02% loss, 0.39 edge load but cannot sustain 500 Mbps. eMBB may drop to 750 Mbps with 15 ms latency in turn 12 under icing. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Accept training now on eMBB with 840 Mbps, accepting 13 ms latency and 0.1% loss, assuming no degradation in next 3 turns.
options.B: Reject training and maintain current mission, preserving telemetry integrity and avoiding SLA violation risk under mMTC degradation.
options.C: Switch to URLCC slice immediately for lower latency (8 ms) and loss (0.02%), accepting throughput limitation (115 Mbps) and potential training failure.
options.D: Delay training for 2 turns to allow battery recharge and network stabilization, risking customer penalty but reducing edge load to 0.45.

records.question: The UAV is executing an immersive inspection mission under icing conditions with wind at 8.5 m/s from 240 degrees, currently at 25m altitude within a 10–120m bound. It has 100% battery and active RGB, LIDAR, and GNSS sensors, but thermal and radar remain offline. Network slice eMBB currently delivers 840 Mbps throughput at 13ms latency with 2.0ms jitter and 0.1% loss, while edge load is 0.50. A competing AR session requires 900 Mbps and 10ms latency SLA, and the next waypoint demands lidar scanning with 800 Mbps minimum throughput. If edge load exceeds 0.85, the system throttles all slices by 30%. Over the next two turns, wind may increase to 10.5 m/s, potentially raising jitter by 1.5ms and latency by 3ms. Which option should be selected to ensure mission continuity while minimizing regret across both turns?

options.A: Maintain eMBB slice; accept 13ms latency and 840 Mbps throughput; project edge load to reach 0.55 next turn and 0.60 in two turns; assume no wind degradation.
options.B: Switch to URLLC slice; accept 115 Mbps throughput and 8ms latency; project edge load to 0.39 next turn and 0.37 in two turns; ignore throughput constraint for lidar scan.
options.C: Switch to mMTC slice; accept 1.2 Mbps throughput and 130ms latency; project edge load to 0.88 next turn and 0.91 in two turns; assume throttling will not occur.

options.B: Switch to compressed position only updates over mMTC at 0.9 to 1.2 Mbps to tolerate 8.5 to 9.2 percent loss and avoid slice switching overhead.
