options.C: Schedule a constrained federated update with reduced payload using URLLC now and plan aggregation over the next turn, tolerating throughput as low as 90 Mbps.
options.D: Offload federated training to the edge aggressively because edge load dropped to 0.2 at turn 10 and loss on URLLC was only 0.04 pct then.

records.question: During hail and gusts, the UAV resumes thermal scanning after RGB degradation while flying at 28.0 mps at 50.0 m altitude inside a 30.0 to 350.0 m policy band. Across turns 7 to 11, URLLC latency ranges from 6 to 11 ms, jitter ranges from 1 to 2 ms, loss ranges from 0.04 to 0.12 pct, throughput ranges from 90 to 140 Mbps, and edge load ranges from 0.2 to 0.42. The perception task requires fused sensing to keep end to end latency under 12 ms with minimal false negatives during hover and immediate resumption. Thermal, lidar, and GNSS are available, while radar is offline and RGB is degraded by hail. Fusing more streams improves detection but increases load and risks congestion if edge load drifts upward by one more turn. If degradation persists for two more turns, the worst case assumes the highest observed latency and loss coincide with the highest observed edge load. A single stream reduces load but risks missed defects during motion at 28.0 mps when hover ends. The network can choose between different fusion strategies that trade throughput and robustness. Each option incurs some downside within the next three turns if conditions do not improve. Which sensing stream and fusion strategy should be selected?

options.A: Select thermal only on URLLC to minimize throughput near 90 Mbps and edge load near 0.32 while keeping latency near 9 ms.
options.B: Fuse thermal plus lidar on URLLC accepting throughput near 105 Mbps and edge load near 0.42 to improve detection.
options.C: Fuse thermal plus GNSS on eMBB using throughput near 800 Mbps and latency near 14 ms to offload the edge.
options.D: Fuse thermal plus lidar plus GNSS on URLLC pushing throughput toward 140 Mbps and edge load toward 0.42 for maximum robustness.

records.question: At turn 10, the UAV is returning to base under mMTC slice with latency 60ms, jitter 15ms, loss 0.6%, throughput 0.9Mbps, and edge load 0.4. The mission requires telemetry upload within 3 turns, with SLA latency cap of 50ms and minimum throughput of 1Mbps. Historical data shows eMBB slice has 20% probability of latency spiking to 110ms next turn, while URLLC slice has 10% chance of throughput dropping below 1Mbps due to edge load exceeding 0.35. If the UAV switches to eMBB now, projected edge load next turn is 0.55; if it stays on mMTC, edge load rises to 0.45. The UAV must complete telemetry upload before battery drops below 20%, which occurs in 4 turns. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Switch to eMBB immediately: current latency 20ms and throughput 700Mbps exceed SLA, and edge load 0.5 is acceptable for next turn.
options.B: Stay on mMTC: latency 60ms exceeds SLA but throughput 0.9Mbps is near minimum, and edge load 0.4 is low; switch only if latency exceeds 70ms next turn.
options.C: Switch to URLLC: latency 6ms and jitter 0.8ms are optimal, throughput 105Mbps exceeds minimum, and edge load 0.28 is safe for next turn.
options.D: Delay decision until turn 11: monitor network metrics and switch only if mMTC throughput drops below 0.8Mbps or latency exceeds 65ms.

records.question: At turn 5, the agent adapts to network degradation by adjusting the video stream and initiating handover monitoring. The current eMBB slice shows latency of 110 ms, jitter of 25 ms, loss of 1.8%, throughput of 620 Mbps, and edge load of 0.75. The URLLC slice offers 9 ms latency, 1.5 ms jitter, 0.1% loss, 95 Mbps throughput, and 0.35 edge load. The mission requires continuous video streaming for 3 more turns with a SLA of max 50 ms latency and 1% loss. The edge load is projected to increase by 0.1 per turn if eMBB is retained. Under worst-case jitter growth of +2 ms per turn and potential loss spike to 2.5%, which slice should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next 3 turns?

options.A: Retain eMBB: throughput supports high-res video, current latency is acceptable, and edge load is manageable for 1 turn.
options.B: Switch to URLLC: meets SLA latency and loss bounds, but throughput may limit resolution, and edge load will rise to 0.45 by turn 8.
options.C: Switch to mMTC: lowest edge load at 0.2, but latency 50 ms exceeds SLA, and throughput 1.2 Mbps is insufficient for video.
options.D: Negotiate hybrid slice: combine URLLC for control and eMBB for video, but no such slice exists in current policy and edge load would exceed 0.8.

records.question: At turn 9, the UAV detects an anomaly requiring immediate analysis using a 1.2GB model with 80ms inference latency on-device, but offloading to edge incurs 10ms latency with 0.1% loss and 0.32 edge_load, while cloud offload adds 45ms latency with 0.05% loss and 0.15 edge_load. The current URLLC slice has 10ms latency and 1.2ms jitter, but edge_load is projected to rise to 0.45 by turn 11 under worst-case traffic. Battery is at 68% and must remain above 20% for return. If the anomaly analysis fails, mission success drops by 40%. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Offload to edge: latency 10ms, edge_load 0.32, loss 0.1%, battery drain 3% per analysis
options.B: Offload to cloud: latency 45ms, edge_load 0.15, loss 0.05%, battery drain 1% per analysis
options.C: Run on-device: latency 80ms, no network dependency, battery drain 5% per analysis
options.D: Delay analysis until turn 11: edge_load may drop to 0.25, but risk 40% mission failure if anomaly escalates

records.question: The UAV agent has completed its inspection mission and is preparing to retire from active duty. Current telemetry shows battery at 35%, edge load at 0.5, and network slice eMBB with 700 Mbps throughput and 20 ms latency. Policy mandates retirement if battery drops below 20% or edge load exceeds 0.7 for two consecutive turns. Historical data shows battery depletes at 8% per turn under eMBB, and edge load increases by 0.1 per turn if no migration occurs. A backup agent is available but requires 3 turns to activate and consumes 15% battery during handover. If the UAV continues operating under eMBB, it will violate SLA in 2 turns due to edge load. If migrated to URLLC, throughput drops to 110 Mbps but edge load stabilizes at 0.3. If retired immediately, mission data must be offloaded via mMTC, which has 0.9 Mbps throughput and 60 ms latency, risking data loss if interrupted. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Retire immediately and offload data via mMTC, accepting 60 ms latency and 0.9 Mbps throughput to avoid edge load violation.
options.B: Migrate to URLLC slice now, accepting 110 Mbps throughput to stabilize edge load at 0.3 and extend operational window by 3 turns.
options.C: Continue under eMBB for one more turn to complete data compression, risking edge load violation in turn 12 and battery drop to 27%.
options.D: Activate backup agent immediately, consuming 15% battery during handover, and migrate data over URLLC to avoid both edge load and battery risks.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is operating under mMTC slice with 25ms latency, 10ms jitter, 1.2% loss, and 1.5Mbps throughput while edge load is at 95%. The mission requires inference for obstacle avoidance with a hard SLA of 30ms end-to-end latency and 0.5% max loss. Onboard inference consumes 12ms with 0% loss but reduces battery by 8% per inference cycle. Edge inference under current mMTC conditions risks violating SLA by 5ms worst-case and may drop frames due to loss. If the UAV continues streaming at reduced quality, edge load will rise to 98% next turn, increasing jitter to 15ms. Alternatively, switching back to URLLC would restore 6ms latency and 0.04% loss but requires 3 turns to re-establish stable connection, during which inference must run onboard. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Run inference onboard for next 3 turns to avoid SLA violation, accepting 8% battery drain per cycle and no network dependency.
options.B: Switch to URLLC immediately; accept 3-turn delay in stable connection but guarantee SLA compliance once reconnected.
options.C: Continue using mMTC edge inference; accept 5ms SLA margin and 1.2% loss, assuming edge load stabilizes at 95%.
options.D: Reduce inference frequency to once every 2 cycles to halve battery drain and network load, accepting 24ms latency per inference.

records.question: At turn 7, edge load reaches 0.95 under mMTC slice with 25ms latency and 1.2% loss, while URLLC slice shows 6ms latency and 0.04% loss at edge load 0.5. The UAV must maintain SLA of latency <10ms and loss <0.1% for critical control. Thermal sensor remains offline, and fog reduces RGB utility. If edge load increases by 0.05 per turn under current mMTC usage, and URLLC capacity allows only 2 concurrent control streams, what is the latest turn by which degradation must begin to avoid SLA violation? If degradation is delayed, projected edge load at turn 9 exceeds 1.0, risking total failure. Option A delays degradation until turn 8, assuming URLLC can absorb load. Option B initiates degradation at turn 7 by reducing autonomy to manual override. Option C switches to URLLC immediately but disables all non-critical telemetry. Option D maintains mMTC with reduced stream quality, accepting 10% higher jitter. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Delay degradation to turn 8, assuming URLLC can absorb load with 0.55 edge load projected.
options.B: Initiate degradation at turn 7 by reducing autonomy to manual override, accepting 20% slower response.
options.C: Switch to URLLC immediately but disable all non-critical telemetry, risking sensor fusion loss.
options.D: Maintain mMTC with reduced stream quality, accepting 10% higher jitter and 0.98 edge load by turn 8.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is operating under mMTC slice with 25ms latency, 10ms jitter, 1.2% loss, and 95% edge load while streaming low-bandwidth video in fog with 9.5m/s wind. The policy requires latency < 20ms and edge load < 90% for offloading trust. If the next turn projects 10% higher edge load and 5ms latency increase under worst-case wind persistence, and the thermal sensor remains offline, which option should be selected to avoid violating trust constraints while maintaining mission continuity? A: Continue mMTC offloading with current settings. B: Switch to URLLC slice despite 60Mbps throughput limit. C: Abort all offloading and process locally with 100% battery. D: Request eMBB slice with 110Mbps throughput but 18ms latency and 85% edge load.

options.A: Continue mMTC offloading with current settings.
options.B: Switch to URLLC slice despite 60Mbps throughput limit.
options.C: Abort all offloading and process locally with 100% battery.
options.D: Request eMBB slice with 110Mbps throughput but 18ms latency and 85% edge load.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is operating under mMTC slice with latency 25ms, jitter 10ms, loss 1.2%, throughput 1.5Mbps, and edge load 0.95. The SLA requires latency ≤10ms, loss ≤0.1%, and edge load ≤0.8. Wind speed is 9.5m/s from 270°, and the UAV is at 80m altitude with 100% battery. If the current degradation persists, the edge load will increase by 0.05 per turn due to fog-induced congestion. The next turn’s SLA violation probability is 80% under mMTC, 30% under eMBB, and 5% under URLLC. Switching to URLLC now incurs a 3-second handover delay and reduces throughput to 60Mbps, while eMBB offers 110Mbps but with 15ms latency and 0.2% loss. Which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next two turns?

options.A: Remain on mMTC: current metrics are acceptable under relaxed policy, and edge load may stabilize.
options.B: Switch to eMBB: higher throughput supports mission continuity, and latency is within 5ms of SLA.
options.C: Switch to URLLC: lowest violation probability and meets SLA bounds, despite handover delay.
options.D: Switch to URLLC after one turn: defer handover to avoid immediate throughput drop, assuming recovery.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is streaming RGB video under eMBB with 90 Mbps throughput, 18 ms latency, 6 ms jitter, and 0.5% loss, while edge load is at 0.85. The thermal sensor remains offline, and fog reduces visibility. The operator must now decide whether to expose edge compute capacity to a third-party analytics service that requires 1.2 Gbps sustained throughput and 10 ms latency SLA, with a 5% penalty for violation. The service offers $1200 per hour but requires 30% of current edge load. If the UAV continues streaming, edge load will rise to 0.98 next turn, risking SLA violation. If the UAV switches to mMTC, edge load drops to 0.95 but throughput falls to 1.5 Mbps, making third-party service impossible. If the UAV aborts streaming now, edge load drops to 0.5, allowing third-party service with 0.2 margin to SLA. If the UAV delays decision until turn 8, edge load may recover to 0.7 if network stabilizes, but fog may persist and degrade analytics accuracy. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Expose compute to third-party service immediately while continuing RGB stream, accepting 0.02 edge load margin and risking SLA penalty.
options.B: Abort RGB stream now and expose compute, achieving 0.2 edge load margin and full SLA compliance.
options.C: Switch to mMTC now, preserving edge load at 0.95 but forfeiting third-party revenue and analytics capability.
options.D: Delay decision to turn 8, hoping for network recovery to 0.7 edge load while risking SLA violation if fog persists.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is operating under mMTC slice with latency 25ms, jitter 10ms, loss 1.2%, throughput 1.5Mbps, and edge load 0.95. The thermal sensor remains offline, fog persists, and the next turn requires geofence validation and separation check under URLLC SLA of max 10ms latency and 0.1% loss. Projecting edge load increases by 0.05 per turn under current conditions, and jitter may spike to 15ms with 30% probability. If the UAV remains on mMTC, the next safety check will violate SLA with 80% probability; switching to URLLC now incurs 200ms handover delay but guarantees SLA compliance for the next two turns. Option A retains mMTC to preserve low bandwidth usage. Option B switches to URLLC immediately despite handover cost. Option C switches to eMBB for higher throughput but risks 18ms latency and 0.5% loss. Option D delays switch until turn 8, risking SLA violation if jitter spikes. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Retain mMTC to minimize bandwidth consumption and avoid handover delay.
options.B: Switch to URLLC immediately to guarantee SLA compliance for safety checks despite 200ms handover cost.
options.C: Switch to eMBB for higher throughput, accepting 18ms latency and 0.5% loss as within acceptable bounds.
options.D: Delay switch until turn 8, assuming jitter will not spike and SLA will be met.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV agent detects network degradation with latency at 25ms, jitter at 10ms, packet loss at 1.2%, and edge load at 0.95 while operating under mMTC slice. The thermal sensor remains offline, and fog persists with wind at 9.5 m/s from 270 degrees. The agent must now decide whether to re-authenticate under URLLC for critical control, remain on mMTC to preserve battery, switch to eMBB for sensor data recovery, or initiate emergency identity revocation due to SLA violation. The URLLC slice currently supports 60 Mbps throughput with 6ms latency and 0.04% loss, but edge load is projected to rise to 0.65 next turn if two more agents join. The eMBB slice offers 90 Mbps but with 18ms latency and 0.5% loss, and its edge load is already at 0.85. The UAV battery is at 100% but will deplete 15% per turn under high-bandwidth streaming. The mission SLA requires latency under 10ms and loss under 0.1% for control commands. What should the agent select to minimize maximum regret over the next two turns under worst-case network drift?

options.A: Re-authenticate under URLLC slice to ensure control latency under 10ms, accepting 15% battery drain per turn and projected edge load of 0.65 next turn.
options.B: Remain on mMTC slice to preserve battery, accepting 25ms latency and 1.2% loss, with edge load at 0.95 and no immediate SLA violation for non-control tasks.
options.C: Switch to eMBB slice to recover thermal sensor data, accepting 18ms latency and 0.5% loss, with edge load at 0.85 and 15% battery drain per turn.
options.D: Initiate emergency identity revocation due to SLA violation, grounding the UAV and forfeiting mission, with no further network or battery cost.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is operating under mMTC slice with latency 25ms, jitter 10ms, loss 1.2%, throughput 1.5Mbps, and edge load 0.95. The thermal sensor remains offline, and the RGB stream was downgraded to reduce bandwidth. The next 3 turns require federated model updates from 3 edge nodes with 800MB total data, each node having 15% battery and 200ms max allowable latency. The URLLC slice offers 6ms latency but only 60Mbps throughput, while eMBB offers 110Mbps but 18ms latency with 0.5% loss. If network degradation persists, the edge load may rise to 0.98 by turn 9. Which option should be selected to minimize regret over the next 3 turns while ensuring model convergence and battery safety?

options.A: Schedule federated updates over URLLC slice immediately, accepting 6ms latency and 60Mbps throughput, risking edge overload if load exceeds 0.97 by turn 9.
options.B: Delay updates until turn 9, using URLLC slice then, assuming edge load drops to 0.45 as in turn 10, but risking model staleness if latency exceeds 20ms.
options.C: Use eMBB slice now with 18ms latency and 110Mbps throughput, accepting 0.5% loss, but risking convergence failure if jitter exceeds 8ms in turn 8.
options.D: Split updates across URLLC and eMBB slices: 400MB over URLLC at 6ms, 400MB over eMBB at 18ms, balancing load but risking synchronization failure if one slice degrades.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is operating under mMTC slice with latency 25ms, jitter 10ms, loss 1.2%, throughput 1.5Mbps, and edge load 0.95, while thermal sensor remains offline and fog persists. The swarm agent requests full telemetry exposure for path recalculation, but the edge load is projected to exceed 0.98 in the next turn if throughput remains below 2Mbps. Regulatory policy mandates that third-party exposure must not exceed 80% edge load under SLA, and trust score for the swarm agent is 0.72, which degrades by 0.05 per turn under degraded network. If the UAV continues mMTC, projected edge load in turn 8 will be 0.98, violating SLA; switching to URLLC now would reduce latency to 6ms but cap throughput at 60Mbps, which may not sustain swarm coordination if fog worsens. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Grant full telemetry exposure under mMTC with current edge load 0.95, assuming recovery in turn 8.
options.B: Switch to URLLC slice and grant partial telemetry (excluding lidar and radar) to keep edge load under 0.80.
options.C: Deny all exposure until turn 8, when edge load is projected to drop to 0.5 under URLLC, despite swarm coordination delay.
options.D: Grant full exposure under URLLC with throughput capped at 60Mbps, accepting 0.85 edge load and 0.05 trust decay per turn.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV detects network degradation with latency spiking to 25ms, jitter at 10ms, packet loss at 1.2%, and edge load at 95%, while operating under mMTC slice. The policy mandates latency under 20ms for safety-critical control and loss under 0.5% for sensor telemetry. Historical data shows URLLC slice recovers within 2 turns but has max throughput of 60Mbps, while eMBB offers 120Mbps but with 18ms latency and 0.5% loss under fog. If the UAV must transmit emergency telemetry for 3 more turns before landing, and edge load is projected to increase by 0.05 per turn under current slice, which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret under worst-case degradation persistence?

options.A: Remain on mMTC slice; accept 25ms latency and 1.2% loss for 3 turns, risking telemetry corruption but preserving battery.
options.B: Switch to URLLC slice; accept 60Mbps throughput cap but guarantee latency under 6ms and loss under 0.04%, despite edge load rising to 0.55 next turn.
options.C: Switch to eMBB slice; leverage 120Mbps throughput for telemetry burst, accepting 18ms latency and 0.5% loss, with edge load projected at 0.90 next turn.
options.D: Initiate emergency landing immediately; terminate all telemetry, accept 0ms latency risk, but violate mission completion policy requiring 3-turn telemetry.

records.question: During swarm coordination, the focal UAV experienced slice changes from eMBB to URLLC and briefly to mMTC while executing maneuvers with other members. At turn 6 the network showed mMTC latency of 110 ms, jitter of 30 ms, loss of 3.0 percent, throughput of 0.9 Mbps, and edge load of 0.88. In earlier and later turns, URLLC showed latency between 7.5 and 9 ms, jitter between 0.7 and 1.2 ms, throughput between 100 and 130 Mbps, and edge load between 0.4 and 0.5. eMBB showed latency between 10 and 12 ms, jitter between 1.5 and 2 ms, throughput between 800 and 900 Mbps, and edge load between 0.3 and 0.35. Swarm collision avoidance requires consistent low latency for the next two turns, but slice fairness requires not monopolizing capacity if edge load remains high. There is uncertainty whether the elevated edge load of 0.88 will persist one more turn or drop back toward 0.5 as seen later. If the poor conditions persist, mMTC risks delayed coordination, while URLLC risks starving other swarm members due to limited throughput. If conditions recover, eMBB may suffice but has higher latency than URLLC. Considering worst case persistence for one to two more turns and minimizing maximum regret across the swarm, which slice selection should be made now?

options.A: Remain on mMTC with latency 110 ms and throughput 0.9 Mbps to be fair under edge load 0.88.
options.B: Switch to URLLC with latency near 8 ms and throughput around 110 Mbps despite edge load near 0.5.
options.C: Switch to eMBB with latency around 11 ms and throughput near 900 Mbps since edge load was 0.35 earlier.
options.D: Alternate between URLLC at 9 ms latency and eMBB at 10 ms latency each turn to balance fairness.

records.question: At turn 6 the UAV is mid mission with speed 18.0 mps and altitude 10.0 within the 5.0 to 60.0 bounds. Network conditions have degraded on mMTC with latency rising from 120 ms at turn 5 to 110 ms at turn 6, jitter fluctuating between 25 and 30 ms, loss increasing from 2.5 to 3.0 percent, throughput dropping from 1.2 to 0.9 Mbps, and edge load climbing from 0.85 to 0.88. Earlier turns on URLLC showed much lower latency between 7 and 9 ms and edge load between 0.4 and 0.5, but that recovery is uncertain if congestion persists. The thermal and radar sensors are already offline, reducing perception redundancy under autonomy. Battery is still at 100.0 percent, so immediate energy failure is unlikely, but continued network volatility could affect command responsiveness over the next two turns. If the mMTC degradation persists one more turn, worst case loss and jitter could remain at the higher observed values. If autonomy is not downgraded now, a delayed reaction may occur while executing maneuvers near the geofence polygon. Each possible action trades current performance against future safety margin under uncertain recovery. Considering worst case network behavior over the next one to three turns, which option should be selected?

options.A: Maintain full autonomy for the next two turns since latency improved from 120 to 110 ms and battery is 100.0 percent.
options.B: Immediately downgrade to supervised autonomy now to limit maneuver authority given loss up to 3.0 percent and edge load at 0.88.
options.C: Wait one more turn to see if URLLC conditions return, then downgrade only if latency exceeds the earlier 120 ms value.
options.D: Switch back to URLLC immediately and keep full autonomy because prior URLLC latency was below 9 ms and edge load below 0.5.

records.question: At turn 6 the AI scheduler has shifted traffic after observing instability across slices. The mMTC slice shows latency values of 110 and 120 ms across turns with jitter moving between 25 and 30 ms and loss rising from 2.5 to 3.0 percent while edge_load increases from 0.85 to 0.88. Earlier URLLC turns showed latency between 7 and 9 ms with jitter from 0.7 to 1.2 ms but edge_load also climbed from 0.4 to 0.5 after adaptations. The eMBB slice before and after degradation showed latency from 10 to 12 ms with jitter between 1.5 and 2 ms and edge_load around 0.3 to 0.35. The UAV speed is constant at 18.0 mps and battery remains at 100.0 percent so timing risk dominates energy risk. The scheduler must be reconfigured now and kept consistent for the next two turns assuming the worst case that mMTC conditions persist and URLLC load continues trending upward. If the decision is myopic it may succeed this turn but force reversal next turn when edge_load saturates or loss spikes. If uncertainty is ignored the apparent average performance hides the worst observed values. Each option below trades current latency against future regret under these constraints. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Lock all control and telemetry to URLLC based on 7 to 9 ms latency despite edge_load already reaching 0.5.
options.B: Maintain mMTC for consistency since throughput near 0.9 to 1.2 Mbps is sufficient and avoid scheduler churn despite 110 to 120 ms latency.
options.C: Reconfigure to eMBB for control and telemetry because latency stays near 10 to 12 ms with edge_load around 0.3 to 0.35 across turns.
options.D: Dynamically alternate URLLC and mMTC each turn to average latency and jitter values observed so far.

records.question: Across the last ten turns the operator considers exposing spare edge compute to third parties while the UAV mission is concluding. Telemetry shows edge_load moved from 0.3 and 0.35 early to 0.85 and 0.88 on mMTC at turns 5 and 6 before dropping back near 0.5 on URLLC. Latency simultaneously spiked to 120 ms and 110 ms on mMTC but stayed between 7 ms and 9 ms on URLLC. Throughput ranged from 0.9 to 1.2 Mbps on mMTC and from 100 to 130 Mbps on URLLC, while loss_pct ranged from 0.01 to 3.0. The marketplace proposal must hold for the next one to three turns in case the mMTC degradation persists or recurs. Third parties request bursty compute that would add load but are tolerant to reduced throughput. One option prioritizes immediate revenue by exposing resources during the current low edge_load snapshot. Another option conservatively limits exposure to protect future mission safety even if utilization looks safe now. A third option shifts exposure only to slices that recently looked stable without considering the worst observed values. A fourth option pauses exposure entirely, accepting opportunity cost but minimizing regret if poor conditions return. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Expose compute broadly now on all slices since edge_load has returned near 0.5 and URLLC latency is about 8 ms with throughput above 100 Mbps.
options.B: Expose compute only on URLLC because its latency stayed between 7 and 9 ms and loss_pct stayed below 0.03 despite prior mMTC congestion.
options.C: Expose compute on eMBB only because it previously delivered 800 to 900 Mbps at edge_load 0.3 to 0.35, assuming recovery persists.
options.D: Pause third party exposure for the next turns because worst case edge_load reached 0.88 with latency above 110 ms and could recur.

records.question: During swarm coordination, the UAV must decide how to federate state with a peer collision avoidance agent while network conditions fluctuate across turns. At turn 4 the link used URLLC with latency 7 ms, jitter 0.7 ms, loss 0.01 percent and edge_load 0.42, which supported successful a2a coordination. At turns 5 and 6 the link degraded to mMTC with latency 120 ms then 110 ms, jitter 25 ms then 30 ms, loss 2.5 percent then 3.0 percent, throughput 1.2 Mbps then 0.9 Mbps and edge_load 0.85 then 0.88. The UAV altitude must remain within the policy bounds of 5.0 to 60.0 while traveling at 18.0 mps, so delayed collision updates can cause rapid boundary violations. The operator expects coordination to persist for the next two turns even if mMTC conditions continue. One option is to keep full-state federation to maximize shared awareness, another is to switch to minimal beacons, another is to pause federation until eMBB returns, and another is to force URLLC reservation. Jitter and loss are uncertain because they have already varied between turns 5 and 6. Under worst case assumptions, loss may remain at 3.0 percent and jitter at 30 ms for two more turns. A single turn view favors richer data, but multi turn regret depends on sustained edge_load and packet loss. Each choice risks either safety degradation or network collapse in the next two turns. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Maintain full state federation at 0.9 Mbps on mMTC because throughput is nonzero and edge_load 0.88 has not yet saturated.
options.B: Switch to minimal beacon federation assuming loss stays near 2.5 percent and latency improves from 110 ms next turn.
options.C: Pause federation until eMBB returns since latency was 10 ms with edge_load 0.3 at turn 10.
options.D: Downgrade to minimal beacon federation sized for URLLC class metrics even if the slice remains mMTC.

records.question: At turn 10 the operator considers scheduling a federated model update using data collected during the mission. Across turns 1 to 10 the network alternated between eMBB, URLLC, and mMTC with latency values of 7.5, 8, 9, 10, 11, and 12 ms and jitter between 0.8 and 30 ms. Throughput varied from 0.9 and 1.2 Mbps in mMTC to 800 and 900 Mbps in eMBB, while edge_load ranged from 0.3 to 0.88. Battery remains at 100 percent, so compute is not energy constrained, but edge congestion risk persists. The last two turns show URLLC at 7.5 and 8.5 ms latency with edge_load 0.4 and 0.48, while the immediately prior worst case showed mMTC at 110 to 120 ms latency and edge_load 0.88. Assume training requires two consecutive turns of acceptable connectivity and that degradation could persist for one more turn. A single turn plan would favor immediate aggregation, but a two to three turn horizon must consider regret if congestion returns. One option is to push a full federated round now on URLLC, another is to delay until stable eMBB reappears, another is to run local-only training with deferred aggregation, and another is to opportunistically aggregate on eMBB now. Each choice risks either wasted bandwidth, stalled learning, or future blockage. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Start a full federated aggregation immediately on URLLC using the current 7.5 to 8.5 ms latency and 100 to 130 Mbps throughput despite edge_load near 0.4 to 0.48.
options.B: Delay all federated activity until eMBB is confirmed again with 800 to 900 Mbps throughput and edge_load near 0.3 as seen at turns 1, 2, and 10.
options.C: Run local-only training now and defer aggregation until after two more turns to avoid the 0.88 edge_load and 110 to 120 ms latency seen in mMTC.
options.D: Opportunistically aggregate a partial update on eMBB at turn 10 with 10 ms latency and 800 Mbps throughput while accepting possible reversion to URLLC.

records.question: At turn 6 the operator monitors a digital twin while the UAV executes maneuvers under a degraded link. records.question: At turn 7 the UAV has rgb and lidar sensors ok while thermal and radar are offline, and the network has just recovered to URLLC with latency 9 ms and jitter 1.2 ms after two turns on mMTC with 120 ms then 110 ms latency and jitter up to 30 ms. records.question: During a disaster-response UAV mission, the agent observes that at turn 5 the network switches to mMTC with latency 120 ms, jitter 25 ms, loss 2.5 percent, throughput 1.2 Mbps, and edge load 0.85 while the UAV is flying at 18.0 mps with battery at 100 percent. records.question: At turn 6 the monitoring system flags a potential volumetric attack because the network has oscillated between slices and shows stressed metrics. Across turns 5 and 6 the mMTC slice reports latency of 120 ms then 110 ms and jitter of 25 ms then 30 ms with loss increasing from 2.5 percent to 3.0 percent. records.question: The UAV is returning to base under snowstorm conditions with wind at 8.0 m/s from 260 degrees, and its current slice is mMTC with 60 ms latency, 15 ms jitter, 2.0% loss, 0.8 Mbps throughput, and 0.71 edge load. options.B: Switch to URLLC: latency drops to 7 ms, jitter to 1 ms, and edge load to 0.24, but the 3-second switch delay may cause a missed waypoint if wind gusts increase speed by 2 m/s.
options.C: Switch to eMBB: throughput jumps to 780 Mbps, supporting sensor streaming, but jitter may spike to 8 ms under wind gusts, risking control instability during descent.
options.D: Negotiate hybrid slice: combine URLLC for control and eMBB for telemetry, but this requires 5 seconds of negotiation and may exceed 0.75 edge load if both slices are active.

records.question: The UAV is returning to base under snowstorm conditions with wind at 8.0 m/s from 260 degrees, currently at 100m altitude within geofenced airspace. records.question: The UAV has completed its mission and is returning to base under deteriorating snowstorm conditions with wind at 8.0 mps from 260 degrees. records.question: An AI agent operating under snowstorm conditions must decide its next identity registration policy for persistent network slice selection. records.question: The UAV is returning to base under snowstorm conditions with battery at 87%, thermal sensor offline, and radar offline. records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is operating under snowstorm conditions with radar offline and thermal sensor failed, requiring collision avoidance via third-party swarm agent. options.D: Project worst-case: edge load 0.35 next turn adds 4ms latency, battery drops to 72% in 3 turns; switch to eMBB now to preserve throughput for emergency comms, accepting 11ms latency.

records.question: The UAV has completed delivery and is returning to base under snowstorm conditions with wind at 8.0 mps from 260 degrees. records.question: At turn 6 the operator has switched to URLLC with latency 9 ms, jitter 1.5 ms, loss 0.1 percent, throughput 55 Mbps, and edge load 0.4 after degradation at turn 5 showed 45 ms latency, 12 ms jitter, 2.5 percent loss, throughput 40 Mbps, and edge load 0.75. records.question: During post-fault coordination, the primary UAV must federate with a swarm agent and a mission control agent to share thermal substitutes and landing intent. records.question: At turn 6 the UAV is executing an emergency reroute with thermal and radar offline while RGB and LiDAR remain ok and GNSS is offline. records.question: During a snow and wind 3.5 mps mission, a UAV with battery at 100 percent and speed 22.0 mps has lost thermal and radar sensors while operating within altitude bounds 0.0 to 25.0. records.question: During turn 6 the network briefly degraded while attempting a thermal sensor restart, showing a slice with 200 ms latency, 50 ms jitter, 5.0 loss_pct, 1.2 throughput_mbps, and edge_load 0.75. records.question: At turn 6 the UAV is flying in rain at 25.0 m altitude with battery at 100.0 percent and speed 25.0 mps while the thermal sensor restart has failed. options.B: Switch to eMBB: current throughput is 105Mbps, sufficient for 1.2GB in 30s, and edge load may drop if traffic redistributes.
options.C: Switch to mMTC: latency is 50ms which exceeds control SLA, but throughput is adequate for data offload and edge load is low at 0.2.
options.D: Hybrid mode: use URLLC for control and eMBB for data, but this risks 220ms latency spikes and 8.5% loss if eMBB degrades further.

records.question: The UAV agent is currently operating under URLLC with latency 10ms, jitter 1.8ms, loss 0.09%, throughput 105Mbps, and edge load 0.41. Historical data shows eMBB degraded to 220ms latency and 8.5% loss at turn 6, and mMTC has 50ms latency and 0.5% loss but only 1.2Mbps throughput. The mission requires continuous sensor fusion with lidar offline, and the next waypoint is 3.2km away at 55m/s speed, requiring 58 seconds of uninterrupted control. Policy mandates SLA of <20ms latency and <0.5% loss for critical control. If network degradation persists for one more turn, which option minimizes maximum regret while preserving agent identity integrity and mission continuity? A) Stay on URLLC despite throughput constraints. B) Switch to eMBB for higher throughput, accepting risk of latency spike. C) Switch to mMTC to reduce edge load, accepting throughput collapse. D) Initiate emergency identity re-registration to force network renegotiation.

options.A: Stay on URLLC despite throughput constraints.
options.B: Switch to eMBB for higher throughput, accepting risk of latency spike.
options.C: Switch to mMTC to reduce edge load, accepting throughput collapse.
options.D: Initiate emergency identity re-registration to force network renegotiation.

records.question: The UAV is currently operating under URLLC with latency 10ms, jitter 1.8ms, loss 0.09%, throughput 105Mbps, and edge load 0.41. Battery is at 100% but will deplete at 2.5% per minute during active patrol. The next waypoint is 1200m away at 55m/s, requiring 22 seconds of flight. Federated model update requires 80MB of data upload with 95% success probability under current URLLC, but if edge load exceeds 0.65 in the next turn, success probability drops to 60%. eMBB offers 750Mbps throughput but latency 16ms and edge load 0.6, risking SLA violation if used for model sync. mMTC has 1.2Mbps throughput and 50ms latency, insufficient for timely model sync. If the UAV delays model sync for one more turn, edge load may rise to 0.55 due to swarm coordination, reducing URLLC success probability to 80%. Which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next two turns while ensuring model convergence and battery sustainability?

options.A: Immediately initiate federated model sync over URLLC, accepting 95% success probability and 0.41 edge load, preserving battery for patrol.
options.B: Switch to eMBB for model sync, leveraging 750Mbps throughput despite 16ms latency and 0.6 edge load, risking SLA violation if load spikes.
options.C: Delay model sync for one turn to allow edge load to stabilize, accepting 80% success probability under URLLC and risking battery depletion during idle hover.
options.D: Use mMTC for model sync, accepting 1.2Mbps throughput and 50ms latency, ensuring no edge load increase but guaranteeing sync failure.

records.question: The UAV is operating under crosswind conditions at 12.0 m/s with battery at 100% and altitude at 150.0m, within geofenced airspace bounded by [0.0,0.0] to [8000.0,6000.0]. If the UAV continues patrol with this agent, projected edge load in turn 13 will reach 0.51, exceeding policy. Which option should be selected to maintain compliance while minimizing mission disruption over the next three turns?

options.A: Grant full access under URLLC with real-time monitoring; edge load is currently 0.41 and latency is 10ms, both within limits.
options.B: Grant limited access under eMBB with 750Mbps throughput; latency is 16ms and loss is 0.3%, acceptable for non-critical data.
options.C: Deny access and switch to mMTC for logging only; latency is 50ms but edge load is 0.2, ensuring policy compliance.
options.D: Grant conditional access under URLLC with 10ms latency but cap data rate to 80Mbps; projected edge load in turn 13 is 0.49, under threshold.

records.question: At turn 11, the UAV resumes patrol under URLLC with latency 10ms, jitter 1.8ms, loss 0.09%, throughput 105Mbps, and edge load 0.41. Historical data shows eMBB degraded from 16ms latency and 0.3% loss at turn 5 to 220ms latency and 8.5% loss at turn 6, then recovered partially to 14ms and 0.2% at turn 3. Given uncertainty in wind-induced packet loss up to ±0.05% and potential edge load growth of 0.03 per turn, which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next 3 turns?

options.A: Stay on URLLC: latency 10ms, loss 0.09%±0.05%, throughput 105Mbps, edge load 0.41+0.03/turn — meets SLA and throughput, edge load stays under 0.50 in 3 turns.
options.B: Switch to eMBB: latency 14ms, loss 0.2%±0.05%, throughput 800Mbps, edge load 0.5 — throughput exceeds requirement but loss may hit 0.25% and edge load may reach 0.59 in 3 turns, risking SLA violation if degradation recurs.
options.C: Switch to mMTC: latency 50ms, loss 0.5%±0.05%, throughput 1.2Mbps — violates throughput SLA by 98.8Mbps and latency by 30ms, but edge load 0.2 is safe; however, sensor fusion will fail.
options.D: Initiate network isolation: force eMBB with 100% priority, accepting 220ms latency and 8.5% loss for 1 turn to reset edge load to 0.3 — risks mission failure due to SLA breach but may restore stability if degradation was transient.

records.question: At turn 10 the operator authorizes return to base while the UAV is in icing with wind at 8.0 mps and policy altitude bounds of 5.0 to 120.0. The current network slice is mMTC with latency 30.0 ms, jitter 15.0 ms, loss 3.0 pct, throughput 4 Mbps, and edge load 0.9. Earlier URLLC operation showed latency between 3.2 and 5.0 ms and jitter between 0.7 and 1.3 ms across multiple turns. The UAV speed was previously reduced from 15.0 mps for separation and battery remains at 100.0 pct. The intent message requires safe return within geofence while maintaining control link feasibility for the next two turns. If poor mMTC conditions persist one more turn, worst case latency and jitter must still allow command execution. Switching slices increases edge load but lowers latency, while slowing further increases exposure time in icing. Altitude must remain within 5.0 to 120.0 and no new sensors can be enabled. Each adjustment has a downside either in network risk or mission delay. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Keep mMTC at latency 30.0 ms and jitter 15.0 ms and maintain reduced speed to minimize edge load 0.9 impact this turn.
options.B: Switch immediately to URLLC with latency near 5.0 ms and jitter near 1.3 ms despite edge load rising toward 0.5 over the next turn.
options.C: Climb toward the upper altitude bound of 120.0 to improve link margin while staying on mMTC with throughput 4 Mbps.
options.D: Delay return for one turn on eMBB with latency 10.0 to 15.0 ms and jitter 2.5 to 4.2 ms to finish data transfer first.

records.question: During an icing inspection mission, the agent initially operates under an inspection intent with URLLC latency 3.2 ms and edge load 0.35 at turn 1. By turn 4, user-authorized thermal routing occurs under eMBB with latency 15.0 ms, jitter 4.2 ms, and edge load 0.75 while altitude remains within the 5.0 to 120.0 policy bounds. At turn 6, proximity monitoring switches to mMTC with latency 25.0 ms, jitter 12.0 ms, loss 2.5 percent, and edge load 0.85, followed by speed reduction at turn 7. Thermal capture at turn 8 uses eMBB with latency 10.0 ms and edge load 0.6, after which an anomaly is reported at turn 9 under URLLC with latency 4.0 ms. The user then authorizes return at turn 10 under mMTC with latency 30.0 ms, jitter 15.0 ms, loss 3.0 percent, and edge load 0.9. The original intent emphasized inspection data quality, but later turns emphasize minimizing communications and return execution. Assume worst case altitude uncertainty spans the full 5.0 to 120.0 range and poor network conditions persist for two more turns. Each possible interpretation below triggers a different monitoring or alerting response. One option appears acceptable if only the current turn is considered, while another fails only if worst case network degradation persists. No option avoids some form of regret over the next three turns. Which option should be selected as the best detection of intent drift?

options.A: Maintain inspection intent because URLLC latency returns to 4.0 ms at turn 9 and throughput remains 50 Mbps despite edge load 0.42.
options.B: Flag partial drift because edge load rises from 0.35 to 0.75 and mMTC latency reaches 25.0 ms, but inspection actions still occur at turn 8.
options.C: Flag full drift to recovery intent because the shift to mMTC with 30.0 ms latency, 15.0 ms jitter, and 0.9 edge load aligns with return execution under worst case persistence.
options.D: Defer drift detection because battery remains 100.0 percent and altitude stays within the 5.0 to 120.0 bounds.

records.question: During the anomaly report and preparation for return, the UAV has alternated slices across recent turns with URLLC at 4.0 ms latency, 1.1 ms jitter, 0.2 percent loss, 50 Mbps throughput, and 0.42 edge load, while eMBB earlier showed 10.0 to 15.0 ms latency, 2.5 to 4.2 ms jitter, 0.3 to 1.1 percent loss, 90 to 110 Mbps throughput, and 0.6 to 0.75 edge load. mMTC was observed during monitoring with 25.0 to 30.0 ms latency, 12.0 to 15.0 ms jitter, 2.5 to 3.0 percent loss, 4 to 5 Mbps throughput, and 0.85 to 0.9 edge load. The UAV is returning under icing conditions with speed previously reduced from 15.0 mps and battery still near the initial 100 percent, so control stability matters more than payload data rate. Across the last three turns, URLLC latency ranged from 3.5 to 5.0 ms and jitter from 0.7 to 1.3 ms, defining the uncertainty bounds to consider. Edge load has shown a worst case of 0.9 on non-URLLC slices, and congestion may persist for one to two more turns during return. A hybrid slice would split traffic, reducing control risk but raising aggregate edge load relative to pure URLLC. If congestion persists one more turn, a myopic choice that only optimizes current throughput could amplify delay variance. If recovery does not occur, the worst case must still keep control links stable while accepting some data delay. Each slice choice incurs regret either in control risk or delayed anomaly reporting over the next two turns. Which slice should be selected now to minimize maximum regret over the next two turns?

options.A: Select pure URLLC with latency near 4.0 ms and edge load around 0.42, accepting throughput near 50 Mbps for the next turns.
options.B: Select pure eMBB with throughput near 90 to 110 Mbps despite latency of 10.0 to 15.0 ms and edge load up to 0.75.
options.C: Select a hybrid URLLC plus eMBB slice, assuming control stays near 5.0 ms latency while total edge load approaches 0.75.
options.D: Select mMTC to minimize edge scheduling priority, tolerating 25.0 to 30.0 ms latency and edge load up to 0.9.

records.question: At turn 9 the UAV has just reported an anomaly while flying in icing with wind at 8.0 mps and altitude 10.0 m within the policy bounds of 5.0 to 120.0. Battery is still at 100.0 pct and current speed after reduction is below the earlier 15.0 mps setting. The active network slice is URLLC with latency 4.0 ms, jitter observed between 0.7 and 1.3 ms across recent turns, loss at 0.2 pct, throughput 50 Mbps, and edge load 0.42. Over the last three turns, eMBB and mMTC showed latency rising to 30.0 ms, jitter up to 15.0 ms, loss up to 3.0 pct, and edge load as high as 0.9. Lidar and radar remain offline, leaving thermal and RGB as the only sensors in icing conditions. The coordinator expects at least two more turns before landing if return is delayed, and network degradation could persist at the worst observed levels. Continuing inspection could yield more data but risks control lag if the slice shifts under load. Immediate return reduces exposure but may forfeit confirmation imagery already planned. A conservative continuation is defined as the option that minimizes worst case regret over the next three turns under the highest observed jitter and loss. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue inspection for two more turns on URLLC because current latency is 4.0 ms and loss is only 0.2 pct, accepting possible edge load growth from 0.42 toward 0.5.
options.B: Switch to eMBB to finish one more capture since throughput reached 110 Mbps earlier even though latency reached 15.0 ms and edge load 0.75.
options.C: Immediately continue flight but slow further below the prior 15.0 mps and commit to return after one turn, assuming jitter stays near 0.7 ms.
options.D: Abort inspection now and return to base within two turns to stay within alt bounds 5.0 to 120.0 and avoid worst case jitter of 15.0 ms and loss of 3.0 pct.

records.question: At turn 10 the scheduler has just shifted return-to-base commands onto an mMTC slice with 30.0 ms latency, 15.0 ms jitter, 3.0 percent loss, throughput 4, and edge load 0.9. Earlier URLLC turns showed latency between 3.2 and 5.0 with jitter below 1.3 and edge load between 0.32 and 0.5. The UAV is at altitude 10.0 within policy bounds of 5.0 to 120.0 and speed has already been reduced from 15.0 due to proximity handling. Weather remains icing with wind 8.0 from 270.0, increasing control sensitivity to jitter. Over the next two turns the scheduler may either persist on mMTC or revert to eMBB conditions seen earlier with 12.5 to 15.0 latency and edge load up to 0.75. Consistency requires that waypoint execution, telemetry, and anomaly reporting remain aligned despite slice changes. If jitter stays at its worst observed value for one more turn, control messages risk reordering. If the system overreacts and locks URLLC, edge capacity may saturate again as seen previously. Each candidate reconfiguration incurs some regret either in latency, load, or policy margin. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Force URLLC for all tasks since latency was 5.0 or less before and edge load was only 0.5 at turn 11.
options.B: Keep mMTC for return because throughput 4 is sufficient and altitude 10.0 stays within the 5.0 to 120.0 policy bounds.
options.C: Hybrid reconfigure by pinning control to URLLC while leaving telemetry on eMBB with 12.5 to 15.0 latency and edge load below 0.75.
options.D: Switch everything to eMBB now because 10.0 to 15.0 latency is acceptable and loss stayed near 1.1 or lower earlier.

records.question: At turn 10 the operator authorizes return to base while the network is on mMTC with latency 30.0 ms, jitter 15.0 ms, loss 3.0 percent, throughput 4 Mbps, and edge load 0.9. Earlier return execution at turn 11 succeeded on URLLC with latency 5.0 ms, jitter 1.3 ms, loss 0.4 percent, throughput 40 Mbps, and edge load 0.5. Across prior turns URLLC jitter ranged from 0.7 to 1.3 ms and eMBB latency ranged from 10.0 to 15.0 ms, indicating uncertainty if conditions persist. The UAV speed was reduced earlier from 15.0 mps for separation and consistency argues against reversing that choice without strong margins. The airspace policy altitude bounds remain 5.0 to 120.0 m and no altitude change is planned during return. If poor mMTC conditions persist one more turn, command retries increase edge load and risk inconsistent replanning. If URLLC saturates again, its edge load could rise toward 0.5 to 0.6 based on prior swings. The decision must minimize worst case regret over the next two turns rather than optimize the current link snapshot. One option keeps minimal comms consistent with turn 11, another chases higher throughput, another reverts speed, and another changes slices mid return. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Lock URLLC for return with minimal telemetry only, accepting 5.0 ms latency and 0.4 percent loss while keeping reduced speed despite edge load potentially rising from 0.5.
options.B: Switch to eMBB to gain 110 to 120 Mbps throughput seen earlier even if latency returns to 15.0 ms and jitter to 4.2 ms during the next turn.
options.C: Stay on mMTC because it was authorized at turn 10 and tolerate 30.0 ms latency and 15.0 ms jitter while increasing retries under 0.9 edge load.
options.D: Increase speed back to 15.0 mps and alternate between URLLC and eMBB each turn to hedge against uncertainty in jitter from 0.7 to 15.0 ms.

records.question: At turn 6 the primary UAV agent must decide how to federate data with a swarm agent and an inspection coordinator while operating under icing and proximity constraints. Recent exchanges used URLLC with latency 3.5 to 4.1 ms and loss 0.1 to 0.2, eMBB with latency 10.0 to 15.0 ms and loss 0.3 to 1.1, and mMTC with latency 25.0 to 30.0 ms and loss 2.5 to 3.0. Edge load simultaneously ranged from 0.32 on URLLC to 0.9 on mMTC, and throughput ranged from 4 to 120 Mbps. The UAV speed was reduced to manage separation, battery was at 100 percent, and altitude had to remain within the policy bounds of 5.0 to 120.0. Thermal imagery sharing is required for the next two turns, but lidar and radar are offline, increasing dependence on timely cross agent updates. The coordinator expects anomaly reports before the return authorization at turn 10 when the network degraded to the worst observed mMTC values. If degradation persists one more turn, the federation choice must still avoid violating safety margins despite higher jitter up to 15.0 ms. A single turn view favors maximum throughput, but a multi turn view must minimize worst case regret if loss spikes to 3.0 percent. All options introduce some delay or load risk across the next one to three turns. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Federate all thermal data and control messages over eMBB at 110 to 120 Mbps accepting 10.0 to 15.0 ms latency and up to 1.1 percent loss to maximize current detail.
options.B: Use URLLC only for all federation traffic relying on 3.5 to 4.1 ms latency and 0.1 to 0.2 percent loss despite throughput falling to 40 to 60 Mbps and rising edge load risk.
options.C: Split federation by sending control and anomaly summaries over URLLC and bulk thermal frames over eMBB while monitoring edge load between 0.32 and 0.75 across the next two turns.
options.D: Defer federation to mMTC to reduce edge contention now, tolerating 25.0 to 30.0 ms latency and 2.5 to 3.0 percent loss with 4 to 5 Mbps throughput.

records.question: At turn 9 the agent reports an anomaly to a third-party inspection coordinator over URLLC with latency 4.0 ms, jitter 1.1 ms, loss 0.2 percent, throughput 50 Mbps, and edge load 0.42. The UAV is returning to base with battery at 100.0 percent earlier but facing icing weather and wind at 8.0 mps, and future turns have shown mMTC conditions with latency up to 30.0 ms, jitter 15.0 ms, loss 3.0 percent, throughput 4 Mbps, and edge load 0.9. Policy altitude bounds are 5.0 to 120.0 meters and the current waypoint changes were accepted under user authorization at turn 10. The third-party agent requests continued access for thermal imagery APIs, raw telemetry, and limited compute offload during the next two turns. Thermal imagery requires eMBB-like throughput near 90 to 110 Mbps as seen at turn 8, while control telemetry has previously relied on URLLC at around 3.5 to 5.0 ms latency. If network degradation persists for one more turn, worst observed jitter and loss from mMTC may apply. Revoking access entirely increases coordination delay but reduces data exposure risk under uncertain consent continuity. Granting full access now could saturate edge load beyond 0.75 as previously observed at turn 4 and 10. A partial exposure could cap data while allowing status-only APIs over URLLC. Considering worst-case network conditions, policy bounds, and regret over the next two turns, which option should be selected?

options.A: Grant full data, API, and compute access using eMBB at 90 to 110 Mbps despite edge load rising toward 0.75 to 0.9.
options.B: Deny all third-party access immediately to avoid any exposure under 3.0 percent loss and 15.0 ms jitter conditions.
options.C: Allow status-only telemetry and anomaly reports over URLLC at 4.0 to 5.0 ms latency while withholding thermal imagery and compute.
options.D: Allow thermal imagery APIs only over mMTC with 4 to 5 Mbps throughput and accept higher jitter of 12.0 to 15.0 ms.

records.question: At turn 5, the UAV is streaming thermal video at 4 Mbps over eMBB with latency 35 ms, jitter 12 ms, and 0.8% loss, while edge load is 0.85 and rising. The SLA requires inference latency under 40 ms with loss under 1%. The thermal payload requires 20–120 m altitude and operates in rain. If the UAV continues streaming, edge load may reach 0.95 next turn, increasing jitter to 18 ms and loss to 1.2%. Onboard inference consumes 0.8 W and adds 5 ms latency but reduces data transmission to 0.5 Mbps. URLLC offers 7 ms latency and 0.01% loss but only 45 Mbps throughput, insufficient for 4 Mbps streaming if other payloads activate. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Offload inference to edge using eMBB; current latency 35 ms is under SLA and edge load 0.85 is acceptable for one more turn.
options.B: Switch to URLLC and offload inference; latency 7 ms is safe and loss 0.01% meets SLA, despite throughput being tight for 4 Mbps.
options.C: Perform inference onboard; adds 5 ms latency but eliminates transmission dependency, ensuring SLA compliance even if edge degrades further.
options.D: Pause streaming and wait for edge load to drop; risk violating mission timeline but avoids SLA breach under current conditions.

records.question: At turn 8, the UAV is returning home under mMTC slice with 92% edge load, 50ms latency, 20ms jitter, and 1.5% loss, while carrying a thermal payload requiring 4Mbps and operating within 20-120m altitude. The next turn will see edge load rise to 95% if no action is taken, and the thermal payload’s SLA mandates latency under 40ms with loss under 1%. If the UAV descends to 15m, it can switch to URLLC with 10ms latency and 0.03% loss but must deactivate thermal imaging, reducing mission value by 30%. Alternatively, it can maintain current altitude and slice, risking SLA violation in turn 9 with 95% edge load and projected 60ms latency. A third option is to activate RGB payload at 100m under eMBB, which offers 110Mbps throughput but 35ms latency and 0.8% loss, exceeding thermal SLA but preserving some imaging. The fourth option is to hover at 50m and wait for edge load to drop below 85%, which may take 2 turns and consume 15% battery. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Descend to 15m and switch to URLLC, deactivating thermal payload to meet SLA with 10ms latency and 0.03% loss, accepting 30% mission value loss.
options.B: Maintain current altitude and mMTC slice, accepting 60ms latency and 1.5% loss in turn 9, risking SLA violation but preserving thermal imaging.
options.C: Activate RGB payload at 100m under eMBB, accepting 35ms latency and 0.8% loss, which exceeds thermal SLA but retains imaging capability.
options.D: Hover at 50m for 2 turns to wait for edge load to drop below 85%, consuming 15% battery but avoiding immediate SLA risk.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is streaming thermal imagery at 4 Mbps over URLLC with 9 ms latency and 0.02% loss, while edge load is 0.36. The thermal payload requires minimum 20m altitude and operates in light rain, which is current weather. The edge server’s SLA mandates latency under 15 ms and loss under 0.1% for safety-critical offload. However, edge load is projected to rise to 0.88 by turn 9 if current offloading continues, and jitter may increase to 3.5 ms under worst-case wind gusts. If the UAV switches to local processing, it will consume 12W extra power and reduce battery life by 18 minutes, but avoid network risk. If it continues offloading, it risks violating SLA by turn 9 under worst-case load and jitter. If it switches to eMBB, throughput rises to 110 Mbps but latency jumps to 28 ms and loss to 0.15%, violating SLA immediately. If it delays offloading until turn 8, edge load will hit 0.92 and latency may exceed 50 ms under mMTC. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue offloading over URLLC; current metrics are within SLA and edge load is still low at 0.36.
options.B: Switch to local processing; avoid future SLA violation risk despite higher power draw and reduced flight time.
options.C: Switch to eMBB; higher throughput justifies temporary SLA breach for faster data transfer.
options.D: Delay offloading until turn 8; edge load will be higher but network may recover to URLLC by then.

records.question: At turn 5, the UAV is streaming thermal video at 4 Mbps over eMBB with latency 35 ms, jitter 12 ms, packet loss 0.8%, and edge load 0.85. The SLA requires latency ≤ 30 ms, jitter ≤ 10 ms, loss ≤ 0.5%, and edge load ≤ 0.8. Historical trends show latency increases by 3–7 ms per turn, jitter by 1.5–3 ms, loss by 0.05–0.15%, and edge load by 0.05–0.08 per turn. Switching to URLLC at turn 5 would cap latency at 10 ms, jitter at 2 ms, loss at 0.05%, and edge load at 0.4, but reduce throughput to 45 Mbps, risking video buffer underrun if bitrate exceeds 40 Mbps. The thermal payload requires 4 Mbps, but the next mission phase may require 8 Mbps for dual-streaming. Given uncertainty in degradation rates and future bandwidth needs, which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue on eMBB; current metrics are within 10% of SLA limits and may stabilize.
options.B: Switch to URLLC immediately; worst-case SLA violation is certain by turn 7.
options.C: Switch to URLLC only if edge load exceeds 0.9; current load is 0.85 and may not breach 0.9 by turn 6.
options.D: Remain on eMBB until turn 6, then switch if latency exceeds 40 ms; projected latency at turn 6 is 38–42 ms.

records.question: The UAV is currently operating at 120m altitude under eMBB slice with 35ms latency, 12ms jitter, 0.8% loss, and 95Mbps throughput while edge load is at 0.85. A third-party analytics service requests compute access for real-time thermal video processing, requiring 80Mbps sustained throughput and latency under 40ms. The edge node can allocate compute but will increase load to 0.92 if accepted. Which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next two turns while ensuring mission continuity?

options.A: Accept the third-party request on eMBB, accepting edge load of 0.92 and risking throughput drop to 80Mbps under weather degradation.
options.B: Reject the request and switch to URLLC slice to guarantee latency under 10ms, sacrificing throughput and compute access.
options.C: Delay the decision for one turn to monitor weather impact, risking missed analytics window and potential SLA violation.
options.D: Accept the request but throttle video bitrate to 40Mbps to fit URLLC, degrading analytics quality but ensuring latency compliance.

records.question: At turn 5, the UAV is streaming thermal video at 4 Mbps over eMBB with latency 35 ms, jitter 12 ms, packet loss 0.8%, and edge load 0.85. The mission requires thermal imaging within 120 m altitude, and the next 2 turns may see edge load rise to 0.95 under worst-case weather persistence. URLLC offers 7 ms latency and 0.01% loss but only 45 Mbps throughput, while mMTC has 50 ms latency and 1.5% loss with 1.2 Mbps throughput. If the thermal stream must remain uninterrupted for 3 more turns and the edge load increases by 0.05 per turn, which network slice should be selected to minimize maximum regret under worst-case latency and loss bounds while preserving mission continuity?

options.A: Stay on eMBB: current throughput 95 Mbps exceeds 4 Mbps requirement, and latency is acceptable for non-critical telemetry.
options.B: Switch to URLLC: guarantees sub-10 ms latency and near-zero loss, even if throughput margin shrinks to 41 Mbps under load.
options.C: Switch to mMTC: conserves edge resources with minimal throughput, suitable for low-priority metadata only.
options.D: Wait one turn: monitor if edge load stabilizes below 0.9, then decide based on updated telemetry.

records.question: The UAV agent is currently operating under eMBB slice with latency 35ms, jitter 12ms, loss 0.8%, throughput 95Mbps, and edge load 0.85, while carrying thermal and RGB payloads requiring 4Mbps and 6Mbps respectively. The mission requires continuous thermal imaging at 300m range with 640x512 resolution, constrained to altitudes 20–120m, and must complete within 3 turns before battery drops below 20%. The fourth option is to deactivate RGB and retain thermal under eMBB, preserving 95Mbps but risking SLA violation if jitter exceeds 15ms next turn. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Switch to URLLC and keep both payloads active, accepting edge load 0.45 next turn and throughput 45Mbps.
options.B: Remain on eMBB but deactivate RGB payload, reducing total bitrate to 4Mbps and preserving 95Mbps throughput.
options.C: Switch to mMTC for telemetry-only mode, accepting 50ms latency and 1.5% loss to conserve battery and reduce edge load.
options.D: Stay on eMBB with both payloads, projecting worst-case jitter of 18ms next turn and 0.95 edge load, risking mission failure.

records.question: The UAV is currently streaming thermal video at 4 Mbps over eMBB with 35 ms latency, 12 ms jitter, and 0.8% loss while edge load is at 0.85. The thermal payload requires at least 2 Mbps throughput and under 50 ms latency to maintain operational integrity. records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is operating under mMTC slice with latency 55 ms, jitter 12 ms, loss 3.0%, throughput 1.0 Mbps, and edge load 0.8. records.question: At turn 8, the UAV has just switched back to URLLC after experiencing mMTC degradation with edge_load rising from 0.75 to 0.8, latency spiking to 55ms, and throughput collapsing to 1.0Mbps. records.question: At turn 6 the UAV has just switched to URLLC with latency 9 ms, jitter 1.1 ms, loss 0.08 percent, throughput 110 Mbps, and edge load 0.41. records.question: At turn 5 the operator observes severe network degradation while the UAV is mid mission with battery at 100.0 percent and speed 35.0 mps. records.question: An immersive AR inspection session is running while the UAV coordinates swarm avoidance and then resumes approach over the next three turns. records.question: The UAV is en route to its final destination under snow conditions with wind at 7.2 m/s from 310 degrees. records.question: At turn 10 the user commands return to base while the network slice shifts to mMTC with latency 50 ms, jitter 10 ms, loss 2.5 percent, throughput 1 Mbps, and edge load 0.85. records.question: At turn 9 the agent has been executing a survey mission with thermal mapping after adjusting heading at turn 3 and climbing at turns 6 and 7.
