records.question: The UAV is currently at 120m altitude with 100% battery and has just captured thermal data for federated model update. Network slice is eMBB with 700 Mbps throughput, 20ms latency, 5ms jitter, 0.3% loss, and 0.5 edge load. The next turn will see edge load rise to 0.65 if no action is taken, and the SLA requires latency under 25ms and loss under 0.5% for model sync. A relay UAV is available but introduces 15ms fixed overhead. The mission allows one more data chunk transmission before aborting. If the thermal data is 1.2GB and model sync requires 800MB, which option should be selected to ensure federated update completion without violating SLA in the next two turns, while minimizing regret if edge load degrades further?

options.A: Transmit full 1.2GB thermal data now via eMBB; accept 0.3% loss and 20ms latency; risk SLA violation next turn if edge load hits 0.65.
options.B: Transmit 800MB model sync via eMBB now; defer thermal data; accept 20ms latency; risk 0.65 edge load next turn may push latency to 28ms.
options.C: Switch to URLLC slice (100Mbps, 10ms latency, 0.08% loss, 0.22 edge load) and transmit 800MB model sync; accept 12s transmission time; guarantee SLA for next turn.
options.D: Use relay UAV with 15ms overhead; transmit 800MB model sync via eMBB; total latency 35ms; violate SLA immediately but ensure data delivery.

records.question: At turn 5, the UAV detects a faulty antenna and initiates collision avoidance scan with swarm agent. Network slice is URLLC with 9ms latency, 1.5ms jitter, 0.1% loss, 110Mbps throughput, and 0.25 edge load. The swarm agent has a trust score of 0.72, and its last 3 interactions had 0.05, 0.08, and 0.12 packet loss respectively. Regulatory policy requires exposure to third-party agents only if projected edge load remains below 0.4 for next 2 turns and SLA latency bound is 15ms. If the swarm agent’s next interaction is projected to increase edge load by 0.15 and latency by 3ms under worst-case jitter, and the UAV must decide whether to grant full API access, limited telemetry, or deny access, which option should be selected?

options.A: Grant full API access: swarm agent trust score exceeds 0.7 and current edge load is 0.25, below threshold.
options.B: Grant limited telemetry: current latency 9ms is under SLA, but projected edge load 0.40 is at boundary; deny full access to avoid violation.
options.C: Deny access: worst-case latency projection 12ms is safe, but edge load may reach 0.40 next turn and 0.55 in turn 7 if swarm scales, violating SLA.
options.D: Grant full API access with throttling: trust score justifies access, and throttling can cap edge load at 0.35 even if swarm scales.

records.question: At turn 9, the UAV is returning under mMTC slice with latency 60ms, jitter 15ms, loss 2.0%, throughput 0.8Mbps, and edge load 0.7. The next turn’s weather forecast indicates microburst risk may increase wind speed to 12m/s, potentially degrading network performance by 25% across all metrics. The UAV’s battery is at 45% and must land within 3 turns to avoid critical depletion. A diagnostic at turn 5 revealed a faulty antenna, reducing effective throughput by 15% under high loss. The mission policy requires maintaining at least 95% data integrity for thermal imagery transmission. If the UAV switches to URLLC now, latency drops to 10ms but throughput caps at 100Mbps, insufficient for queued thermal data. If it remains on mMTC, edge load may exceed 0.85 by turn 10, risking slice collapse. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Switch to URLLC immediately to minimize latency and jitter, accepting partial data loss due to throughput cap.
options.B: Remain on mMTC for one more turn to transmit queued data, then switch to URLLC if edge load exceeds 0.8.
options.C: Initiate emergency landing now to preserve battery, sacrificing all queued data transmission.
options.D: Request relay UAV to boost throughput on mMTC, accepting 30% higher jitter and 5% additional loss for next turn.

records.question: At turn 6, network conditions degrade to mMTC slice with 45ms latency, 12ms jitter, 2.5% loss, 1.2Mbps throughput, and 85% edge load. The UAV is en route to waypoint 3 at 20m altitude with 100% battery and thermal sensor offline. SLA requires inference latency under 30ms and edge load under 90%. If degradation persists for two more turns, onboard inference consumes 15ms with 5% battery drain per turn, while edge inference incurs 45ms latency with 0.5% battery drain per turn. Thermal sensor reactivation would add 8ms inference latency and 3% battery drain per turn. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Use onboard inference with thermal sensor deactivated; latency 15ms, battery drain 5% per turn, edge load 0%
options.B: Use edge inference with thermal sensor deactivated; latency 45ms, battery drain 0.5% per turn, edge load 85%
options.C: Use onboard inference with thermal sensor reactivated; latency 23ms, battery drain 8% per turn, edge load 0%
options.D: Use edge inference with thermal sensor reactivated; latency 53ms, battery drain 3.5% per turn, edge load 85%

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is operating under mMTC slice with 50ms latency, 15ms jitter, 3.0% packet loss, and 0.9 edge load, while battery is at 85% and wind gusts are increasing to 12m/s. The SLA mandates latency under 30ms and edge load under 0.85 for autonomous navigation. Projecting forward, edge load will rise to 0.95 by turn 8 if no action is taken, and latency may spike to 65ms under worst-case wind-induced interference. Deactivating thermal sensor reduces edge load by 0.08 but sacrifices thermal obstacle detection, while switching to URLLC slice reduces latency to 8ms but increases edge load to 0.92 due to coordination overhead. Maintaining current state risks SLA violation by turn 8, and returning to base now incurs 120s delay but resets edge load to 0.2. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Deactivate thermal sensor: reduces edge load to 0.82, latency remains 50ms, preserves navigation autonomy for 2 more turns.
options.B: Switch to URLLC slice: latency drops to 8ms, edge load rises to 0.92, SLA violated on edge load by turn 8.
options.C: Maintain current state: edge load projected to 0.95 by turn 8, latency may hit 65ms, SLA violated on both metrics.
options.D: Return to base immediately: resets edge load to 0.2, incurs 120s delay, forfeits current mission but avoids SLA breach.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is operating under mMTC slice with latency 50ms, jitter 15ms, packet loss 3.0%, throughput 0.9Mbps, and edge load 0.9. The policy requires latency under 40ms for offloading trust, and the mission demands at least 1.5Mbps throughput for sensor fusion. Wind gusts may persist for 2 more turns, increasing edge load by 0.1 per turn. If the UAV continues offloading, projected edge load at turn 9 will reach 1.1, violating trust thresholds. Option A proposes switching to URLLC with 7ms latency and 130Mbps throughput but risks 0.4 edge load and potential SLA breach if wind persists. Option B suggests staying on mMTC with degraded performance, accepting 3.0% loss and 0.9 edge load, but risking mission failure if throughput drops below 0.8Mbps. Option C recommends deactivating all sensors to reduce load, preserving 0.9 edge load but forfeiting thermal and lidar data needed for next waypoint. Option D proposes immediate return to base, abandoning the mission but guaranteeing no trust violation. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Switch to URLLC slice despite edge load risk, prioritizing latency and throughput for sensor fusion.
options.B: Remain on mMTC slice, accepting current degradation but risking throughput collapse under wind persistence.
options.C: Deactivate all sensors to reduce edge load, preserving network trust but sacrificing critical sensor data.
options.D: Return to base immediately, abandoning mission to avoid any trust violation or SLA breach.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is operating under mMTC slice with latency 50ms, jitter 15ms, loss 3.0%, throughput 0.9Mbps, and edge load 0.9. The SLA requires latency ≤ 30ms, jitter ≤ 5ms, loss ≤ 1.0%, and throughput ≥ 5Mbps. Wind gusts are increasing with 8.0m/s sustained and 12.0m/s peak gusts expected next turn. Battery is at 78% and decreasing at 3% per turn. If the UAV continues on current path, projected edge load next turn is 0.95 with 90% confidence. The mission requires 3 more turns to complete. Which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next 3 turns?

options.A: Switch to URLLC slice immediately; latency drops to 7ms but throughput limited to 130Mbps, edge load 0.4, and battery drain increases by 1.5% per turn due to higher control frequency.
options.B: Continue on mMTC with reduced sensor usage; latency may rise to 60ms next turn, jitter to 20ms, loss to 4.0%, throughput drops to 0.6Mbps, edge load 0.95, but battery drain remains 3% per turn.
options.C: Switch to eMBB slice; latency 14ms, jitter 2.5ms, loss 0.15%, throughput 800Mbps, edge load 0.4, but battery drain increases by 2% per turn and wind-induced drift may cause altitude violation with 30% probability.
options.D: Request emergency reroute to lower altitude; reduces wind impact but increases edge load to 0.98, latency to 55ms, jitter to 18ms, loss to 3.5%, throughput 0.7Mbps, and battery drain to 4% per turn due to climb/descent.

records.question: At turn 8, the UAV is operating under wind gusts with battery at 85%, altitude adjusted by +5m, and edge compute load at 0.4. The network slice is URLLC with latency 7ms, jitter 1ms, loss 0.08%, throughput 130Mbps. A third-party request arrives to offload compute for a latency-sensitive application requiring 95th percentile latency <10ms, jitter <2ms, and throughput >100Mbps, with a 15% probability of sudden edge load spike to 0.95 in the next turn. The SLA penalty is $500 per ms over 10ms latency. Option A reserves 30% of edge capacity at $0.08/GB with guaranteed SLA. Option B offers best-effort at $0.03/GB with no SLA. Option C defers until turn 10 when edge load is projected to drop to 0.35. Option D allocates 20% capacity now at $0.05/GB but risks SLA violation if load spikes. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Reserve 30% capacity at $0.08/GB with guaranteed SLA despite current edge load of 0.4.
options.B: Offer best-effort at $0.03/GB with no SLA, accepting risk of latency violation.
options.C: Defer allocation until turn 10 when edge load is projected to be 0.35, risking opportunity loss.
options.D: Allocate 20% capacity now at $0.05/GB, accepting 15% risk of SLA violation if load spikes to 0.95.

records.question: At turn 6, network telemetry shows mMTC slice with 45ms latency, 12ms jitter, 2.5% loss, 1.2Mbps throughput, and 85% edge load. The UAV is at 20m altitude, 15m/s speed, and 100% battery. Policy allows altitudes 10–120m. Wind is 8m/s from 270°. The next 3 turns require telemetry sync, navigation, and payload prep. Option A: expose full telemetry under mMTC with 3.0% loss worst-case. Option B: switch to URLLC (7ms latency, 1ms jitter, 0.08% loss, 130Mbps, 40% edge load) but risk 15% throughput drop if edge load exceeds 0.5. Option C: use eMBB (18ms latency, 4ms jitter, 0.3% loss, 700Mbps, 60% edge load) with 10% jitter increase risk. Option D: defer telemetry exposure until turn 9 when URLLC is scheduled, risking 2 turns of blind navigation. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Expose full telemetry under mMTC with 3.0% loss worst-case.
options.B: Switch to URLLC with 15% throughput drop risk if edge load exceeds 0.5.
options.C: Use eMBB with 10% jitter increase risk.
options.D: Defer telemetry exposure until turn 9 when URLLC is scheduled.

records.question: At turn 8, the UAV is operating under wind gusts with battery at 85%, altitude at 20m, and thermal sensor offline. Network slice is URLLC with latency 7ms, jitter 1ms, loss 0.08%, throughput 130Mbps, edge load 0.4. Policy allows altitude up to 120m. If wind gusts persist, latency may increase by 3ms per turn with 90% probability, and edge load may rise to 0.65 by turn 10. The UAV must maintain SLA of latency < 15ms and edge load < 0.7 for identity validation. Option A: Stay at 20m, retain URLLC, accept 10% risk of SLA breach by turn 10. Option B: Ascend to 50m, switch to eMBB, latency 12ms, edge load 0.45, but risk 20% sensor failure due to wind. Option C: Descend to 15m, remain on URLLC, latency 6ms, edge load 0.35, but violate minimum altitude policy. Option D: Ascend to 80m, switch to eMBB, latency 15ms, edge load 0.6, but risk 15% GNSS drift. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Stay at 20m, retain URLLC, accept 10% risk of SLA breach by turn 10.
options.B: Ascend to 50m, switch to eMBB, latency 12ms, edge load 0.45, but risk 20% sensor failure due to wind.
options.C: Descend to 15m, remain on URLLC, latency 6ms, edge load 0.35, but violate minimum altitude policy.
options.D: Ascend to 80m, switch to eMBB, latency 15ms, edge load 0.6, but risk 15% GNSS drift.

records.question: At turn 6, network conditions degrade to mMTC slice with 45ms latency, 12ms jitter, 2.5% loss, 1.2Mbps throughput, and 85% edge load. The UAV must initiate federated model aggregation within the next 3 turns while preserving 20% battery for return. Thermal sensor data is critical for model accuracy but consumes 15% battery per turn. Edge load is projected to increase by 5% per turn if aggregation is delayed. URLLC offers 7ms latency but only 130Mbps throughput, insufficient for full model sync. eMBB offers 800Mbps but latency exceeds 15ms, risking SLA violation if aggregation takes >2 turns. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Initiate aggregation now over mMTC despite 3% loss and 50ms worst-case latency, accepting 10% accuracy drop to preserve battery.
options.B: Wait one turn for potential network recovery, risking edge load reaching 90% and forcing aggregation over mMTC with 4% loss.
options.C: Switch to URLLC immediately and compress model to 100MB, accepting 20% longer sync time but guaranteeing <10ms latency.
options.D: Switch to eMBB and delay aggregation until turn 8, accepting 18ms latency and 0.5% SLA violation risk if edge load exceeds 95%.

records.question: The UAV is operating under wind gusts at 8.0 m/s from 270°, currently at 20m altitude with 100% battery, and has just executed an altitude adjustment via URLLC slice with 7ms latency and 0.08% loss. The edge load is 0.4, and the next two turns will require telemetry sync with a third-party swarm agent under uncertain network conditions: eMBB may degrade to 18ms latency and 0.3% loss, or mMTC may persist with 50ms latency and 3.0% loss. The swarm agent requires access to GNSS, IMU, and barometer data for coordination, but exposing all sensors risks violating the 10ms latency SLA for critical control if network degrades. Option A exposes all sensors under URLLC with 10ms worst-case latency projection. Option B exposes only GNSS under eMBB with 18ms latency and 0.3% loss. Option C exposes GNSS and IMU under mMTC with 50ms latency and 3.0% loss. Option D delays exposure until next turn with 90% probability of network recovery to URLLC. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Expose all sensors (GNSS, IMU, barometer) via URLLC with 10ms worst-case latency projection.
options.B: Expose only GNSS via eMBB with 18ms latency and 0.3% loss.
options.C: Expose GNSS and IMU via mMTC with 50ms latency and 3.0% loss.
options.D: Delay exposure until next turn with 90% probability of network recovery to URLLC.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is operating under mMTC slice with latency 50ms, jitter 15ms, packet loss 3.0%, throughput 0.9Mbps, and edge load 0.9. The mission requires telemetry updates every 2 seconds, each requiring 1.2Mbps throughput and tolerating max 20ms latency. Wind gusts may persist for 2 more turns, forcing altitude adjustments that consume 0.3Mbps additional bandwidth. A security anomaly has been flagged: the edge load is rising at 0.05 per turn, and if it exceeds 0.95, the network will isolate the UAV. The next 3 turns must include at least one telemetry update and one altitude adjustment. Option A: Stay on mMTC and accept 100% telemetry failure risk. Option B: Switch to URLLC with 110Mbps throughput, 10ms latency, 0.12% loss, and 0.5 edge load, but risk exceeding 0.95 edge load in 2 turns if wind persists. Option C: Switch to eMBB with 800Mbps throughput, 14ms latency, 0.15% loss, and 0.4 edge load, but latency may spike to 25ms under load, violating SLA. Option D: Deactivate all sensors and switch to URLLC, reducing telemetry demand to 0.5Mbps, but losing situational awareness for 3 turns. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Stay on mMTC and accept 100% telemetry failure risk.
options.B: Switch to URLLC with 110Mbps throughput, 10ms latency, 0.12% loss, and 0.5 edge load, but risk exceeding 0.95 edge load in 2 turns if wind persists.
options.C: Switch to eMBB with 800Mbps throughput, 14ms latency, 0.15% loss, and 0.4 edge load, but latency may spike to 25ms under load, violating SLA.
options.D: Deactivate all sensors and switch to URLLC, reducing telemetry demand to 0.5Mbps, but losing situational awareness for 3 turns.

records.question: At mission start the network intent implicitly favored high throughput eMBB with latency near 12 ms and edge load near 0.35 while the UAV flew at 20 m altitude with a policy range of 10 to 120 m. By turn 3 the slice switched to URLLC with latency 8 ms and throughput 120 Mbps while coordination actions increased and edge load rose to 0.42. A sharp anomaly appeared at turn 6 when eMBB latency jumped to 120 ms with 8.5 percent loss and edge load 0.88. At turn 7 the agent switched back to URLLC restoring latency to 10 ms and edge load to 0.52 while the stated mission remained delivery. Over the next two turns latency stabilized between 7 and 9 ms and throughput rose from 115 to 130 Mbps while edge load declined to 0.44. The UAV speed stayed 15 mps and battery remained at 100 percent so mission urgency did not numerically increase. The only explicit range constraint is altitude policy which still had a margin of at least 100 m from violation. Consider worst case recurrence where the turn 6 degradation repeats once in the next three turns. A correct detector must minimize regret by flagging intent change only if behavior implies a persistent shift rather than a transient adaptation. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Flag intent drift because URLLC latency of 8 to 10 ms across turns 3 to 9 proves a permanent safety intent despite throughput staying near 120 Mbps.
options.B: Do not flag intent drift because the switch at turn 7 was a reactive response to 120 ms latency and 8.5 percent loss and subsequent metrics reverted to stable values.
options.C: Flag intent drift because edge load peaked at 0.88 and then stayed above 0.5 indicating sustained coordination intent even if degradation does not recur.
options.D: Defer judgment for one more turn because current latency of 7 ms and edge load 0.4 meet all bounds and single turn recovery is sufficient evidence.

records.question: At turn 7 the agent has just switched slices after a severe anomaly was reported one turn earlier. Over recent turns URLLC latency has varied between 7 and 10 ms with jitter between 0.7 and 1.2 ms and loss between 0.0 and 0.04, while edge load has ranged from 0.44 to 0.52. The alternative eMBB slice showed 120 ms latency, 25 ms jitter, 8.5 loss, 45 throughput, and 0.88 edge load at the anomaly. The UAV is flying at 15 mps with battery at 100 percent and must remain within altitude bounds of 10 to 120 m for the next few turns. Throughput on URLLC has stayed between 105 and 130 while eMBB previously reached 900 before collapsing. Assume the anomaly could persist for one to three more turns and that edge load tends to increase when throughput demand spikes. In the worst case URLLC metrics drift to their observed maxima and eMBB recovers only partially. A hybrid slice would split traffic so that control uses URLLC characteristics and payload uses eMBB characteristics drawn from the same observed values. Each option risks either control instability or data backlog over the next few turns. Which slice selection minimizes maximum regret over the next one to three turns under these conditions?

options.A: Stay on pure URLLC since latency stays under 10 ms and edge load has not exceeded 0.52 so far.
options.B: Switch back to pure eMBB hoping throughput returns toward 900 despite the prior 120 ms latency and 0.88 edge load.
options.C: Adopt a hybrid slice splitting control on URLLC at 7 to 10 ms latency and payload on eMBB constrained by the observed 45 throughput.
options.D: Remain on URLLC only for the next turn and defer a decision since current jitter is near 0.7 ms.

records.question: At turn 7 the swarm just recovered from a severe network anomaly observed at turn 6. The eMBB slice at turn 6 showed latency 120 ms, jitter 25 ms, loss 8.5 percent, throughput 45 Mbps, and edge load 0.88. After switching back to URLLC at turn 7 the metrics improved to latency 10 ms, jitter 1.2 ms, loss 0.04 percent, throughput 115 Mbps, and edge load 0.52. The policy altitude bounds remain a hard range from 10 m to 120 m while the UAV is currently at 20 m and executing collision avoidance with other swarm members. Over turns 3 to 10 the URLLC edge load has varied between 0.42 and 0.52, showing possible contention growth if another UAV also switches slices next turn. Assume worst case that another anomaly like turn 6 reoccurs for one turn if load exceeds recent highs. One option favors immediate fairness by returning to eMBB, one favors strict safety by staying on URLLC, and two options involve partial or delayed switching. The decision must minimize maximum regret over the next two turns if congestion or anomalies persist. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Immediately switch back to eMBB now because throughput was 900 Mbps at turn 2 and edge load was only 0.38 then.
options.B: Stay on URLLC for the next two turns since latency stays below 10 ms and edge load has already dropped from 0.52 to 0.48 to 0.44.
options.C: Switch to eMBB for one turn only to reduce URLLC contention, then return to URLLC if latency exceeds 11 ms again.
options.D: Delay any slice change until edge load exceeds 0.52 again, keeping URLLC while altitude remains within the 10 m to 120 m policy range.

records.question: At turn 6 a sudden network anomaly appears while the mission is mid flight and the agent must predict whether an SLA violation is likely to recur. Earlier turns on eMBB showed latency of 12 and 11 with jitter of 2 and 1.8 and edge_load of 0.35 and 0.38. URLLC between turns 3 and 5 showed latency between 7 and 9 with jitter between 0.7 and 1.1 and edge_load rising from 0.42 to 0.5. The anomaly at turn 6 on eMBB reports latency 120 jitter 25 loss 8.5 throughput 45 and edge_load 0.88. After switching back to URLLC at turn 7 latency returns to 10 with jitter 1.2 loss 0.04 and edge_load 0.52. Assume the implicit SLA is that latency must stay at or below 10 and loss at or below 0.04 as seen during stable URLLC operation. Consider uncertainty by taking worst case future values within the previously observed ranges of latency 7 to 120 and edge_load 0.35 to 0.88. Over the next two turns assume edge_load may increase by the same increment observed from turn 3 to turn 5. Each option below predicts whether an SLA violation will occur and recommends a stance. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Predict no violation because current URLLC latency is 10 and loss is 0.04 with edge_load only 0.52.
options.B: Predict a violation because worst case latency can revert to 120 and edge_load may exceed 0.88 if the anomaly persists.
options.C: Predict no violation because recent trend from turn 7 to 9 shows latency improving from 10 to 8 and edge_load falling from 0.52 to 0.44.
options.D: Predict a possible violation only if edge_load rises above 0.5 again since that boundary was crossed at turn 5.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV has just switched back to URLLC after an eMBB spike where latency hit 120 ms and loss reached 8.5 percent. Current URLLC telemetry shows latency 10 ms, jitter 1.2 ms, loss 0.04 percent, throughput 115 Mbps, and edge load 0.52. Earlier URLLC edge load increased from 0.42 at turn 3 to 0.5 at turn 5, indicating an upward trend across turns. The UAV is flying at 20 m altitude within a policy band of 10 to 120 m, at 15 mps speed, with battery at 100 percent. Thermal and radar sensors are offline, leaving reliance on rgb and lidar. Assume worst case that edge load continues increasing next turn by the same increment seen from turn 3 to turn 5 and that a transient eMBB-like degradation could recur for one turn. Full autonomy requires sustained low latency and low loss over the next two turns, while degraded autonomy tolerates higher latency but reduces maneuver aggressiveness. Manual hold minimizes network dependence but delays mission progress. Considering the next two turns and worst case network behavior, which option should be selected?

options.A: Maintain full autonomy on URLLC since latency is 10 ms and loss is 0.04 percent with edge load only 0.52.
options.B: Preemptively downgrade to degraded autonomy mode now, accepting reduced maneuvering while edge load is below 0.6.
options.C: Switch back to eMBB because throughput of 115 Mbps is lower than earlier 900 Mbps and edge load might rise.
options.D: Enter manual hold immediately to avoid any risk if latency spikes again above 120 ms.

records.question: At turn 7 the agent has just switched the network slice back to URLLC after an eMBB anomaly at turn 6. The current URLLC telemetry shows latency 10 ms, jitter 1.2 ms, loss 0.04 percent, throughput 115 Mbps, and edge load 0.52. Over the last three URLLC turns the latency values observed were 8 ms, 9 ms, and 10 ms while jitter ranged from 0.7 ms to 1.2 ms. The previous eMBB state at turn 6 had latency 120 ms, jitter 25 ms, loss 8.5 percent, throughput 45 Mbps, and edge load 0.88. Battery is still at 100 percent and altitude remains within the 10 to 120 bounds, so no immediate mission abort is forced. The operator expects the mission to continue for at least two more turns without contradictory replanning decisions. There is uncertainty whether the network anomaly could recur for one more turn before stabilizing. If the agent changes slices again now and then has to reverse in the next turn, that would violate decision consistency. Considering worst case latency under jitter bounds and the regret of having to replan again within the next two turns, which option should be selected?

options.A: Remain on URLLC at latency 10 ms and edge load 0.52, accepting possible jitter up to 1.2 ms over the next two turns.
options.B: Switch back to eMBB because throughput was 900 Mbps earlier despite the recent 120 ms latency spike and 0.88 edge load.
options.C: Toggle to eMBB for one turn to test recovery, planning to return to URLLC if latency exceeds 11 ms.
options.D: Pause route execution now to wait for network stabilization even though URLLC currently shows 8 to 10 ms latency.

records.question: At turn 7 the operator must decide how to onboard a newly discovered swarm coordination agent into the mission identity system while the UAV continues flying. Across turns 6 to 10 the network shows eMBB latency jumping to 120 ms with loss 8.5 percent and edge load 0.88 before switching back to URLLC with latency between 7 and 10 ms, loss between 0.0 and 0.04 percent, throughput between 105 and 140 Mbps, and edge load between 0.4 and 0.52. The UAV is at altitude 20 within allowed bounds 10 to 120, moving at 15 mps with battery at 100 percent, so flight safety is not the immediate limiter. Identity onboarding can be done as a single global identity mapped at the edge, as per-agent ephemeral identities, as a deferred registration after delivery, or as a hybrid with provisional local identity and later reconciliation. A single global identity reduces authentication chatter now but risks reauthentication storms if edge load rises again toward 0.88. Per-agent ephemeral identities increase control messages but localize failure if URLLC capacity tightens. Deferred registration avoids current load but risks loss of audit continuity if degradation persists another turn. The hybrid option adds some overhead now and some later but bounds worst-case failures. Considering worst-case recurrence of turn 6 conditions over the next two turns and the observed URLLC variability, which onboarding option should be selected?

options.A: Register a single global identity at the edge now, assuming URLLC latency near 7 to 10 ms and edge load near 0.5 will hold.
options.B: Issue per-agent ephemeral identities immediately, accepting higher message volume under URLLC throughput between 105 and 140 Mbps.
options.C: Defer all identity registration until after delivery since battery is 100 percent and altitude is within 10 to 120.
options.D: Use a hybrid approach with provisional local identities now and delayed global reconciliation after the next two turns.

records.question: At turn 6 the UAV must interoperate with a swarm collision avoidance agent while the network shows sharp divergence between slices. The eMBB slice reports latency 120 ms, jitter 25 ms, loss 8.5 percent, throughput 45 Mbps, and edge load 0.88. The URLLC slice in adjacent turns shows latency fluctuating between 7 ms and 10 ms, jitter between 0.7 ms and 1.2 ms, loss between 0.01 and 0.04 percent, throughput between 105 and 130 Mbps, and edge load between 0.44 and 0.52. Swarm coordination requires frequent state exchange across at least the next two turns while the UAV continues at 15 mps with battery still near 100 percent. If degradation on eMBB persists for one more turn, federation messages may queue behind edge load 0.88 and amplify delay. If URLLC edge load rises toward 0.52 for two turns, throughput remains constrained relative to eMBB but latency stays low. A federation choice must minimize worst case regret if conditions do not recover by turn 8. One option optimizes current throughput, another minimizes current latency, another hedges by partial data sharing, and another delays coordination. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Federate fully over eMBB to exploit 45 Mbps throughput despite 120 ms latency and assume recovery next turn.
options.B: Federate fully over URLLC accepting 105 to 130 Mbps throughput with 7 to 10 ms latency and edge load up to 0.52.
options.C: Split federation with control messages on URLLC and bulk data on eMBB while tolerating 8.5 percent loss on eMBB.
options.D: Defer federation for one turn to wait for edge load to drop from 0.88 and reduce immediate risk.

records.question: At turn 6 a customer requests an on-network fine-tuning job that would run for the next two turns while the UAV continues its mission. The recent network history shows eMBB collapsing to 45 throughput with 120 latency and 8.5 loss at edge_load 0.88, followed by recovery on URLLC to latency between 7 and 10 with throughput between 110 and 140 and edge_load between 0.4 and 0.52. The job would consume a constant fraction of available throughput and would add pressure proportional to current edge_load for two turns. Battery is still at 100 and speed is 15 so energy is not the limiting factor. If degradation recurs, the worst case is that the slice must switch back to conditions seen at turn 6 for one additional turn. If conditions stay good, URLLC metrics remain near turn 9 to 10 levels for two turns. Accepting now yields immediate revenue but risks violating QoS for flight control if regret accumulates over multiple turns. Deferring by one turn delays revenue but may avoid compounding edge load during a possible relapse. Rejecting entirely avoids network risk but forfeits all revenue even if recovery holds. Considering worst case across the next two turns, which option should be selected?

options.A: Accept the training job immediately on URLLC using the current 110 to 140 throughput while edge_load is near 0.44.
options.B: Accept the training job immediately but switch back to eMBB to exploit the earlier 850 to 900 throughput.
options.C: Defer the training job by one turn and reassess after observing whether latency stays near 7 to 9 and edge_load near 0.4.
options.D: Reject the training job outright to keep latency below 10 and loss near 0.01 for all future turns.

records.question: At turn 6 the monitoring system flags a severe network anomaly after earlier stable operation. Telemetry shows latency jumped to 120 ms with jitter 25 ms, loss 8.5 percent, throughput 45 Mbps, and edge load 0.88 on eMBB. In prior and subsequent turns on URLLC, latency ranged from 7 ms to 10 ms, jitter from 0.7 ms to 1.2 ms, loss from 0.0 percent to 0.04 percent, throughput from 105 Mbps to 140 Mbps, and edge load from 0.4 to 0.52. The detection model estimates that over the next two turns latency could fall anywhere between 7 ms and 120 ms depending on whether the anomaly persists. Automated responses available include isolation, slice switching, rate limiting, and delayed recovery, each with side effects on throughput and edge load. Immediate isolation reduces loss but increases edge load by keeping traffic local near 0.52. Slice switching to URLLC restores low latency now but risks capacity stress if edge load trends upward. Rate limiting caps throughput near 45 Mbps but keeps edge load below 0.5. Delayed recovery leaves the system exposed for one more turn but avoids added load. Considering worst case persistence for two more turns and minimizing maximum regret, which option should be selected?

options.A: Immediately switch to URLLC only, accepting current edge load around 0.52 and latency near 9 ms while assuming recovery continues.
options.B: Fully isolate the affected segment now, tolerating edge load near 0.52 but preventing a repeat of 120 ms latency and 8.5 percent loss.
options.C: Apply rate limiting to hold throughput near 45 Mbps so edge load stays under about 0.5 even if latency returns to 120 ms.
options.D: Delay any action for one turn, relying on recent latency of 7 to 10 ms and loss under 0.04 percent to persist.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is experiencing severe network degradation with mMTC slice latency at 120ms, jitter at 25ms, loss at 2.5%, throughput at 1.2Mbps, and edge load at 0.85. The customer requests immediate initiation of a 500MB LLM fine-tuning job requiring 100Mbps sustained throughput and latency under 50ms for 3 turns. The UAV battery is at 100% but will deplete 15% per turn if training runs. The SLA mandates 99.9% completion probability and allows 10% data loss. If the job starts now, edge load will rise to 0.95 next turn, risking network collapse. If delayed, the UAV may enter a rain-induced signal shadow zone in turn 9, increasing latency to 200ms. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Accept the job now using mMTC slice; accept 2.5% loss and 120ms latency as within SLA tolerance.
options.B: Delay job until turn 9; assume weather clears and edge load drops to 0.6, enabling eMBB slice with 800Mbps throughput.
options.C: Switch to URLLC slice immediately; accept 40Mbps throughput and 8ms latency, but risk battery depletion to 70% by turn 10.
options.D: Reject the job; preserve battery and network stability for emergency landing, accepting 100% regret if weather improves.

records.question: The UAV is executing an emergency landing under rain with wind at 8.5 m/s from 240°, currently at 50m altitude with 100% battery, but network slice has degraded to URLLC with 7ms latency, 0.7ms jitter, 0.02% loss, 42 Mbps throughput, and 0.38 edge load. The mission requires transmitting high-fidelity AR overlays for ground crew guidance, which demands at least 100 Mbps throughput and sub-10ms latency for 3 more turns. If wind increases by 15% next turn, edge load may rise to 0.45, and if battery drops below 85% in 2 turns, throughput must be preserved for telemetry. URLLC guarantees latency but caps throughput at 50 Mbps; eMBB offers 800 Mbps but latency may spike to 20ms under load. Which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret across the next 3 turns while ensuring AR fidelity and safe landing?

options.A: Remain on URLLC: latency is guaranteed under 10ms, edge load is 0.38, and battery is 100%; throughput is insufficient but AR can be downgraded to 30fps at 720p.
options.B: Switch to eMBB: current throughput is 800 Mbps, latency is 15ms, and edge load is 0.6; if wind increases, latency may hit 20ms, risking AR desync, but battery remains sufficient for 3 turns.
options.C: Switch to mMTC: throughput is 1.5 Mbps, latency is 110ms, edge load is 0.8; this is unacceptable for AR but preserves battery for telemetry if landing fails; not viable for immersive guidance.
options.D: Hybrid mode: allocate 70% of edge resources to URLLC for control and 30% to eMBB for AR; projected edge load becomes 0.52, latency averages 12ms, throughput peaks at 250 Mbps; risk of violating SLA if wind increases further.

records.question: At turn 7, network slice has degraded to mMTC with 120ms latency, 25ms jitter, 2.1% loss, and 1.5Mbps throughput while edge load is 0.85. The UAV must process thermal imagery with SLA requiring <50ms latency and <1% loss. Onboard inference consumes 0.8W and takes 40ms, but edge inference under current conditions risks SLA violation. If network recovers to URLLC in 1 turn with 90% probability, or degrades further to 150ms latency with 10% probability, and edge load increases by 0.1 per turn, which placement minimizes maximum regret over the next 2 turns? Option A runs inference onboard. Option B queues for edge with current mMTC. Option C waits 1 turn for potential URLLC recovery. Option D switches to eMBB despite higher jitter. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Run inference onboard: latency 40ms, no network dependency, but consumes 0.8W and delays next task by 1 turn.
options.B: Queue for edge under mMTC: expected latency 120ms, 2.1% loss, violates SLA, edge load 0.85, may block future tasks.
options.C: Wait 1 turn for URLLC recovery: 90% chance of 10ms latency, 10% chance of 150ms latency, edge load rises to 0.95, risk of SLA breach.
options.D: Switch to eMBB: latency 35ms, jitter 6ms, loss 0.5%, throughput 80Mbps, edge load 0.6, but may not sustain if load increases.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is operating under mMTC slice with latency 120ms, jitter 25ms, packet loss 2.1%, throughput 1.5Mbps, and edge load 0.85. The SLA mandates latency under 100ms and edge load under 0.8. The next turn will involve a mandatory telemetry upload requiring 5Mbps throughput. Wind speed is 8m/s and battery is at 100%. If edge load increases by 0.05 per turn under current conditions, and latency degrades by 10ms per 0.1 edge load increase, which option minimizes maximum regret over the next two turns while preserving mission continuity? A: Stay on mMTC, accept SLA violation, and hope for recovery. B: Switch to URLLC immediately, accepting 50Mbps throughput cap and 0.32 edge load, but risking future overload if telemetry upload fails. C: Switch to eMBB, accepting 30ms latency and 0.5 edge load, but risking 0.6 edge load next turn if upload succeeds. D: Disable non-critical sensors, reducing edge load by 0.15, and remain on mMTC with projected 0.7 edge load next turn, accepting 110ms latency.

options.A: Stay on mMTC, accept SLA violation, and hope for recovery.
options.B: Switch to URLLC immediately, accepting 50Mbps throughput cap and 0.32 edge load, but risking future overload if telemetry upload fails.
options.C: Switch to eMBB, accepting 30ms latency and 0.5 edge load, but risking 0.6 edge load next turn if upload succeeds.
options.D: Disable non-critical sensors, reducing edge load by 0.15, and remain on mMTC with projected 0.7 edge load next turn, accepting 110ms latency.

records.question: At turn 7, network telemetry shows mMTC slice with 120ms latency, 25ms jitter, 2.1% loss, 1.5Mbps throughput, and 85% edge load. The UAV is at 200m altitude with 100% battery, and policy restricts altitude to 100–1200m. Wind is 8m/s from 240°, and radar is offline. If degradation persists, edge load may rise to 92% next turn, increasing latency to 150ms with 30ms jitter. URLLC offers 10ms latency but only 55Mbps throughput and 40% edge load, while eMBB has 35ms latency but 80Mbps throughput and 60% edge load. Given that mission-critical telemetry must be offloaded within 100ms to avoid SLA violation, and assuming worst-case jitter adds 30ms to latency, which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret over the next two turns?

options.A: Offload via URLLC: latency 10ms + 30ms jitter = 40ms, within 100ms SLA, edge load 40% leaves 60% headroom, throughput 55Mbps sufficient for telemetry.
options.B: Offload via eMBB: latency 35ms + 30ms jitter = 65ms, within SLA, throughput 80Mbps higher, but edge load 60% may rise to 75% next turn, risking 85ms latency + 35ms jitter = 120ms violation.
options.C: Delay offload until next turn: current mMTC latency 120ms + 25ms jitter = 145ms violates SLA; projected 150ms + 30ms jitter = 180ms, guaranteeing violation if delayed.
options.D: Attempt local processing: UAV CPU load is 70%, thermal sensor generates 120MB/min, local storage has 2GB free, but processing latency 200ms exceeds SLA by 100ms.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV is operating under mMTC slice with latency 120ms, jitter 25ms, packet loss 2.1%, throughput 1.5Mbps, and edge load 0.85. The SLA requires latency < 50ms, loss < 1.0%, and throughput > 5Mbps for mission-critical telemetry. Wind is 8m/s from 240°, and battery is at 85%. If degradation persists, latency may rise to 150ms next turn with 95% confidence, and edge load may hit 0.95. The UAV must complete one more telemetry read before initiating return. Option A switches to URLLC now, guaranteeing latency 10ms but reducing throughput to 55Mbps and risking battery drain to 70% by landing. Option B stays on mMTC, risking SLA violation with 80% probability next turn and potential mission abort. Option C switches to eMBB, offering 30ms latency and 95Mbps throughput but with 30% chance of jitter spiking to 15ms, which may trigger safety protocols. Option D delays decision until turn 8, accepting 100% SLA violation risk this turn but preserving battery for emergency maneuvers. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Switch to URLLC immediately to guarantee latency compliance despite battery cost.
options.B: Remain on mMTC to preserve battery, accepting high SLA violation risk next turn.
options.C: Switch to eMBB for balanced latency and throughput, accepting jitter uncertainty.
options.D: Delay decision until turn 8, accepting immediate SLA violation to preserve battery.

records.question: At turn 7, the network slice has degraded to mMTC with 120ms latency, 25ms jitter, 2.1% loss, and 1.5Mbps throughput while edge load is at 0.85. The UAV is 1.2km from home, traveling at 35m/s, and battery is at 78%. A third-party request offers $1200 for 30 seconds of edge compute to process thermal imagery, requiring 2Mbps throughput and 50ms latency SLA. Another request offers $800 for 20 seconds of URLLC-grade compute with 10ms latency and 1Mbps throughput. A third party proposes $1500 for 40 seconds of compute but allows 150ms latency and 1Mbps throughput. The fourth option is to reject all and reserve compute for mission-critical telemetry, which requires 0.5Mbps and 100ms latency. Given that edge load may increase by 0.1 per turn if compute is allocated, and network recovery to eMBB is uncertain within 3 turns, which option should be selected?

options.A: Accept the $1200 request requiring 2Mbps and 50ms latency, as it offers the highest immediate revenue and current throughput exceeds requirement.
options.B: Accept the $800 URLLC request, as it aligns with current slice capabilities and minimizes latency risk.
options.C: Accept the $1500 request allowing 150ms latency, as it maximizes revenue and current latency is 120ms, leaving a 30ms margin.
options.D: Reject all and reserve compute for telemetry, as edge load is already 0.85 and any allocation risks exceeding 1.0 within 2 turns.

records.question: At turn 7, network telemetry shows mMTC slice with 120ms latency, 25ms jitter, 2.1% loss, 1.5Mbps throughput, and 0.85 edge load. The UAV is at 200m altitude with 100% battery, and the mission requires RAG-augmented decision-making for next 3 turns under fog and 8m/s wind. Policy allows altitude between 100m and 1200m. If latency must stay under 50ms for RAG to function and edge load must not exceed 0.9, and assuming worst-case jitter adds 30ms to latency and loss may increase by 0.5% per turn, which option should be selected to minimize maximum regret over turns 8–10 while preserving mission continuity?

options.A: Switch to URLLC slice now; latency 10ms, jitter 2ms, loss 0.1%, throughput 55Mbps, edge load 0.4 — but may not sustain 3 turns if edge load rises above 0.85.
options.B: Stay on mMTC; latency 120ms exceeds RAG limit, but edge load 0.85 is under 0.9 — risk mission failure if latency remains high for 3 turns.
options.C: Switch to eMBB; latency 30ms, jitter 5ms, loss 0.3%, throughput 95Mbps, edge load 0.5 — but jitter may push latency to 60ms under worst-case, violating RAG.
options.D: Delay decision until turn 8; assume network recovers to eMBB with 25ms latency — but if degradation persists, RAG fails for 3 turns with 120ms+ latency.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV agent detects severe network degradation with latency spiking to 120ms, jitter at 25ms, packet loss at 2.1%, and edge load at 0.85, while throughput drops to 1.5Mbps under mMTC slice. The agent must now decide whether to re-authenticate under a new identity to access a prioritized slice, knowing that identity reassignment incurs a 3-second handover delay and risks temporary loss of swarm coordination. The policy allows identity reassignment only if projected edge load after reassignment remains below 0.75 for the next two turns, and the UAV must maintain at least 95% sensor availability over the next 3 turns. Given that the current mission requires thermal imaging every 2 turns and lidar navigation is active, which option should be selected?

options.A: Reassign identity to URLLC slice immediately; projected edge load after handover is 0.35, but thermal imaging will be delayed by 3 seconds and may miss the next scheduled capture.
options.B: Maintain current mMTC identity; edge load is 0.85 which exceeds policy limit, but thermal imaging can proceed without delay and lidar navigation remains unaffected.
options.C: Reassign identity to eMBB slice; projected edge load is 0.68, within policy, but latency will remain above 25ms, risking collision avoidance failure if wind gusts increase by 20%.
options.D: Delay reassignment for one turn to monitor recovery; current edge load is 0.85, but if it drops to 0.70 next turn, reassignment becomes permissible without handover penalty.

records.question: At turn 7, the UAV’s network slice degraded to mMTC with 120ms latency, 25ms jitter, 2.1% loss, and 1.5Mbps throughput while edge load hit 0.85. The UAV must initiate federated model aggregation with three edge nodes: Node A (battery 85%, 100m distance, 50ms max latency SLA), Node B (battery 70%, 300m distance, 80ms max latency SLA), and Node C (battery 95%, 500m distance, 100ms max latency SLA). The UAV’s current battery is 78% and consumes 0.5% per km flown. The mission requires at least 80% battery upon return. If network conditions remain at worst-case mMTC levels for the next two turns, and edge load increases by 0.1 per turn, which node should the UAV prioritize for federated update to minimize regret over the next three turns while preserving safety margins?

options.A: Node A: closest, lowest latency SLA, but requires 0.1km flight (0.05% battery), and edge load may exceed 0.95 by turn 9 under worst-case.
options.B: Node B: medium distance, 80ms SLA, requires 0.3km flight (0.15% battery), edge load projected to hit 0.95 by turn 9, risking SLA violation if jitter spikes.
options.C: Node C: farthest, 100ms SLA, requires 0.5km flight (0.25% battery), edge load projected to hit 0.95 by turn 9, but SLA margin is largest at 20ms under current jitter.
options.D: None: abort federated update; preserve battery and avoid SLA risk under mMTC degradation and rising edge load.

records.question: At turn 7, network slice degrades to mMTC with 120ms latency, 25ms jitter, 2.1% loss, and 1.5Mbps throughput while edge load hits 0.85. The UAV’s thermal sensor is active, consuming 8Mbps bandwidth, and the mission requires transmitting thermal imagery to a third-party analytics agent under GDPR Article 9 constraints. The analytics agent has a trust score of 0.65 and a historical SLA compliance rate of 82% ± 3%. If the UAV continues transmission, projected edge load in turn 8 will exceed 0.9 under worst-case jitter amplification. Alternatively, disabling the sensor reduces throughput demand to 0.5Mbps but forfeits 70% of mission value. A third option routes data via a trusted relay with 0.85 trust score but adds 40ms fixed latency. A fourth option delays transmission until turn 9, when network recovery is projected at 75% probability, but risks mission timeout if recovery fails. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue transmission to third-party agent; trust score 0.65 exceeds minimum 0.6, and SLA compliance 82% is acceptable under GDPR.
options.B: Disable thermal sensor; reduces edge load to 0.5Mbps, avoids network overload, and preserves UAV safety under current conditions.
options.C: Route via trusted relay; adds 40ms latency but ensures 0.85 trust score and avoids edge load violation with 95% confidence.
options.D: Delay transmission until turn 9; leverages 75% recovery probability to restore eMBB slice, minimizing regret if recovery occurs.

records.question: At turn 7, telemetry reveals network degradation: latency spiked to 120ms, jitter to 25ms, packet loss to 2.1%, throughput collapsed to 1.5Mbps, and edge load reached 0.85 under mMTC slice. The UAV is at 200m altitude with 100% battery, and radar remains offline. If degradation persists for two more turns, edge load may hit 0.95, risking SLA violation. The mission requires at least 5Mbps throughput and under 50ms latency for safe navigation. Option A switches to URLLC immediately, guaranteeing 10ms latency and 55Mbps throughput but consuming 15% battery per turn. Option B stays on mMTC, risking throughput drop to 0.5Mbps next turn and potential collision due to delayed telemetry. Option C reverts to eMBB, which previously delivered 95Mbps but with 35ms latency and 0.5% loss, though edge load may exceed 0.7 next turn. Option D initiates emergency landing, forfeiting mission but preserving 100% battery and ensuring zero network risk. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Switch to URLLC slice immediately, accepting 15% battery drain per turn to guarantee sub-10ms latency and 55Mbps throughput.
options.B: Remain on mMTC slice, accepting risk of throughput falling below 0.5Mbps and latency exceeding 150ms in next turn.
options.C: Revert to eMBB slice, accepting 35ms latency and 0.5% loss, with edge load projected to exceed 0.7 next turn.
options.D: Initiate emergency landing, forfeiting mission but preserving full battery and eliminating all network risk.

records.question: The mission began as an inspection using eMBB with low loss at 0.05 to 0.2 percent and latency around 11 to 14 ms, then briefly shifted to URLLC with latency 7 to 9 ms and loss 0.01 to 0.03 percent. During turns 6 and 7 the network degraded on mMTC with latency rising to 45 and then 52 ms, jitter reaching 12 to 15 ms, loss increasing to 1.8 and 2.1 percent, and edge load peaking at 0.91. The user intent at turn 6 was framed as reporting fluctuation, but at turn 8 the user requested resuming high quality streaming while edge load was still 0.62. Over the last three turns the agent alternated between degraded adaptation, pending restoration, and full URLLC execution. The UAV remained within policy altitude bounds of 10 to 120 m, but battery was initially 100 percent and no recharge occurred. If network degradation persists one more turn at the worst observed values, the system must infer whether the user intent has drifted from safe inspection completion to performance prioritization. One option is to interpret the restore request as benign because URLLC metrics look good at turn 8. Another option is to flag intent drift because the request increases future risk under worst case mMTC recurrence. A third option is to defer judgment until after the spiral inspection already completed at turn 9. A fourth option is to assume intent consistency because the final return to home was later requested. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Treat the restore request as benign since latency dropped to 9 ms and loss to 0.03 percent on URLLC at turn 8 despite edge load 0.62.
options.B: Flag intent drift because requesting high quality streaming while worst case loss is 2.1 percent and edge load reached 0.91 increases future mission risk.
options.C: Defer intent assessment until after turn 9 since the spiral inspection completed with latency 6 ms and edge load 0.55.
options.D: Assume no drift because the user later requested return to home with stable eMBB latency of 13 ms and loss 0.1 percent.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV is in icing conditions and has just reduced stream quality while operating on the mMTC slice. The observed network metrics are latency 52 ms, jitter 15 ms, loss 2.1 percent, throughput 0.9 Mbps, and edge load 0.91. One turn earlier on mMTC the latency was 45 ms with edge load 0.88, showing a rising congestion trend. Earlier in the mission URLLC showed latency between 6 and 9 ms with throughput between 120 and 160 Mbps but edge load climbed as high as 0.62. The UAV speed is 28 mps and altitude must remain within the policy bounds of 10 to 120 m. Battery is still 100 percent so endurance is not the immediate constraint. The operator must decide whether to switch slices again or hold steady for the next two turns to finish data transfer and navigation safely. Assume the worst case that congestion persists or slightly worsens next turn rather than recovering. Also assume that switching slices incurs at least one turn of adaptation instability under icing conditions. No option avoids some performance loss over the next two turns. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Immediately switch to URLLC because its latency was as low as 6 to 9 ms earlier even though its edge load reached 0.62.
options.B: Stay on mMTC for the next two turns despite 52 ms latency and 0.91 edge load, relying on reduced stream quality to cap further degradation.
options.C: Switch back to eMBB which previously had 13 to 14 ms latency and edge load around 0.41 to 0.51.
options.D: Defer any decision for one turn and then switch slices only if latency exceeds the current 52 ms value.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV is mid mission in icing conditions with wind at 8.5 mps and is navigating while network health has degraded. Recent telemetry shows latency rose from 45 ms at turn 6 to 52 ms at turn 7 with jitter increasing from 12 ms to 15 ms and loss from 1.8 pct to 2.1 pct on the mMTC slice. Edge load also increased from 0.88 to 0.91 while throughput dropped from 1.2 Mbps to 0.9 Mbps. Battery remains at 100 pct and speed is 28 mps within altitude bounds of 10 to 120 m. The operator considers whether to continue the mission for the next two turns assuming the degradation may persist or partially recover. Policy requires safe command and control even if the worst recent network values repeat. If the network recovers to URLLC levels seen earlier with latency 9 ms and jitter 1.1 ms the mission could finish efficiently. If the worst case persists for two more turns the edge load could remain near saturation and loss above 2 pct. Each option below has some downside either now or in the next two turns. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Continue immediately with high quality streaming restored, relying on the recent URLLC values of 9 ms latency and 0.03 pct loss seen at turn 8.
options.B: Abort the mission now and return to home despite battery at 100 pct and stable speed of 28 mps.
options.C: Continue conservatively with reduced stream quality under mMTC, accepting 45 to 52 ms latency and 12 to 15 ms jitter while monitoring edge load near 0.9 for the next two turns.
options.D: Switch to URLLC control only and increase data uploads assuming throughput of 130 to 160 Mbps will remain available.

records.question: At turn 6 the operator must decide how to onboard and authenticate the UAV agent identity while the network shifts from URLLC to mMTC. Recent telemetry shows latency varying between 7 ms and 52 ms across turns, jitter between 0.7 ms and 15 ms, and loss between 0.01 pct and 2.1 pct. Edge load has risen from 0.48 to 0.91, while throughput has dropped from 150 Mbps to 0.9 Mbps. The UAV battery is at 100 pct and speed is 28 mps, so mission continuation is not energy limited. Identity onboarding requires periodic re authentication traffic that competes with mission data on the same slice. If the degradation persists for the next two turns, re authentication delays can accumulate. If recovery occurs as in turn 8, high frequency re binding may waste capacity. The goal is to minimize worst case regret across both futures rather than optimize the current turn. All options satisfy baseline security policy but differ in identity mapping stability and network cost. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Bind the agent to a persistent device identity with cached credentials, requiring no re authentication traffic for the next two turns even if latency reaches 52 ms and edge load stays near 0.91.
options.B: Use a fully ephemeral session identity that re authenticates every turn, assuming average latency near 12 ms and throughput above 100 Mbps will return quickly.
options.C: Migrate the agent to a shared edge hosted identity that synchronizes state each turn, adding control traffic proportional to edge load 0.88 to 0.91.
options.D: Delay identity onboarding until after return to home, relying on current URLLC performance at 7 ms latency and 0.48 edge load.

records.question: At turn 7 the UAV is in icing conditions with wind at 8.5 mps and is executing thermal inspection while RGB and thermal sensors are available but lidar and radar remain offline. The network has degraded to mMTC with latency rising from 45 ms at turn 6 to 52 ms at turn 7, jitter increasing from 12 ms to 15 ms, loss between 1.8 and 2.1 percent, throughput below 1.2 Mbps, and edge load near 0.91. Earlier URLLC turns showed latency between 6 and 9 ms but edge load climbed as high as 0.62, creating uncertainty about sustained recovery. The UAV speed is 28 mps and altitude must stay within the 10 to 120 m policy bounds during the next two turns as it completes navigation and return. The perception task needs obstacle awareness over the next two turns even if mMTC conditions persist one more turn. High resolution RGB requires eMBB-like throughput, while thermal-only streams tolerate lower throughput but degrade spatial detail. Edge fusion reduces uplink load but increases edge load, which is already high. Local fusion reduces network dependence but increases onboard uncertainty without lidar or radar. Considering worst case latency and loss if mMTC persists and edge load spikes again, which sensing stream and fusion strategy should be selected?

options.A: Select high resolution RGB plus thermal with edge-based fusion assuming URLLC recovery to 9 ms latency and 130 Mbps throughput next turn despite current 0.91 edge load.
options.B: Select thermal-only streaming with local fusion at current quality, accepting 52 ms latency and up to 2.1 percent loss to minimize dependence on edge load over the next two turns.
options.C: Select downsampled RGB plus thermal with edge fusion, counting on eMBB throughput near 780 Mbps while edge load remains below 0.62 as seen previously.
options.D: Select thermal-only with edge fusion, assuming loss stays near the 1.8 percent mean and ignoring the worst case 2.1 percent under mMTC.

records.question: During turn 7 the UAV is en route in icing weather with wind at 8.5 mps and battery still at 100 percent while operating within the 10 to 120 meter altitude policy. Network telemetry has degraded from earlier URLLC performance to mMTC with latency rising from 45 to 52 ms, jitter from 12 to 15 ms, loss from 1.8 to 2.1 percent, throughput falling to 0.9 to 1.2 Mbps, and edge load increasing from 0.88 to 0.91. Over the previous turns the agent alternated slices, with URLLC showing latency as low as 6 to 9 ms but edge load up to 0.62. The operator expects the inspection to continue for at least the next two turns unless aborted. Collision avoidance coordination depends on timely updates, but high quality streaming is not strictly required to maintain safety. If degradation persists one more turn, worst case network conditions must be assumed rather than mean values. Command escalation to other agents increases coordination overhead and edge load in the following turn. Reducing stream quality lowers throughput demand but may require longer mission time within the same altitude band. Switching immediately back to URLLC improves latency now but risks capacity saturation if edge load grows. Considering worst case metrics across the next two turns, which option should be selected?

options.A: Immediately switch to URLLC since latency can drop to 9 ms and loss to 0.03 percent, accepting edge load around 0.62 for the next turn.
options.B: Remain on mMTC while keeping reduced stream quality, tolerating latency up to 52 ms and loss up to 2.1 percent to avoid increasing edge load beyond 0.91.
options.C: Escalate coordination to additional agents now, increasing edge load above 0.91 but aiming to shorten mission time within the 10 to 120 meter policy band.
options.D: Abort inspection and return to home immediately, avoiding further exposure to loss above 1.8 percent but forfeiting completion after turn 7.

records.question: At turn 9 the UAV has completed a spiral scan and queued data to an edge storage agent while operating under URLLC with 6 ms latency, 0.7 ms jitter, 0.01 percent loss, 160 Mbps throughput and edge load 0.55. Earlier turns showed a degradation case on mMTC with latency rising to 52 ms, jitter to 15 ms, loss to 2.1 percent, throughput falling to 0.9 Mbps and edge load peaking at 0.91. The third party edge storage agent requests expanded exposure including raw thermal frames, write access to upload APIs and temporary compute to preprocess data. The UAV battery is at 100 percent and speed was 28.0 mps during flight, but future network behavior over the next two turns is uncertain given the prior oscillation between URLLC and mMTC. The airspace policy enforces altitude bounds between 10.0 and 120.0 which constrains recovery maneuvers if control traffic is delayed. If the next turn regresses to the worst observed mMTC conditions, edge load could again exceed 0.88 while throughput remains below 1.2 Mbps. Limiting exposure reduces immediate data utility but may preserve control margin under high loss. Granting more exposure improves single turn upload success but risks compounding congestion if degradation persists for two turns. Revoking access entirely avoids risk but creates data backlog that must be transmitted later under the same constraints. Considering worst case network regression over the next two turns and minimizing maximum regret across outcomes, which exposure option should be selected?

options.A: Grant full raw data, full upload API access and edge compute now because current URLLC latency is 6 ms and throughput is 160 Mbps at edge load 0.55.
options.B: Grant raw data read and upload API access but deny edge compute since prior mMTC loss reached 2.1 percent and edge load peaked at 0.91.
options.C: Grant only downsampled thermal summaries with rate limiting and no edge compute, deferring raw uploads until network stability improves.
options.D: Revoke all third party access until mission end because altitude bounds of 10.0 to 120.0 limit maneuvering under delayed control.

records.question: At turn 8, the UAV is in emergency hover mode due to network degradation, with edge_load at 0.65, latency at 45ms, and packet loss at 2.1%. Data capture requires sustained loss below 1.0 percent or buffering will accumulate and delay return. Reducing sensor resolution lowers throughput demand by the same factor already applied at turn 7, while switching slices trades latency for capacity. If buffering exceeds one turn, projected return is delayed into a third turn with higher regret due to airspace occupancy. Which option should be selected to keep the intent feasible with minimum worst case regret over the next three turns?

options.A: Remain on URLLC with current sensor settings, relying on observed 9 ms latency and 0.02 percent loss to finish the next two turns quickly.
options.B: Switch immediately to eMBB to exploit 800 plus Mbps throughput despite 14 ms latency and 0.2 percent loss seen previously.
options.C: Stay on URLLC but keep reduced sensor resolution and cached waypoints, accepting 110 to 130 Mbps throughput and edge_load near 0.5.
options.D: Defer survey data transmission entirely for one turn, continue capture at full resolution, and tolerate potential 115 ms latency if mMTC recurs.

records.question: At turn 9 the mission nominally resumes survey, but earlier turns show rapid intent and network shifts. The UAV speed is 35.0 mps and altitude policy bounds are 50.0 to 1200.0 while the vehicle is already at survey altitude. Network latency moved from 12 ms on eMBB at turn 1 to 120 ms on mMTC at turn 6 and then back to 9 ms on URLLC by turn 9. Edge load increased from 0.35 at turn 1 to 0.85 at turn 6 before dropping to 0.48 at turn 9. Packet loss peaked at 8.0 percent at turn 6 and recovered to 0.02 percent by turn 9. Over the next one to three turns the worst case is that edge load rebounds toward 0.85 while URLLC capacity remains limited. A detector must decide whether the dominant intent has drifted from recon to risk containment rather than simply reacting to transient network noise. Which option should be selected?

options.A: Classify no intent drift because URLLC latency is 9 ms with 0.02 percent loss at turn 9 and continue recon despite prior 120 ms latency.
options.B: Classify temporary network-induced deviation only, since throughput recovered to 125 Mbps and edge load fell to 0.48, and ignore the return-to-base request.
options.C: Classify intent drift toward mission termination because the sequence from 8.0 percent loss and 0.85 edge load to a return-to-base request minimizes worst-case regret if degradation persists one more turn.
options.D: Classify sensor-management drift because resolution was reduced at turn 7 when throughput was 1.8 Mbps, assuming network conditions will stay near turn 9 values.

records.question: At turn 9 the UAV resumes survey while returning data and the network has recently oscillated across slices. URLLC shows latency values of 9 ms with jitter 1.3 ms, loss 0.02 percent, throughput 125 Mbps, and edge_load around 0.48. Earlier URLLC readings ranged from 7 to 10 ms latency and edge_load from 0.42 to 0.5 across turns 4 to 8. eMBB previously provided 14 ms latency, 2.5 ms jitter, 0.2 percent loss, 800 Mbps throughput, and edge_load 0.4 at turn 10. A severe anomaly occurred at turns 6 and 7 on mMTC with latency 115 to 120 ms, jitter above 22 ms, loss above 7.5 percent, throughput below 1.8 Mbps, and edge_load above 0.82. Assume worst case persistence of the highest observed edge_load and latency for any selected slice over the next two turns.
